The night isn’t as hot as it’d been over the last week, but sweat still trickles down the sides of my body. I’ve applied enough aftershave and deodorant to hide any smell my body can come up with, though there’s more than enough aftershave and perfume already hanging in the air. Walking down this street has me scented for free within seconds.
zh_text:
開滿酒吧與餐館的牛津街人稱條紋區。那是個人肉市場，廉價的女孩會在那裡挑逗幾十個男人，最後每個都會跟她們上床。光這個街區裡就有七、八家這種酒吧，全都面臨河景。位於河道另外一邊的斜對角上，距離最近的酒吧約莫一百公尺的地方就是警局。禮拜五晚上雅芳河裡的尿跟水的比例大概是一比一。鰻魚翻肚漂在河面上、鴨子在河岸叼起用過的保險套，小魚爲了逃離河水而癱在河畔的草地上等死，偶爾還會跟不省人事的酒鬼躺在一起。
接近條紋區時，我自腰帶上拔出手槍，塞到夾克口袋裡，然後脫下夾克，拿在手上。汗水沿著身側流下。我擦了足以掩飾體味的鬍後水和芳香劑，不過空氣中已經瀰漫著過量鬍後水和香水的味道。在這條街上走個幾秒就讓我免費擦了一層香水。

en_text: It’s after midnight and The Strip is getting livelier. All week long women are heading straight home from work and locking their doors, afraid that what has been happening to their counterparts in the news might happen to them. Any other day of the week, there is a general awareness that things are not as safe as they ought to be. Yet come Friday and Saturday nights, all those fears are pushed aside so that the good times can roll. Here, most of the women are young and underdressed. They try to cram their way into clubs they think must be popular because of the lines of people waiting outside. Bouncers stand with their arms crossed and their muscles bulging. They have attitude problems they like everyone to know about.
zh_text: 午夜已過，不過夜生活才剛要開始。條紋區人聲鼎沸。女人一整個禮拜下班過後都直接回家，鎖上大門，深怕發生在新聞中的女人身上的事情也會發生在她們身上。一週中其他的日子，人們都會意識到他們的生活不如想像中安全。然而每到禮拜五和禮拜六晚上，她們就會放下所有恐懼，盡情狂歡。這裡大部分的女人都很年輕，而且穿得很少。她們努力擠進因為門口大排長龍所以必定很熱門的俱樂部。保鏢鼓脹的手臂橫抱胸前，站在門口。他們的脾氣都不好，而且希望所有人知道這一點。

en_text: The Strip is the highlight of town for most locals. Already the drum ’n’ bass, the techno, and the hip-hop deafen me. The only thing I know about hip-hop is that I hate it, and I ﬁgure that’s all anybody knows about it. We may have evolved from something that crawled out of a swamp and continued to evolve as monkeys became men, but boy-racers and hip-hop music are proof we’ve hit our peak and are now heading backward. It could take at least thirty minutes to get inside any of these places, so I head deeper into the city, walking down Cashel Mall passing shoe shops and clothing stores in search of another club or bar. Perhaps one that’s quieter. I ﬁnd it eventually—a club with an open front where the music isn’t quite so loud and a lot more bearable and there’s room to sit. The crowd seems to be made up of people from their midtwenties through to their late thirties. Guess that makes me average.
zh_text: 條紋區對大部分的本地人而言是城內最熱鬧的地方。鼓和貝斯、電音，以及嘻哈音樂震耳欲聾。要進入任何一間俱樂部起碼都得排上三十分鐘，於是我深入城內，走向凱歇爾購物中心，尋找其他俱樂部或酒吧。或許找間比較安靜點的。最後我終於找到了——大門敞開的俱樂部，音樂沒有那麼大聲，而且裡面還有空的座位。顧客的年齡層介於二十五歲到四十歲之間，看來我的年齡適中。

en_text: I make my way inside, sidestepping the bouncer with a smile and without a comment from either of us. There’s a sea of people to greet me, but not an ocean. I push my way through, keeping a tight grip on my jacket. At the bar I’m served by a delicious blonde—tight white top, short black skirt, great tits. I order myself a gin and tonic. Expensive, but you can’t go into town on a Friday or Saturday night and not expect to spend a small fortune. I could have stayed at home and had the same drink for a quarter of the price, but there would be nobody to watch. I sit at the bar, nurse my drink, and watch the crowd around me. Mostly men wearing expensive clothing they can’t afford, attempting to look richer and more impressive than they really are. Caretakers, laborers, plumbers, shop assistants—all dressed to look like lawyers. Whereas the lawyers are at other bars, dressed to look like casual guys. The women, even the fat chicks, dress to look like sluts. Not that I’m complaining. It’s here where men ﬂock to get a glance at potential bedtime stories to tell their friends on Monday morning. Women come here to be easy. To be free.
zh_text: 我走了進去，橫跨一步，在一言不發的情況下笑著路過保鏢。裡面人山人海，不過還沒到一片汪洋的地步。我在人群中擠來擠去，一手緊握夾克。吧台有位美味可口的金髮女侍爲我服務——緊身白上衣、黑短裙、棒呆了的咪咪。我點了一杯橙味伏特加。很貴，不過想在禮拜五或禮拜六晚上進市區鬼混就得要有花錢的準備。我可以待在家裡，花四分之一的錢享受同樣的飲料，但是這樣就沒人可供欣賞了。我坐在吧台上，慢慢喝著酒，看著四周的人群。大部分的男人都穿著他們負擔不起的昂貴服飾，試圖裝扮出比他們本身有錢有勢的模樣。工友、勞工、水電工、店員——全都打扮成像是律師。真正的律師則都在其他酒吧裡，打扮成像是普通男子的模樣。這裡的女人，包括胖妞在內，全作蕩婦打扮。倒不是說我有什麼好抱怨的。男人就是在這種地方找尋可以在禮拜一早上跟同事炫耀的床邊故事。女人則是來這裡讓人釣的，免費。

en_text: From all corners of the club, lights ﬂicker and dance and throb and pulse at my eyes. I ﬁnish my drink, order another. I look up at the roof and check for any surveillance cameras covering the bar. Nothing. The music is getting louder. My ears are humming.
zh_text: 俱樂部中每個角落傳來的光線都在我的眼中閃爍、飛舞、衝擊、跳動。我喝完飲料，又點了一杯。我抬起頭來，觀察有沒有監視攝影機可以照到吧台。沒有。音樂越來越大聲。我的耳朵嗡嗡作響。

en_text: In a place like this, women only speak to you for one of three reasons: you’re either extremely good-looking, you look extremely rich, or they’re telling you to get lost and stop bothering them. Tonight I’m wearing expensive clothing. Money’s no object when it comes to clothes, because a few of my victims have had husbands my size. I’m also wearing a rather expensive wristwatch—a Tag Heuer that cost victim number three’s husband three thousand dollars. It has a sapphire crystal face that can’t be scratched and a metal bracelet strap. Not as costly as a Rolex, but Rolexes don’t retain a high market value; they’re ugly, worn only by old men and Asians.
zh_text: 在這種地方，女人只會爲了三個理由與你交談：要嘛就是你非常英俊，不然就是看來極度有錢，再來就是告訴你快點滾開，別煩她們。今晚我身穿昂貴的服飾。花錢買衣服的時候我絕不手軟，因爲有些被害人的丈夫跟我一樣帥。我同時也帶著一支昂貴的手錶——花了第三號被害人老公三千塊的豪雅錶。耐刮的藍寶石水晶錶面以及金屬錶帶。沒勞力士那麼貴，不過勞力士根本沒有那個價值；它們很醜，只有老人和亞洲人才喜歡。

en_text: It takes thirty minutes and three drinks for a woman to come up to me. Out of the overalls, I don’t look like the simple guy the guys at the station think I am. Clothes make all the difference. She forces her way to the bar and stands next to me. She turns and smiles. Acknowledges my existence. A good start. She orders a drink. Just one.
zh_text: 在三十分鐘和三杯飲料過後，一名女子來到我的面前。脫掉工作服後，我看起來一點也不像警局那些人眼中的單純男子。穿著能夠改變一切。她擠到吧台前，站在我的身旁。她轉過身來，向我微笑。承認我的存在。好的開始。她點了一杯飲料。就一杯。

en_text: “Hi there.” I have to shout to be heard over the music.
zh_text: 「嗨，妳好。」我必須用吼的才能蓋過音樂。

en_text: “Hi.” I peg her to be around twenty-seven, maybe twenty-eight years old. Five feet six, slim. Like the chick behind the bar, she has a nice pair. In this light she looks like she has purple skin. Maybe she does. Her hair looks purple too. I can’t tell what color her eyes are.
zh_text: 我猜想她二十七，或許二十八歲。五呎六吋，身材苗條。就像吧台後方的小妞一樣，她也有一對好咪咪。在這種燈光下，她的皮膚看起來像是紫色的。或許真是紫色。她的頭髮也像紫色。我看不出她的眼睛是什麼顏色。

en_text: “How’s it going?” I shout.
zh_text: 「妳好嗎？」我叫道。

en_text: “Good,” she says, nodding. “Good. And you?”
zh_text: 「不錯。」她點頭說道。「不錯。你呢？」

en_text: “Yeah. Good,” I say, then suddenly realize I don’t know what to say next. That’s always been my problem. Social skills don’t come easy to me. If they did, I wouldn’t have to break into women’s homes; I’d be able to talk my way in. So . . . Come here often? No, I’m not going to ask that. “Boy, I wish I could come up with something that made me sound impressive.” She laughs, and maybe that’s because she’s heard the line before, or knows how quickly our conversation became awkward. “I was hoping you’d be impressive.”
zh_text: 「是啊。不錯。」我說，接著突然發現我不知道接下來該說什麼。這一直都是我的問題。我不擅長社交技巧。要是擅長的話，我就不用闖入女人家中；我就可以靠一張嘴混進去。「那麼……」常來嗎？不，我才不要問那個。「天呀，真希望我能想出什麼令妳印象深刻的台詞。」她笑了，或許是因為她聽過這句台詞，或是察覺我們的對話迅速變得尷尬。「我原本期待你能讓我印象深刻。」

en_text: This is a good sign. Funny. Good sense of humor. Great smile. And she’s still here, hasn’t told me to get lost. I study her outﬁt. A short black skirt. A dark red top that shows the tops of her ﬁrm breasts. The back of the top shows most of her back, except where the material strings across to hold it in place. She isn’t wearing a bra. Black leather shoes that have ﬁnger-width strands of leather crisscrossing over them. She’s wearing a thin gold necklace, and a gold watch that looks like an expensive Omega. I shrug. “I was kind of hoping for the same thing.”
zh_text: 這是個好兆頭。愛開玩笑、有幽默感、甜美的微笑，而且她還在我面前，沒叫我滾開。我打量她的裝扮。黑短裙。凸顯堅挺乳房的深紅上衣。上衣後方露出她大部分的背部，除了固定上衣用的細線。沒穿內衣。她戴著一條細細的金項鍊，還有一支看來十分昂貴的歐米茄金錢。我聳肩。「我原本也是如此期待。」

en_text: The other thing I keep in mind is that even though women who frequent these places may look like sluts, and may in fact be easy, going home with one takes a mighty amount of skill, charm, persuasion, or dumb luck—none of which I have in spades. It’s all about salesmanship. Here you have a good-looking woman, wanting to make a purchase, just looking for the right guy, and knowing that if you’re not it, there’s another one a few feet away.
zh_text: 另一件我始終牢記的事情就是儘管常來這裡的女人看起來都像蕩婦，也可能真的很容易勾搭，不過想要帶她們回家還是需要一大堆技巧、魅力、勸說，或是好運——而我在這些方面都不突出。說到底還是要看推銷能力。你面前站著一名美貌女子，想要跟個男人回家，只是在挑恰當的對象，而且深知如果你不是她要找的人，旁邊還有很多其他選擇。

en_text: She smiles at me. The biggest tool you can have in your armory, besides being good-looking and rich, is humor. If you can make her laugh right away, then you have a chance. If she really laughs—not one of those stupid, polite laughs because you think you’re funny—then you’re deﬁnitely in. At some point in the evening you’re assured of at least a friendly grope in the bathroom out back.
zh_text: 她向我微笑。除了英俊和多金外，你軍械庫裡最強大的武器就是幽默。如果你有辦法讓她立刻笑出來，那你就有機會了。如果她是真的在笑，而不是在你自認幽默的時候發出禮貌性的微笑，那你肯定有甜頭吃。起碼表示今天晚上你可以在後面的廁所裡來場友善的愛撫。

en_text: I’m hoping for a friendly something else.
zh_text: 我期待能夠來場友善的其他活動。

en_text: “You work at the police station, right?”
zh_text: 光線轉爲橘色。她也是。

en_text: I nod. “Something like that.”
zh_text: 「喬。」我說。

en_text: Now her smile gets a little bigger. “I thought so. I’ve seen you there.”
zh_text: 「你是做什麼的，喬？」她還在吼叫。

en_text: She shakes her head. “No. So you’re a cop?”
zh_text: 她笑容滿面，彷彿我剛剛告訴她說我是百萬富翁一樣。「真的？你是警察？不是開玩笑」「啊，我算不上是真的警察。」我說，不過立刻後悔這麼說。我有什麼理由不能爲她當個警察？她又不會發現。

en_text: “Something like that.”
The light changes to orange. So does she.
zh_text: 「有時候很有趣。」

en_text: “Joe,” I say. “So what are you working on at the moment?” She knocks back the rest of her drink, sets the glass on the bar next to mine, and continues to give me the sweetest smile. My drink is empty aside from the ice cubes, which are melting in the heat as I keep my hand gripped around the glass.
zh_text: 所以現在警方在向你諮詢什麼？她將剩下的飲料一飲而盡，將杯子放在我的杯子旁，開始左顧右盼。我的杯子裡只剩下冰塊，由於我雙手捧著杯子，所以冰塊正在融化。看得出來我快要失去她了。

en_text: “Get you another drink?” I ask.
zh_text: 「幫妳再點一杯？」我問。

en_text: “A Red Bull and vodka,” she says.
zh_text: 她聳肩。「當然。瑪格麗特。」

en_text: Great. So I order a gin and tonic for me and the most expensive drink in the bar for her. I sip at my drink and look at her one, thinking it does look pretty good, but I don’t want to mix drinks: headache material for the following morning, memory loss for the night before. It doesn’t happen to me often, but there have been a few times over the last ten years. “You were about to tell me what you’re working on,” she says.
zh_text: 我自己又點了一杯橙味伏特加。喝混酒會造成第二天早上頭痛，還會想不起來前晚發生的事情。這種情況不常發生在我身上，不過過去十年中還是發生過幾次。

en_text: “You’ve been reading about the serial killer?” “You’re working on the Burial Killer case?”
zh_text: 「妳有看過連續殺人魔的報導嗎？」

en_text: “That’s the one,” I tell her.
zh_text: 「這嘛，就是工作。」

en_text: “That’s amazing!” she says, and she really sounds like she means it. “Well, I do what I can,” I say. “It’s pretty noisy here,” she says.
zh_text: 「這裡很吵。」她說。

en_text: I agree. Yes. Damn noisy.
zh_text: 我同意。沒錯。他媽的吵。

en_text: We move away from the bar to a table near the front of the club, but not in view of the street. It’s less noisy, though only just. Darker, though. Fine by me. At least we no longer need to shout. To the right on the dance ﬂoor men and women are trying to lose themselves in an attempt at rhythm. They look like marionettes being controlled by puppeteers with a sense of humor.
zh_text: 我們離開吧台，來到前門附近的一張桌子，不過看不到門外的街景。這裡沒那麼吵，但也只是安靜一點而已。不過光線比較昏暗。我無所謂。至少我們不需要用吼的了。右邊的舞池裡有許多男女試圖迷失在音樂的節奏裡。他們看起來像是由有幽默感的操偶師操控的牽線木偶。

en_text: “So, what can you tell me about the case? You close to catching him?” she asks, leaning forward. She is running her ﬁnger around the rim of her glass, playing with the salt.
zh_text: 「那麼，你可以聊聊這個案子嗎？你們快要抓到他了？」她湊上前來問道。她手指在杯緣移動，沾起上面的鹽。

en_text: I start nodding. “Soon.”
zh_text: 我開始點頭。「快了。」

en_text: “How can you be so sure?”
zh_text: 「你怎麼這麼肯定？」

en_text: “I’m not allowed to say.”
zh_text: 「我不能說。」

en_text: “You know who the guy is?” She licks at the salt, then goes back for more. “I’m getting a pretty good idea,” I tell her. “But you can’t tell me,” she says.
zh_text: 「你們知道兇手是誰？」她舔了舔鹽，然後又回去沾。

en_text: “So you’ve seen the women he killed, huh?”
zh_text: 「那你看過死在他手上的女人，嗯？」

en_text: “Yeah, I’ve seen them.” I take a sip at my drink. This one has been mixed stronger than the other one. “What did they look like?”
zh_text: 「是，我看過她們。」我啜飲一口飲料。這一杯比剛剛兩杯烈一點。「她們看起來是什麼樣子？」

en_text: “He really made a mess of them, huh?”
zh_text: 他真的把她們搞得很慘，嗯？

en_text: I shrug, but it’s obvious I’m indicating the mess was bad. We talk about the case and I give her a few of my insights. She seems impressed, but doesn’t offer any opinions of her own, though she does tell me she’s been following the case closely.
zh_text: 我聳肩，不過顯然是表示情況真的很淒慘。我們談論兇殺案，我說了一些我的看法。她似乎很佩服，不過沒有提出她自己的見解，不過她倒是有說她也有在密切注意此案。

en_text: “So what do you do?” I ask, ﬁnally changing the subject. She seems disappointed.
zh_text: 「做什麼的？」我問，終於轉變話題。她似乎有點失望。

en_text: “I’m an architect.”
zh_text: 「我是建築師。」

en_text: Wow. I’ve never killed an architect. “How long you been doing that for?” “Eight years.”
zh_text: 哇。我沒殺過建築師。「做這行多久了？」

en_text: “You’re kidding.”
zh_text: 「說笑吧？」

en_text: “No. Why’s that?”
zh_text: 「沒。爲什麼這麼說？」

en_text: “I could have sworn you were only twenty-two.”
zh_text: 「我敢發誓妳才二十一歲。」

en_text: She gives me a laugh, that clichéd laugh reserved for when you totally fuck their age up in the right direction.
zh_text: 她笑了笑，專門保留給男人恭維她們年齡時的那種笑容。

en_text: “I’m a bit older than that, Joe.”
zh_text: 「我比二十一歲大一點，喬。」

en_text: I shrug like I can’t believe it. “You come here to wind down?”
zh_text: 我難以置信地聳肩。「你是來這裡放鬆的嗎？」

en_text: “This is about my third time here.”
zh_text: 「大概第二次來。」

en_text: “This is my ﬁrst time anywhere.”
zh_text: 「這是我第一次出來混。」

en_text: “Oh?”
Another shrug. “Couldn’t sleep. Decided to see what fun people do.”
zh_text: 再度聳肩。「睡不著。想說出來看看人們怎麼找樂子。」

en_text: Again the laugh. “What do you think so far?”
zh_text: 「目前爲止感覺如何？」

en_text: I put my glass down on the ring of moisture it had left behind. “So far it isn’t as scary as I’d thought.” “It may get scarier.”
zh_text: 我將杯子放在之前的水氣印子上。「目前爲止沒有我想像中那麼可怕。」「或許會越來越可怕。」

en_text: She’s got that part right.
zh_text: 這點她倒沒有說錯。

en_text: “You live in Christchurch, Joe?” “Yeah. All my life. What about you?”
zh_text: 「你住在基督城嗎，喬？」

en_text: Perfect. It also means she isn’t a regular at this bar, so not too many people will be keeping an eye on her to see where she goes. I don’t normally pick up women at bars. Only once before have I done it. It’s all about the challenge. Picking up a woman at a bar is difﬁcult enough, but breaking her afterward is reward enough for the effort. Getting killed is the last thing they expect—though it’s always at the front of their mind as their biggest fear. It’s one of life’s biggest ironies, and they probably see that just before they die.
zh_text: 「將近一個月。」完美。這表示她認識的人不多。同時也表示她不是這間酒吧的常客，不會有太多人注意她上哪去了。我通常不會在酒吧釣女人。之前只做過一次這種事情。那只是爲了挑戰自我。在酒吧中釣女人是件很難的事情，不過在事後令她崩潰則讓一切都值回票價。她們絕對沒有想到會遭人殺害——儘管這一直都是她們心中最大的恐懼。這是生命中最大的諷刺之一，而她們很可能要到死前才會了解這一點。

en_text: Like Angela—I could have just broken into her house. Like Candy—I could have simply hired her out. But work is a routine. Life is a routine. Taking the time to enjoy what we love in life isn’t a routine, it’s a commandment. If you have little to live for, then you need to enjoy it. You need to savor it.
zh_text: 就像安琪拉——我本來只要闖入她家就好了。像坎蒂——我本來可以付錢了事就好了。不過工作是例行公事。生活是例行公事。花時間享受我們愛做的事情卻不是例行公事，那是一種戒律。如果你的人生沒有什麼值得活下去的理由。那你就必須享受它。你必須品嚐它。

en_text: “So you here with friends?” I ask.
zh_text: 「妳是跟朋友一起來的嗎？」我問。

en_text: She shakes her head. “Sitting at home alone on a Friday night was killing me.”
zh_text: 不是。我在城裡沒有熟人，但是禮拜五晚上坐在家裡是會要命的。

en_text: I don’t say anything about her choice of words. Don’t mention that coming out is what will end up killing her. “Can I get you another drink?” “Sure. Another one of these,” she says, holding up her empty glass.
zh_text: 我沒有針對她的說法發表任何意見。我沒說出來混才會要她老命。「我能再幫妳點杯飲料嗎？」

en_text: She laughs. “You really are funny,” she says. I shrug on my jacket casually as if I’m cold, even though it’s at least eighty-ﬁve degrees in here with all these people around. I’m hoping Melissa isn’t thinking I’m taking it because I don’t trust her or not coming back.
zh_text: 我彷彿會冷般若無其事地穿上我的夾克，儘管在這麼多人的地方室溫起碼有三十度。我希望梅莉莎不會認爲我穿走夾克是因爲不信任她。

en_text: I bounce between a hundred other people. My mind is relaxed. It has this weird soft feeling. I order tonic water. No vodka. I can’t risk my mind growing any fuzzier. I buy her another Red Bull and vodka, not sure what the weird mix will do to her senses.
zh_text: 我在一百名顧客間穿梭。心情很輕鬆，有種奇特的舒適感。我點了一杯柳橙汁。不加伏特加。我不能冒險讓腦筋變得更不清楚。我又幫她點了一杯瑪格麗特。

en_text: Back at the table she turns the conversation toward the case. Toward crime and punishment. We pause to buy new drinks when we need them. Every glance at my watch informs me time is slipping away quite nicely. The atmosphere is loud yet relaxed. I actually feel as though I could stay here all night, just drinking tonic water and making conversation with this beautiful woman.
zh_text: 她將聊天的內容轉回謀殺案上。話題在罪與罰之間打轉。我們會在需要飲料的時候停止交談。每看手錶一眼都在提醒我時間正悄悄地流逝。四周人聲鼎沸，不過氣氛卻很輕鬆。我甚至覺得可以在這裡待一整個晚上，就這麼喝著柳橙汁，與這位美女閒聊。

en_text: Until four o’clock rolls around, that is, because then I decide that although I could stay all night, I won’t. It’s time to wrap things up. Other than confessing what my hobbies are, I can’t think of a single thing I could say right now to stop her wanting to come home with me.
zh_text: 四點過後，我認爲儘管我能待一整個晚上，我還是不想這麼做。該是結束這個階段的時候了。除了坦承我的嗜好之外，這時我不管說什麼都不能讓她打消跟我回家的念頭。

en_text: “I’d better be going. Way past my bedtime.” I push away from the table. So does she. The music is a little quieter now and the bar has turned more lights on.
zh_text: 「我該走了。早就過了我的睡眠時間。」我離開桌子。她也是。

en_text: They want us to leave too. “You want to share a taxi?” she suggests.
zh_text: 「要一起坐計程車嗎？」她提議。

en_text: I was about to suggest a similar thing. “Sure.”
zh_text: 我正打算提出類似的提議。「當然。」

en_text: The night is still warm on account of the breeze. The night-clubbing population has dropped by around half. Others are ﬂoating up and down the streets, looking stoned and drunk. Several of them are coagulating in fast-food stores that make thousands at this time of night. A few are looking for ﬁghts. Some are just looking for something to do. The taxi stands have long lines.
zh_text: 在西北風輕輕地吹拂下，室外的氣溫依然溫暖。夜店裡的人數已經減少一半。其他人都在街道上游蕩，不是喝醉了就是吸茫了。有些人擠在深夜這個時候已經賺翻了的速食店前面。少數人在惹是生非。還有些純粹是在找點事做。計程車招呼站排了很多人。

en_text: “Shall we walk?” I ask.
zh_text: 「走走嗎？」

en_text: She takes my arm to steady herself. She’s drunk far more than me, and that was the plan. “I don’t see why not, Joe.”
zh_text: 她勾住我的手臂，藉以穩定身形。她比我要醉多了，這點符合我的計畫。「有何不可，喬。」

en_text: I carry my jacket over my arm so she isn’t leaning against the gun or knife. Then I ask the all-important question. “Which way?” I ask.
zh_text: 我將外套掛在手臂上，不讓她靠到槍或刀。「往哪兒走？」我問。

en_text: “Where do you live, Joe?” she says, giving the all-important answer.
zh_text: 「你住哪兒，喬？」

en_text:
“Not too far away. An hour or so if we walk.”
“Let’s start walking.”
zh_text:
「不遠。用走的大概一個小時。」
「走吧。」

en_text: I keep my arm around Melissa, and we’re walking, but the distance to my house doesn’t seem to be closing. I’m thinking about where I’m going to dump her body. Maybe at the faggot’s house. I can imagine his face. One morning he wakes up to crumbs and an empty Coke can, the next he wakes up to a corpse. We keep moving at an even pace, but for every step we take, our destination takes another pace away. After a while Melissa takes off her shoes and starts carrying them. She must be one of those women who chooses style over comfort. I’m nowhere near drunk, but there’s still a small amount of gin ﬂoating around my brain because things aren’t as sharp as they ought to be. Melissa is way beyond it. I feel like we’ve been walking forever, but she’s probably thinking ﬁve minutes have gone by.
zh_text: 我摟著梅莉莎，一起散步回家，不過我家似乎一點都沒有變近。我開始考慮該把她的屍體丟到哪兒去。或許丟到那個同性戀的家裡。我可以想像他的表情。前一天早晨起床發現麵包屑和空可樂罐，第二天又在屍體旁醒來。我們以穩定的步調前進，不過每跨出一步，我們的目的地彷彿都飄出更遠的距離。一段時間過後，她脫下鞋子，提在手上。她必定是那種爲了時尚而不顧舒適的女人。我還沒到喝醉的地步，不過腦袋還是微微受到伏特加的影響，因爲眼前的景象不如往常清晰。梅莉莎酩酊大醉，我覺得好像已經走了一輩子，不過她可能以爲才走了五分鐘。

en_text: We stumble west. Follow the roads. The ratio of hookers per corner slowly decreases until there are no hookers at all. We make clever conversation on the way, but it’s mostly me telling her about the case. An occasional taxi passes us, but we don’t bother trying to wave it down. The scenery starts to change, from new town houses painted funky colors to run-down homes with broken windows and doors covered in some kind of funky mold. Unkempt lawns and pieces of abandoned cars killing off patches of grass. Newspapers and advertising circulars litter the front yards.
zh_text: 我們搖搖晃晃地朝向西方前進。沿著馬路走。街角的妓女數量逐漸減少，直到角落的數量大於妓女，然後妓女完全消失。我們一路上輕鬆交談，不過大部分是我在告訴她這件案子的案情。偶爾會有計程車路過，不過我們都沒費心揮手攔車。街景開始轉變，從色彩鮮豔的新房屋到門窗破爛的舊建築。雜亂的草坪和廢棄車輛扼殺了偶爾出現的綠地。花園中隨處可見報紙和廣告傳單。

en_text: After half an hour Melissa starts to complain that she’s getting cold, so I give her my jacket. It’s like getting Candy to carry my briefcase. It’s exciting to watch them carrying the weapon about to kill them. I imagine it’d be like getting somebody to dig their own grave.
zh_text: 半小時後，梅莉莎說冷，於是我把夾克給她穿。那感覺就像讓坎蒂幫我拿公事包。看著她們拿著即將殺死她們的武器令我十分興奮。我認爲那跟叫人挖掘自己的墳墓沒有什麼不同。

en_text: “There’s a gun in there,” I say. The alcohol has dulled my mind, but it hasn’t taken the edge off the excitement. “You’re kidding me.”
zh_text: 「夾克裡有把槍。」我說。酒精令我心思遲緩，不過還不至於讓我興奮過頭。「你在說笑？」

en_text: I shake my head. “It’s a Glock nine-millimeter automatic.”
zh_text: 我搖頭。「葛拉克九釐米自動手槍。」

en_text: “You carry a gun?”
zh_text: 「你有配槍？」

en_text: “Standard law enforcement issue.”
zh_text: 「制式執法配備。」

en_text: “Wow.”

Nothing about my automatic is standard. The Glock 17 was issued to the New Zealand police, but isn’t carried by many ofﬁcers. It ﬁres seventeen rounds and weighs over a pound and a half. It’s made from a synthetic that’s stronger than steel and nearly ninety percent lighter. The gun itself contains a mere thirty-three parts.
zh_text: 我的自動手槍一點也不制式。紐西蘭警方是有配發葛拉克十七型手槍，但是沒有多少警員配戴。它的彈匣可以容納十七發子彈，重量超過七百公克。槍殼是種比鋼還硬的合成材質，而且重量只有前者的九成。槍本身是由三十三個零件組成。

en_text: “Can I see it?”
zh_text: 「我可以看看嗎？」

en_text: Mine, however, is the Glock 26. The basics are the same, but it’s lighter and far more compact. Much easier to conceal.
zh_text: 然而，我的槍是葛拉克二十六型。基本上是一樣的東西，不過更輕也更小巧。非常方便藏在身上。

en_text: “I shouldn’t take it out.”
zh_text: 我不應該拿出來。

en_text: “I would really like to see it, Joe. And touch it.”
zh_text: 「我真的很想看看它，喬。還想摸摸它。」

en_text: I’d like her to see it and touch it.
zh_text: 我也想讓她看，讓她摸。

en_text: “Plus there’s nobody else around,” she says.
zh_text: 而且附近又沒別人。

en_text: She’s right. We’re all alone out here. Well, if she wants to see it, who am I to object?
zh_text: 她說得沒錯。附近的街道空無一人。好吧，既然她想看，我又有什麼理由反對呢？

en_text: As I reach around her waist, she nuzzles her face into the side of my neck. Her breath is hot on my skin. Her lips ﬂick against me. I unzip the pocket, take hold of Mr. Glock, and bring him out.
zh_text: 我伸手繞過她的腰間時，她的臉在我脖子上磨蹭。我感覺到她熱呼呼的氣息。她的嘴唇輕觸我的皮膚。我拉開夾克拉鍊，握住葛拉克先生，將之取出。

en_text: She leans away, looks at it, and repeats a previous sentiment. “Wow.”
zh_text: 她向後一點，打量手槍，重複之前的評論。「哇。」

en_text: I hand it to her. She studies the handle, the stainless-steel slide, the dark blue steel frame. It’s a nice gun. Some would say a ladies’ gun.
zh_text: 我遞槍給她。她打量槍柄、不鏽鋼滑套、深藍色的鋼架。這是一把好槍。有些人會說是女性用槍。

en_text: Well, sure. I’ve only ever used it on ladies.
zh_text: 好吧，當然。我也只有拿來射過女人而已。

en_text: “You ever shot anybody?”
zh_text: 「你有對人開過槍嗎？」

en_text: I shrug. Look at the uncocking safety lever on the side. “A couple of times.”
zh_text: 我聳肩。看著槍側的擊錘保險桿。「兩次。」

en_text: “My God. I bet you killed them, huh?”
zh_text: 「天啊。我敢說你殺了他們，嗯？」

en_text: She’s looking the most excited she’s been all night. Some women love the element of danger. Some live for it. Some die. “It’s part of the job,” I tell her.
zh_text: 她此刻處於整個晚上最興奮的狀態。有些女人喜歡危險的元素。有些爲了危險而生。有些爲了危險而死。工作的一部分。

en_text:
She puts her small hand around the handle, points it ahead, into the street. “Pow!”
“Pow indeed.”
zh_text:
她伸出小手握住槍柄，對準前方的街道。「砰！」
「射得好。」

en_text: It’s time to get the pistol back.
zh_text: 該是拿回手槍的時候了。

en_text: “Is it loaded?”
zh_text: 「有子彈嗎？」

en_text: “Uh huh.”
zh_text: 「嗯哼。」

en_text: The Glock, as I said, cost me a lot of money. That makes it difﬁcult for me to be parted from it. I’m sober enough to identify that.
zh_text: 之前說過，這把葛拉克手槍花了我一大筆錢。我在型錄上看到的最新報價是七百美金。除了匯差之外，我還要多付黑市的變相加價。這些錢讓我跟槍難捨難分。我還沒有醉到不記得這一點。

en_text:
“German made, huh? Germans have the highest quality.”
I shake my head and lean my hand out to grab it. They do have the highest quality.
zh_text:
「德國製造，呃？德國人最著重品質。」
我搖了搖頭，伸手去拿槍。德國槍確實品質優良。

en_text:
“Austrian,” I say. “Made guns for the Austrian army. They ﬁrst started supplying them to Norway and Sweden, until the United States came into the picture. Then things really took off. Law enforcement agencies all over the world use Glocks.”
“You know your stuff.”
zh_text: 「奥地利製。」我說。「奥地利軍用槍。一開始他們外銷到挪威和瑞典，後來美國人也跑來了。接著情況一發不可收拾。如今世界各地的執法單位都採用葛拉克的槍。」

en_text: Sure, I know something about guns. I know if you use jacketed hollowpoint bullets, you can make a real mess. The bullet has an opening in the jacket and, on impact, the bullet expands. Small penetration. Huge exit. Yep. I sure know that. Bonded hollow-point bullets can go through the person and carry on, sometimes hitting the next person down the line. The bullets in my Glock are fairly standard. They don’t do a lot of damage, and many law enforcement places don’t use them for that reason. They have a low stopping power.
zh_text: 當然，我對槍枝小有研究。我知道如果使用全被甲中空彈的話可以把人打得血肉模糊。這種子彈的外殼下是中空的，擊中目標時彈頭會擴張。入口傷小，出口傷大。是啊。我很肯定這一點。黏合中空彈能夠射穿人體，然後繼續前進，有時候還能擊中彈道上的下一個人。我的葛拉克裡裝填的子彈是標準彈。不會造成太大的傷害，而很多執法單位基於這個理由不使用這種子彈。它們的制止力不足。

en_text: I take the gun from her. Fold my ﬁngers around the handle. Feels good.

en_text: I tuck the gun into the waistband of my jeans and pull my shirttail out to cover it. A few minutes later we come across a park only a half mile or so from home. “It’s quicker if we go through here,” I say, indicating the park with a sweeping gesture of my arm.

en_text: The sky above becomes crazy with purple light as the dawn begins to intersect with the night. In the park everything is hazy gray, but not black. The breeze has cooled down since we started walking and become refreshing; the air no longer feels like the inside of an indoor swimming complex. Away from town, away from the drunken lights and insulting music, there’s just fresh air and this green park that is damp beneath my feet. This is the Garden City. My city. zh_text: 一副手銬。太好了。「幹嘛？」

en_text: She points the gun at my dick. I pick the handcuffs up.
zh_text: 他以槍口對準我的老二。我撿起手銬。

en_text: “Snap one of them on your left wrist.”
zh_text: 一只銬住你的左手。

en_text: “What are you going to do?” I ask.
zh_text: 「妳要幹嘛？」

en_text: “What am I going to do?” she repeats, in case I hadn’t heard my own question. “I’m going to shoot your balls off if you don’t do what I ask.”
zh_text: 「我要幹嘛？」她重複，以免我沒聽見我自己的問題。「我要射掉你的睾丸，如果你不照我的話做。」

en_text: I quickly snap one of the cold metal bracelets around my wrist. The ratchet in the mechanism clicks as it locks into place.
zh_text: 我立刻將一只冰冷的金屬手銬銬上我的手腕。裡面的齒輪鎖到定位。

en_text: “Lie down on your back, stretch your arms around the tree, and handcuff yourself on the other side.”
zh_text: 「躺下，兩手伸到樹後，銬住另外一隻手。」

en_text: “You sure?”
zh_text: 「妳確定？」

en_text: “Positive.”
zh_text: 「確定。」

en_text: “Still time to change your mind.”
zh_text: 「還有時間改變心意。」

en_text: “Do it before I get annoyed with your charm.”
zh_text: 「在我受不了你的魅力前快點銬好。」

en_text: I follow her orders. The grass itches at my back as I lie on it. I can’t get comfortable, but I doubt that would worry her. Nice view from here, though. The stars are still out but fading. It’s as though they’re leaving this universe, dying in this purple light. I reach around the tree and lock my other wrist into place.
zh_text: 我遵命行事。我的背被草弄得很癢，怎麼躺都不舒服，不過我懷疑她會關心這種事情。這個角度看出去的景色倒是不錯。天上還有星星，不過越來越少。彷彿它們正離開這個宇宙，在紫光中逐漸死去。我伸手到樹後，銬上另外一隻手。

en_text: She keeps the gun pointed at me, walks around the tree, and checks. Bending down she tightens the cuffs where I failed. They squeeze against the bones in my wrist. It hurts, but I don’t groan, don’t show any signs of pain. Yep, I’m a real man. A real man with no idea what’s going on.
zh_text: 她槍口保持在我身上，走到樹後檢查。她蹲下身去，壓緊手銬。手銬擠壓我的骨頭。很痛，不過我沒有呻吟，沒有露出任何疼痛的表情。沒錯，我是真正的男子漢，一個完全搞不清楚狀況的男子漢。

en_text: She comes back around to face me and pulls out another set of handcuffs. She seems to have come prepared.
zh_text: 她走回我的面前，拿出另外一副手銬。她似乎有備而來。

en_text: I consider kicking up at her as she locks them into place around my ankles. Won’t do me any good, though. She has the gun. She has the keys. I’ve nothing but an erection that can’t reach her from here. I pull at the handcuffs, then pull at the tree, but it’s no use.
zh_text: 我考慮在她銬住我的腳踝時出腳踢她。不過這樣做對我沒有好處。她有槍，有鑰匙。我只有一根插不到她的大老二。我扯了扯手銬，然後拉了拉樹，一點用都沒有。

en_text: “Comfortable, Joe?” “Not really.”
zh_text: 「舒服嗎，喬？」「不太舒服。」

en_text: She grabs the sides of my jacket and pulls them outward. “What else do you have in here?”
zh_text: 她抓住我的夾克側裡，拉到外面。「你還帶了些什麼？」

en_text: I’m not answering. Whether I lie or not, she’s still going to check. She rummages through the pockets and ﬁnds the knife.
zh_text: 我沒有回答。不管我撒不撒謊，她都會去檢查。她在口袋中翻找，拔出那把刀。

en_text: “You carry some interesting items, Joe.”
zh_text: 你身上帶了些有趣的道具，喬。

en_text: I shrug, though she doesn’t see it. It’s a smaller motion when you’re lying down with your arms stretched over your head. She tosses the knife in the air—end over handle, handle over end—and catches it by the hilt, blade pointing ahead. She handles it better than I do. Maybe she’s a chef. She hunts through my jeans and ﬁnds my wallet.
zh_text: 我聳肩，不過她看不出來。當你躺在地上，手臂舉在頭上時，聳肩就變成一種不明顯的動作。她將刀子拋到天空，轉了幾圈，接住刀柄，刀尖向前。她耍刀的手法比我還高明。或許她是廚師。她翻翻我的牛仔褲，拿出我的皮夾。

en_text: “No identiﬁcation, huh?”
zh_text: 「沒有身分證，嗯？」

en_text: “I’m old enough to drink, if that’s your point.”
zh_text: 「我有到法定喝酒年齡，如果你好奇的話。」

en_text: “How long you been a cop, Joe?”
zh_text: 「你當警察多久了，喬？」

en_text: She knows I’m not a cop. Probably has known from the moment we met.
zh_text: 她知道我不是警察。很可能打從我們碰面開始就知道了。

en_text: “About as long as you’ve been an architect.”
zh_text: 「跟妳當建築師差不多久。」

en_text: She laughs. “I bet the police would love to get a look at this knife. They could probably connect it to a few bad things that have happened lately.”
zh_text: 她笑。「我敢說警方一定很想要這把刀。他們或許可以將它和最近一些不好的事情牽連在一起。」

en_text: “You’re talking about my salads?”
zh_text: 「妳是指我廚房裡的沙拉？」

en_text: She ignores my quip and carries on. “I bet the gun has quite a history too.”
zh_text: 她忽略我的油嘴滑舌，繼續說道：「我敢說這把槍也有一段過去。」

en_text: “Everything has a history,” I say. “What’s yours?”
zh_text: 「所有東西都有過去。」我說。「妳的過去又是如何？」

en_text: She walks up to me and tosses my wallet—now empty—onto the ground. She stuffs my money into my jacket pocket, telling me I can say good-bye to my jacket too. “I told you my history,” she says. “I used to live here, I moved away, and now I’m back.”
zh_text: 她走過來，丢下我的皮夾——空空如也——落在地上。她將我的錢塞入我的夾克，等於是叫我跟我的夾克說再見。

en_text: Melissa, if that’s her name, crouches next to me, the gun in her left hand, the knife in her right. I remember thinking of them as the essential weapons before I left home, which starts me reﬂecting on the previous ten minutes that have brought me here, but my chance of stopping whatever is about to happen ended when I snapped those handcuffs on my wrists. Maybe this was meant to happen all along. In this crazy, mixed-up world. I spend another moment wondering why handcuffs aren’t called wristcuffs, then I start considering my options. Once again God is doing nothing to help me out, so there’s no point in even praying to the guy. I’ll leave the toga-wearing hippie alone and keep my prayers to myself.
zh_text: 梅莉莎（如果她真叫梅莉莎）在我身旁蹲下，左手持槍，右手持刀。我還記得出門時將這兩樣東西視爲不可或缺的武器，這又讓我想起讓我身處這種處境之前的那十分鐘，不過在我將手銬銬上手腕的那一刻起，我就已經失去了阻止即將發生之事的機會。或許事情早就註定會走到這個地步。這是個瘋狂混亂的世界。我又花了一點時間思考爲什麼手銬不叫腕銬，接著我開始考慮我的處境。再一次，上帝沒有幫助我脫離險境，所以跟那傢伙祈禱是沒有意義的。我決定不要去煩那個穿長袍的老嬉皮，把祈禱留給自己。

en_text: “Do you really want me to tell you more?”
zh_text: 「你真的想知道我的過去？」

en_text: She holds the knife above me, not in the dagger-plunge style of a virgin sacriﬁce, more in the way of slicing the top layer off a roast chicken. She rests the side of the blade against my stomach. It’s colder than the rest of my shivering body. My erection is lying on the bottom of my stomach. The tip of the knife is only a couple of inches away. Now I do start praying to God, the same God Sally prays to, the same God she wants me to come along and visit on Sunday mornings—and I’ll go too, I promise, if He gets me out of this in one piece.
zh_text: 她將刀舉在我的身上，不是祭祀處女的持刀手法，比較像是割下烤雞第一層皮的手法。她以刀刃側面抵住我的肚子。它比我冷得發抖的身體還要冰冷。我的老二癱在肚子底下，刀尖離它不過數公分之遙。這下我終於開始向上帝祈禱了——就是莎莉祈禱的那個上帝，就是她要我週日早晨前去拜訪的上帝。

en_text: “No,” I answer, shakily. No, I don’t want to know her history. It will only scare the shit out of me. I don’t need to know why she left Christchurch or why she came back. I don’t want to know how she has treated some of the men in her past. I show the same respect to the women I mess with. It’s my good nature.
zh_text: 「不。」我聲音顫抖地回答道。我不想知道她的過去。她的過去只會把我嚇得屁滾尿流。我不想知道她是如何對待過去的那些男人。我對被我搞過的女人展現過同等的尊重。那是我的本性。

en_text: It’s my humanity.
zh_text: 那是我的人性。

en_text: She tilts the knife so the tip of the blade touches my stomach just above my belly button. Then she pushes down. My stomach offers the same resistance as the skin of a less-than-ripe tomato, then surrenders. The knife cuts into me, but only enough to draw blood. A warm stinging rather than hurting. As I watch, straining my neck to look, she starts running it up my body. I’ve been cut before. I know what to expect.
zh_text: 她斜過刀鋒，刀尖接觸我的肚臍眼上方。接著她插了下去。皮膚生出一股跟熟番茄差不多的反抗力道，接著投降。刀刃插入我的體內，不過深度只到剛好見血而已。我感到一股熱呼呼的刺痛，並不像是身受刀傷。我挺起脖子，瞪眼觀看，她開始向上移動刀尖。我以前被人拿刀割過，我知道接下來會是什麼場面。

en_text: I’m getting the view thousands of homeless people across the country are getting: a cloudless sky, with fading stars barely twinkling like holes in a purple curtain covering Heaven. If God is up there looking through one of those holes with His large knowing eyes, I wonder what He’s thinking. Can He see me? If He can, does He care?
zh_text: 我眼前出現了全國數千名流浪漢看見的景象：萬里無雲的天空，逐漸消失的星星發出黯淡的光芒，如同遮蔽天堂的紫色幃幔上的小洞。如果上帝在天上，正以全知的大眼透過這些小洞觀看人間，我很好奇祂在想些什麼。祂能看到我嗎？如果看得到，祂會在乎嗎？

en_text: “Are you scared, Joe?” Melissa asks, playing the knife along my body.
zh_text: 「你害怕嗎，喬？」梅莉莎邊問邊劃開我的身體。

en_text: I am scared, but I try not to show it. “Do you want me to be scared?”
zh_text: 「妳希望我害怕嗎？」

en_text: “It’s up to you.”
zh_text: 「看你決定。」

en_text: “Should I be scared?” I ask, trying to control my voice.
zh_text: 「我應該要怕嗎？」我問，試圖控制我的聲音。

en_text: When the knife reaches my chest, it has formed a reasonably straight line up to the center of my body, spotted only where the skin hasn’t broken. The line is red. “I know I’m not,” she says.
zh_text: 子劃到我胸口時，我身體正面中央已經被劃出一條長長的直線，那條線是紅色的。「我知道我不害怕。」她說。

en_text: “No? What are you then?”
zh_text: 「不怕嗎？妳到底是什麼人？」

en_text: “I’m the one with the knife and the gun.”
zh_text: 「我是手裡有刀和槍的人。」

en_text: “Want to swap?”
zh_text: 「想要交換嗎？」

en_text: “No, thank you.”
zh_text: 「不了，謝謝。」

en_text: “I’ll let you have the knife after we’ve ﬁnished. As a keepsake.”
zh_text: 束之後我會讓妳留著刀。當作紀念品。

en_text: “You’re so generous, Joe, but I already have the knife. And the gun. What more could I want?”
zh_text: 「你真大方，喬。不過刀已經是我的了。還有槍。我還奢求什麼呢？」

en_text: I’m not sure, and that’s the problem. She traces a ﬁnger down the cut on my body, moving it at the same slow pace she was running it over her lips. It tickles and feels kind of nice, yet my skin is crawling. The blood smears into the width of her ﬁngertip.
zh_text: 她伸出手指，以之前撫摸嘴唇的步調沿著我的傷口輕撫。我覺得很癢，而且有點爽，不過我的皮膚還是冒出雞皮疙瘩。鮮血染紅了她的指尖。

en_text: “How’s that feel, Joe?”
zh_text: 「感覺如何，喬？」

en_text: “I can show you.”
zh_text: 「我可以讓妳體驗一下。」

en_text: She gets to the end of the line and takes her ﬁnger to her mouth, then sucks on the end. She closes her eyes and starts to moan. Then she pulls her ﬁnger out, opens her eyes, and smiles. Her blue eyes are locked on mine. I wonder what she sees behind them. In a quick movement, she folds her body so her face is above my chest. Slowly she angles her tongue to touch the cut. Just as slowly, she runs the length of the cut as though she were licking the inside ﬂap of an envelope. Her face moves down to my crotch, but stops right where she really should keep going.
zh_text: 她摸到傷口末端，將手指放到嘴裡，吸吮指尖。她閉上雙眼，開始呻吟。接著她抽出手指，睜開雙眼，面露微笑。她的藍眼睛緊盯著我的。我很好奇她在我的雙眼中看見了什麼。突然之間，她撲到我的身上，臉部對準我的胸口。慢慢地，她伸出舌頭，對準傷口。她以同樣緩慢的動作舔著傷口，彷彿在舔信封彌封口一樣。她的臉移動到我的股間，不過在真的應該繼續舔下去的地方打住。

en_text: She looks up at me and shudders. “Tastes good.”
zh_text: 她抬頭看我，微微顫抖。「味道真好。」

en_text: “I try to eat well.”
zh_text: 「我飲食均衡。」

en_text: I’m aroused again. The evidence is plain.
zh_text: 我再度性慾高漲。證據十分明顯。

en_text: She stands up and looks down at me.
zh_text: 她站起身來，低頭看我。

en_text: “I know who you are, Joe.”
zh_text: 「我知道你是谁，喬。」

en_text: “Oh?”
“The gun. The knife. The scars. I’d have to be stupid not to know. You’re him.” “Who?”
zh_text: 「這把槍。這把刀。這些傷。這樣還猜不出來就太蠢了。你就是他。」「誰？」「基督城屠夫。」

en_text: I shake my head. “No,” I say. Mom’s advice about lying hasn’t been forgotten, it’s just been relegated to the bottom of my priorities.
zh_text: 我搖頭。「不是。」我說。我沒有忘記我媽叫我不要撒謊，我只是把它排到優先順序的最後面去而已。

en_text: She gives a small giggle, the type a schoolgirl would give when confronting her rock idol. She points the gun at me. “Pow!” I ﬂinch and the handcuffs dig into my wrists and ankles. She laughs. “You’re him all right. I know it. I was going to be your next victim.”
zh_text: 她咯咯嬌笑，就是女學生在搖滾偶像面前會發出的笑聲。她將槍口對準我。「砰！」我身體一緊，手銬陷入我的手腕和腳踝。她大笑。「你就是他，我知道！我本來會是你的下一個被害人。」

en_text: “Don’t ﬂatter yourself.”
zh_text: 「不要太抬舉自己了。」

en_text: “I’m not ﬂattering myself, Joe. I’m nobody special. Just a girl who likes the night. Just a girl who knows the police don’t use Glock twenty-sixes. They use the seventeen.” “You’re basing it on that?”
zh_text: 「我沒有抬舉自己，喬。我不是什麼特殊人物。只是一個喜歡黑夜的女孩。只是一個知道警方不會配戴葛拉克二十六型手槍的女孩。他們用的是十七型。」

en_text: She smiles. “You’re just too smart, Joe, aren’t you? Would you like to know more?” “Not really.”
zh_text: 她微笑。「你太聰明了，喬，是不是？還想知道更多嗎？」並不特別想。

en_text: “It wasn’t pure luck I stood next to you, Joe. I recognized you. I’ve seen you come and go from the police department because sometimes I like to follow cops home. I’ve seen you coming and going in your overalls. What are you, a janitor? I still thought you might be interesting to talk to, that maybe you could amuse me for a few moments. Then you said you were a cop and I was curious as to where you were going with it. Then we talked about the case. Your case. You had too many insights, knew too much about the murders, way too much for a guy who shows up and leaves work in a pair of overalls and catches the bus. I hadn’t even ﬁnished my second drink when I started to suspect who you were. I’m good at reading people, Joe, really good. I didn’t used to be, and it’s gotten me into trouble in the past, but people learn faster when the mistakes and consequences are bigger, which makes me an expert these days. I just needed to test you. And that was easy. All I had to do was tell you I wasn’t from around here, and right away you saw me as a perfect victim. Someone nobody would miss right away. And this,” she says, shaking the gun a little, “this just conﬁrms everything I thought about you.”
zh_text: 「我會站到你身邊純粹只是運氣而已，喬，而當你說你是警察時，好吧，我立刻知道我該深入了解你一點。警方不會找顧問諮詢連續殺人案，至少不會是你這種顧問。他們會去國外找專家過來。這個國家裡沒人擁有那種專業知識。接著我們聊起案情。你知道太多內幕，熟知太多內情。這一切都不太合理。當你提起那把槍的時候，我就肯定事情有鬼了。你對案情的理解絕不可能是從報紙上看來的。你不是普通人。想要確認你的身分並不困難。我只要告訴你我才搬來不久，你立刻就會把我當成完美的獵物。短期內不會有人發現失蹤的人。」

en_text: “You’re wrong.”
zh_text: 「妳錯了。」

en_text: “I’m not wrong, Joe.”
zh_text: 「我沒錯，喬。」

en_text: “You don’t know enough about police work to make these assumptions. You don’t know enough about serial killers.”
zh_text: 「妳不熟悉警方工作，不該妄加揣測。妳對連續殺人魔的了解也不夠透徹。」

en_text: “Don’t I? You know, Joe, I love cops. I love things that cops do. I also like going through houses. Call it a fetish, call it whatever you want, but I like being inside a place when people are sleeping. Especially a cop’s place. Like I said, that’s why I recognize you.”
zh_text: 「不夠嗎？你知道，喬，我愛警察。我喜歡警察做的事情。我也很喜歡跑到別人家去。說我有病也好，隨便你怎麼說，總之我喜歡趁人睡覺的時候溜進別人家。特別是警察家。」

en_text: “So?”
zh_text: 「所以?」

en_text: “I think it’s the control. You know all about control, don’t you, Joe? That’s part of who you are. Don’t you love the way cops can order you around? When they tell you to jump, you jump. The police are the ultimate in control, Joe, the ultimate. We know it. They know it. I like to collect police things. I’ve got all these books at home on cops, both New Zealand police and overseas. I’ve got posters, documentaries, movies. I’ve even got one of these,” she shakes the Glock, “but mine’s made from plastic. Different model too, but this will replace it nicely. en_text: “Joe?”
“Please. Sally. Something has happened. I’m sick. Really, really sick. I don’t know what to do. I’m in pain. A lot of it. Can you help me? Is there anything you can do?”
zh_text: 「拜託。莎莉。我出了點事。我不舒服。真的，真的很不舒服。我不知道該怎麼辦。我好痛。非常非常痛。妳能幫我嗎？妳有辦法幫我嗎？」

en_text: “I can call you an ambulance.”
zh_text: 「我可以幫你叫救護車。」

en_text: “No. No ambulance. Please, I need you to understand this,” he asks, talking as if she’s the one mentally challenged and not him. “I need painkillers. And ﬁrst aid. Please, I need you to pick some up and come to my house. It hurts so bad. Please. Do you understand?”
zh_text: 「不。不要救護車。拜託，妳一定要清楚這一點。」他說，講得好像有智力障礙的人是她，而不是他。「我需要止痛藥。急救箱。拜託，我需要妳買點東西，帶來我家。我好痛。拜託。妳聽懂了嗎？」

en_text: “Where do you live?”
zh_text: 「你住在哪裡？」

en_text: “Live? I . . . I don’t remember.”
zh_text: 「住？我……我不記得。」

en_text: “Joe?”
“Wait, wait. Hang on. Pen? Do you have one?”
zh_text: 「等等，等等。先等一下。筆？妳有嗎？」

en_text: “I’ve got one.”
zh_text: 「我有筆。」

en_text: He gives her his address, and then he’s gone. She stares out the window at the vegetable garden in the backyard her father has been at war with for the last few years (he is slowly accepting defeat). All the plants and weeds also seem to be at war with each other. The phone call already feels like it just didn’t happen. It was short and confusing and so unlike Joe. She realizes she’s still holding the phone. That’s proof he just rang. She didn’t at all like the way he sounded. She punches two of the three required numbers to call an ambulance, then hangs up. She’ll hold off calling for help till she’s seen Joe. For all she knows, it could be something as simple as a splinter. Sometimes her brother would be the same way for something equally as small.
zh_text: 喬把地址給她，然後掛斷。她凝視著窗外後院裡那座過去數年間她父親一直努力征服的菜園（他已經開始接受失敗了）。裡面的植物和雜草似乎也在彼此征戰。她很擔心喬，一點也不喜歡他講話的聲音。她拿起電話叫救護車，按下三個號碼中的兩個，然後掛斷。她打算看到喬之後再打電話叫救護車。她回到臥室，自床下拿出一個急救箱，打開箱蓋，確定裡面的配備齊全，雖然她明知東西都在裡面。她告訴父母自己晚點回來，然後走去開車。

en_text:
Up in her bedroom she pulls out a ﬁrst-aid kit from beneath her bed, unzips the top, and checks to make sure it’s fully stocked, even though she knew it would be. She tells her parents she’ll be back later, then heads out to her car. It’s gray outside, there are a few patches of blue sky out to the east, but not many.
Joe’s neighborhood is on the decline, she thinks, as she follows the streets on her map. Many of the buildings and houses need work. Some more than others. A coat of paint and a lawn mower would solve some problems, but nothing short of demolition would ﬁx others. This area wouldn’t need to be this way, she thinks, if more people cared. Joe’s apartment building is only a few stories high. It’s made of brick, which in places has been tagged by teenagers’ spray paint. None of the windows are clean, mildew and mold have discolored the bottom third of the building, and cracks have been patched with mortar and paint. The pathway out front has some weird stains on it and smells like rotten food. The staircase is dimly lit and smells a little like urine, but it’s not dim enough to miss seeing patches of blood every few steps or so. By the time she reaches the top ﬂoor she’s extremely worried. She looks at the different doors and ﬁnds Joe’s apartment. As she reaches out and knocks she notices her hands are shaking.
zh_text:
喬住的地方環境不好，她一邊按照地圖開車一邊想著。這裡很多建築都需要整修。油漆和除草機可以解決一些問題，不過其他問題就得要把房子拆掉才能改善。這個地方沒有必要變成這個樣子，她心想，只要更多人關心這裡就好了。
喬的公寓只有幾層樓高。磚造建築，外牆佈滿青少年的塗鴉。窗戶骯髒，底下三分之一的部分都已發霉褪色，不少地方都以泥灰與油漆修補裂縫。
樓梯間燈光黯淡，不過還沒有黯淡到看不見每幾級階梯上沾染的血跡。她抵達頂樓，查看門牌號碼，最後找到喬的住處。伸手敲門時，她發現自己的手在抖。

en_text: A minute goes by and Joe doesn’t answer. Was it him who actually called? It didn’t sound like him, but who else could it have been? A second and far worse thought comes to her. What if Joe was so badly hurt, he’s died? That’s the thought that makes her try the handle. She reaches out and twists it, and when she opens the door the stench of decay and disinfectant pushes out at her, and she has to stiﬂe the compulsion to start gagging.
zh_text: 一分鐘過去了，喬沒有來應門。電話真的是喬打的嗎？聲音不像他，但是還有可能是誰打的？她伸手轉動門把，開門之後，一股腐臭和消毒水的味道撲鼻而來，她必須屏住呼吸才能克制噁心的感覺。

en_text: The apartment is small by any standards. Daylight is ﬂooding through the single window on the far side and it hits every particle of ﬂoating dust along the way, making it look as though she’s walking into a sandstorm. She’s been wondering what Joe’s place would look like, but she hadn’t pictured this: wallpaper hanging from the walls, ﬁlthy and damaged ﬂoorboards, old furniture full of cracks and splits, not that she ever pictured she would see it under these circumstances. She hadn’t imagined such a mess either, but when she spots Joe lying on the bed she realizes it must only be because of the state he’s in. His clothes are heaped on the ﬂoor, covered in blood and grass stains and vomit. Bandages and tissues are piled in the middle of the ﬂoor. Next to them lies an empty bottle of wine, cotton swabs, rags, even a bottle of disinfectant. A bucket that reeks of bad things stands next to the couch. Her immediate thought upon seeing all of that is that he’s been stabbed. Stabbed and killed.
zh_text: 就各種標準而言，這都是一間小公寓。陽光自對面牆壁唯一的窗戶上灑落，照亮了所有飄浮在空中的微塵，感覺彷彿走入了一場沙塵暴般。她常常想像喬住的地方是什麼樣子，不過沒想過是這個樣子：壁紙垂在牆上，骯髒損毀的地板，破破爛爛的老舊家具。她也沒想過他家會這麼亂，不過在看見躺在床上的喬時，她心知一定是因為他此刻無力整理房間的關係。他的衣服堆在地上，沾滿了血液、草漬與嘔吐物。地板上堆了一堆繃帶和面紙。旁邊還有一瓶空酒瓶、棉花棒、抹布，甚至還有一瓶消毒劑。沙發旁擺了一個散發惡臭的水桶。

en_text: She closes the door behind her, then quickly makes her way over to him. He’s naked, except for a sheet that covers his waist. His entire body is covered in a ﬁlm of sweat, and has taken on a grayish tinge. His eyes are barely open, and she isn’t sure he can even see her. She can see the rise and fall of his chest. She smooths away his damp hair and rests a hand on his forehead. He’s burning up.
zh_text: 她關上房門，迅速來到喬的身邊。他一絲不掛，只有一條被單遮住腰部。喬全身冒汗，呈現一種灰色的光澤。喬雙眼微睜，不確定看不看得見她。她拂開喬汗濕的頭髮，一手放上他的額頭。他在發高燒。

en_text: “Joe? Joe, can you hear me?”
zh_text: 「喬？喬，你聽得到我嗎？」

en_text: His eyes open slightly further. “Mom? What’s happening?”
zh_text: 喬眼睛睜大一點。「媽？出了什麼事？」

en_text: “Joe, it’s Sally.”
zh_text: 「喬，我是莎莉。」

en_text: “Mom?”

His eyes close. The sheet covering his waist has patches of blood on it. More has dried on his stomach. His body is covered in scars, and a recent cut runs down his stomach. The blood on his hands and caked under his ﬁngernails is mixed with dirt. There are smears of vomit on his upper body, along with streaks of grass and dirt.
zh_text: 他閉上雙眼。蓋在腰上的被單上染有血跡。肚子上還有些乾掉的血塊。他的身上佈滿傷疤，肚子上有一條剛割出來的。他掌心的血跡和指甲中的血塊都混雜著泥土。他上半身看得出有嘔吐物抹掉的痕跡，還有許多雜草和泥土擦過的痕跡。

en_text: “Joe, can you tell me how this happened?”
zh_text: 「喬，你能告訴我發生什麼事了嗎？」

en_text: “Attacked. I was attacked.”
zh_text: 「打我。有人打我。」

en_text: “I’m going to call the police, then I’m going to call an ambulance.”
zh_text: 「我先報警，然後叫救護車。」

en_text: “No. No. No ambulance. No police. Please.”
zh_text: 不。不。不要叫救護車。不要叫警察。拜託。

en_text: Before she can ask him why, he reaches out and wraps his hand around her wrist. He tightens his grip, manages to keep a hold for a few seconds before it falls away. “I’m Joe Victim,” he says, “but Joe doesn’t want to be a victim. No police. Just medicine.”
zh_text: 他突然伸手，一把抱住她的腰。他手中使劲，抓了幾秒，然後鬆手。「喬不想當被害人。不要報警。只要吃藥。」

en_text: Gently she reaches out and picks up the corner of the sheet. Joe starts to shiver. She slowly lifts it aside not sure what to expect, but certainly not this, and what she sees makes her gasp and tears well up and spill down her cheeks. “Oh, my poor sweet Joe,” she says. “Who did this to you?”
zh_text: 她輕輕伸手，拉住床單角落。喬開始發抖。她緩緩掀起床單，看到的景象令她淚流滿面。「喔，可憐的喬。」她說。「是誰這麼對你？」

en_text: “Nobody,” he answers, only managing a whisper.
zh_text: 沒有人。他擠出一點聲音說道。

en_text: “We need more help.”
zh_text: 「我們必須找人幫忙。」

en_text: “People can’t know. People laugh at Joe. Laugh more if they ﬁnd out.” “I have to call the police.” She reaches out and grabs hold of the phone. “No!” Joe screams, sitting up and grabbing hold of her hand again, his hand wrapping around her wrist with so much force she’s worried he’s going to break it. “They’ll kill me!”
zh_text: 「不能讓別人知道。別人會笑喬。知道了會笑更大聲。」「我必須報警。」她伸手握住電話。

en_text: Then, the pain of sitting up hits him, he ﬂops down, his eyes roll back in his head, and he passes out.
zh_text: 「不！」喬大叫，坐起身來，再度抓住她的手。「他們會殺了我！」用力起身引發了一陣疼痛，他躺回床上，兩眼一翻，昏了過去。

en_text: Yes, but a professional would know when she was out of her depth. She would know when to call for an ambulance.
zh_text: 她拿起被單，放到旁邊的地板上。站在床邊，看著傷口，她不禁認爲自己是在侵犯喬的隱私，不過此刻她的身分當然是名護士：專業人士。這就是她在學校學的技能，她想要做的工作。沒錯，不過專業人士會知道自己的能力範圍。她會知道什麼時候該叫救護車。這種想法一點也沒錯。她沒有能力處理這種情況。她不知道該怎麼做。

en_text: That’s exactly right. This isn’t what she trained for. But a professional making that decision could get Joe killed, if what he said is true. At the very least she’ll see what she can do to help him, then reassess the decision. She reaches up to bring the cruciﬁx up to her chin. She holds it there for a few seconds before taking it off and wrapping the chain around Joe’s hand so Jesus rests in his palm. Moving back she crouches down to look at the wound from another direction. Joe’s penis is lying on an angle, upward across the base of his stomach and pointing at his shoulder. He’s placed a piece of duct tape across it, to hold it away from the wound.
zh_text: 「不，妳知道。」她低聲道，伸手將十字架貼緊下巴。她維持這個姿勢幾秒，然後取下十字架，將項鍊纏在喬的手上，讓耶穌待在他的掌心。她彎下腰去，自其他角度打量傷口。喬的陽具躺在他的肚子下方，向上指著他的肩膀。一塊膠布將其固定在那裡，顯然是爲了不要讓它去碰到傷口。

en_text: “Poor Joe,” she says, almost in tears. The way to continue is with the basics. She tells herself this over and over as she pulls on a pair of latex gloves, and as she does, she notices other pairs lying around the apartment. What does Joe use them for? Cleaning, most likely. She reaches over and pushes down on the side of Joe’s thigh, trying to get a better look at the wound without touching it. His testicle has been squeezed, mashed, and destroyed by a tool. Her guess is a pair of pliers, or vise grips.
zh_text: 「可憐的喬。」她說，差點聲淚俱下。處理這種傷口得要從基本做起。她在戴上乳膠手套時一再如此告訴自己，同時她又發現公寓裡還有其他乳膠手套。喬拿這些手套做什麼？最大的可能是用來打掃環境。她伸出手去，壓壓喬的大腿，試圖在不觸碰傷口的情況下觀察傷口。他的睪丸被人拿工具壓扁、打爛、摧毀了。她猜是用鉗子，或是扳手。

en_text: “Mugged,” Joe murmurs. His eyes are open again.
zh_text: 「打劫。」喬喃喃說道。他再度張眼。

en_text: “Who mugged you?”
zh_text: 「什麼人幹的？」

en_text: He doesn’t answer. Just keeps looking straight ahead.
zh_text: 喬沒回答。只是一直看著前方。

en_text: She continues to assess the wound. The testicle has to be removed. She wishes there were a way around that, but can’t see one. There’s no doubt it has to go, just as there’s no doubt she lacks the qualiﬁcations—or even the conﬁdence—to do the procedure.
zh_text: 她繼續評估傷口。睪丸必須割除。她希望有其他方法，但是看不出來。非割不可，毫無疑問，就像她沒有能力——也沒有自信——動手割除一樣。

en_text: “We have to get you to a hospital, Joe.”
zh_text: 「我們得要送你去醫院，喬。」

en_text: “Can’t. They’ll come back. Hurt me. Please, can you make it better?” She smiles down at him. “Of course,” she says.
zh_text: 不行。他們會回來找我。傷害我。拜託，妳能治好我嗎？「我試試看。」她違背本願說道。

en_text: The ﬁrst thing she does is open the window. It has to be close to a hundred degrees in here, and already she’s sweating. Fresh air starts to roll in. While she waits for some water to boil, she soaks a cloth in cold water and rests it on Joe’s forehead. He hardly seems to notice. Her ﬁrst-aid kit is more advanced than most, as it contains items she has owned since nursing school. One thing she’s missing is any form of local anesthetic, but if she’s lucky Joe will stay unconscious through most of this. Actually, Joe needs to be the one who is lucky.
zh_text: 她做的第一件事就是打開窗戶。屋子裡室溫肯定將近四十度，她已經開始冒汗了。新鮮空氣開始流通。趁著等待煮開水的時候，她拿一塊沾了冷水的布放在喬的額頭上，他似乎沒有察覺。她的急救箱比一般急救箱齊全，因為裡面放了她在護校求學時的工具。她缺乏局部麻醉劑，不過只要她運氣夠好，喬在手術過程中可能根本不會醒來。事實上，需要好運的是喬。

en_text: She pulls out the handle of her scalpel and drops it in the boiling water. The blade is wrapped in foil, already sterile. She unfolds a plastic sheet and tries to roll Joe on his side and slip it beneath him, but he’s too heavy. She does know how to move patients, but not a patient with a testicle that has been ripped into shreds. She rocks him slightly to the side and does the best she can. She leaves the tape over his penis. It’s a crude job, but effective enough. She soaks a few small pads in iodine, then begins to wipe the area around the wound. The risk of infection is high, but this is the best she can do.
zh_text: 她取出手術刀的刀柄，丟到開水裡。刀片已經消毒過了，包在鋁箔裡。她攤開一張塑膠床單，試圖將喬推成側躺，把床單塞到他身體下，可是他太重了。她知道該如何移動傷患，不過不是睪丸被打爛的傷患。她將他扶側一點，然後盡力塞入床單。她沒撕開陽具上的膠帶。那種作法很粗糙，不過固定得很好。她拿些小襯墊沾了碘酒，然後開始擦拭傷口附近。感染的風險很高，不過她也只能做到這樣了。

en_text: “Are you sure you don’t want to go to a hospital? Joe?”
zh_text: 「你確定不要上醫院嗎，喬？」

en_text: Joe is staring at her as if he wasn’t expecting her to be here. His eyes move to the goldﬁsh bowl on the table. She hadn’t noticed it until now.
zh_text: 喬瞪視著她，彷彿沒想到她會在這裡一樣。他的目光移動到桌上的魚缸。她直到現在才注意到它。

en_text: “Joe?”

“Please . . .” He points to the empty bottle of wine. She takes a closer look and realizes it’s still about a third full. She reaches out and hands it to him. It will help, she thinks. She also pulls the belt out of his discarded and bloody jeans. The belt will help too.
zh_text: 「麻煩妳……」喬指向空酒瓶。她細看之下，發現裡面還有三分之一的酒。她將酒瓶遞給喬。喝酒會有幫助，她心想。她同時也抽出丟在旁邊的牛仔褲上的皮帶。皮帶也幫得上忙。

en_text: She looks down at her hands. They’re no longer shaking. She rips open the foil packaging of the scalpel blade and prepares to go to work.
zh_text: 她低頭看著自己的手。已經不抖了。她撕開手術刀的鋁箔包裝，準備開始工作。

en_text: I dream of death and wish I was there. I dream of pain and this is where I live.
zh_text: 我夢見死亡，希望自己置身死後世界。我夢見痛苦，而那才是我所生存的地方。

en_text: My teeth bite down on the end of the wine bottle and I start swallowing what I can. I’m lucky I even own wine. I bought it six months ago when it was my mother’s birthday. I thought we might celebrate. She accused me of trying to poison her, and I ended up bringing it back home. Normally the smell of wine is enough to make me gag. Now I cling to the feeling it’s giving me, a feeling of hope that I might just slip away from all of this. I try to hold my tongue aside so I don’t have to taste it, but it doesn’t work. I feel like vomiting after a few seconds, but the more I get through, the less concerned I become about the taste, and the more I begin to enjoy the sensation it’s giving me. I let my head rest against the pillow, and look at the person crouching in front of my crotch. The person is wearing a surgeon’s mask, but I can tell it’s a woman. I pray it isn’t Melissa. I don’t know why she’s here. I can’t remember calling for help, and I realize I must be hallucinating. Or just lucky. My face is growing numb, and my vision becomes slow. When I turn my head it takes my eyes a second to catch up. The pain starts to ﬂare up again. I look around the room, but the surroundings are familiar, not like they ought to be if I were in a hospital. I try to bite down on the bottle, but ﬁnd I am already biting down on something else. It’s my belt. Not the sort of thing a doctor would use. My hands are shaking, and my entire body feels warm. I don’t know how the doctor does it, but she moves so quickly that one moment she’ll be holding something sharp in the air, and the next she’ll be dabbing something on me. I blink once, she changes position; I blink again, she’s somewhere else—I’m slipping in and out of consciousness. Mostly her words are disjointed, but she’s trying to reassure me. I watch as she removes pieces of skin and ﬂesh, then I can watch no more.
zh_text: 我的牙齒緊咬酒瓶瓶口，盡可能開始吞噬酒精。幸虧家裡有酒。那是六個月前我媽生日的時候買的。我想跟她慶祝慶祝。她指控我想毒死她，最後我就把酒帶回家了。正常情況下，光是聞到紅酒的味道我就受不了。如今我擁抱它所帶來的感覺，一種希望我能擺脫這一切的感覺。我試圖縮起舌頭，不去接觸酒味，但是這樣沒用。幾秒鐘後，我開始想吐，不過喝得越多，我就越不在乎酒味。我將腦袋靠在枕頭上，看著在我胯下旁的那個人。那個人戴著外科口罩，不過看得出來是個女人。我希望她不是梅莉莎。我不知道她為何來此。我不記得有打電話找人幫忙，接著我了解這一切都是幻覺。又可能是我運氣好。我的臉越來越麻，視線開始模糊。轉頭之時，我的眼睛要過一會兒才會跟著轉過來。我又開始痛了。我環顧四周，身處環境看來十分熟悉，如果在醫院裡的話應該不會這樣。我試圖緊咬酒瓶，不過卻發現我在咬其他東西。我伸手摸了摸，發現那是我的皮帶。這可不是醫生會用的道具。我的雙手在抖，全身都感到一陣暖意。我不知道醫生是怎麼辦到的，但是她的動作飛快，前一刻手裡還握著某樣尖銳的東西，下一刻她已經在擦拭我的身體。我眨了眨眼，她改變位置；我又眨眼，她又出現在別處——我在意識邊緣遊走。她的話聽來斷斷續續，但是我知道她在安慰我。我看著她割下皮膚和肉塊，接著我再也看不下去了。

en_text: I stare up at the ceiling. It is sagging slightly in the middle. I try talking to my doctor, but I’m not really sure what I’m saying. Is this all a dream? Am I operating on myself?
zh_text: 我凝視著天花板。天花板中央有點下沉。我試圖跟醫生交談，不過不太確定我究竟在說些什麼。我是在做夢嗎？我是在給自己開刀嗎？

en_text: I don’t know how much time passes, but when I look up again, the doctor is gone. I am all alone, just as my testicle is now all alone. I start to reach down my body, but then think better of it. I’m too scared to see what the damage could be. I close my eyes. Open them again. The doctor is in. I close them. The doctor is out.
zh_text: 我不知道過了多久，不過當我再度抬頭時，醫生已經不在了。我孤零零地，就像我的睪丸一樣孤零零。我開始伸手去摸下體，不過想想還是不要這麼做比較好。我不敢去看底下的慘狀。我閉上雙眼。再度睜開。醫生回來了。我閉上雙眼。醫生又消失了。

en_text: What is happening to me?
zh_text: 我到底怎麼了？

en_text: Am I dying?
zh_text: 我要死了嗎？

en_text: I stare at the ceiling and hope that I am.
zh_text: 我凝望天花板，希望我真的快要死了。

en_text: Sally sits on the couch and stares at the goldﬁsh bowl. When she reaches out and sprinkles in some food, the two ﬁsh inside quickly head toward the surface and begin eating.
zh_text: 莎莉坐在沙發上，看著金魚缸。當她伸手丟入一些飼料時，裡面的兩條魚立刻游到水面來大快朵頤。

en_text:
The surgery, if she can call it that, has gone well. She suspects the chances of infection are slim. She has neatly removed the damage done by the pliers, and used dissolvable stitches internally and normal stitches externally. Of course only time will tell. Now that she’s ﬁnished, she’s hung the cruciﬁx back around her neck.
She had ﬁgured Joe needed it more during that time.
zh_text:
那場手術，如果可以稱爲手術的話，進行得不錯。她認爲感染的機率很低。她順利移除了鉗子造成的傷害，用可溶式縫線縫合內部，用正常縫線縫合外傷。當然會不會感染有待時間證明。如今完工了，她又將十字架掛回脖子上。
她認爲手術過程中喬比較需要它。

en_text: She’s decided that as much as she wants to call the police, she won’t do it. She wants Joe to be healed professionally, and she wants the people who did this to be caught and convicted, but she’ll wait until she can discuss it with him. There isn’t room out on the streets for people who can commit such an evil act. She thinks about the Christchurch Carver, about the hell he’s been putting women through. It’s true that the devil can walk among us.
zh_text: 她想打電話報警。她希望喬能有專業的醫療照顧，而且她希望犯案的人被逮捕定罪。世界上絕對容不下有能力做出這等邪惡之舉的人。她想到基督城屠夫，想到他讓女人經歷過的地獄。魔鬼真的會行走人間。

en_text: Joe’s life is different enough, and she doesn’t blame him for not wanting to be the mentally challenged man who was deprived of his money and his dignity. She respects Joe’s right to not be known as the man who has lost a testicle. When he is capable, when he is fully aware, she will help him understand that the right path will be to involve others who can help him. She thinks about the scars on his chest. What sort of life has he had? Who abused him? Is this why he never speaks of his parents?
zh_text: 喬的人生與衆不同，她不怪他不想當個財富與尊嚴都遭受剝奪的心理障礙人士。她認爲喬有權利不讓其他人知道他失去了一顆睪丸。當他醒過來，完全恢復意識後，她會讓他了解接受其他人的幫助才是正確的作法。她想到他胸口的傷疤。他到底有著什麼樣的過去？是誰虐待他？這就是他不願提起父母的原因嗎？

en_text: Joe is unconscious, so she rolls him onto one side, then the other, maneuvering the bloody sheets from beneath him. She wraps the pieces of ﬂesh she has cut away in the plastic sheet and places it in a plastic bag, then throws the bedsheets, jeans, underwear, and shirt into the washing machine and sets the cycle going. She ﬁnds a second plastic shopping bag and begins ﬁlling it with all the rubbish from the surgery. She wraps the scalpel blade securely to ensure it can never hurt anybody. She takes off her latex gloves and drops them in the bag too.
zh_text: 喬不省人事，於是莎莉將他翻向一側，然後又翻向另一側，抽出底下血淋淋的床單。她把剛剛割下來的皮肉包到塑膠床單裡，然後摺成塑膠袋，接著又將被單、牛仔褲、內衣和上衣丟到洗衣機，讓機器開始運作。她又找到一個塑膠購物袋，開始將所有手術時產生的垃圾塞到裡面。她謹慎包裹手術刀片，確保它不會割傷任何人，然後她脫掉乳膠手套，丟入塑膠袋中。

en_text: She puts on another pair, then starts tidying and cleaning the apartment. The dishes piled up in the sink haven’t even been rinsed. The food stains on the countertop match the food stains on the table. When she ﬁnds a vacuum cleaner, she decides to run it brieﬂy over the ﬂoors. None of the noises wake Joe. When the washing machine is ﬁnished, she bundles the items into the dryer and sets it going. The paperbacks on the couch are all romance novels. Martin never read anything like this; he only ever read comic books. She ﬁnds it odd at ﬁrst, but encouraging that Joe would read something with more of a story. As she picks up the folders next to the books, the contents of one spill.
zh_text: 莎莉又戴上另一雙乳膠手套，開始打掃公寓。堆在碗槽裡的碗盤都沒泡水。沙發上的食物印子跟桌上的印子一模一樣。當她翻出一台吸塵器時，她決定花點時間吸吸地板。這些噪音都沒有吵醒喬。洗衣機洗好後，她將裡面的衣物放到烘乾機裡。沙發上的平裝本小說全部都是言情小說。馬丁從來不看這種東西；他只看漫畫。她一開始覺得這樣有點奇怪，不過又很高興喬願意閱讀故事性較高的東西。當她拿起書旁的檔案夾時，裡面的文件掉了出來。

en_text: “What are you doing, Joe?” she whispers to herself. She recognizes the photograph of one of the dead women. She scoops them up, ﬂicks through them, then puts them back into the folder before moving on to the next. Joe has the complete set—the Christchurch Carver’s victims. He also has information on the detectives investigating the case. She looks through them, trying to ﬁgure out why Joe would have these here. Does he know the women in these pictures are dead?
zh_text: 「你在做什麼，喬？」她自言自語道。她認出其中一名死者的照片。她撿起文件，隨手翻閱，然後將它們放回檔案夾，跟著又去看其他檔案夾。喬收集了所有檔案——基督城屠夫的被害人檔案。他同時也有一份調查此案的警探名單。她仔細翻閱它們，試圖弄清楚喬的家裡為什麼會有這種東西。他知道這些照片裡的女人已經死了嗎？

en_text: Joe wouldn’t bring these things home unless there was a good reason, and she’s sure he wouldn’t be doing it for money. Either somebody’s threatening him, or he’s got them for himself. But why? Does it have something to do with his attack?
zh_text: 除非有很好的理由，不然喬不會帶這種東西回家，而她很肯定他不是爲了錢。要嘛就是有人威脅他這麼做，不然就是自己要的。但是爲什麼？

en_text: When she looks over at Joe, she sees another folder, this one on the small bedside table. It’s a psychological proﬁle of the Christchurch Carver. No way in the world could Joe possibly understand any of this. So why have it? And why have it next to his bed, as if he had recently been reading it? Outside, the streetlights have come on. The road is empty except for a few parked cars and for the ﬁrst time it’s starting to feel like autumn. She closes the window.
zh_text: 她望向喬，看到床頭桌上擺著另外一份檔案。那是基督城屠夫的心理概況。喬絕不可能看得懂這些東西。那他究竟爲什麼要拿回來呢？爲什麼要擺在床頭，而且好像最近才閱讀過的樣子？街燈已經亮起。馬路上空蕩蕩的，只有幾輛車停在路邊。

en_text: She empties the bucket in the sink and rinses it out, then ﬁlls it a quarter of the way with water and sets it next to Joe’s bed. She imagines he’ll use it to urinate into—he won’t be able to walk for a few days. She checks the dressing on his wound. No signs of blood. When the dryer stops its cycle, she pulls out the sheets, rolls Joe to one side, then the other, tugging one sheet beneath him. She tucks the second sheet over him, but it’s still too warm in here for a blanket. His briefcase, which is heavier than she thought, she puts within reach of his bed in case he needs it. She spends a few seconds thinking that she should open it, that perhaps there are answers in there, then decides against it. Joe trusted she would come and help him, not to go through his belongings.
zh_text: 她倒光碗槽裡的水桶，清洗乾淨，然後倒了四分之一的清水，放在喬的床旁。她想喬應該會拿它來尿尿——他接下來幾天內都無法行走。她檢查包紮傷口的繃帶。沒有滲血。烘乾機烘好之後，她拿出床單，幫喬翻好，將床單塞到他身體下。她又拿了一張被單蓋在他身上，外加一條毯子。她將他比想像中來得沉重的公事包放到床邊，以免他需要用到。

en_text: She checks that everything is tidied away, picks up his keys, her ﬁrst-aid kit, and heads back out to her car.
zh_text: 她確定一切整理妥當，拿起他的鑰匙以及她的急救箱，朝自己的車走去。

en_text: Sunday. Not in the morning, or even in the afternoon, but late in the evening. I have slept for over a day. My internal clock tells me nothing. I am somewhere between hell and the torment of life. I pass in and out of consciousness, hardly aware of the fact that I am even alive. I look at my alarm clock. It’s nine forty.
zh_text: 星期天。不是早上，甚至不是下午，而是傍晚。我睡了超過一天。我的生理時鐘沒有叫我起床。我身處地獄和痛苦的人世間，不斷昏迷甦醒，根本弄不清楚自己是死是活。我望向鬧鐘。九點四十分。

en_text: When I toss aside the blankets I’m relieved to see little in the way of blood. A white dressing around my crotch has been methodically applied. It is mostly dry. I try to focus on what happened after I managed to get home yesterday morning, but come up with nothing except a headache.
zh_text: 當我掀開毯子，只看到一點血跡時，我覺得鬆了一大口氣。我的胯下整整齊齊地包紮了一塊白繃帶。基本上是乾的。我努力回想昨天早上回家後發生了什麼事情，但是什麼也想不起來。

en_text: I have nothing to get up for. My ﬁsh need feeding. But my ﬁsh can wait. I don’t know how long they can survive without food, but we all might be ﬁnding out. The bucket, which looks relatively clean considering I’ve ﬁlled it with water and antiseptic, I now piss into. My urine stings and comes in short spurts. When I ﬁnish, my room smells worse than normal.
zh_text: 我沒有起床的理由。我的魚需要吃東西，不過他們可以等。我不知道他們能在缺乏食物的情況下存活多久，不過我們都有機會試出這個答案。我此刻用來尿尿的水桶看起來還算乾淨，雖然我昨天拿它去裝水和清潔劑。我的尿有點刺痛，而且斷斷續續的。尿完之後，我的房間聞起來比平常臭。

en_text: I close my eyes. I can see a woman standing over me with a mask over her face and a scalpel in her hand. She shimmers, the mask disappears, the scalpel becomes a pair of pliers, my bedroom ceiling becomes a purple sky with dying stars, and the stranger becomes Melissa. Melissa did this to me. Melissa ripped away my testicle.
zh_text: 閉上雙眼，我可以看見一個戴著口罩、手持手術刀的女人站在我的面前。她身形一閃，口罩消失，手術刀變成一把鉗子，我的臥房天花板變成一片紫色夜空，掛著幾顆黯淡的星星，而那個女人變成梅莉莎。梅莉莎對我做出這種事情。梅莉莎奪走了我的睪丸。

en_text: And it was Melissa who came to help me. Had to have been.
zh_text: 而來幫我療傷的也是梅莉莎。一定是她。

en_text: “Goddamn her,” I say, opening my eyes. I pull the covers over my body and lean back into the pillow. I need rest, but I’m not tired. I need to think about something other than Melissa, if only for a few minutes. I reach out to my bedside table and grab the folder.
zh_text: 「該死的女人。」我說著睜開雙眼，拉回毯子，靠回枕頭上。我需要休息，不過我不累。我需要想想梅莉莎以外的事情，就算只是分心片刻也好。我伸手到床頭桌上，拿起了那份檔案。

en_text: A loner. Caucasian, as crimes like these seldom cross racial lines and all the women are white. Early thirties. Killings are all at night, suggesting he has a job, but it will be something menial. He feels the job is beneath him, that he is far too good for what he is doing. He lives with a woman who is domineering, perhaps a mother or an aunt. I remember Melissa asking me about the domineering mother ﬁgure. She believes the same bullshit as whoever wrote this.
zh_text: 獨居。白種人，因為這種犯罪鮮少跨越種族，而受害女子都是白人。三十歲左右。全部都是夜間犯案，表示他有工作，不過是個低賤的工作。他認為工作配不上自己，他有能力做更好的工作。他跟一名跋扈專擅的女人住在一起，或許是母親或是阿姨。我想起梅莉莎問我有沒有喜歡掌控一切的母親形象的人物。她的想法跟寫這份狗屎的人不謀而合。

en_text: He does not have the ability to stand up to this woman and, through transference, he gets back at her by killing different women. It is not the sex he wants, but the domineering power. He uses sex as a weapon. It is highly probable he has a previous police record. Peeping and peering—voyeurism—would be a good guess. Burglary just as likely. The report goes on to say that I don’t have a multiple personality, and that I’m not insane, which means they got at least something right.
zh_text: 他沒有能力起身對抗這個女人，透過移情作用，他以殺害這些不同的女子來報復她。他要的不是性，而是掌控的權力。他將性當作武器。他很可能有犯罪紀錄。可能是偷看與窺視——窺淫狂，也可能有竊盜前科。報告繼續提到我沒有多重人格，而且我也沒有精神異常，這表示他們至少有些地方沒有弄錯。

en_text: If there are constant compulsions for him to rape and kill, then these are not consistent with the times he has committed the acts. Mostly there have been gaps of a month between the deaths. This could be because he has been picked up on other, unrelated charges. Other times there is a gap of only a week. The fact that his victims cooperate suggests he threatens them with a weapon, and since none of the victims has been killed while her husband or partner was home, it is reasonable to assume he is unwilling to risk an encounter with another male.
zh_text: 根據犯案的時間研判，他不會經常出現強暴與殺人的衝動。兩次犯案之間通常間隔一個月的空窗期。這很可能是因為他為了其他無關的案件而遭到逮捕。也有犯案間隔僅僅一週的情況。被害人都很合作的事實顯示他以武器威脅她們就範，而由於沒有受害人是在丈夫與伴侶在家時遭到殺害，我們可以合理假設他不希望冒險與其他男性衝突。

en_text: He shows a lack of organization, using items from the scene to bind the woman rather than bringing items of his own. His sexual nature is becoming more perverse as he continues his attacks. He plans his attacks perhaps weeks before committing them. The covering of victims’ faces and the turning down of photographs show he likes to depersonalize them. He covers their faces before he kills them to fantasize that he is killing somebody else, the dominant woman in his life, rather than covering them afterward out of any feelings of guilt. He keeps items as trophies, underwear and jewelry from the scenes, perhaps to relive the moments. He has sociopathic tendencies, he has no conscience, and he does not see his victims as real people.
zh_text: 他缺乏組織性，利用現場的物品綑綁被害人，而不自備綑綁用具。他的性傾向有越來越變態的趨勢。他犯案之前可能會計畫幾個禮拜。遮住被害人的面孔以及翻倒現場的照片顯示他喜歡物化她們。他在殺人之前遮蔽她們的面孔是爲了假裝自己在殺另一個人，那個掌控他一生的女人。他不是出於罪惡感而於殺人之後遮臉。他會保留紀念品，現場的內衣及珠寶，或許是爲了重溫當時的景況。他有反社會傾向，缺乏良知，不將被害人當作真人看待。

en_text: Grave sites should be kept under surveillance as he may show up, not out of remorse, but to relive the crime. He may call the police to offer help, to offer a witness statement, all to learn where the investigation is at. He may try to hang around police bars, may try talking about the case with them to learn what he can. . . .
zh_text: 警方應該持續監視被害人的墓地，因為他有可能出現，不是出於悔恨，而是想要重溫犯案時的情況。他可能會爲了得知調查狀況而致電警方提供線索，提供證詞。他可能會去警察常去的酒吧，嘗試跟警方討論案情……

en_text: The report goes on. It mentions that rape is a violent crime where sex is the weapon. Mentions that sex is used for power and control, that it’s used to dominate. Are they right about why I covered their faces? Was I depersonalizing them, or pretending they were somebody else? I’m not sure. They’re right about the graves, though. I did consider going there, but luckily I found out that they were under surveillance before I ever tried. When I was in my late teens, I used to lie in bed at night and think about my neighbors. I used to wonder what they were doing at that exact moment. Were they thinking of me? I used to imagine moving from house to house under the darkness of night, taking what I wanted from them, doing what I wanted to anybody. Back then the fantasy was in getting away with it—not the killing, but the succeeding. Back then I always believed that I could commit the perfect crime. These days the fantasy has become reality. And that’s what the proﬁle is missing.
zh_text: 報告繼續。它提到強暴乃是以性作爲武器的暴力罪行。性乃是權力與支配的工具，是爲了要掌控大局。我遮蔽她們的面孔是出於他們所說的理由嗎？我是在物化她們，或是將她們當作其他人？我不確定。墓地的事情倒是沒有說錯，我確實有考慮過要去走走，幸運的是我在這麼做之前就發現警方在監視墓地。青少年晚期，我經常夜裡躺在床上，想著我的鄰居。我很好奇他們當時都在幹些什麼。他們有在想我嗎？我經常幻想自己趁著夜色跑到他們家去，取走我想要的東西，對他們爲所欲爲。當時我的幻想著重在脫罪之上——不是殺人，而是成功犯案。當時我始終相信我能犯下完美的罪行。最近我將幻想化爲現實，而這份心理報告沒有提到這一點。

en_text: I turn off the light and close my eyes. I’m tired, but the soreness keeps me awake. I get up to four before deciding that counting sheep is one stupid idea.
zh_text: 我關上燈，閉上眼。我很疲憊，但又痛得睡不著。數到第四隻羊時，我認定數羊是個愚蠢的主意。

en_text: I don’t know how it happens, but the next thing I know I’m waking up in the morning, my alarm clock helping me to escape from another nightmare. I dreamed of Melissa and her pliers. Each time I screamed for her to stop, but nothing would stop her.
zh_text: 我不知道是怎麼睡著的，不過接下來我就發現自己於天亮後醒來，我的鬧鐘讓我逃過另外一場惡夢。我夢到梅莉莎和她的鉗子。每一次我都大聲叫她住手，但是她怎麼樣也不肯住手。

en_text: I call work. No, I’m not sick, but my mother is. Yes, it’s sad. Yes, I’ll give her their best. Yes, I’ll let them know how she is. Yes, I’ll take as long as needed to make sure she is going to be okay. Yes, yes, fucking yes. It hurts to talk, and I feel like my nuts have been run over by a train. I use my bucket to urinate.
zh_text: 我打電話到警局。不，我沒生病，病的是我媽。是，很難過。好，我會代他們向她問好。好，我會讓他們得知她的狀況。好，我會等她沒事再來上班。好，好。他媽的好。我一講話就會痛，而且我覺得好像蛋蛋被火車輾過一樣。我拿水桶出來尿尿

en_text: I’m tempted to get up for a glass of water, but the temptation loses out to my reluctance to produce more pain than I can handle. Instead I remain thirsty until I ﬁnally fall back to sleep. When I awake I’m covered in sweat. My sheets are wet, my face sticky. I’m so thirsty I ball up the sheets and try sucking the sweat out of them. When I can’t ﬁnd enough moisture, I glance at my bucket of urine, but it isn’t something I can resort to. I stagger to my feet and hobble away from the bed to grace the sink with my presence. I throw up into it before ﬁlling a glass of water and knocking it back. Fill it back up. Wash out the sink. Then I throw up again. The kitchen counter is tidy. I can’t remember doing it. In fact the entire apartment looks like I’ve cleaned it. Just what in the hell have I been doing while I’ve been passed out?
zh_text: 我很想起床倒杯水喝，不過因爲不想讓自己痛到難以承受而作罷。我就這麼口渴下去，直到終於躺回去睡著爲止。醒來時渾身冒汗。我的被單濕了，臉黏答答的。我渴到想從被單上擰出一點汗水來喝。在發現擰不出來後，我將目光移動到尿桶上，不過我實在無法接受喝尿這種事情。我掙扎起身，跌跌撞撞地走近水槽。我先嘔吐片刻，然後倒杯清水，一飲而盡。然後我又開始吐。廚房的料理台還算乾淨。我不記得有打掃過。事實上，整間公寓看起來都像是清理過的樣子——我昏迷時究竟幹了些什麼事情？

en_text: In the process of half shufﬂing and half dragging my feet toward the sofa, I trip and pain explodes through my groin as I hit the ﬂoor. The world disappears, and when I come to, I’m in bed. A glass of water with ﬂecks of ice in it rests on my bedside table, alongside a bottle of pills without a label. Several hours have passed. Maybe even an entire day.
zh_text: 在拖拖拉拉地走向沙發的過程中，我一不小心摔了一跤，落地時胯下傳來一陣劇痛。世界消失了，再度醒來時，我發現自己躺在床上。床頭桌上放著一杯有加冰塊的冰水，旁邊還有一罐沒有標示的藥丸。又過好幾個小時了。

en_text: I take out one of the pills. It has to be some sort of antibiotic. I swallow it down with some water. I close my eyes. I don’t even know what’s real anymore.
zh_text: 我拿出一片藥丸。那應該是某種抗生素。我搭配清水將藥丸吞了下去，閉上雙眼，再也無法分辨真實與虛幻。

en_text: I get out of bed, lean against the sofa, and sprinkle some ﬁsh food into the bowl. I don’t hang around to watch them eat. I look around. My clothes have been washed and folded. The sheets have very little blood on them. I look down at the dressing around my wound. There seems to be less blood there than yesterday. Did Melissa change the dressing when she helped me back into bed? Or did I change the dressing when I helped myself back there? Jesus, what’s wrong with me? I pass out the moment I touch the bed.
zh_text: 我下床，靠在沙發上，丟了點魚飼料到魚缸裡。我沒有留下來看他們吃。我環顧四周。我的衣服洗過也摺好了。床單上沒有多少血跡。我低頭看著傷口上的繃帶，上面的血跡似乎比昨天還少。是梅莉莎扶我上床的時候順便更換繃帶的嗎？還是我自己爬回床上時換的？天啊，我到底怎麼了？我一回到床上立刻陷入昏迷。

en_text: When I wake up, I pick up the phone and dial the number.
zh_text: 醒來後，我拿起電話撥號。

en_text: “Joe? Is that you?”
zh_text: 「喬，是你嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah, Mom. Listen, I can’t come over for dinner tonight.”
zh_text: 「是，媽。聽著，我今晚不能過去吃飯了。」

en_text: It’s an effort to talk, but I do my best to sound as normal as a guy who only has one functioning testicle can. “I have meatloaf, Joe. You love meatloaf.”
zh_text: 說話很費力，不過我盡可能擠出只有一顆睾丸的男人所能擠出最正常的聲音。「我做了烤肉餅，喬。你愛吃烤肉餅。」

en_text: “Right.”
zh_text: 「沒錯。」

en_text: “I don’t mind cooking you meatloaf. You enjoy it, don’t you?”
zh_text: 「我不介意幫你做烤肉餅。你很愛吃，對吧？」

en_text: “Sure, Mom, but—” “Your father never enjoyed my meatloaf. Said it tasted like rubber-soled shoes.”
zh_text: 「當然，媽，但是……」「你爸從來不愛吃我做的烤肉餅。說它吃起來像橡膠鞋底。」「媽……」

en_text: “Mom—” “Because if you don’t like it, all you have to do is say.”
zh_text: 「如果你不爱吃，只要說一聲就好了。」

en_text: What in the hell is she going on about? Christ. “Listen, Mom, I can’t come around. I’m tied up with work.”
zh_text: 她到底在講什麼？老天啊。「聽著，媽，我不能過去。我工作太忙了。」

en_text: “How can you be tied up with work? You sell cars. Listen, Joe, I can make something else if you like. How about I make spaghetti Bolognese?” At ﬁrst I’m not sure what she’s getting at, that she must be talking about my cousin, but then I remember that for the last few years I’ve been telling her that I sell cars. I ﬁnd I’m gripping the phone. Hard. “I can’t come around, Mom.”
zh_text: 「你怎麼可能工作太忙？你是賣車的。聽著，喬，我可以幫你做點其他的東西吃。義大利肉醬麵怎麼樣？」一開始我不確定她在講什麼，接著我想起來過去幾年裡我都告訴他我在賣車。我發現自己緊握話筒，非常用力。「我不能過去，媽。」

en_text: “Seven o’clock then?”
zh_text: 「那就七點吧？」

en_text: “I can’t come around.”
zh_text: 「我不能過去。」

en_text: “Supermarket has chicken on special. Do you think I should buy some?”
zh_text: 「超市有雞肉在打折。你覺得我該買些回來嗎？」

en_text: I’m shaking my head, gritting my teeth. My remaining ball is throbbing. “Whatever.”
zh_text: 我用力搖頭，咬牙切齒。我的睪丸在抽痛。「隨便。」

en_text: “Number eight chickens are cheap.”
zh_text: 「眞的很便宜。」

en_text: “Buy some, then.”
zh_text: 「那就買一點。」

en_text: “You think I should?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你覺得我該買？」

en_text: “Sure.”
zh_text: 「當然。」

en_text: “Do you want me to buy some for you?”
zh_text: 「要我幫你買點嗎？」

en_text: “I don’t mind.”
zh_text: 「我不介意。」

en_text: “I’m ﬁne, Mom.”
zh_text: 「我不用，媽。」

en_text: “Are you okay, Joe? You sound sick.”
zh_text: 「你還好嗎，喬？你聽起來不太舒服。」

en_text: “I’m tired. That’s all.”
zh_text: 「我累了。如此而已。」

en_text: “You need more sleep,” she says. “I have just the thing. You want me to come over?”
zh_text: 「你得多睡一會兒。我有東西可以幫助睡眠。要我過去一趟嗎？」

en_text: “You don’t want me to see your house? Do you have gay things there, Joe? Do you have one of those homosexuals living with you?” “I’m not gay, Mom.”
zh_text: 「你不要我去你家？你在那裡藏了什麼嗎，喬？是不是有個同性戀跟你住在一起？」「我不是同性戀，媽。」

en_text: “So what am I supposed to do with this meatloaf? Throw it out, I suppose?”
zh_text: 「那我要怎麼處理這些肉餅？丟掉，我想。」

en_text: “Freeze it.”
zh_text: 「冰起來。」

en_text: “I’ll come around next Monday, Mom. I promise.”
zh_text: 「我下禮拜一過去，媽。我保證。」

en_text: “I guess we’ll wait and see. Bye, Joe.”
zh_text: 我想我們走著瞧。再見，喬。

en_text: “Bye, Mom.”
zh_text: 「再見，媽。」

en_text: I’m sweating. I’m also amazed she said good-bye ﬁrst. I look down at the bucket. The smell of urine has gone. The water looks clear. I piss into it, my crotch throbbing.
zh_text: 我在冒汗。我也很驚訝她會先道再見。我低頭看著水桶。尿味消失了。水看起來乾淨多了。我尿在裡面，胯下持續抽動。

en_text: Hanging up the telephone gets me remembering. When I came home from the park, I’m pretty sure I made a phone call. But to who?
zh_text: 掛下電話讓我想起某件事情。剛從公園回家的時候，我很肯定自己打了通電話。但是打給誰？

en_text: Sally?
zh_text: 莎莉？

en_text: I get up and walk to the fridge. Her number is still there, but smudged across the paper are patches of blood. I came home. I was in pain. I made a phone call. I think I made a phone call.
zh_text: 我起身走向冰箱。她的電話號碼還在上面，但是紙上染有血跡。我回家。我很痛。我打了通電話。我想我打了通電話。

en_text: I go back to bed. My testicle is gone and when I try to remember cutting it away, I picture ﬁrst Melissa behind a doctor’s mask, and then Sally behind one. I wonder where I put it. Or they put it. Light and dark, sleep and consciousness, awareness of everything and then of nothing. I glide through this existence as best as I can, not bothering to count the hours in case they’re not passing by. Other times I am standing in front of Pickle and Jehovah—not even aware of having stood up and moved over to them —watching them swim and wondering if a goldﬁsh had its testicle removed, would it remember? My testicle is gone and so is my sanity. The former will never come back. I’m holding out hope for the latter.
zh_text: 我回到床上。我少了一顆睾丸，而當我試圖回想怎麼割掉的時候，一開始我想像梅莉莎戴口罩的模樣，然後換成莎莉。我不知道我把口罩放到哪裡去了，還是她們把口罩放到哪裡去了。光明與黑暗，昏迷與甦醒，意識到一切，然後忘記一切。我盡力跳過這種虛實不定的存在，沒有費心去計算時間，以免時間根本不曾流逝。其他時候我會站在泡菜和耶和華之前——甚至不記得我有起身走過去——看著他們游泳，好奇金魚的睪丸被割掉會怎麼樣。他會記得嗎？我的睪丸不見了，理智也跟著消失。前者永遠不會回來，我期待還能找回後者。

en_text: My internal alarm wakes me at seven thirty on Monday morning. An entire week has passed. Just like that. I climb from bed and ﬁnd myself walking better than I have all week. At the window I stare out my shitty view, which today is even shittier than normal. It looks cold outside.
zh_text: 我的生理時鐘在禮拜一早上七點半的時候叫我起床。一整個禮拜過去了。就這樣。我爬下床，發現自己走路比上個禮拜順暢多了。

en_text: I follow my normal weekday routine. I shower and shave, though it takes slightly longer. I make some toast. I feed my ﬁsh. My apartment doesn’t smell as bad as I would have thought. The bucket I’ve been pissing into looks like I’ve only used it a few times. When I go to make lunch, I ﬁnd most of the food in my apartment has gone off. Still, I feel like I’ve gone through the week from hell and come out in pretty good shape considering.
