The stairs are awkward and I struggle to walk down them, but I make it without any blood appearing on the front of my overalls. The temperature has dropped by half since the last time I was outside. Gray skies above and black clouds far in the distance, none of it looks like it’s moving. I have to explain to Mr. Stanley why I haven’t seen him for a week. Yeah, Mom’s been sick. On the bumpy bus, what remains of my ball sac threatens to tear open. What I need is a man tampon. Or a time machine.
zh_text: 我展開正常的例行公事。沖了個澡，刮了個鬍子，不過花的時間比正常要長一點。我做了些吐司，餵了魚。我的公寓沒有想像中那麼臭。我拿來尿尿的水桶看起來才尿過幾次而已。去做午餐時，我發現公寓裡大部分的食物都不翼而飛。樓梯寸步難行，我努力下樓，在工作服上沒有滲出任何血液的情況下抵達一樓。我必須向史丹利先生解釋為什麼一個禮拜沒搭公車。是的，我媽病了。在顛簸的公車上，我僅存的陰囊差點裂開。我需要男用衛生棉條，或是時光機。

en_text: Mr. Stanley lets me off the bus. I hobble across the road and prepare to start another working week.
zh_text: 史丹利先生讓我下車。我搖搖晃晃地過了馬路，準備展開一天的工作。

en_text: “I heard you were back at work,” Sally says, and her face seems to be torn between trying to look both happy and concerned.
zh_text: 「我聽說你回來上班了。」莎莉說，她的表情彷彿糾纏在快樂和憂心之間。

en_text: I am downstairs in the holding cells, throwing a mop back and forth, trying to wipe up all the vomit and piss the weekend drunks have sprayed all over the place. Out of all the things I do here, this has to be the worst. Every month contracted cleaners come in to really give the cells an overhaul, but it’s amazing how painted cinder-block walls and cement ﬂoors can really soak up the smell, it smells like a zoo, if the zookeepers boxed the animals into smaller cages and never cleared away the shit. I’ve just spent ten minutes on one particular bad stain that I couldn’t say what its ingredients were, and know it will take another ten minutes to ﬁnish the job.
zh_text: 我位於樓下的拘留室，前後用著拖把，試圖清理乾淨週末待在這裡的酒鬼所留下來的嘔吐物和排泄物。我在這裡做的諸多雜務裡，這肯定是最噁心的一件。每個月都有承包的清潔工跑來徹底清掃拘留室，不過我實在很難想像煤渣磚牆和水泥地板竟然這麼能夠吸收嘔吐與糞便的味道。

en_text: I take off the face mask that protects me from the God-awful smell. The cells, with their metal front doors and concrete construction, are damn cold to be in even in the middle of summer, and it’s not summer anymore, and the frigid air at the moment is making my ball throb.
zh_text: 我脫掉抵擋惡臭的面具。即使在炎熱的夏天裡，這些有著金屬前門和水泥牆壁的拘留室依然很冷，而此刻冰冷的空氣令我的睾丸不住抽痛。

en_text:
“My mother’s okay,” I say, knowing she must have heard why I was gone.
“Sorry?”
zh_text:
「我媽沒事了。」我說，心知她必定聽說我請假的理由。
「什麼？」

en_text: “My mother. She was sick all week. That’s why I wasn’t here.”
zh_text: 「我媽。她病了一個禮拜。所以我才沒來上班。』

en_text: “Your mother was sick?”
zh_text: 「你媽生病了？」

en_text: “Yeah. I thought you must have heard. That’s why I wasn’t here. Everybody probably knows about it.”
zh_text: 「是啊。我想妳一定聽說了。我是因為這樣才沒來上班的。可能所有人都知道。」

en_text: “Oh, sure, I get it,” she says in hush-hush tones, dragging out the oh and the I, making it sound like a conspiracy. As if we’re having an affair. “Your mother was sick. That’s why you had to take the week off.”
zh_text: 「喔，當然，我懂了。」她說，刻意放低音量，拖長「喔」和「我」兩個音，聽起來神秘兮兮的。好像我們在偷情一樣。「你媽病了。所以你才請假一個禮拜。」

en_text: “Yeah. That’s what I said,” I say, and something in the way she sounds is wrong, oh so wrong. “And she’s better now?”
zh_text: 「是啊，我剛剛就是這麼說的。」我說，不過她的語氣聽來很不對勁，喔，太不對勁了。「她現在好點了？」

en_text: “Sure,” I answer, dragging out the word and nodding slowly, trying to ﬁgure it out. Does she know what happened? Did this woman with an IQ of seventy show up at my house and operate on me?
zh_text: 「當然。」我說，拖長語音，緩緩點頭，試圖搞清楚怎麼回事。她知道出了什麼事嗎？難道這個智商七十的女人跑到我家來幫我動手術？

en_text: “And how are you, Joe? Are you better now too?”
zh_text: 「那你呢，喬？你好一點了嗎？」

en_text: “I’m coping. Time heals all wounds—that’s what my mom says,” I say, wondering if my mom had a ripped-off-testicle kind of wound in mind when she said it.
zh_text: 「我還可以。時間可以治癒所有傷痕——我媽是這麼說的。」

en_text: “That’s right. Look, Joe, remember that if you need anything, if you want me to help with . . . your mother . . . then just let me know.”
zh_text: 「說得對。聽著，喬，記住如果你有什麼需要，如果你要我幫助……你媽……跟我說一聲就行了。」

en_text: Of course the kind of help I really need with my mother isn’t the type she would actually be able to offer. Still, if more people were like Sally, maybe the world would be a better place. The problem though is that she sounds like we’re both in on the big secret, the one where Joe woke up one morning in a park after having his testicle ﬂattened in a pair of pliers and had to make his own way home.
zh_text: 當然我需要別人幫我對我媽做的事情絕對不是她所能提供的。儘管如此，如果莎莉這種人多一點的話，或許世界就會變得更好。問題在於她聽起來彷彿我們之間分享了一個大秘密，就是在睪丸被鉗子壓扁後於公園中醒來然後自己回家的秘密。

en_text: “Joe?”

However, I can’t imagine there ever being a secret both Sally and myself were in on. This is just Sally being Sally. Just trying to help me out with my mother the same way she helps me out by making me lunch. She’s just trying to get on the inside track to getting me into bed. “Joe? Are you okay?” “Always,” I tell her.
zh_text: 然而我無法想像莎莉跟我可以分享什麼秘密。這只是莎莉本來的樣子。只是想要以類似幫我做午餐的方式幫忙照顧我媽，她只是在想辦法要和我上床而已。

en_text: “My mother is as healthy as an ox,” I tell her. “I wouldn’t worry. I have to get back to work, Sally.”
zh_text: 當然，很好。我說。「我最好回去工作，莎莉。」

en_text: “Okay,” she answers, but doesn’t move. She stares at me and I end up staring at the ﬂoor, not wanting to make eye contact with her in case she takes it as a sign to start undressing.
zh_text: 「好。」她應道，不過沒有移動。她凝視著我，而我凝視著地板，不願與她目光接觸，以免她誤解我的意思，開始脫衣服。

en_text: “Can I ask you something personal, Joe?”
zh_text: 「我可以問你一個私人問題嗎，喬？」

en_text: No. “Yes.”
zh_text: 不行。可以。

en_text: “Do you ﬁnd murder fascinating?”
zh_text: 「你對謀殺案有興趣嗎？」

en_text: Yes. “No.”
zh_text: 有。「沒有。」

en_text: “What about the ongoing investigation?”
zh_text: 「正在調查的案件呢？」

en_text: “Which one?”
zh_text: 「哪一件？」

en_text: “The Christchurch Carver.”
zh_text: 「基督城屠夫案。」

en_text: “He must be intelligent.”
zh_text: 「他一定很聰明。」

en_text: “Why do you say that?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你爲什麼這麼認爲？」

en_text: “Because he hasn’t been caught,” I say. “Because he keeps getting away. He must be really smart.” “I guess he must be. Does that interest you?”
zh_text: 「因為他還沒被抓。因為他一直有辦法逃走。他一定非常聰明。」「我想是的。這讓你感興趣嗎？」

en_text: “Have you . . . looked at any of the folders? The photographs of the dead women? Anything like that?” “I’ve seen pictures on the wall in the conference room. That’s all. The pictures are horrible.”
zh_text: 你有……去看那些檔案夾嗎？被害女子的照片？那類的東西？我看過會議室牆壁上的照片。就那些了。那些照片很可怕。

en_text: “If somebody forces you to steal because they’re hurting you, then it isn’t really stealing. And the best thing to do would be to go to the police.”
zh_text: 「如果有人強迫你偷取那些檔案，那並不算是真的偷竊。最好的作法就是報警。」

en_text: I don’t know what leap she’s just made, but it makes no sense at all. She’s rehashing the sort of Christian morality bullshit that somebody has force-fed her. She’s no idea what we’re even talking about now. She could be saying that killing is bad, that vengeance belongs to God, that using his name in vain is bad, that selling your daughter into slavery isn’t frowned upon. All these things are in the Bible and for some reason she thinks we’re debating it. She could easily have just told me that drowning the elderly is bad.
zh_text: 我不知道她怎麼會講成這樣，但是聽起來一點道理也沒有。她在拿別人強行灌輸給她的基督教道德狗屎出來講。她根本不知道我們在講什麼。她可能想說殺人是不好的，復仇屬於上帝，濫用祂的名諱是不好的，將女兒賣給奴隸販子並不是罪。這些都寫在聖經裡，而基於某些理由，她認爲我們在辯論這個。

en_text: “You’re right, Sally. If somebody was forcing you to do something you didn’t want to, that would be bad. The police help people when things happen to them,” but of course they don’t. I can vouch for that. I can even show pictures. Then I start to wonder—is somebody doing something mean to Sally?
zh_text: 「妳說得對，莎莉。如果有人強迫妳做妳不想做的事，那是不好的。警察會幫助遇到這種事情的人。」他們當然不會。我敢保證這一點。我甚至有照片爲證

en_text: She seems to take that as some sort of answer to some half-formed dilemma going on inside her head, because she smiles, tells me she should get back to work, and leaves.
zh_text: 我不知道能說什麼，於是聳了聳肩。她似乎將這個動作視爲腦中某種尚未成型的難題解答，因為她面露微笑，告訴我她該回去工作了，然後離開。

en_text: Sally disappears, but my paranoia remains, my earlier thought that she could have come to my house is enough to make me nauseous. If Sally did come to my house, then I might have to repay the favor. There are things she might have seen, things I might have told her that would mean a visit to her house in the middle of the night would be in order.
zh_text: 莎莉走了，但是我還在疑神疑鬼，光是之前她有可能來過我家的想法就足以令我反胃。如果莎莉真的來過我家，那我或許應該禮尙往來。她可能看到一些東西，一些我或許告訴過她我會在深夜跑去她家造訪的東西。

en_text: I sit on the bunk in the cell I’m cleaning and lean my forehead against the broom handle. Over the following minutes, I slowly convince myself that I’m going crazy. No way could Sally have come around to my apartment. If she had, she wouldn’t be able to shut up about it. She would be asking me how my testicle was. She would think that the very fact that she saw me naked meant we were engaged to be married. Sally is too dimwitted to have helped me, too innocent not to have called the police, too in love with me not to have stayed by my side every minute of the week I was laid up in bed. She’s too many lots of things. And I can’t imagine Sally getting hold of any antibiotics. No, it had to have been Melissa. Which means she is still up to something.
zh_text: 我於正在打掃的拘留室床鋪上坐下，額頭靠著掃帚柄。接下來的幾分鐘內，我慢慢說服自己這種想法太瘋狂了。莎莉絕不可能跑來我家。如果她來過，她不可能不提。她會問我睪丸怎麼樣。她會將看過我的裸體視爲訂婚的象徵。莎莉的智力不足以幫助我，她的天真也一定會讓她打電話報警，而對我的愛則會令她一整個禮拜都待在我的床邊。而且我也無法想像莎莉有辦法取得抗生素。不，一定是梅莉莎。這表示她依然有所圖謀。

en_text: Before lunch I spend twenty minutes in the conference room studying the information and swapping my tapes while I clean the windows and wipe down the blinds. I’m reading statements, studying photographs, making sure nobody is watching me. The sky outside the conference room window is getting darker, and as it does it feels like it’s getting closer, like the world is closing in on me.
zh_text: 午餐前，我在會議室裡待了二十分鐘，趁著清理窗戶、擦百葉窗葉的時候研究案情、更換錄音帶。我閱讀證詞，研究照片，確定沒有人盯上我。

en_text: I discover several local prostitutes have been approached in connection with the deaths. Hmm . . . interesting. Questions have been asked about their clients. Is there anybody who has a bizarre fetish? Somebody who enjoys perverse sexual acts? Somebody abusive with unusual requests? It’s a feeble and wasted effort. They’re hoping that at some point in my life I’ve vented my sexual aspirations on a whore. I’d never do that. I mean, I’d never do that and keep one alive.
zh_text: 我發現警方偵訊了數名本地妓女。哼……有趣。他們問了些關於她們顧客的問題。有沒有人有奇特的性癖好？喜歡變態性行爲？具有不尋常的虐待傾向？這是一項浪費人力的舉動。他們期望我會在生命中某個時間點上去找妓女發洩性慾。我從不曾這麼做過。我的意思是，我從來不曾在這麼做之後還留下活口。

en_text: The prostitutes have provided a list to the police. An extremely short list. Not many names and, so far, not many leads.
zh_text: 妓女提供了一份名單給警方。非常短的名單。沒有幾個名字，而截至目前爲止，沒有什麼線索。

en_text: Before my workday ends, I successfully get four color photographs, one each of the four men on my list. Schroder and McCoy each have recent photographs in their ﬁles, but it’s a struggle to get current pictures for the other two—until I realize they’ve most likely been photographed by journalists and cameramen over the last few weeks. While I vacuum a room upstairs, I use the Internet and search through newspaper sites until I ﬁnd pictures of a high enough standard I can print out.
zh_text: 一天的工作結束前，我成功地取得了四張彩色照片，我名單上的嫌犯一人一張。施羅德和麥考伊的檔案裡都有近期照片，不過要弄另外兩個傢伙的近期照片就不是那麼容易了——直到我發現他們很可能在過去幾個禮拜裡讓記者和攝影師拍過照片。趁著清理樓上一個房間的時候，我使用網路搜尋新聞網站，找到符合標準的照片列印出來。

en_text: When I leave work Sally offers me a lift home along with the chance to talk about my mother, and I decline. I forgo my usual bus, and stop at a bank and draw out some cash, ﬁguring I’m going to need it over the next few nights. Melissa took all the cash I was using a few weeks ago, along with my ATM card. Stepping into the bank is like stepping into a small nature reserve. With a few ﬂoor-to-ceiling potted plants brightly lit under the glare of halogen lights, and several small ones crammed into most available spaces, it wouldn’t be a surprise if there were wild animals living in here. Standing in a line from the counter to the wall is a line of people I don’t want to join, but I have no choice. We stand waiting together without daring to make conversation because if any of us did, we’d look like freaks. Eventually the line shufﬂes forward a few times, and I make it to the teller. She is a tall, masculine woman with large hands who smiles at me a lot, but no amount of smiling would ever get me to sneak through her front door late at night.
zh_text: 下班的時候，莎莉說要開車送我，不過被我拒絕。我放棄常搭的公車，前往銀行提領一筆現金，因為今晚可能會需要用到。步入銀行感覺像是步入一塊自然保育區。裡面有幾棵碰到天花板的高大盆栽，由鹵素燈以及其他較小型的燈光提供充足的光線，給人一種就算有野生動物住在裡面也不會令人驚訝的感覺。從櫃檯到牆壁之間站了一排我不打算加入的隊伍，不過我沒得選擇。我們排排站好，不敢交談，因為一旦交談，我們就會看起來像是怪人。隊伍前進了幾次，我終於來到出納員面前。她是個身材高壯的女人，手很大，一直對我笑，不過不管笑成怎樣都不能讓我晚上溜入她家大門。

en_text: From the bank I walk over the road to a supermarket, since most of the food in my house has expired. I walk around, allowing myself to limp slightly now that I’m away from work. It seems strange being here, as if I’ve slipped into a slice of life that I shouldn’t be allowed in, as if the supermarket for serial killers and men who have been assaulted with pliers is the supermarket down the road next to the deli. I stare at beautiful women as I shop, and I begin to feel ill. These women would laugh at me if I attacked them. They would call me Numb Nuts, or maybe even One Nut.
zh_text: 離開銀行後，我穿越馬路前往超級市場，因為我家大部分的食物都過期了。我逛了逛，由於已經遠離工作場所，所以我容許自己跛腳走路。來這裡感覺很奇怪，彷彿我滑入了一個不該允許我進入的生活，彷彿專爲連續殺人魔以及被鉗子夾爆睾丸的男人而設的超級市場就在街尾的熱食店旁。我一邊購物一邊欣賞美女，接著我開始感到不適。如果我襲擊這些美女，她們將會嘲笑我。他們會叫我「麻痺蛋蛋」，或甚至是「獨蛋人」。

en_text: The girl working the checkout smiles at me and asks how my day is going. I want to unzip my ﬂy and show her just how okay it’s going. I’m angry as hell. The left one was my favorite.
zh_text: 我以現金付款，因為我從來沒有辦過信用卡。付帳櫃檯的女孩對我微笑，問我今天過得如何。我很想拉下褲子拉鍊，讓她看看我今天過得如何。我氣炸了。我最喜歡左邊那顆了。

en_text: I climb on the bus and the bumpy bus ride threatens to tear my testicle open. When I reach home it takes me ﬁve minutes to climb the stairs. Much harder than climbing down them. I enter my apartment. The light on the answering machine is ﬂashing. A sliver of sunlight arcs through the window as part of the sky clears up. At least the place doesn’t smell of disinfectant and stale piss. I can smell the food that has started to go off, though. I open a window before throwing out the old food and replacing it with the new. I sit down on the sofa and try to relax, to regain some energy. Pickle and Jehovah swim for me after they swallow every grain of ﬁsh food in sight.
zh_text: 我上了公車，顛簸的旅程差點再度撕裂我的陰囊。回家時，我花了五分鐘才爬上樓梯。上樓比下樓困難多了。我進入我的公寓，答錄機的小燈在閃。一道陽光自窗口灑入。至少空氣裡沒有消毒水和積尿的味道。我可以聞到食物開始腐敗。我打開一扇窗戶，丟出之前的食物，然後拿剛買的食物取代。我坐在沙發上，試圖放鬆精神，恢復活力。泡菜和耶和華在吃完觸目所及所有飼料之後游泳給我欣賞。

en_text: I push play on the answering machine, fearful of what Mom will have to say, but it’s the woman from the vet. Jennifer. And she has good news, and good news is something I haven’t had in a while. She tells me the cat has made a full recovery. The owners haven’t contacted them. She wants to know exactly where I found poor little puss, wants to know if I know anybody who wants a cat. Tells me to call her when I get in tonight. She’ll be at work until two o’clock.
zh_text: 我按下答錄機上的播放鈕，戰戰兢兢地聽我媽打來說些什麼，結果是獸醫的那個女人打來的。珍妮佛。她告訴我那隻貓已經痊癒了。貓主人沒有跟他們聯絡。她想知道我究竟是在哪裡撿到那隻可憐的貓咪，想知道我認不認識任何想要養貓的人。請我今晚回家後跟她聯絡。她兩點之前都還待在診所。

en_text: Do I want a damn cat? Not really, but I’ve become somewhat responsible for it. I wonder if I could give the thing to Mom. It would keep her company. Might mean she won’t feel the need to call me every two minutes to ask why I don’t love her. Hell, she can even cook the ﬂuffy bastard meatloaf every day.
zh_text: 我想養隻可惡的貓咪嗎？不特別想，不過我似乎必須對牠肩負起一些責任。我考慮能不能把貓交給老媽。牠可以陪伴她。或許能讓她不要每兩分鐘就想打電話來問我爲什麼不愛她。見鬼了，她甚至可以每天幫這隻毛茸茸的混蛋做烤肉餅。

en_text: Only she would think I was somehow trying to kill her—the cat would give her allergies, or would suffocate her during the night, or pour rat poison into her coffee.
zh_text: 可惜她一定會認爲我送貓給她是爲了要害死她——貓可能讓她過敏，或在晚上掐死她，或是在她的咖啡裡添加老鼠藥。

en_text: After four rings, Jennifer answers, and her voice suddenly takes on an excitable tone when I identify myself. She explains in her seductive voice everything she already explained on the answering machine. She makes cat surgery sound sexy. She wants to know if I want to keep the cat, the whole time sounding as though she is only a step away from asking me if I’ll sleep with her. I tell her I’ll think about the cat and contact her tomorrow night. We wish each other a good night and hang up. I’m expecting her to say No, you hang up ﬁrst, and when she doesn’t it makes me a little sad.
zh_text: 響四聲後，珍妮佛接起電話，並且在我表明身分後語氣變得興奮起來。她以其性感誘人的聲音把剛剛在答錄機中解釋過的東西通通解釋一遍。她讓貓咪手術聽起來十分性感。她想知道我願不願意收養那隻貓，過程中始終給我一種接下來就要問我要不要跟她上床的感覺。我問她如果我不收養的話，他們會如何處置那隻貓。她說牠會被送往動物收留所。我沒問她收留所會如何對待貓。我說我願意收養，她說世界上如果多點像我這種人的話一定會變得更加美好。我們互道晚安，然後掛斷。我以為她會說：「不要，你先掛。」謝天謝地，她沒這麼說。

en_text: At six o’clock, I arrive at Mom’s. We make the sort of conversation that makes me wonder how the hell she really could be my mother. We eat dinner, and then I have to watch her do some of her jigsaw puzzle for thirty minutes before we catch up with her soap-opera friends. I feel violently ill and manage to excuse myself from Mom and her Monday night and, amid the complaints of how I never treat her right, I make my way outside.
zh_text: 六點時，我抵達老媽家。我們展開了一段讓我懷疑她怎麼可能是我媽的交談。我們共進晚餐，然後我看著她玩了三十分鐘拼圖，接著才跟她的肥皂劇朋友敘舊。我感覺非常不舒服，於是跟老媽和她的禮拜一夜晚道別，在那陣我都不對她好的抱怨聲中離開她家。夜深了，一陣毛毛雨讓四周變得有點霧茫茫的感覺。

en_text: It’s starting to rain. I catch a bus back into town, keeping my hand on my briefcase the entire journey, staring out the window as fat drops of rain smash against it, the attack lasting only ﬁve minutes. I take a detour past Daniela Walker’s house and she doesn’t seem to mind. Two blocks away I steal a car. It’s nearly ten o’clock when I reach Manchester Street, armed with photographs and cash. Hookers are walking the streets, some starting work, others back from ten- or ﬁfteen-minute gigs sitting in parked cars in dark alleyways. In the back of my mind I keep asking myself whether this is a valid line of investigation. It didn’t work for the police. Why would it work for me? For a start, I have photographs to show them. The detectives didn’t. Prostitutes probably need visual stimulation to jog their memories. I watch as two of them get into a shoving match, which is broken up by a third, then a moment later it’s hugs all around. Within a minute all three have been picked up by three different cars, making me think their ﬁght was a show for the kind of people who like picking up hair-pulling, palmslapping girls. I forgo the massage parlors where the women are monitored by violent men with dirty money and bad reputations. The men who frequent them, if not regulars, are caught on surveillance or, at the very least, remembered.
zh_text: 我搭乘公車回市區，全程手都放在公事包上。我繞路前往丹妮耶拉·沃克家，她似乎並不介意。我在兩條街口外偷了一輛車。快十點的時候，我帶著照片和現金來到曼徹斯特街。街上到處都是阻街女郎，有些開始上工，有些則剛從停在陰暗巷道中的車輛裡結束一段工作回來。內心深處，我一直在問我自己來這裡查案到底是不是浪費時間。警方在這裡一無所獲。憑什麼我就查得到線索？首先，我有照片可以拿來問人。那些警探沒有。妓女們可能需要視覺刺激才能喚回記憶。

en_text: This isn’t the kind of place a policeman visits unless he’s swapping sex for leniency. The other factor I have to consider is the availability of women prepared to be paid to live out the perverted fantasy of the killer. That sort of thing doesn’t happen in parlors without a lot of people knowing about it. A policeman doesn’t want a lot of people knowing about it. He doesn’t want repercussions such as blackmail and extortion. The ﬁrst hooker I talk to has a deep voice that’s almost scary. I don’t get a name from her and don’t want one. Even after I’ve identiﬁed myself as a policeman, she still asks me if I want to fuck her. I say no. She shows me some nipple, and I still say no. Even if my testicles were intact I wouldn’t put them near her. She doesn’t recognize any of the photos.
zh_text: 我跳過有聲名狼藉的暴力分子監控妓女的按摩廳。在那種地方，所有男人不光只有熟客，都會被監視器錄下來，或至少有人記得長相。這裡不是警察會來的地方，除非他打算將性當作交換條件。我還必須考慮到有多少女人願意收錢滿足兇手的變態性幻想。這種事情在按摩廳裡是瞞不住的。他可不想引來勒索敲詐。我遇上的第一個妓女聲音低沉到令我害怕。我沒從她口中問出消息，也不想問出消息。即使在我表示自己是警察後，她依然問我要不要幹她。我說不要。她露出乳頭，我還是不要。就算我的睪丸完整無缺，我還是不會讓它們去接近她。她不認得任何照片上的男人。

en_text: The second hooker doesn’t either. At this point I’m deciding not to say I’m a policeman, but a concerned citizen, and she asks me anyway if I’m a cop. She wears a red wig large enough to conceal a small handbag.
zh_text: 第一名妓女也不認得。這時我決定不要自稱警察，當個關心此案的好市民就好了。她頭上戴著一頂大到足以藏下小皮包的紅色假髮。

en_text: I go from slut to whore, hooker to skank, showing them the pictures and getting no helpful response from any of them. My ball starts throbbing as I walk from corner to corner. Of the prostitutes I talk to, none deﬁnitely recognizes any of the four men. Some of them ﬁnd it hard to remember. I give them money, and it doesn’t help. I’m having a bad run. The handgun. The knife. Now I’m paying for information that I’m not even getting, and getting wet in the process.
zh_text: 我從私娼問到妓女、阻街女郎問到舞小姐，拿照片給她們看，不過沒有得到任何有用的回應。我走過許多街角，睪丸開始抽痛。我問過的妓女中沒人見過那四個警探。有些妓女宣稱記性不好，我給了她們錢，不過沒有幫助。我最近運氣不佳。槍沒了，刀沒了。如今我還爲了得不到的資訊東奔西跑。

en_text: Monday night is less than an hour from Tuesday when my luck starts to change.
zh_text: 在禮拜一晚上剩下不到一個小時就要變成禮拜一早上的時候，我的運氣開始轉變了。

en_text: I encounter two prostitutes who I believe actually do recognize one of the four photographs, silencing the small voice in the back of my mind telling me this was a waste of time. It speaks again, though, when each of the two women recognizes a different picture.
zh_text: 我遇上了兩名我相信真的認得四張照片上其中一張裡的男人的妓女，終於讓我腦中那個說我是在浪費時間的聲音沉寂下去。不過當這兩名妓女認出的照片是不一樣的時候，那個聲音又再度發聲。

en_text: The ﬁrst woman, Candy (that’s right—sixty hookers, maybe seven names), points to the photo of Detective Inspector Schroder. Carl. I can’t be sure she isn’t just recognizing him from being interviewed last week for the same reasons. For only four hundred dollars, Candy will show me what she let Schroder do to her.
zh_text: 第一名女子，坎蒂（沒錯——六十個妓女大概只有七個名字）宣稱見過施羅德偵緝督察。我無法肯定她是不是在上禮拜施羅德爲了同樣的理由前來偵詢時見過他的。只要四百塊錢，坎蒂就會讓我見識一下她讓施羅德對她做的事情。

en_text: The second woman, Becky, points to one of the out-of-town cops. Detective Calhoun. From Auckland. Robert. I ask what he’d wanted. She says for two grand, I can ﬁnd out. Two thousand dollars compared with four hundred. I ﬁgure for a street hooker to claim two grand for a performance it has to be one hell of a repertoire.
zh_text: 第一名女子，貝琪，認出外來警探之一。卡爾霍恩警探。來自奧克蘭。我問他來做什麼。她說她要兩千塊才告訴我。兩千塊跟四百塊。我想讓一個阻街女郎索價兩千塊的怪癖一定很有看頭。

en_text: Two grand. Sure. Why not. I have the money.
zh_text: 兩千塊。當然。有何不可？我有兩千塊。

en_text: I walk Becky to my car and drive her to the Walker residence. I was here earlier in the evening, just after I stole the car. I removed the police tape from inside and hid away any evidence markers. I checked at work today to see if the house was still under surveillance. The answer was no. I open the door and the smell hits me again. The place needs some fresh air.
zh_text: 我領著貝琪上了我的車，開車前往沃克家。稍早的時候我曾來過這裡一趟，就在我偷車前。我扯掉屋內的警方封條，藏起所有證物牌。我今天上班的時候確認過警方有沒有監視這裡，答案是否定的。我打開房門，臭味再度來襲。這地方需要新鮮空氣。

en_text: Becky doesn’t mention the smell. Perhaps she doesn’t notice.
zh_text: 貝琪沒有提起臭味。或許她沒有聞到。

en_text: We walk into the kitchen and make small conversation as I offer her a drink, then I remember I’ve taken all the beer already. I open the fridge and it’s been cleaned out, all the expired food has gone, just empty shelves now.
zh_text: 我們來到廚房。我一邊聊天一邊拿飲料給她喝。

en_text: “Just water,” Becky says, and I feel relief. Becky looks like she’s in her early twenties, but I imagine her life has given her the maturity of somebody twice her age. She has black hair that is completely straight and hangs over her shoulders. Her eyes are slightly bloodshot, but in them ﬂicker the signs of a sad intelligence. They’re pale green and look like they’d make a nice set of marbles. She’s wearing a tight, black, short leather miniskirt. Knee-high leather boots. No bra, and a dark red camisole does little to hide her ﬁrm breasts. She wears a thin, black leather jacket that rides up her back and has about a million tassels hanging from it. I like the touch of irony in the small silver cruciﬁx hanging around her neck. The selection of cheap jewelry across her ﬁngers looks plastic. Her diamond studs are cubic zirconia or possibly even glass. She has a small handbag that’s probably full of condoms, money, and tissues.
zh_text: 貝琪看起來像是二十出頭，不過我猜她的人生歷練已經讓她跟兩倍歲數的人一樣成熟。她留著一頭黑色的直髮，垂在肩膀上。她的雙眼有點充血，不過隱現著一股悲哀的智慧之光。眼珠是淡綠色的，看來像美麗的彈珠。她身穿一件緊身黑色迷你裙，及膝的皮靴，沒穿內衣，深紅色的小可愛完全遮不住她堅挺的乳房。黑皮薄夾克上大概垂有一百萬條流蘇。我很欣賞掛在她脖子上的小十字架流露出來的諷刺意味。她手指上的廉價珠寶看起來像是塑膠做的。戒指上的鑽石大概是方晶鋯石，也有可能是玻璃。她的小手提袋裡多半裝滿了保險套、現金以及面紙。

en_text: My legs are sore from walking around and, more importantly, my crotch is killing me. I sit down at the kitchen table opposite her and slowly start drinking from a glass of water. As requested earlier, I open my wallet and produce two thousand dollars in cash. I’d withdrawn three grand from the bank. Right now, I hand two-thirds of it over to Becky.
zh_text: 我走得腳都痠了，而且更重要的是，我的胯下痛得要命。我在她的對面坐下，緩緩喝著我的啤酒。如同之前要求，我打開皮夾，取出兩千塊現金。我在銀行提了三千塊。此刻我拿了三分之二的現金給貝琪。

en_text: I ﬁgure I’ll be getting it back.
zh_text: 反正我會拿回來。

en_text: She sits opposite me and, while drinking her water, she counts through the money twice, as if she thinks she’s being ripped off. I watch her face as she studies each of the notes. Her lips are moving as she counts. A smile ﬂickers across her mouth. I’ve already paid her, and she hasn’t done a thing yet. I can see her thinking she’ll shorten her version of the erotica she possibly shared with Detective Robert Calhoun. I can also see her already spending it. She’s thinking about taking the week off, or buying a trip to Fiji.
zh_text: 她坐在我對面，一邊喝啤酒一邊數錢，還數兩次，好像我在搶劫一樣。我看著她細看每一張鈔票。她數錢的時候嘴唇微動。臉上露出一絲微笑。我已經付錢了，而她什麼都還沒做。我看得出她在考慮縮短她可能跟羅伯特·卡爾霍恩警探幹過的風流事。我同時也看到她已經開始花這些錢了。她在考慮休假一個禮拜，或是去斐濟旅遊。

en_text: “Shall we?” I ask.
zh_text: 「可以開始了嗎？」我問。

en_text: She takes her jacket off. “You want to do it here?”
zh_text: 她脫下夾克。「你要在這裡做？」

en_text: “Upstairs.”
zh_text: 「樓上。」

en_text: I pick up my briefcase and walk upstairs. At the top I head for the master bedroom then stop, turn back, and head for the kids’ bedroom instead. “Hot up here,” she says.
zh_text: 我拿起公事包，朝樓上走去。上樓後，我走向主臥室，停下腳步，轉頭走向小孩的房間。「上面好熱。」她說。

en_text: “I hadn’t noticed.”
zh_text: 「我沒注意到。」

en_text: I walk into the children’s bedroom.
zh_text: 我步入小孩房間。

en_text: “In here?” she asks, tossing her handbag onto the ﬁrst of two single beds.
zh_text: 「在這裡？」她問，將手提袋丟在兩張單人床的第一張上。

en_text: “You need more room?”
zh_text: 「妳需要更大的空間嗎？」

en_text: She shakes her head. “Kind of kinky.”
zh_text: 她搖頭。「有點變態。」

en_text: “Kind of,” I agree.
zh_text: 有一點。我同意。

en_text: Here will be good for two reasons. First, I want some variety with this house. Life is a routine and all that stuff. Second, the smell of death isn’t embedded in the sheets.
zh_text: 在這裡做有兩個理由。第一，我希望這間房子有點變化。人生充滿了太多一成不變的事物。一，這裡的床單沒有沾染死亡氣味。

en_text: We sit down on opposite beds. She begins by leaning back so I can see up her skirt. She’s wearing no underwear for quick access.
zh_text: 我們面對面坐在兩張床上。她一開始先向後躺下，讓我看見她的裙底。她爲了方便起見而沒穿內褲。

en_text: “What can you tell me about him?” I ask.
zh_text: 「聊聊那個男的吧？」我問。

en_text: “Who?”
“The man in the photograph.”
zh_text: 「照片上的男人。」

en_text: “What do you want to know?” “Everything.”
zh_text: 「你想知道什麼？」「都想知道。」

en_text: She shrugs. Looks disappointed, though I don’t know why. Wouldn’t she rather be paid for talking than acting?
zh_text: 她聳肩。表情有點失望，我看不出原因。收錢聊天不是比較好嗎？

en_text: “Well, he paid me two thousand dollars to let him do pretty much what he wanted.” “Two grand buys that?”
zh_text: 好吧，他付了兩千塊給我讓他爲所欲爲。「兩千塊就能爲所欲爲了？」

en_text: “Two grand will buy a lot, honey.”
zh_text: 「兩千塊可以買到很多東西，蜜糖。」

en_text: I guess it does. “How often have you seen him?”
zh_text: 我想想也對。「妳見過他幾次？」

en_text: “Just the once.”
zh_text: 一次而已。

en_text: “When?”
zh_text: 「什麼時候？」

en_text: “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」

en_text: “Well, think.”
zh_text: 想一想。

en_text: “Could have been a month ago. Maybe two.”
zh_text: 「可能是一個月前。也可能兩個月。」

en_text: For a woman like this, time doesn’t have too big a meaning. She probably has a baby back at home, being looked after by some drug-infested friend who has got off the game but is too damn lazy to make the effort to get her friend off too. Becky will be spending her money on cigarettes and weed, and she’ll be sitting back in one of her tie-dyed dresses, smoking in front of the baby. She’ll be girlfriended to three or four guys—each with criminal convictions for burglary, drug possession, and assault. There’ll be bruises on her thighs that will never heal, but the pain is masked by the drugs. She’ll have no long-term goals other than to stay alive and stay inside a drug-afﬂicted world. To wake from the nightmare she lives in would be to wake to a reality that as a little girl she never believed could exist. Life wasn’t supposed to be like this. She was her daddy’s little princess.
zh_text: 對這種女人而言，時間不一定具有多大的意義。她可能家裡有個小孩，交給已經戒毒但是懶得花費心力幫助她一起戒毒的朋友照顧。貝琪會把這筆錢花在香菸和大麻上，然後她會穿著紮染的洋裝在自己的小孩面前抽。她會當三到四個男人的女友——每個都有竊盜、藏毒，以及傷害前科。她的大腿上會有瘀傷，而且永遠不會癒合，不過毒品倒是可以減輕痛苦。她沒有任何長期目標，除了不要死以及繼續待在充滿毒品的世界裡。自她所存在的惡夢中甦醒過來就等於是讓她進入一個小時候絕對無法相信真實存在的世界。人生不應該是這個樣子，她是爹地的小公主。

en_text: I know these people. They’re of no use to the community other than to take up space. They spit out babies, not because they can’t afford contraception when their welfare checks go toward getting high, but because with every baby that comes along they receive another one of those government subsidies that’s never enough to raise a kid properly. This is Becky’s world. Some just can’t escape, or don’t know what to escape to. I wonder if she even knows she’s trapped there.
zh_text: 我了解這種人。他們除了浪費空間外，對於社會一點用處都沒有。他們會生小孩，不過不是因為他們的救濟金無法支付避孕費用，而是因為多生一個小孩就能多領一份絕不足以養活小孩的政府補助。這就是貝琪的世界。有些人永遠無法逃離，或是不知道能夠逃往何處。我很好奇她到底知不知道自己被困在那裡。

en_text: Tonight I’m going to offer her an escape from the pain of life. That’s my humanity.
zh_text: 今晚我將提供一條逃離痛苦人生的出路。這就是我的人性。

en_text: The children’s bedroom has all that happy jolly stuff I never had as a kid. Posters of cartoon characters are stapled to the walls; they chase each other with stupid smiles and homosexual gestures. Even the bedspreads can’t just be normal. They too have characters running across them, frozen in a moment of excitement. The clock radio on the small blue desk is in the shape of a clown. The eyes move back and forth, counting the minutes that have passed since the occupants of this room lost their mother. But the clown doesn’t know it. He’s still smiling, his bright red lips almost the same shade as Becky’s, his eyes looking back and forth, back and forth, searching for something he’ll never ﬁnd. Colorful toys are scattered across the ﬂoor. Stuffed teddy bears look like they have been massacred by toy soldiers, their bodies dumped in this battleﬁeld of chaos. Piles of plastic board games are stacked in one corner. One is open on the ﬂoor and the pieces inside are strewn over the carpet. A bookcase containing more toys than books is pushed against the wall.
zh_text: 小孩的房間裡有著各式各樣我小時候見都沒見過的歡樂飾品。牆上釘著卡通人物的海報；他們以愚蠢的微笑和同性戀般的姿勢相互追逐。就連床罩都不能用正常點的。它們上面也有卡通人物在跑跑跳跳，凍結在興奮的時刻裡。小藍書桌上的鬧鈴收音機是小丑形狀的。它的眼睛會前後轉動，計算著打從房間主人失去母親至今過了多少時間。不過小丑並不知道這一點。他還在微笑，鮮紅色的嘴唇幾乎跟貝琪一模一樣，他的眼睛前後轉動，尋找著某樣永遠找不到的東西。地板上散落形形色色的玩具。填充泰迪熊看來像是被玩具兵屠殺過一樣，屍體被棄置在這座混亂的戰場上。牆角堆了一疊棋盤遊戲。其中一盒打開擺在地上，裡面的棋子攤落一地。一座玩具比書多的書櫃貼牆而立。

en_text: The main colors of the room are blue and light pink. Relaxing colors, or so they believe. They’ve spent thousands of dollars on case studies to prove this. Happy colors mean happy kids. As a kid, I had gray walls in my room. Put a poster up, and I got grounded. Yet look how happy I am. I could have saved those researchers all that money if they’d come to me ﬁrst.
zh_text: 房間主要的配色是藍色與粉紅色。愉快的顏色，至少他們是這麼相信的。他們花了好幾千塊錢去研究證明這一點。快樂的顏色表示會有快樂的小孩。我小時候牆壁是灰色的。只要貼上一張海報，我就被禁足了。但看看我現在過得多愉快？如果那些研究員先來問我的話，我就可以幫他們省下一大筆錢。

en_text: “You think you last saw him two months ago?” I ask, conﬁrming her guess. “Yeah. I suppose so.”
zh_text: 「妳認爲最後一次見到他是兩個月前？」我問，肯定她的說詞。「是。我想沒錯。」

en_text: “Thought you’d remember a client who was paying two thousand dollars.”
zh_text: 「我以爲妳會記得一個付妳兩千塊的客人。」

en_text: She shrugs. “Go ﬁgure. I remember the money more than anything else.”
zh_text: 她聳肩。「自己去想吧。我比較記得錢，不太記得人。」

en_text: “What was his name?” “His name? What’s in a name?”
zh_text: 「他叫什麼名字？」

en_text: “Everything,” I say, wondering if she’s trying to quote Shakespeare. I decide I can’t credit her with that intelligence, and chalk it up as a ﬂuke. Still, I ﬁnd it unsettling. Could a whore actually be that clever?
zh_text: 「代表一切。」我說，不知道她是不是在引用莎士比亞的台詞。我認爲她沒有足夠的智力這麼做，決定將其歸類爲巧合。儘管如此，我還是覺得這點令我不安。妓女有可能這麼聰明嗎？

en_text: She shrugs. “He didn’t tell me.”
zh_text: 她聳肩。「他沒告訴我。」

en_text: “What did he tell you?”
zh_text: 「他告訴了妳什麼？」

en_text: “Just what he wanted.”
zh_text: 只有他想幹什麼。

en_text: “And what was that?”
zh_text: 「他想幹什麼？」

en_text: She tells me. It’s so graphic I nearly blush. “And you gave him that for two grand?”
zh_text: 「是啊。」她說給我聽。描述得生動寫實，聽得我差點臉紅。「兩千塊就能讓妳做那種事？」

en_text: “Yeah.” Can’t quite discern if that had been a bargain or not. What I do understand is the similarity between this encounter and the death of Daniela Walker. Same signature.
zh_text: 我眞的難以判斷這樁買賣値不值得。不過我倒是知道此事與丹妮耶拉·沃克之死有很多相似之處。同樣的簽名特徵。

en_text: “Where did he take you?”
zh_text: 「他在哪裡上妳？」

en_text: “I thought I just explained all that.”
zh_text: 「我以為我已經解釋清楚了。」

en_text: I shake my head. “I mean did he take you back to his house, or to your house, or to a motel room, or what?” “Oh, that. Well, it was a motel room. We don’t usually go to the john’s house.”
zh_text: 我搖頭。「我的意思是他帶妳回家，還是去妳家，還是去汽車旅館，還是哪裡？」「喔，那個。好吧，是間汽車旅館。我們通常不去客人家。」

en_text: “Can you remember the motel?”
zh_text: 「妳記得是哪間汽車旅館嗎？」

en_text: “Some seedy joint across town. The Everblue. Heard of it?”
zh_text: 「很遠的一間破爛旅館。長藍汽車旅館。有聽過嗎？」

en_text: I nod. Never been there, but driven by it a few times. “He booked a room while you were there?” “No. He already had one. We drove straight there and went directly to his room.”
zh_text: 我點頭。沒去過，不過有開車經過幾次。「他是去了才登記房間的嗎？」不。他已經有房間了。我們開到旅館，然後直接進房。

en_text: “Was he living there?”
zh_text: 「他是住在那裡嗎？」

en_text: “Huh?”
“Did you see any suitcases? Any extra clothes?”
zh_text: 「妳有看到行李箱嗎？有多餘的衣服嗎？」

en_text: “No, but I wasn’t looking for any.”
zh_text: 「沒有，不過我沒刻意去看。」

en_text: I ﬁgure he wasn’t staying there. The Everblue is a dive that charges for rooms by the hour, not overnight, just for people like Becky and her colleagues. Becky seems eager to tell me more now. Before she was defensive, guarded about everything. Now she senses she’s going to make two grand for talking, and after her candid explanation of the perverse sex Calhoun ordered, she has no reason to hold back.
zh_text: 我認爲他不是住在那裡。長藍是間以小時計費的休息旅館，不是過夜用的，專爲貝琪和她的同事這種人而設。如今貝琪似乎很想多告訴我一點了。之前她防禦心很重，對我處處提防。如今她察覺可以靠聊天就賺入兩千塊，而在坦率描述卡爾霍恩要求的變態性行爲後，她已經沒有什麼好隱瞞的了。

en_text: “Where did he pick you up?”
zh_text: 「他在哪裡找上妳的？」

en_text: “Same place you did.”
zh_text: 「跟你同樣的地方。」

en_text: “Anybody else around?”
zh_text: 「當時附近還有其他人嗎？」

en_text: “Nobody.”
zh_text: 「沒有。」

en_text: “Pimp?”
zh_text: 「皮條客？」

en_text: “Are you a cop or something?”
zh_text: 你是警察還是什麼其他人物？

en_text:
It is a question I can see she was tempted to ask immediately. Her greed stopped her then, but now that she has the money, and perhaps a switchblade in her purse to protect it, she can ask whatever she wants.
“Or something.”
zh_text:
我看得出來這個問題她早就想問了。不過貪婪阻止了她。如今錢已到手，她皮包裡或許還擺了把防身用的彈簧刀，她可以問我任何問題。
「我是其他人物。」

en_text: “If you’re a cop, this is entrapment.”
zh_text: 「如果你是警察，這就算是誘捕。」

en_text: Great. A Goddamn scholar. “I’m not a cop.”
zh_text: 太好了。天殺的學者。「我不是警察。」

en_text: She doesn’t look disappointed or relieved at this confession. “Are you going to have sex with me or what?” “Not sure yet.”
zh_text: 聽我這樣說，她沒有露出失望或是鬆懈的表情。「你到底要不要做？」「還不確定。」

en_text: “’Cause I should be charging you extra for these questions.”
zh_text: 「因為問這些問題應該要多收錢。」

en_text: “Fine. Two grand for the answers. If I want sex, I’ll pay normal rates.” She seems happy with this.
zh_text: 「好。兩千塊就當是問題費。如果想做，我就會按照公定價付費。」她似乎很滿意。

en_text: “So, did your pimp see him?” I ask.
zh_text: 所以，妳的皮條客有看到他嗎？

en_text: “I don’t have a pimp.”
zh_text: 「我沒有皮條客。」

en_text: “You serious?”
zh_text: 「當眞？」

en_text: “Yeah. Used to, but he was pretty violent.”
zh_text: 「是啊。以前有，但是他太暴力了。」

en_text: “I thought girls without pimps got hassled by the girls that do have them,” I say, but to be honest I don’t really have any understanding of the pimp-whore world, only what I’ve seen on TV.
zh_text: 「我以爲有皮條客撐腰的女孩會找其他女孩麻煩。」

en_text: “This guy was worse than the girls.”
zh_text: 「這傢伙比那些女孩更麻煩。」

en_text: “So nobody knows you went with him?”
zh_text: 所以沒人知道妳跟他走了？

en_text: “Just him, me, and God.”
zh_text: 只有他、我，和上帝。

en_text: God. Huh. I ﬁnd it interesting she mentions Him. Like He would take the time to look over a piece of trash like her. Like anybody would take the time. Yet she wears the cruciﬁx around her neck because she is a Godluvin’ Christian. It doesn’t make sense. The good news is she’s just told me that only God and I know she’s here.
zh_text: 上帝。呃。我沒想到她竟然會提到上帝。好像祂會把時間浪費在像她這種垃圾身上。好像任何人會把時間浪費在她身上一樣。儘管如此，她脖子上依然掛著十字架，因為她是個熱愛上帝的基督徒。這實在沒有道理可言。好消息是她剛剛告訴我只有上帝和我知道她在這裡。

en_text: “So you got no name at all from him.”
zh_text: 所以他沒有告訴過妳他的名字？

en_text: “Listen, honey, nobody gives me names, and those who do are lying. Apart from that, names and faces I forget. It’s the sex I remember, and only then if it’s something out of the ordinary. Which this was.”
zh_text: 「聽著，蜜糖，沒人告訴過我名字，就算有也都是假名。再說，我不記得名字和長相。我只記得做的過程。」

en_text: “Is there anything you can tell me about him? Type of car? Where he dropped you off? Anything at all that might help?”
zh_text: 「妳可以提供任何細節嗎？他開什麼車？把妳送到哪裡？任何有幫助的東西。」

en_text: “Help what? Why are you looking for this guy?”
zh_text: 「幫助什麼？你找這傢伙想幹嘛？」

en_text: “I’d think for two grand, only I should be asking the questions.”
zh_text: 「我認爲看在兩千塊的份上，應該只有我能問問題。」

en_text: “Whatever.”
zh_text: 「隨便你。」

en_text: “So, can you remember the car?”
zh_text: 「那妳記得他開什麼車嗎？」

en_text: “Sort of. It was nice. Late model.”
zh_text: 「有點印象。好車。新款。」

en_text: “That’s pretty detailed.”
zh_text: 「描述得眞仔細。」

en_text: “Don’t be a smart-ass.”
zh_text: 「別跟我耍嘴皮子。」

en_text: “You think it was a sports car?”
zh_text: 「妳認爲是跑車嗎？」

en_text: “No. A sedan. I remember thinking he was going to want me to blow him in the backseat.” “Did you?”
zh_text: 「不。轎車。我還記得我原先以爲他要我在後座幫他口交。」「妳有嗎？」

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「沒有。」

en_text: “What about the front seat?”
zh_text: 「前座有嗎？」

en_text: It really doesn’t. “What color car?”
zh_text: 「什麼顏色的車？」「不記得。不過那車不是他的。」「喔？」

en_text: “Can’t remember. It was dark. What I remember most is how the sex was so violent and strange, and afterward he was real nice to me.”
zh_text: 他沒有送我回城，而是送我回家。那感覺很奇怪。我們做的時候很暴力、很詭異，但是完事之後他卻對我很好。

en_text: I can imagine. “Did you let him drop you back off at home?”
zh_text: 我可以想像。「妳有讓他送妳回家嗎？」

en_text: “Shit, no. I didn’t want a sicko like that knowing where I lived. I got him to drop me off at an apartment complex and waited for him to go before ﬁnally going home.”
zh_text: 「見鬼了，當然沒有。我可不想讓那種變態知道我住哪裡。我讓他在一間公寓外放我下車，等他離開之後才回家。」

en_text: “How much did he hurt you?”
zh_text: 「妳傷得多重？」

en_text: She shrugs. “I’ve been hurt before.”
zh_text: 她聳肩。「我以前就被打傷過。」

en_text: “How much?”
zh_text: 「多嚴重？」

en_text: “I couldn’t walk home, had to get a taxi. Could hardly walk for three days.” I know what that’s like. “How bad was it?”
zh_text: 「我沒辦法走回家，得要叫計程車。幾乎有整整三天不能走路。」我知道那種感覺。「傷成怎樣？」

en_text: “God, it wasn’t as though he raped me, if that’s what you’re getting at.”
zh_text: 「天啊，他沒有強暴我，如果你想問的是這個的話。」

en_text:
Prostitution and rape. Two things that closed-minded people think go hand in hand. Some people think prostitutes even deserve it. Some people think a lot of stupid things. Some even think that raping a prostitute isn’t rape at all, that the only difference is whether you fork out your ﬁfty bucks.
“You’ve experienced the difference, huh?”
zh_text:
嫖妓與強暴。思想保守的人會覺得這兩件事情是一體的兩面。有些人認爲妓女活該被強暴。有些人的觀念裡有很多愚蠢的想法。有些人甚至認爲強暴妓女根本不算強暴。唯一的差別在於你有沒有付四十塊錢。
「妳有被強暴過，呃？」

en_text: She doesn’t answer. Instead just looks at me and uses her hands to ﬁsh a cigarette packet from her purse so ﬂuidly that one second her ﬁngers are empty, the next they’re holding on to it.
zh_text: 她沒回答。她只是看著我，伸手自皮包中取出一包菸，而且動作自然流暢到前一秒鐘還是空手，下一秒鐘已經把菸握在手中。

en_text: “You mind?” she asks.
zh_text: 「介意嗎？」

en_text: I shrug. Think about how the smoke is only going to help mask the smell that’s coming from a few rooms down. “Go to it.”
zh_text: 我聳肩。心裡想著這根菸會留下來的味道。「抽吧。」

en_text: I notice her hands are shaking slightly. “He told me if any cops wanted to know about him, I was to keep my mouth shut. Said he’d kill me if I didn’t.”
zh_text: 我注意到她的手在微微顫抖。「他告訴我如果有警察問起的話，我必須守口如瓶。不然他就把我殺了。」

en_text: I can’t ﬁgure why he just didn’t kill her anyway. It’s the best way to keep somebody quiet. Maybe he hadn’t reached that point in his life.
zh_text: 我想不透他爲什麼不當場把她幹掉。這是讓人保持緘默最好的辦法。或許當時他還沒有走到人生的那個點上。

en_text: “So why are you talking to me?” I ask.
zh_text: 「那妳爲什麼要告訴我？」我問。

en_text: “I’ve got bills to pay.”
zh_text: 「我有帳單要繳。」

en_text: Sure, that and the fact that money will always win out over fear, loyalty, truth, or whatever other bullshit shoves its way into a prostitute’s life. She pulls the cigarette from her pack, bites on the end of it, and pulls out a lighter. She’s still silent, just giving her cigarette head. She lets three smoke rings fall from her dry lips.
zh_text: 當然，帳單，還有金錢永遠勝過恐懼、忠誠、真相或是妓女生命中其他狗屎的事實。她從菸盒中拿出一根菸，咬著菸屁股，然後拿出打火機。她一聲不吭，默默吸菸。乾巴巴的嘴唇中吐出三個煙圈。

en_text: “Have you got an ashtray anywhere around here?”
zh_text: 「你家裡有菸灰缸嗎？」

en_text: “Below your feet. The maid will get it.”
zh_text: 「彈在腳下就好了。」

en_text: She taps the ash onto the red carpet.
zh_text: 她將菸灰彈到紅地毯上。女僕會清理。

en_text: “I keep thinking I’m going to give up one day,” she says, looking at the cigarette, but I bet she’s thinking about the hooking. “It’ll kill you,” I say.
zh_text: 「我一直在想有一天要戒菸。」她看著香菸說道，不過我敢說她是在想香菸廣告。「抽菸會害死妳的。」

en_text: “Everything will kill you these days.”
zh_text: 「這年頭什麼東西都會害死你。」

en_text: She’s so right. “So do you think he was a cop?” I ask. She shrugs. “Acted like a cop.”
zh_text: 她說得真對。「妳覺得他是警察嗎？」我問。她聳肩。「行爲舉止像。」

en_text: “Acted how?”
zh_text: 「行爲舉止？」

en_text: “You know. Kind of reserved. Always looking around to see who was watching. Stiff body action. Knew what he was doing. Decisive like.”
zh_text: 你知道。有點沉默。總是左顧右盼，看看有沒有人在看。動作很僵硬。很清楚自己在做什麼。看起來很果斷。

en_text: “You can tell he’s a cop from that?”
zh_text: 「妳憑這幾點就看得出他是警察？」

en_text:
“In my line of work, you get a gut feeling for that kind of thing. When he ﬁrst pulled up I wasn’t going to go with him. Thought I was going to be arrested for something, though I don’t know what—it’s not like what I’m doing is illegal.”
“It is if you’re not paying your taxes,” I tell her, which is true.
zh_text: 「直覺。他一開始停車的時候，我並不打算跟他走。我還以爲我要被逮捕了。有時候你就是知道被人監視或是問話的人是警察。」

en_text:
“Yeah, well, anyway, my point is he was a cop. I could tell.”
“You asked him if he was a cop?”
zh_text:
「妳有問他是不是警察嗎？」
「有差別嗎？他有可能說謊。直到他告訴我他想做什麼，我才知道他是認真的，不是來抓人的。」
「他事前還是事後付款？」

en_text: “Does it matter? He would have lied. Anyway, so we drive directly to the Everblue and I’m starting to freak out a little because I’m thinking maybe he wants more than he’s told me, but he’s paid me up front and no matter what you think, I’m a professional and it felt too late to back out. I ﬁgured a motel was still safer than the bush, and I ﬁgured it’d be better than telling him I’d changed my mind. Some people don’t like that.”
zh_text: 「開始沒訴什麼。我們直接開到長藍。我當時有點害怕。他告訴過我想幹什麼，不過在開車途中，我開始懷疑他會不會想做其他事情。我們即將前往一間汽車旅館，遠離我所認識的人，不會有任何人可以幫助我。」「但妳還是跟他去了。」「當然。我想汽車旅館還是比樹叢安全，而且我想跟他去總比說我改變主意要好。有些人不喜歡這樣。」

zh_text: 「如果不是去汽車旅館，妳通常會上哪裡去？」

en_text: “Not far from where you picked me up. I generally just sort them out down a nearby alleyway.”
zh_text: 「離你讓我上車的地方不遠。我通常都會到附近的小巷子裡解決。」

en_text: From what she said a few minutes ago about Calhoun’s preferences, an alleyway would have been far from sufﬁcient. With the type of noise they needed to make, I’m surprised the motel room had been adequate. Then again nobody’s going to complain about the noise because people in twenty other adjoining rooms are also making it. There’s even a chance Calhoun booked the two adjoining rooms, just to make sure not as many people heard him having the time of his life.
zh_text: 根據她之前提到卡爾霍恩的癖好，小巷子絕對無法滿足需求。照他們將會發出的噪音來看，我很驚訝旅館能夠任由他們那樣搞。不過話說回來，不會有人抱怨噪音，因為他們附近房間裡的人也都在搞。卡爾霍恩也有可能把兩旁的房間都租下來，只爲了確保沒有那麼多人聽見他在享受這輩子最美好的時光。

en_text:
I take the photograph out of my jacket pocket. “Are you sure it was the same guy as the photograph?” I ask her this without showing her the picture.
“Positive.”
zh_text:
道。我自夾克口袋中取出照片。「妳確定就是照片裡的這個人？」我還沒把照片拿給她看就問
「確定。」

en_text:
“What does he look like?” I ask. I hold the picture facing away from her.
I’m basically testing her memory, even though she saw it half an hour earlier.
zh_text: 「他長什麼樣子？」我把照片背對她問道。基本上我是在測試她的記憶，雖然她半小時前還見過那張照片。

en_text: “Like that,” she says, nodding toward the photo.
zh_text: 就像那樣。她說著朝向照片點點頭。

en_text: “Describe him.”
zh_text: 「描述一下。」

en_text: “Huh?”
“Describe him. Tell me what he looks like.”
zh_text: 「描述一下。告訴我他長什麼樣子。」

zh_text: 「這個，他身了一件白色襯衫，淡棕色的運動外套，黑褲子。」

zh_text: 「我不是在問他穿什麼，婊子……」

“Tell me what he looked like.”
zh_text: 「告訴我他長什麼樣子。」

zh_text: 「別叫我婊子。」

en_text:
“Just answer the fucking question.”
“Fuck you.”
zh_text:
「他媽的回答問題。」
「我操。」

en_text: Where is all this coming from? Why the sudden hostility?
zh_text: 這到底是怎麼回事？幹嘛突然充滿敵意？

en_text: I open the briefcase. Take out a knife.
zh_text: 我打開公事包，拿出一把刀。

en_text: “Hey, what are you doing?”
zh_text: 「嘿，你在幹嘛？」

By the end of the night nobody is going to pay shit to screw you. The only way you’ll ever score another client is if you’re wearing a paper bag over your head.”

en_text: I study her face, waiting for a reaction. I’m expecting surprise, right? Or for her to even be stunned. Scared maybe. But she starts yawning. When she ﬁnishes she puts the cigarette back into her mouth and sucks in another mouthful of cancerous smoke, like she doesn’t even care. Becky has obviously been threatened before.
zh_text: 我打量她的表情，等待她的反應。我期待她會驚訝，對吧？甚至會目瞪口呆。可能很害怕。但她竟然開始打呵欠。打完呵欠後，她將香菸放回嘴裡，又吸了一口致癌的白煙，一副毫不在乎的模樣。貝琪顯然曾被威脅過。

zh_text: 「你以爲你嚇得了我嗎？」

en_text: Yes. Yes, I do think I scare her. I tell her this.
zh_text: 沒錯。沒錯，我確實認爲我嚇得了她。我這麼告訴她。

en_text: “You like that?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你喜歡嗎？」她問。

en_text: “Huh?”
“Scaring people.”
zh_text: 「嚇人。」

en_text: “It’s what I do.”
zh_text: 「那是我的專長。」

en_text: “Oh.”

I’m holding the knife so the blade is pointing toward her. For the ﬁrst time, I’m beginning to doubt that I’ll use it. There’s something about her I’m starting to like. No, I’m not going soft, and I’m certainly not going to propose to her, but I’m starting to wonder if it’s really necessary to cut her open.
zh_text: 我手握刀柄，將刀尖對準她。第一次，我開始懷疑我會不會使用它。我開始喜歡上她所散發出的一種特質。不，我不能心軟，而且我肯定不會向她求婚，不過我開始懷疑是否眞有必要將她開膛剖肚。

en_text: I’m not sure how to carry on, which is probably what she wants.
zh_text: 我不太確定該如何繼續下去，或許這就是她的目的。

en_text: “So what are you going to do with this information?” she asks, ignoring the knife.
zh_text: 「所以我跟你說了這些後，你打算怎麼做？」她問。

en_text: “What’s it to you?”
zh_text: 「妳管這個幹嘛？」

en_text: “I’d think a man in your position would be a bit friendlier.”
zh_text: 「我以為在你這種處境下的男人應該友善一點。」

en_text: A man in my position. What position? I’m the one with the knife. She’s going nowhere unless I allow her to. What she doesn’t understand is that my threat is no empty one, unlike those made by the losers she’s screwed.
zh_text: 「我這種處境？什麼處境？拿刀的人是我。除非有我允許，她哪裡也不能去。她不了解的地方在於我跟其他敗類不同，我並非虛張聲勢。」

en_text: I consider apologizing, but don’t want to.
zh_text: 我考慮向她道歉，不過我不想。

en_text: “I think he killed somebody,” I confess.
zh_text: 「我認爲他殺過一個人。」我坦白道。

en_text: “Pretty sure.”
zh_text: 「非常確定。」

en_text: “You think he killed Lisa Houston?”
zh_text: 「你認爲他殺了麗莎・休士頓？」

en_text: “Who?”
“Lisa Houston.”
zh_text: 「麗莎・休士頓。」

en_text: “Yeah.”
“You’re saying a cop killed her?”
zh_text: 「你是說殺她的是個警察？」

en_text: Sure. Why not? There’s nothing she can do with the information. “That’s the way it’s looking.” “Unbelievable.”
zh_text: 當然。有何不可？反正她也不可能出去亂說。「看起來是這樣。」「難以置信。」「妳認識她？」

en_text: “You knew her?” “We all know each other, honey.”
zh_text: 「我們通通認識，蜜糖。」

en_text: “You liked her?”
zh_text: 「妳喜歡她嗎？」

en_text: “Couldn’t stand her. Didn’t mean I wanted her dead, but since she is, I guess I’m happy about it.” “Happier than Lisa, anyway.”
zh_text: 「我受不了她。並不是說我要她死，不過既然她已經死了，我倒是覺得挺開心的。」「總之比麗莎開心。」

en_text: “Huh. I guess you’re right.”
zh_text: 呃，我想你說得沒錯。

en_text: I am right. I’m in the ideal position to make a solid comparison. “So what can you tell me about him?”
zh_text: 我說得沒錯。我絕對有資格如此比較。「那妳能提供些什麼嗎？」

en_text: She gives me a detailed description. Nails him to a T. I show her the photograph for the second time. She conﬁrms it’s him. In a matter of maybe an hour, I’ve narrowed my list down to one suspect. Detective Robert Calhoun. Father to a dead boy. Husband to a disappointed wife. Partner to his morbid desires.
zh_text: 她詐細拈述他的長相，就是他沒錯。我再度拿照片給她看。她確認是他。經過約莫一個小時的努力後，我將嫌犯清單減少到一個人——羅伯特·卡爾霍恩警探。有個早夭的兒子、失望的妻子，以及變態的慾望。

en_text: We talk for a bit more. I put the knife back into the briefcase and close down the lid. She doesn’t look relieved to see it gone. It’s like she never even cared. Just sits there, sucking on her cigarette and talking. And thinking about her money. I’m picturing my two grand in her purse. I don’t want her to have it anymore. I glance at my watch.
zh_text: 我們又談了一會兒。我將刀放回公事包，蓋上上蓋。她似乎並沒有因此而鬆懈。那感覺像是她根本不曾在乎過。就這麼坐在那裡，抽菸說話。想著她的錢。我也想著她皮包裡的那兩千塊。我已經不想殺她了。我看了看錢。

en_text: “Getting late, honey?”
zh_text: 「時候晚了，蜜糖？」

en_text: I look up at her. “Yeah.”
zh_text: 我抬頭看她。「是啊。」

en_text: I still have plenty to do tonight, including picking up the cat.
zh_text: 今晚我還有很多事要忙，包括去領那隻貓。

en_text: “So now what?”
zh_text: 「那現在怎麼樣？」

en_text: I shrug. If I’m not going to get my money back, I may as well get my money’s worth.
zh_text: 我聳肩。如果我不打算拿回我的錢，至少我該讓錢花得值得。

en_text: “Is there anything you would like to do?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你有什麼想做的嗎？」她問。

en_text: I nod. I have aspirations. My life is full of things I’d like to do.
zh_text: 我點頭。我慾望無窮。我的生命裡充滿想做的事情。

en_text: “Yeah? What?” she asks.
zh_text: 「是喔？想做什麼？」她問。

en_text: “Well, I suppose we could make use of the bedroom.” But I don’t feel like making use of her, let alone the bedroom. The clown clock with the big moving eyes keeps looking at her, then at me, then at her again. All I feel like doing is going home and hitting the sack. I yawn. Wipe my ﬁngertips at my watering eyes. “Maybe I’ll take a rain check.”
zh_text: 「這個，我想我們可以用這間臥房。」但是我並不想用她，也不想用臥房。大眼睛的小丑鬧鐘一直在看她，然後看我，然後又看她。我唯一想做的事情就是回家睡覺。我打了個呵欠。伸手揉了揉眼睛。「或許改天再說吧。」

en_text: “You sure?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你確定？」她問。

en_text: “Positive.” I stand up and grab my briefcase.
zh_text: 「確定。」我站起身來，拿起公事包。

en_text: “Sure thing, sugar. You ever want to do this again sometime, feel free to call me.”
zh_text: 當然，蜜糖。改天有興趣的話，歡迎來找我。

en_text: I turn off the lights on the way out. I don’t lock the front door behind me. It’s stopped drizzling and the wind is cool. Easily the coldest it has been all year. People are all inside, wrapped up in sheets and blankets. In their dreams, people like me are chasing them. Drops of water reﬂect the streetlights off leaves and fences and my car for the evening.
zh_text: 我關上屋裡的燈，關上大門。雨停了，風很冷。或許是今年裡最冷的一刻。人們全都躲在家裡，裹在床單和毯子下。在他們的夢裡，像我這種人在追逐他們。樹葉、籬笆和我車上的水滴反射著街燈的光芒。

en_text:
We head for town. I can’t be bothered making conversation and she doesn’t seem that eager either, so I turn on the radio. There’s some crappy song on, but I don’t care enough to change stations. “Where do you want me to drop you off?”
“Wherever.”
zh_text:
我們駕車前往市區。我不想再說什麼，她似乎也不太熱衷交談，於是我打開收音機。電台在播一首爛歌，不過我也懶得轉台。「妳想要我在哪裡放妳下來？」
「隨便。」

en_text: Should I or shouldn’t I? I still don’t know. Killing her will get me my two thousand dollars; letting her live still offers her up as help should I need any more information. It’s nothing like the dilemma I had at the gay guy’s house, but it’s still a dilemma. What would God want me to do? He’d probably want me to smite the whore, but she’s too likable for that.
zh_text: 動手還是不動手？我依然無法決定。殺了她可以拿回我的兩千塊；放過她的話，我還可以在需要打探消息的時候回來找她。這跟我在同性戀家裡面對的難題不同，不過依然是個兩難的局面。上帝會想我怎麼做？祂或許會要我殺了這個婊子，但是她實在太可愛了。

en_text: I pull into an alleyway between a couple of shops, the headlights picking out dozens of cardboard boxes, chunks of white Styrofoam, and bags of trash. There are small puddles that have rainbows in them caused by exhaust fumes. I smile at her, lean over, and open the door like a gentleman. This woman has narrowed my list down to one suspect, and for that I’m truly grateful. She smiles back at me, and thanks me for a pleasant evening.
zh_text: 我駛入位於兩間商店中間的巷道，車燈照亮幾個厚紙箱、幾塊保麗龍，以及幾袋垃圾。地上有幾灘因爲沾染廢氣而看起來像是裡面有彩虹般的水窪。我對她微笑，像個紳士般湊過去幫她開門。這個女人將我的名單降到一個人，我對此感到非常感激。她回應我的微笑，謝謝我給她一個愉快的夜晚。

en_text: “You’re welcome,” I say, and thirty seconds later, after her body lands on the cold concrete with a slight thump, I tuck the two thousand dollars into my jacket pocket. I wipe the knife clean on her short skirt, then lean back into the car.
zh_text: 「不必客氣。」我說，三十秒後，當她的屍體輕輕落在冰涼的水泥地上時，我將兩千塊錢塞回夾克口袋。我在她的迷你裙上擦拭刀刃，然後走回車內。

en_text: Always the gentleman till the end.
zh_text: 到死都要保持紳士風度。

en_text: The money feels good inside my pocket. It makes me feel like I’m worth something, that I’m somebody important. The only thing I’m carrying that doesn’t feel so good is the guilt I feel about killing Becky. I can’t believe how quickly it’s hit me. It’s like snapping Fluffy’s neck. The only way I can balance the scales is if I’m driving home tonight and I come across a hooker that’s been hit by a car. As I back away from the alleyway, my headlights washing across her crumpled body, the pain starts to fade. By the time I get stuck at my ﬁrst red light, I don’t feel bad at all.
zh_text: 口袋裡有錢的感覺真好。讓我有種很有身價的感覺，好像我是什麼重要人物。唯一讓我感覺不太好的地方就是殺害貝琪的罪惡感。我不敢相信罪惡感竟會來得這麼快。那就像是扭斷小毛的脖子一樣。大概只有在今晚駕車回家途中路過一名被車撞死的妓女才能讓我心理平衡一點。倒車離開巷子時，我的車頭燈掃過她的殘軀，罪惡感開始消失了，當貝琪離開我的視線，我駛入馬路，停在紅綠燈前時，我已經一點都不難過了。

en_text: I try to ﬁgure out why Calhoun did what he did, and the answer is actually pretty simple. His problem was that sex with Becky the prostitute couldn’t live up to the fantasy he’d imagined. He thought he could quash his desire for rough sex by having it with Becky, but because he was paying her, and she was only pretending to be afraid, it took away the realism. Becky didn’t fear for her life, and Calhoun knew that. It may not have sunk in for a few days, or maybe longer, but in the end he was left needing far, far more. Daniela Walker gave him his fantasy. In the process he knew the differences between right and wrong, gambled with the consequences, and decided the risk was worth it.
zh_text: 我試圖理解卡爾霍恩爲什麼要做這種事情，答案其實非常簡單。他的問題在於跟貝琪的性行爲無法滿足他的幻想。他以爲只靠跟貝琪狠狠地搞一搞就能夠壓抑他的慾望，不過由於他有付錢，所以她只是在假裝害怕而已，這點剝奪了真實感。貝琪並不擔心自己的性命，卡爾霍恩也很清楚。或許這個問題在幾天內甚至更長的時間裡都沒有浮出水面，但到最後他還是發現自己需要更多更多。丹妮耶拉·沃克滿足了他的需求。過程中他都能夠分辨是非，在衡量後果之後，他認定收穫大於風險。

en_text: I don’t bother questioning why he would kill an innocent woman and pass up on the opportunity to kill the hooker, especially when the innocent woman was a harder target. It’s all part of the game, part of the fantasy. It’s a pure rush to be completely superior, so powerful, so unbelievably dominant. Following Daniela home, confronting her, breaking her, would have been one hell of an ego rush.
zh_text: 我甚至沒有費心去管他爲什麼要殺害無辜的女子，而不去動那名妓女，無辜女子比妓女難處理多了。一切都是遊戲的一部分，幻想的一部分。絕對的優越、絕對的權威、絕對的支配能夠帶來一種純粹的快感。跟蹤丹妮耶拉回家，攻擊她，擊垮她，肯定能夠帶來至高無上的快感。

en_text: The car has a weighty feel, but that’s because Candy version two, the four-hundred-dollar hooker, is lying in the trunk where I put her not long ago. I pull over outside the park where Melissa changed my life with a pair of pliers, and walk around to the back of the car.
zh_text: 車子感覺有點重，不過那是因為坎蒂二號，那個收費四百元的妓女，不久前被我塞到後車廂裡的關係。我將車停在梅莉莎拿鉗子改變我一生的公園外面，繞到車後。

en_text: Candy’s short blouse is covered in blood. Her puffy eyes are open and staring at me, through me, and I wonder exactly what it is she’s trying to focus on. Her skin is so pale she looks as though she could have been locked in the trunk for the last six months. In contrast, her painted lips are a vivid red, the color of blood. I close the trunk.
zh_text: 坎蒂的短上衣染澀鮮血。雙眼圓睜，凝視我，看穿我，我很好奇她的焦點落於何處。她的皮膚慘白，看起來像被關在後車廂裡六個月一樣。話說回來，她的嘴唇則是一片鮮紅，血的顏色。我關上後車廂。

en_text: There are no lights on in any of the houses, and just under half of the streetlamps are busted. I can see the dark outlines of the trees in the park, but none of the details. No trafﬁc. No pedestrians. No signs of life.
zh_text: 附近的屋子裡沒有透出任何燈火，下方則有半數街燈都是壞的。我隱約看出公園樹木的陰暗輪廓，不過看不清楚細節。沒有車輛。沒有行人。沒有生命跡象。

en_text: I open the trunk and look down at the dead girl. With my hands gloved, I roll her body over. The pool of blood beneath her looks like oil. Again I look around. When I slammed the trunk on Candy earlier, she was alive. I slam it on her again, only this time she’s dead. I did not kill her.
zh_text: 我打開後車廂，低頭看著女孩的屍體。我手戴手套，將她翻過身去。她身後的血泊看起來像油。我再度左顧右盼。剛剛蓋上車廂蓋時，她還活著。這回再蓋一次，她已經死了。不是我殺的。

en_text: I walk back to the side of the car knowing there can only be one person who’s done this to me: Melissa. I’m not sure exactly when, or why. The same reason she came to my apartment and helped me with the injury. She’s playing with me. Toying with me. She’s setting something up of which I have no idea at all.
zh_text: 我走回車旁，心知只有一個人會對我做出這種事情：梅莉莎。我不確定她什麼時候動手，也不知道她這麼做的理由。應該跟她跑到我家幫我療傷的理由一樣。她在玩我。把我當成玩具。她有所圖謀，而我完全被蒙在鼓裡。

en_text: I’m inside and just shutting my door when a movement to my right stops me. I twist my head to see an old man stepping out of the dark toward me.
zh_text: 我坐回車上，關上車門，右方傳來一陣動靜，我立刻停止動作。我轉過頭，看見一個老男人步出黑暗，向我走來。

en_text: “My God, is that you, Joe?” He gets a few steps closer, and I give him a casual look up and down, as if I’m out shopping for victims. He looks in his late sixties—his gray hair is combed back at the front, but standing up at the back. His face is a collage of wrinkles that are long and deep. He wears glasses that are broken in the middle, and look to be held together with Velcro dots. They’re covered in a thin layer of dust, and I can’t pick the color of his magniﬁed eyes. He’s holding a hand toward me, not quite pointing, but in a gesture that makes me aware he’s about to put his hand on my arm. The sad part is I’m about to let him. He’s wearing a ﬂannel shirt and brown corduroy pants. He looks vaguely familiar. I say nothing. I’m in no mood for conversation.
zh_text: 「我的天，是你嗎，喬？」他走近幾步，我神態輕鬆地上下打量他，彷彿出門找尋獵物一樣。他看起來年近七十，一頭灰髮梳向腦後，不過後面還是翹起來。他滿臉都是又深又長的皺紋，戴著一副從中斷掉的眼鏡，看來是用魔術貼合起來的。鏡面上有一層薄灰，我看不出放大的眼睛是什麼顏色。他對我伸出一隻手掌，不像是在指我，而是在讓我知道他即將拍拍我的手臂。悲哀的是，我會讓他拍。他身穿法蘭絨襯衫和棕色的燈芯絨褲。他看起來有點眼熟。我一言不發。我沒心情聊天。

en_text: “Little Joe? It is you, isn’t it?”
zh_text: 「小喬？是你，對不對？」

en_text: I strain my memory, and in that same moment his face seems to shimmer into focus, along with a name. “Mr. Chadwick?”
zh_text: 我用力回想，在那一刻裡，他的面孔似乎突然聚焦，伴隨一個名字來到我的眼前。「查德維克先生？」

en_text: “That’s right, son. My God, I can hardly believe it.” He starts shaking his head. “If it isn’t little Joe. Evelyn’s boy.”
zh_text: 「沒錯，孩子。我的天，眞不敢相信。」他開始搖頭。「這可不是小喬嗎？愛弗琳的兒子。」

en_text: He offers me his right hand. For a second I imagine it sitting in my briefcase along with a small chunk of his wrist. I step out of the car and shake his hand, hoping he doesn’t pull me into an embrace.
zh_text: 他對我伸出右手。一時之間我想像著它帶著一截手腕躺在我的公事包裡的模樣。我下車，跟他握手，希望他不會將我擁入懷中。

en_text: “How’s your mother, Joe?”
zh_text: 「你媽怎麼樣，喬？」

en_text: I shrug. Mr. Chadwick has always been a nice enough guy, I suppose, once you get past the liver spots and wrinkles, and he certainly seems pleasant enough at the moment. At his age, he must contemplate death quite a lot. I ought to ask him.
zh_text: 我聳肩。查德維克先生向來是個好好先生，我想，習慣他的老人斑和皺紋後，這時的他看起來還挺開朗的。他這個年紀的人必定常常思考死亡的事情。我應該跟他問問。

en_text: “She’s ﬁne, Mr. Chadwick.”
zh_text: 「她很好，查德維克先生。」

en_text: “Call me Walt.”
zh_text: 叫我華特。

en_text: “Sure, Walt. Mom’s just Mom, if you know what I mean.”
zh_text: 當然，華特。我媽還是那個樣子，如果你知道我在說什麼的話。

en_text: “She still doing those jigsaw puzzles?”
zh_text: 「她還是喜歡玩拼圖嗎？」

en_text:
“Yep.” Standing outside of my car, I begin to shiver. A quick glance upward at the covered stars suggests there may be more rain on the way. If so, it’s going to ruin my plans.
“She’s been doing those as long as I remember.”
zh_text:
「是啊。」站在車外，我開始發抖。天上烏雲密布，顯然還會再下雨。如果下雨的話，我的計畫就泡湯了。
印象中的她一直都很喜歡玩拼圖。

en_text: “Yeah, she really likes her puzzles.”
zh_text: 「對啊，她很喜歡她的拼圖。」

en_text: “I bet she’s good at them too. Damn good.”
zh_text: 「我敢說她一定很厲害。非常厲害。」

en_text: “So, um, Walt, what brings you out so late?”
zh_text: 那麼，呃，華特，你這麼晚出門做什麼？

en_text: “I’m walking my dog,” he says, showing me the leash.
zh_text: 「遛狗。」他說著舉起狗繩給我看。

en_text: I look around. “Where is he? In the park?”
zh_text: 我環顧四周。「他呢？在公園裡？」

en_text: “Who?”
“Your dog, Walt.”
zh_text: 你的狗，華特。

en_text: He shakes his head. “No, no. Sparky died two years ago.”
zh_text: 他搖頭。「不，不，史巴齊兩年前就死了。」

en_text: I have no answer for that. I do my best to think that he’s joking, but I’m pretty sure he isn’t. I start nodding slowly, as if I completely understand. He starts nodding slowly too, mirroring me. A few more seconds go by before he speaks.
zh_text: 我無言以對。我努力當他是在開玩笑，不過我很肯定他不是。我開始緩緩點頭，彷彿我完全了解的樣子。他也開始緩緩點頭，模仿我的動作。數秒之後，他再度開口。

en_text: “What about you, Joe?”
zh_text: 「你出門又是做什麼，喬？」

en_text: “I’m just driving. You know how it is.”
zh_text: 「開車兜風，你知道的。」

en_text: “Not really. I don’t drive anymore. Haven’t since the stroke. Doctors tell me I’ll never drive again. You know, Joe, I must catch up with your mother. Boy, she’s some woman. They don’t make them like that anymore.”
zh_text: 「不清楚。我已經不開車了。中風之後就不開了。醫生告訴我永遠都不能開車。你知道，喬，我得要去找你媽敘敘舊。天啊，她真是與衆不同。像她那種女人已經不多了。」

en_text: Don’t make them insane? Yeah, they do, Walt. I shrug and say nothing.
zh_text: 她那種瘋婆子？不，還有很多，華特。我聳肩不語。

en_text: “What are you doing with yourself these days, Joe?”
zh_text: 「你最近都忙些什麼，喬？」

en_text: “I sell cars.”
zh_text: 「賣車。」

en_text: “Really? I’m in the market for a car,” he says, confusing me since he just said he can’t drive anymore, and perhaps he’s confusing himself too. I’m desperate to know whether he saw the corpse in the trunk. “Where do you work?”
zh_text: 「真的？我正想買一輛車。」他說，由於他剛剛才說不能開車，所以我聽得有點糊塗，或許他自己也有點糊塗。我急著想知道他到底有沒有看到後車廂的屍體。「你在哪工作？」

en_text: “Umm . . .” I struggle for a name, “Everblue Cars. Heard of it?”
zh_text: 「呃……」我擠出一個名字。「長藍汽車。聽過嗎？」

en_text: Slowly he nods. “Fine establishment, that one, Joe. You must be proud.” “Thanks, Walt.”
zh_text: 他緩緩點頭。「好地方，那家車行，喬。你一定很驕傲。

en_text: “That one of yours there?” He nods toward the car.
zh_text: 「那是你的車嗎？」他朝向我的車點頭問道。

en_text: “Yeah.” Walt is a witness. Nice old Mr. Chadwick. “Want to take a ride?” “For sale, is it?”
zh_text: 「是啊。」華特是名證人。老好人查德維克先生。「想去兜兜風嗎？」「是賣的嗎，這輛車？」

en_text: “Yep.” I take a stab at the price. “Eight grand.”
zh_text: 「是啊。」我隨便標個價。「八千。」

en_text: He whistles. Like people do after you’ve quoted them a price. The whistling is one step away from tire kicking. “Gee, that’s cheap,” he says, and tries to kick the nearest tire, but misses.
zh_text: 他吹口哨。就像你說出價錢之後人們會有的反應。通常吹玩口哨的人就要踢輪胎了。「天啊，可真便宜。」他說，伸腳去踢最接近的輪胎，不過沒踢中。

en_text: We climb into the car. I do up my seat belt and Walt works on his. He starts whistling again, all the time he’s looking at the dashboard, airconditioning, and radio controls.
zh_text: 我們上了車。我繫上安全帶，華特繫上他的。他又開始吹口哨了。他一直研究著儀表板、空調，還有收音機控制台。

en_text: “You know, Joe, I haven’t seen your mother since your dad died.” I envy him.
zh_text: 你知道，喬，你爸去世後，我就沒有見過你媽了。我真羨慕他。

en_text: “That was a real tragedy,” he adds, sounding upset.
zh_text: 「那眞是一場悲劇。」他補充，聽起來很遺憾。

en_text: I ﬁnd myself nodding. I want to tell him that I thought it was a tragedy too. I want to tell him how it hurt when Dad was no longer with us, how I just wanted him to be alive, but I say nothing. “Yeah,” I manage, keeping my voice under control.
zh_text: 我忍不住點頭。我很想告訴他也認爲那是一場悲劇，我想告訴他我爸的死對我造成多大的創傷，我有多麼希望他還活著，但是我什麼也沒說。「是啊。」我擠出這句話，努力控制我的聲音。

en_text: “Did I ever tell you how sorry I was?”
zh_text: 「我有說過我有多遺憾嗎？」

en_text: I have no idea what in the hell he told me back then. What anybody told me. “You did. Thanks.” He opens his mouth, but says nothing. He seems to be thinking. “How are you coping these days?” “I’m over it,” I say, not bothering to mention how empty life became without him.
zh_text: 我完全不記得他當年跟我說過什麼。不記得任何人跟我說過什麼。「有。謝謝。他張開嘴巴，欲言又止。他似乎在考慮什麼。「那件事情還會影響你嗎？」「已經過去了。」我說，沒有費心提及生活少了爸有多空虛。

en_text: Now it’s his turn to start nodding. “That’s good, Joe. When a man takes his own life, his family can be a mess for years. Thank God you’ve come out of it as a nice young man.”
zh_text: 這下輪到他點頭了。「那很好，喬。家裡有人自殺時，家人總會低潮一陣子。感謝上帝你能走出陰霾，成爲一個大好青年。」

en_text: I’m still nodding. When Dad killed himself, the only thing I felt like doing at ﬁrst was joining him. There were hundreds of questions, but the biggest one was Why? Mom knows, I’m sure of it. Just as I’m sure she’ll never tell me. The second why is just as important: why did he leave me alone with Mom?
zh_text: 我還在點頭。老爸自殺時，我剛開始唯一想做的事情就是隨他而去。我有數以百計的疑問，但是最大的問題還是在於爲什麼？老媽知道，我很肯定。我也很肯定她永遠不會告訴我。第二個爲什麼也同等重要：他爲什麼把我一個人留給媽？

en_text: “She still got the place in South Brighton?”
zh_text: 「她還住在南布萊頓嗎？」

en_text: I stop nodding. I’m thinking of Dad and feeling depressed. I know Melissa is watching me, but for the moment I don’t really care.
zh_text: 我停止點頭。我在想我爸，心情很沮喪。我知道梅莉莎在監視我，不過在這剎那我真的不在乎。

en_text: “Yeah.” I start the car. “Shall we take her for a spin?” I ask, needing to change the subject. “Sure, Joe.”
zh_text: 「對。」我發動引擎。「我們開出去溜溜吧？」我問，因為我需要改變話題。「當然」喬

en_text: We watch the city go by. Life has wound down in this part of the world. We spot only a few other cars on the road. We pass a service station with a police car parked outside and two ofﬁcers standing over a man they have handcuffed laying facedown. Walt makes conversation about the car and the weather, and tells me that his dead dog keeps running away.
zh_text: 我們看著街景在車外飛逝。這附近的生活步調比較沒有那麼緊湊。一路上只有經過幾輛車。我們路過一座加油站，站外停了一輛警車。華特一直聊著這輛車、天氣，並且宣稱他死去的狗經常逃家。

en_text: “My God, who would have thought I’d run into Evelyn’s son? You know, Joe, I’ve known your mother more than forty years.”
zh_text: 「我的天啊，誰會想到我竟然能遇上愛弗琳的兒子？你知道，喬，我認識你媽超過四十年了。」

en_text: “Really.”
zh_text: 「眞的。」

en_text: “We’re both single now. Single and old. Isn’t life sad?”
zh_text: 「現在我們兩個都單身了。單身又年老。生活不是很悲哀嗎？」

en_text: “Sad,” I agree.
zh_text: 「悲哀。」我同意。

en_text: I stop north of the city, turning into a long stretch of road just before the highway where a thousand trees block our view in every direction. Out here, we’re all alone. Out here, I can do what I want.
zh_text: 我在城北停車，轉入一條通往高速公路的道路，四周有上千棵樹阻擋我們的視線。在這裡，只有我們兩人獨處。在這裡，我可以爲所欲爲。

en_text: “Maybe I’ll give your mother a call tomorrow, invite myself around for dinner.”
zh_text: 「或許我該打個電話給你媽，去找她叨擾一頓晚餐。」

en_text: Keeping one hand on the wheel, I reach behind the passenger seat and open my briefcase.
zh_text: 我一手放在方向盤上，另外一手伸到乘客座上打開公事包。

en_text: “Something I can get for you, Joe?”
zh_text: 「我可以幫你拿什麼嗎，喬？」

en_text: “No. I’m ﬁne.”
zh_text: 「不用，我自己來就好了。」

en_text: “Your mother and I knew each other quite well before she met your father. Did you know that, Joe?”
zh_text: 「認識你爸之前，你媽跟我走得很近。你知道嗎，喬？

en_text: “No, I didn’t know that, Walt.”
zh_text: 「不，我不知道，華特。」

en_text: “Would you mind if I called her? I wouldn’t mind getting to know her again.”
zh_text: 「你介意我打電話給她嗎？我想重新認識她。」

en_text: The opportunity knocks so loud I actually drop the knife. Candy’s in the trunk of the car, but Walt doesn’t know she’s there. He couldn’t. He’s too damn old to make sense of anything even if he had seen her, and he’d be blabbing on about her, asking me a whole bunch of questions. I close my briefcase. If I let Walt live, he’s going to spend time with my mother, and that’s time she won’t be able to devote to me.
zh_text: 我腦中靈光一現，興奮得我連刀都握不住了。坎蒂就在後車廂，但是華特並不知情。他不可能知情。他就算有看到她，也已經老到搞不清楚狀況了，而且他一定會喋喋不休地詢問一大堆關於她的問題。我關上公事包。如果讓華特活下來，他就會去跟我媽混，而我媽就不會把那麼多時間花在我的身上。

en_text: “What are you smiling about, Joe?”
zh_text: 你在笑什麼，喬？

en_text: “Nothing. You want to drive back, Walt?”
zh_text: 「沒什麼。你想開回去嗎，華特？」

en_text: “No, son, I’ll let you do the driving.”
zh_text: 「不，孩子，開車的事情還是交給你吧。」

en_text: I drive back toward town. We pass the same trees. Same service station with the same police car parked outside only now the handcuffed guy is in the back of that car. Walt talks the entire way, touching on subjects that I’m still too young to care about. Things about diets and diseases and loneliness. He tells me about my mother, delves into a past that existed before she met my father. Walt speaks so much that I can see why he got on so well with my mother, having the ability to turn nothing into something even less interesting. His sentences ﬂow from one to the next, and mixed in there in those same breaths are directions to his house. The house is small and well kept. It’s obvious Walt’s dead dog doesn’t crap all over the lawn.
zh_text: 我開回市區。我們路過同樣的樹林，同樣的加油站，外面停了同樣的警車。一路上華特都在講話，盡說一些以我的年紀根本毫不在乎的事情。關於節食、疾病還有孤寂的問題。他談論著我媽，講起她遇上我爸之前的陳年往事。華特的話多到讓我了解他之所以能跟我媽相處融洽的原因，因為他擁有一種能把無中生有的事情變得更加無趣的能力。他一句接一句，偶爾還能幫我指示通往他家的途徑。房子很小，保養得很好。顯然華特的死狗沒在草皮上亂大便。

en_text: “I’ll call your mother tomorrow morning,” he says, leaning back into the car and smiling at me.
zh_text: 「我明天一早就打電話給你媽。」

en_text: “I think she might like that. Give her somebody to talk to. I think she has issues more in her age group that I can’t relate to, like pensions and cancer.”
zh_text: 「我想她會很高興的。有人可以聊聊。我想她有些問題不是我的年齡可以理解的，像是退休金和癌症。」

en_text: He gives me a knowing nod, his eyes twinkling a little. “Evelyn,” he says, more to himself than to me, then he turns and heads up the pathway to his door. I pull away and head south. I turn on the stereo and sing loudly. After ten minutes, I pull the car off to the side of the road beneath a bank of trees. The grass, burned dry from the last few months of hot sun, has been sheltered enough by the trees to keep most of the day’s rain off. I study the body again, hoping that I might be able to learn something from it, or more likely, that Melissa has left me a message. I shift the corpse slightly. Deep cuts smile at me. Dark red ﬂesh gleams from beneath thick ﬂaps of skin. I have a good idea what caused the wounds. I wrestle Candy from the car, careful not to get blood on myself, and dump her on the ground, which reveals the murder weapon in the bottom of the trunk.
zh_text: 我駕車離開，朝南行駛。我打開收音機，高聲歌唱。十分鐘後，我將車開向路旁，停在一排樹下。即使今晚有下毛毛雨，讓上個月烈日曬乾的草地依然在我腳下吱吱作響。我再度打量屍體，希望能夠從中看出端倪，或更有可能的情況是，梅莉莎有在上面留下信息。我慢慢移動屍體。傷口很深，向我微笑。下垂的皮膚下露出深紅色的血肉。我很清楚這些傷口是什麼留下來的。我將坎蒂抬出後車廂，小心不讓血沾到身上，然後將她放在地上，露出躺在後車廂底的兇器。

en_text: My knife.
zh_text: 我的刀。

en_text: Or, to be more accurate, a photograph of my knife.
zh_text: 或是，說得更精確一點，刀的照片。

en_text: Seeing this leads me to a couple of conclusions: one, Melissa is deﬁnitely stalking me, and two, I’m in serious trouble. The knife has my ﬁngerprints on it, as does my gun.
zh_text: 看到這張照片讓我得出兩個結論：第一，梅莉莎在跟蹤我；第二，我的麻煩大了。那把刀上有我的指紋，槍也一樣。

en_text: I remove a red plastic container full of gas and set it on the ground.
zh_text: 我拿出一個裝滿汽油的塑膠罐，放在地上。

en_text: Just what game is Melissa playing? If she were going to give the weapons to the police, she would have done so by now. That means she wants something else. And I’m sure she’ll let me know soon enough.
zh_text: 梅莉莎到底在玩什麼遊戲？如果要把兇器交給警方，她應該早就交出去了才是。這表示她另有所求。我肯定再過不久她就會告訴我。

en_text: I dump Candy back into the trunk. Her hands are still tied, her mouth gagged. Both those are my doing. I wonder what she thought when she was desperate for help and a woman came along and opened the trunk. It was the end of things going badly for Candy. It was the end of everything.
zh_text: 我又把坎蒂放回後車廂。她雙手依然緊綁，嘴裡塞著東西。這兩件事都是我幹的。不知道在她絕望無助的時候看到有個女人打開後車廂是什麼感覺。對坎蒂而言，那是苦難的終點。那是一切的終點。

en_text: I roll her onto her side in an attempt to ﬁt her back in nicely, but ﬁnish with one of her legs sticking out. When I slam the trunk down I break her ankle. She doesn’t mind.
zh_text: 我將她側過身去，試圖塞回後車廂，結果有一隻腳露在外面。我用力蓋下車廂蓋，撞斷她的腳踝。她不介意。

en_text: I decide to leave the trunk open. I shake the container back and forth, listening as the gas inside sloshes around. It’s about a quarter full. I use what’s there to soak Candy’s clothes, then toss the container in there with her. I reach into the car for my briefcase and use a knife to cut away Candy’s blouse. Once I pop the gas cap on the side of the car, I stuff the blouse inside, leaving a tongue hanging out.
zh_text: 我決定就讓車廂蓋開著。我搖搖塑膠罐，聽著裡面的汽油晃來晃去。約莫四分之一滿。我浸濕了坎蒂的衣服，將罐子丟到她旁邊。我回車上拿出我的公事包，用刀割下坎蒂的上衣。我打開車身側面的汽油蓋，將上衣塞了進去，留下一點露在外面。

en_text: The car’s cigarette lighter does the job.
zh_text: 我用車上的點菸器點火。

en_text: I am most of the way back into town when I remember the cat. There is nobody to see me as I steal my second car for the evening.
zh_text: 差不多要回到城内的時候，我突然想起那隻貓來。我在附近空無一人的情況下偷了當晚第一輛車。

en_text: Jennifer smiles at me when I walk through the door. She looks at me as if we’re long-lost friends. “Hi there, Joe,” she says, her voice sounding seductive.
zh_text: 進門的時候，珍妮佛對我微笑。她看我的樣子彷彿我們是許久不見的老朋友。「哈囉，喬。她說，她的聲音聽來十分銷魂。

en_text: “Hi.”
She waits for a few seconds, checking to see if that’s all I’m going to say. “I’ll just get him for you.” “Thanks.”
zh_text: 她等了幾秒，想看看我還有沒有別的話說。「我幫你帶他過來。」「謝謝。」

en_text: I’m picturing how Melissa would look in a studded dog collar when Jennifer brings the cat out in a small cage.
zh_text: 我趁珍妮佛去提裝貓的籠子出來時幻想梅莉莎戴狗項圈的模樣。

en_text: “I didn’t think you wanted to take him,” Jennifer says, “after last week.” “Last week?”
zh_text: 「在上個禮拜之後，」珍妮佛說。「我還以爲你不會想領養他了。」「上個禮拜？」

en_text: “When I rang to give you an update, you said you didn’t want any more cats. How many have you got?” “Last week?” I repeat.
zh_text: 「我打電話去時，你說你不想再養貓了。你到底養了多少貓？」「上個禮拜？」我重複。

en_text: Her smile disappears and is replaced with one of caution. “I called you last week.”
zh_text: 她的笑容消失，換上一副謹慎的神色。「我上禮拜有打電話給你。

en_text: “Oh. I was sick last week, really sick. To be honest, I don’t even remember you calling. I was in bed all week. I don’t know what the hell it was I had, but I was pretty delirious. If you called and I was a bastard or something, I’m really sorry.” Though she’s the one who ought to be feeling sorry—I’m the one with a missing testicle. Her caution turns to sympathy.
zh_text: 「喔。我上個禮拜生病了，病得很重。老實說，我甚至不記得妳有打電話來。我一整個禮拜都躺在床上。我不知道我到底得了什麼病，不過我神智不太清醒。如果妳打來的時候我表現得很混蛋，我在這邊向妳道歉。」其實她才應該感到抱歉——睪丸不見的人可是我呀。

en_text: “Getting better. The strange part is that I don’t even have any cats.”
zh_text: 「比較好了。奇怪的地方在於，我根本沒養貓。」

en_text: She smiles, and I wonder why I must keep being nice to people. Why can’t I just take her somewhere and do to her what I’ve been doing to everybody else?
zh_text: 她微笑，我很納悶我爲什麼一定要跟她這麼客氣。我幹嘛不乾脆帶她前往沒人的地方，對她做出我對其他人所做的事情？

en_text: “Well, you’ve got one now. What are you going to call him?”
zh_text: 好吧，现在你有一隻了。你打算叫他什麼？

en_text: “I haven’t really given it any thought. Any suggestions?”
zh_text: 「我沒想過。有建議嗎？」

en_text: “Maybe we could ﬁgure one out over coffee?” she offers.
zh_text: 想到的話，我打電話給你。」她說。

en_text: “I didn’t know cats drink coffee,” I tell her. She smiles, then stops smiling, and looks a little confused. “What do I owe you for the cage?” I ask, ﬁguring it wouldn’t look good if I pulled a plastic bag out of my pocket and stuffed the cat inside. I bet the cage is going to add a good chunk to what is already an expensive mammal.
zh_text: 「這個貓籠多少錢？」我問，心想如果拿口袋裡的塑膠袋來裝貓的話應該不太好看。我敢說這個貓籠肯定要讓本來就已經很貴的哺乳類寵物加上一大筆額外的開銷。

en_text: “Can I trust you to bring it back?”
zh_text: 「我相信你會把它帶回來？」

en_text: “I’m a trustworthy guy.”
zh_text: 我很值得信任。

en_text: “Then it costs nothing.” She smiles. “You want a lift home, or have you got a car?”
zh_text: 「那就免費。」她微笑。「要我開車送你，還是自己有開車？

en_text: A lift home would be good, since it would give me a chance to test a few things out that haven’t been used since my half castration. But my name’s on record here, and it wouldn’t take long for the police to come.
zh_text: 送我聽起來不錯，因為這樣可以讓我有機會嘗試一些打從我被半閹割後就沒嘗試過的事情。但是我曾在這裡留下紀錄，警方要不了多久就會找上門來。

en_text: I thank her for her offer, promise to bring the cage back before the week is out, and ask her to call me a taxi.
zh_text: 我感謝她的好意，保證本週結束之前就會把籠子帶回來，然後請她幫我招計程車。

en_text: The cage moves around beneath my grip. The taxi driver makes some comment on the cat, ﬁguring he can strike up a conversation with me. He ﬁgures wrong. When I get home I put the cat in the bathroom and shut the door. When I go to bed, I can hear it crying. Tomorrow I’ll buy it some food and myself some earplugs. Then I’ll show it around my apartment.
zh_text: 貓籠在我的手中晃來晃去。計程車司機評論那隻貓幾句，以為我想找點話聊。他想錯了。回家之後，我將貓放入浴室，關上房門。上床時，我聽見貓在叫。明天我會買點貓食外帶一副耳塞，然後再帶牠認識環境。

en_text: The following morning my internal alarm clock doesn’t let me down. Things are getting back to as normal as they can be for a guy missing his left testicle. I’m still dreaming, though, which is a concern. Last night I was talking to Dad. The dream was disjointed, but I can remember fragments where he was asking me what I was doing. I guess he was asking me because I was stufﬁng him into the front of the car he was found in. I’d wrapped foam around his wrists, foam and padding, so the rope wouldn’t leave bruises. He couldn’t wind down the windows or open the doors. He couldn’t adjust the air-conditioning or turn off the engine as the carbon monoxide ﬂooded in. He turned blue as he asked me over and over to stop. Mom wasn’t there. She was playing bridge down at the local bingo hall. In fact, that was the last time she ever played. He stopped asking me to stop, then told me that he loved me. Then he died. One moment he was my dad. The next moment he was nothing.
zh_text: 第二天早上我的生理時鐘沒有令我失望，不過我醒來後依然疲憊。對一個失去左睾丸的男人來說，生活已經算是步入常軌。不過我依然會做夢，這倒是令我有點擔憂。昨晚我夢到跟老爸聊天。那個夢沒頭沒尾，不過我依稀記得他問我最近在做什麼。我想他會這麼問是因為當時我正把他塞入他死時的那輛車前座裡。我在他的手腕上裹了一層泡綿，泡綿加襯墊，以免繩子留下瘡痕。他沒有辦法搖下車窗或打開車門。一氧化碳噴入車內時，他無法調整空調或是關閉引擎。他臉色發青，一次又一次地求我住手。媽不在。她去附近的賓果室玩橋牌。事實上，那是她最後一次玩橋牌。他不再求我住手了，然後告訴我他愛我。接著他就死了。前一刻他還是我老爸，下一刻他就什麼也不是了。

en_text: I’m not growing at all accustomed to dreams and I’ve woken from this one feeling shaky and ill. Of course I didn’t kill my father. I loved him dearly and, like my mother, I’d never have done anything to harm him. Walt mentioning my father’s suicide must have given me the imagery. Nobody knows why Dad did what he did. Why he sat himself inside the car parked in the garage and pumped carbon monoxide through the side window with a hose. He didn’t even leave a note.
zh_text: 我完全無法習慣做夢，而自這個夢中驚醒給我一種顫抖與噁心的感覺。當然我沒有殺害我父親。我非常愛他，就像愛我媽一樣，我從來沒有做過任何傷害他的事情。一定是華特提起我爸自殺的關係。沒人知道老爸爲什麼要那麼做。爲什麼要坐到車庫的車裡，自車窗用水管接一氧化碳到車內。他甚至沒有留下遺書。

en_text: I give the cat explicit instructions not to claw the furniture or walls. He doesn’t. He looks around for a few seconds before deciding the best way to take a break from being locked inside the bathroom is to hide beneath my bed. I feed my ﬁsh, make a mental note to buy some food for the cat, go through the usual routines, then ﬁght the cat back into the bathroom with the aid of a broom.
zh_text: 我明確指示貓咪不可抓壞家具與牆壁。牠沒有。牠四下打量片刻，最後決定在被鎖在廁所裡這麼久後，最好的放鬆方式就是躲到我的床下。我餵魚，提醒自己要幫貓買點吃的，做完例行公事，在掃把的幫助下將貓趕回廁所。

en_text: I turn the radio on, listen to the news.
zh_text: 我打開收音機，聽聽新聞。

en_text: The ﬁre from the car spread, as I predicted, but the rain over the last day stopped it from spreading far. They say this as if anybody could care about trees and crops, as if the country’s running low on them. The news guy makes no mention of the dead hookers. Instead he moves on to a report about sheep. Tells us that we’re now outnumbered by them ten to one. He doesn’t mention anything about a revolt, doesn’t explain why we need to increase their numbers by cloning them.
zh_text: 如我所料，車上的火勢延燒，在沒人注意的情況下燒了幾個小時。消防隊員還在現場，不過早已控制火勢。他們說如果不是有下小雨的關係，這場火會燒掉幾公頃的樹木和作物，好像我們國家缺少那種東西一樣。他沒有提到那輛車，沒有提到死去的妓女。播報新聞的傢伙從火災報告跳到下一條跟羊有關的新聞。告訴我們現在羊的數量比人多十倍。他沒有提到抗議的事情，沒有解釋為什麼我們需要利用複製技術提高牠們的數量。

en_text: The walk downstairs is easier than yesterday. The bus ride is also easier. The weather a little worse. It’s raining steadily. I learn nothing at work except that the people I work with have no Goddamn idea what they’re doing.
zh_text: 下樓感覺比昨天輕鬆。坐公車也一樣。除了跟我一起工作的傢伙完全不知道他們在做什麼之外，我在警局一無所獲。

en_text: “I’ve made you some sandwiches,” Sally says, when she meets me outside my ofﬁce just before lunch. “Thanks.”
zh_text: 「我幫你做了些三明治。」午飯前，莎莉在我辦公室外說道。

en_text: I eat her sandwiches and take another of the pills. It feels like it goes down my throat sideways, and I don’t feel any better for it. I think about my dream, and wonder why I’m having so many these days. I put it down to the fact that at the moment I’m not getting to do all the things other people only fantasize about.
