A few hours after lunch I’m carrying my bucket and mop when I see her: Melissa, sitting at a desk. For a second, perhaps even two, the world comes to a complete standstill. I can hear blood pulsing in my head, which is a neat trick because I can swear my heart stops beating. She turns to me and winks. I start toward her, then begin to back away, so I end up motionless. I want to look around at the police who are going to start jumping on me, but I can’t look away from her. After all she’s done to me, there’s something about her I can’t help but admire.
zh_text: 我吃了她的三明治，又吞下另外一顆藥片。感覺好像它神不知鬼不覺地進入我的喉嚨，完全沒有讓我感覺好一點。我又想起我的夢，納悶爲什麼我最近這麼常做夢。我認爲是因為此時我沒有辦法去做那些大部分的人只能幻想的事情。午飯後幾小時，我在拿著水桶和拖把工作時看見了她：梅莉莎，坐在桌子。她轉向我，眨了眨眼。我朝她走去，隨即又向後退開，結果弄到僵在原地。在對我做出那種事情後，我發現她身上有股令我不由自主欣賞的特質。

en_text: Today she’s wearing an expensive light gray suit that makes her look like an overpaid lawyer. Her hair is pulled back neatly, and she is wearing little makeup. She looks like a woman any man would desperately want to believe.
zh_text: 今天她身穿一套昂貴的淡灰色套裝，看起來像是撈過界的律師。她的頭髮整齊後梳，臉上化著淡妝。她看起來像是會讓任何男人樂意相信的女人。

en_text: She ﬂashes a smile at me before turning her attention back to Detective Calhoun. Are they working together?
zh_text: 她對我笑了一笑，接著將注意力轉回到卡爾霍恩警探身上。難道他們狼狽爲奸？

en_text: “Afternoon, Joe. How’s it going there?”
zh_text: 「午安，喬，今天過得如何？」

en_text: I jump and turn and see Schroder standing next to me, sipping from a cup of coffee that I haven’t made. He’s smiling at me. “Fine, Detective Schroder.” “You know her?”
zh_text: 我轉頭看到施羅德警探站在我身邊，啜飲著一杯不是我倒的咖啡。「不錯，施羅德警探。」「你認識她？」

en_text: “Huh?”
He nods his head toward Melissa. “Looked like you recognized her.”
zh_text: 他朝向梅莉莎點頭。「看起來好像你認得她。

en_text: I shake my head. “No.”
zh_text: 我搖頭。「不認得。」

en_text: He grins. “Just staring, huh? Don’t blame you, and don’t feel bad for being caught out.”
zh_text: 他微笑。「那就只是在看人家了，嗯？我不怪你。」

en_text: “Caught out?” I say. Oh, Jesus, it’s come to this, it’s ﬁnally come to this and my gun is in my ofﬁce. I can’t believe it. Weirdly, I feel like crying. “You’re not the only one,” Schroder says. “What?”
zh_text: 她知道我是這裡的清潔工嗎？我的工作服顯然說明了這一點，水桶和拖把也是。她在看到我穿成這樣前就知道了嗎？不過我問錯問題了。我真正需要知道的事情在於她為什麼會在這裡。目前為止還沒有人跑來拿槍指我，要我招供罪行。

en_text: He’s right. Half the men in here are staring at her. “Just don’t let her catch you,” he says, and it’s good advice—better advice than he really knows. He disappears back in the direction he came from, as if he’d only shown up to make chitchat. I’m still standing in the same place I was when I saw Melissa, only now I’m feeling more obvious about it. I need to leave. Do I go for my briefcase in case I need to shoot my way out of here, or do I just head for the door now?
zh_text: 但是如今槍歸建築師小姐所有，就像我也歸她所有一樣。她到底在玩什麼把戲？爲什麼要折磨我、治療我，然後跟蹤我？她今天來是爲了讓我知道誰在掌控大局。我望向我那些刀。看不出來我有機會刺出一條活路。我還有什麼選擇？我已經遭受警方監視了嗎？不。如果她只是想要讓我被警方逮捕，她就不會跑到我的公寓來幫我療傷。

en_text: I carry the bucket and mop back to my ofﬁce, close my door behind me, and grab my briefcase and at the same time I’m opening it, I remember I don’t have my gun anymore. I slump into my chair. I don’t know what to do, with a little more distance between Melissa and my remaining testicle, I can think a little clearer. Melissa didn’t point me out. That’s not why she’s here. She’s here because, just like my gun, she owns me too. This is her game. She’s come here today to make sure I know who’s in control. I get out of my chair. I stare down at the city for a few seconds, the people out there moving quickly through the cold. I take one of the knives out of my briefcase. It’s small and easy to conceal, but I ﬁgure if I’m going down I can take one, maybe two people with me. I slip it into my pocket. When I head into the hallway with the vacuum cleaner, Melissa and Calhoun have gone. They’ll be in the smaller of the two conference rooms up here. It’s similar to an interrogation room, but with nicer décor, designed to get information from nice people in a comfortable way. There will be tea and coffee and a light lunch, nice music. It’s foreplay where the goal is catching a killer. I wish I could be in there listening, and at the same time, I wish I could be a thousand miles away. When I open the door of the main conference room, I see a gaggle of detectives standing around, staring at the board. I expect them to all turn in unison toward me, like I’m a gunslinger entering the local saloon, but only Detective Landry comes over. He’s somewhere in his forties. Has those rugged good looks of a movie actor playing a policeman. His clothes are wrinkled, his sleeves are up, and he looks like the sort of guy about to make a breakthrough. He smells of cigarette smoke.
zh_text: 當我拿著吸塵器回到走廊上時，梅莉莎和卡爾霍恩已經不在了。他們進入小會議室。小會議室跟偵訊室很像，不過裝潢好一點，專門用來從好人口中以舒適的方式取得線索。裡面有茶、咖啡、簡餐和好聽的音樂。那是逮捕兇手的前戲。我希望可以進去旁聽，同時我也希望我能身處千里之外。打開主會議室時，我看到一群警探站在裡面，盯著牆上的佈告板。我期待他們會同時轉過頭來看我，好像我是步入酒館的槍手一樣，不過只有艾力克斯·漢森向我走來。他年過四十，如同扮演警察的電影明星般英俊瀟灑。他衣服很皺，衣袖捲起，看起來像個即將突破案情的傢伙。

en_text: “This probably isn’t a good time, Joe.”
zh_text: 「現在可能不是好時機，喬。」

en_text: “Oh?”
“The room’s pretty clean. Probably won’t need going over for a few more days.”
zh_text: 「會議室很乾淨。可能好幾天都不需要打掃。」

en_text: “Okay, then.”
zh_text: 「那好吧。」

en_text: He pats me on the shoulder. Does he leave his hand there for a second too long? Is he looking at me differently? “Thanks, Joe.”
zh_text: 他拍拍我的肩膀。他的手有在我的肩膀上停留過久嗎？他看我的神情有所不同嗎？「謝謝，喬。」

en_text: I turn toward the door, ﬁghting the temptation to run. I remind myself that I’m the one in control, that I’m the one running this show, but if that were true, I wouldn’t have this God-awful sick feeling in my stomach. Throwing one last glance at the board before I step into the hallway, I see a photograph of a burned car. Christ. I’m learning nothing. I’m out of the loop.
zh_text: 我轉向房門，壓抑著一股想要拔腿就跑的衝動。我提醒自己情況掌握在我手中，是我在主導這場戲，但若果真如此，我心裡就不會有這股超級噁心的感覺。如今真正掌控大局的人是梅莉莎。步入走廊之前，我又瞄了佈告板一眼，看見一張燒毀車輛的照片。天啊。我什麼都不知道。我被排除在外了。

en_text: Then suddenly a chance appears to learn at least something: Detective Wilson Q. Hutton is blubbering toward me, a chocolate bar clutched in his sweaty hand like it’s a tube of insulin. It’s obvious the Q doesn’t stand for quitting. He’s wearing a black turtleneck sweater. Fact is I’ve never seen him wearing anything else. I don’t get the look he’s going for, and I ﬁgure he doesn’t know either. Maybe it makes him feel as though he looks important. Or less fat.
zh_text: 接著突然出現了讓我至少得知一點線索的機會：威爾森·Q·胡頓警探搖搖晃晃地向我走來，汗濕的手中拿著一根巧克力棒，彷彿裡面裝了胰島素一樣。顯然他的Q並不是放棄(Quitting)的意思。他身穿黑色套頭毛衣，儘管警局裡十分悶熱。事實上，我從未見他穿過其他衣服。或許他認爲這樣穿讓他看起來像重要人物，或是看來比較不胖。

en_text: “Afternoon, Joe.”
zh_text: 「午安，喬。」

en_text: “Hi there, Detective Hutton. Looks pretty busy. There something going on?”
zh_text: 「哈囉，胡頓警探。大家好像很忙。出了什麼事嗎？」

en_text: He smiles at me with the same pity in his eyes he always has. “You haven’t heard?”
zh_text: 他眼中帶著一貫的同情向我微笑。「你沒聽說？」

en_text: “Heard what?”
zh_text: 「聽說什麼？」

en_text: “We’ve got a description of the guy.”
zh_text: 「我們弄到了一份兇手的描述。」

en_text: I feel as though I’ve just been punched in the stomach, but I force myself to play Slow Joe. Are these people just playing with me? Is this an elaborate trap to call me out? I reach into my pocket and feel for the knife. A guy like Hutton, I just don’t think the blade is long enough.
zh_text: 我感覺像是肚子被人揍了一拳，不過我強迫自己扮演智障喬。這些傢伙是在耍我嗎？這是一場精心設計的陷阱嗎？

en_text: “How?” I ask, trying to keep my voice under control.
zh_text: 「怎麼弄到的？」我問，努力控制我的語調。

en_text: “There was another victim last night, Joe. Another prostitute. This time a witness saw him driving away from the alleyway where she was dumped.” Jesus, I wonder how Calhoun is feeling now that the woman he paid for sex two months ago has been killed. Is he feeling worse than me? He’ll make the connection with the dead hooker, but will he believe it?
zh_text: 「昨天晚上又有人遇害，喬，又是妓女。這一次有目擊證人看見他從棄屍的巷子裡倒車出來。」老天啊，我心想卡爾霍恩得知他兩個月前嫖過的女人被殺之後會有什麼感覺。感覺會比我還糟嗎？死妓女會讓他聯想到有人在追查他，但是他會相信嗎？

en_text: “Have you caught the bad man yet?”
zh_text: 「你們抓到壞人了沒？」

en_text: Hutton shakes his head. “Not yet. The car used was stolen.”
zh_text: 胡頓搖頭。「還沒。那輛車是偷來的。」

en_text: “You know that already? Wow, you’re smart.”
zh_text: 「你已經知道了？哇，你好聰明。」

en_text: “The car was used to dump another body later in the evening.”
zh_text: 那輛車後來又被用作棄置另外一具屍體。

en_text: “Another prostitute?”
zh_text: 「又是妓女？」

en_text: “I can’t say too much, Joe.” He pauses to take a bite from his chocolate bar, like he needs the energy to come up with the words that he can’t tell me. Chocolate-stained teeth begin mincing the confectionery. A few tiny pieces ﬂake onto the collar of his turtleneck. I’m not sure why he doesn’t just swallow the whole damn thing in one go.
zh_text: 「我不能多說，喬。」他暫停片刻，咬了一口巧克力棒，彷彿他需要能量才能說出他不能告訴我的話。沾有巧克力的牙齒咀嚼口中的零食，一些小碎屑落在高領毛衣的領子上。我不確定他爲什麼不一口吞掉那個可惡的東西。

en_text: “Any suspects?”
zh_text: 「有嫌犯嗎？」

en_text: He shakes his head and keeps chewing. “Better carry on, Joe.” “Sure thing.”
zh_text: 他一邊咀嚼一邊搖頭。「還是去工作吧，喬。」

en_text: I head back to my ofﬁce. My hands are trembling slightly. Calm down. Calm down.
zh_text: 我回到我的辦公室。我的雙手微微顫抖。冷靜。冷靜。

en_text: It’s easy to think, but hard to do. I need to create order from this Goddamn confusion that Melissa has dropped me into. The only problem is I’m coming up with nothing, only more excuses to hurt her. In the end I sneak open my ofﬁce door and glance into the hallway. It’s empty. Could I just leave and follow her? Is it that simple? Will the police let me leave? I wait for thirty minutes, peering out from my ofﬁce every few minutes or so, watching for Melissa, watching for the police escort to take me away. It doesn’t happen, and I start holding out hope that it isn’t going to. I grab the vacuum cleaner and let myself be seen. I mooch around the hallway, sucking dust mites and food crumbs from the carpet, biding my time. Occasionally one or two detectives will come from the conference room and head either to their cubicle, or out to the street, but they don’t glance at me. Other times they simply come to get coffee. They nod and smile at me without really seeing me.
zh_text: 用想的很容易，真要冷靜很難。我必須在梅莉莎丟給我的爛攤子中理出頭緒。唯一的問題在於我什麼辦法都想不到，只有更多傷害她的藉口。最後我偷偷打開辦公室門，瞄了瞄走廊上的景象。空無一人。我可以就這樣溜出去跟蹤她嗎？事情可不可能這麼簡單？我等了三十分鐘，每隔幾分鐘就從辦公室偷看，等待梅莉莎，等待警方將我逮捕。沒人來逮捕我，於是我心中浮現不會被逮捕的期望。我拿起吸塵器，出去露露臉。我在走廊上徘徊，吸著地毯上的灰塵和食物碎片消磨時間。偶爾會有一兩名警探離開會議室，走回辦公隔間或是離開警局，不過他們沒有看我。有時候他們只是出來倒咖啡的。他們對我點頭微笑，渾然不把我當作一回事。

en_text: The day starts to drag. I keep looking at my watch, almost accusing it of lying. I don’t feel so good, and every time I clean a bathroom, I sit in one of the stalls for a few minutes with my face resting in my hands and my fate resting in the hands of those who have sat here before. I keep an eye out for Melissa, but can’t ﬁnd her. I don’t see Calhoun either. Or Schroder.
zh_text: 時間開始變慢。我不斷看錶，差點認定它在說謊。我心情欠佳，每清理一間廁所，我就會坐在馬桶隔間裡幾分鐘，將臉搗在雙掌之間，把我的命運交給之前坐在馬桶上的其他人手裡。我一直在尋找梅莉莎，不過沒看到她。我也沒有看見卡爾霍恩，或是施羅德。

en_text: All the regulars are gone, or maybe they aren’t—maybe they’re just waiting around the corner, watching and waiting. Except for Sally. She’s always there. Just milling around, asking me how I am, how my mother is, asking me if I would like a lift home.
zh_text: 所有廁所的常客都不見了，或許他們沒有不見，或許他們只是等在轉角，默默監視。除了莎莉。她一直都在我的身邊。糾纏著我，問我日子過得如何，我媽好不好，問我要不要搭便車回家。

en_text: I don’t know how, but four thirty eventually arrives. The relief is almost nonexistent, because I have no idea how far I’ll get before somebody calls my name and tells me to stop walking, to get the hell down on the ground, to put my arms behind my back. Back in the hallway, with my briefcase, my hands still trembling, I am barely in time to see that Melissa is only just leaving, being escorted by Detective Calhoun, and I wonder if she has waited around for me to ﬁnish. Nearly three hours she’s been here, talking to detectives. What in the hell has she been saying?
zh_text: 我不知道時間怎麼度過的，不過四點半終於到了。我沒有覺得好一點，因為我不知道什麼時候會有人大喊我的名字，叫我停步，趴在地上，將手抱在腦後。回到走廊上，我帶著公事包，雙手仍在顫抖，剛好看見梅莉莎正在卡爾霍恩警探的護送下離開，我很好奇她是不是在等我下班。她在警局待了將近三個小時，跟警探交談。她到底跟他們說了些什麼？

en_text: I quickly duck back into my ofﬁce and watch from the corner of the door. As she stands there, Detective Landry walks from the elevator. In his hand, sitting across the bottom of a clear plastic bag, is a knife. Not any knife, but my knife. One of my favorites. He’s carrying it as though he’s just found the Holy Grail. Nobody could mistake the look of pride on his face. Melissa and Calhoun head toward him and the elevator, and they pause to talk. I’d love to know what they are saying, and if things go as planned, soon I will. Then Calhoun steps with her into the elevator and the doors slide shut. I rush for the stairwell and race my way to the ground ﬂoor, ignoring the throbbing from my groin. And it’s worth it, because I’m quick enough to see Melissa as she leaves the building. She’s alone now. I head to the door. Nobody puts their hand on my shoulder.
zh_text: 我迅速回到我的辦公室，自門角偷看外面。漢森警探在她等待的時候步出電梯。他手上的塑膠袋裡放著一把刀。不是普通的刀，而是我的刀，我最喜歡的刀之一。沒有人會誤認他臉上的驕傲神情。梅莉莎和卡爾霍恩迎向他和電梯。他們停下來交談。我很想知道他們在聊些什麼，如果一切依照計畫進行的話，我很快就會知道了。接著卡爾霍恩和她一起步入電梯，電梯隨即關門。我衝向樓梯間，急急忙忙來到一樓，完全不顧胯下的刺痛。不過一切都很值得，因為我剛好趕上梅莉莎離開大樓。只剩她一個人了。我走向大門，沒人伸手來搭我的肩膀。

en_text: I turn right. Melissa is heading toward the Avon River, so I take the same route, cross the same road, avoid the same people. The sun has come out overhead, but it doesn’t look like it will be for long, and it’s not helping me feel any warmer. When Melissa reaches the grassy bank, she turns right and keeps moving, staying parallel to the dark water. I do the same, but keep a good ﬁfty yards behind her. I have to be careful, because if she runs from me, I’m in no condition to chase her.
zh_text: 我右轉。梅莉莎朝向雅芳河走，於是我跟了上去，穿越相同的馬路，避開相同的人群。抵達翠綠的河岸時，她轉向右方，繼續前進，與深色的河水保持平行。我也一樣，不過跟她維持五十公尺的距離。我必須小心，因為如果她逃跑的話，以我的身體狀況絕對無法追趕。

en_text: A few moments later she swerves toward a nearby park bench, takes a position sitting at the far end, and looks directly toward me. I stop walking, study the ground like there’s something interesting there. I can feel her still looking at me. When I look up again, she smiles.
zh_text: 幾分鐘後，她突然轉向附近的一張公園長椅，坐在一邊，然後筆直朝我看來。我停止前進，低頭望向下方，彷彿地上有什麼有趣的東西一樣。我感覺到她還在看我。當我再度抬頭時，她面露微笑。

en_text: The long summer is ﬁnally coming to an end, but that’s okay, because she loves autumn. She can’t think of anything better than being outside in a nice nor’west breeze as the leaves are changing color, but as much as she loves it, she dreads the months that are to follow. Winter brings with it a grimy ﬁlm of depression that settles down over the city and soaks into the buildings and the plants and the people, everything touched by rain and the cold wind and the smog.
zh_text: 這將會是個漫長的夏天，不過沒關係，因為她熱愛夏天。她想不出有什麼能比出門吹吹西北風、身處一群對生命充滿希望的人們之中更美好的事情。夏天就會給她這種感覺。接著冬天到來，將這一切通通奪走，讓整座城市籠罩在沮喪氣息之中，將一切浸泡在雨水、冷風以及煙霧裡。

en_text: Sally is confused. About Joe. About his lies.
zh_text: 莎莉感到困惑，喬令她困惑，他的謊言令她困惑。

en_text: She understands why he lied about his mother being sick. That was a lie she was happy to go along with, because it protected him. Joe didn’t want to be known as the man who had a testicle pulped by a pair of pliers. If something like that had ever happened to Martin, well, she would have wanted somebody like her to have looked out for him. All she can do now is hope the penicillin she gave Joe will help the healing process and ﬁght off any infection. It should. If not he’ll have to go to a hospital. He won’t have a choice.
zh_text: 她了解他為什麼要謊稱母親生病。她很樂意配合這個謊言，因為這樣說能夠保護他。喬不想讓人知道有人拿鉗子夾爆他的睾丸。如果這種事情發生在馬丁身上——好吧，她會希望有個像她這樣的人去照顧他。如今她只能期望她帶給喬的盤尼西林足以幫助他復原，並且避免感染。應該可以。如果不行的話，他就得去醫院。他沒得選擇。

en_text: She had shown up the day he had been attacked, and each of the following three days—on one of those occasions she had found him passed out on the ﬂoor. She wanted to go back the next day too, but her father had had a bad fall and she’d been forced to weigh up her priorities. Family had to come ﬁrst. She’d still gone to work—she had no more sick days— but from there she’d gone straight home and helped with her father. He’d dislocated a hip and broken a collarbone, but he was mending.
zh_text: 她在他遇襲的當天去過他家，之後三天也都有去：其中有一次她發現他昏倒在地板上。後來她還想再去，不過她爸不小心摔倒，於是她被迫必須優先照顧她爸。家人總是優先考量。她還得去上班——她沒有病假可請——不過一下班她就會直接回家，幫忙照顧父親。他髖骨脫臼，還摔斷了一根鎖骨，不過情況逐漸好轉。

en_text: She was going to go back and see Joe on Monday—he still had stitches that needed removing—but he’d shown up at work. They didn’t speak directly of the attack. She wants to talk him into going to the police for help, but not at work.
zh_text: 她本來打算禮拜一回去探望喬——他的縫線還沒拆除——不過他來上班了。他們沒有直接談論遇襲的事情。她很想勸他去找警方幫忙，不過不能在上班時間。

en_text: She doesn’t like the fact that he lied to her about only seeing the crimescene photographs in the conference room. He knows it’s stealing, but he’s obviously reluctant to open up to her about it. The man with the big smile looks so innocent that she can’t imagine him deliberately lying, but the man who smiled at her between the elevator doors two weeks ago, well, that was a different Joe, wasn’t it? That was a Joe that looked capable of . . .
zh_text: 她不喜歡他騙她說只有在會議室裡見過犯罪現場照片。他知道那是偷竊的行爲，不過他顯然不願意對她坦白。她實在很難想像這個臉上掛著無辜大微笑的男人竟然會刻意說謊，不過兩個禮拜前在電梯門口朝她微笑的男人，好吧，那是個截然不同的喬，不是嗎？那是看起來有能力……有能力怎樣？做任何事？

en_text: Of what? Of anything? No. Not anything. But he looked capable of lying. He looked smooth, he looked calculating, as if he knew exactly what was going on. She reminds herself it was a ﬂuke smile, that Joe isn’t like that at all. But why the lies?
zh_text: 不。不是任何事。不過看起來像是有能力騙人的樣子。他看起來很冷靜、很精明，彷彿他很清楚周遭所發生的一切。她提醒自己喬只是剛好笑成那樣，他根本不是那種人。

en_text: Every time she stirs around the possibilities in her head, one keeps on coming up to the surface: Joe is being forced to do something he doesn’t want to do. Therefore somebody needs to help him, and it’s up to her. It’s her Christian duty to make sure no harm comes to him.
zh_text: 每當她在心裡盤算種種可能時，一個想法就會不斷浮現腦海：有人強迫喬做一些他不想做的事情。這表示他需要幫助，而只有她能幫他。確保他不會受到傷害乃是她身爲教徒的責任。

en_text: Joe has been nervous and anxious most of the day, more so this afternoon, and she suspects why: the person pressuring him to bring home information has asked him for more. Of course she still can’t ﬁgure out why the folders would still be in Joe’s apartment and not in the possession of the man who attacked him, but she ﬁgures it must have something to do with timing. Perhaps Joe forgot to take the folders with him to a meeting and made the man angry. Perhaps those folders aren’t at Joe’s anymore, but with the man who is threatening him. The only way to know for sure is to keep an eye on Joe. The same way Joe seems to be keeping an eye on the woman who has come to talk to the detectives—which, if Sally is truthful, makes her feel a little jealous. It isn’t only Joe keeping an eye on her—it’s most of the men in the department.
zh_text: 那天大部分的時間裡，喬看起來都很緊張不安，特別是下午，而她想她知道原因：強迫他帶資料回家的人又要他帶更多資料。當然她還想不透爲什麼那些檔案夾還留在喬的公寓裡，而沒有落入暴徒手中，不過她認爲一定是跟時機有關。或許喬忘記把檔案帶去，結果激怒了對方。或許此刻那些檔案已經不在喬那裡，而是被威脅他的人拿走了。唯一弄清楚此事的方法就是持續關注喬，就像喬在關注那個跑來找警探談話的女人一樣。

en_text: Like everybody else, Sally has heard the rumors ﬂying around the station. This woman has seen something that might bring the case to a close. Perhaps then Joe will be safe.
zh_text: 跟所有人一樣，莎莉聽說了已經傳遍整個警局的傳聞。這個女人目擊了可能導致破案的事件。或許到時候喬就安全了。

en_text: Watching Joe watching the woman was unnerving. His fascination was so obvious that at one point Sally was sure he must have known her. But of course he was just learning what he could, so he would have something to tell his tormentor to save him from another attack.
zh_text: 看著喬盯著那個女人給她一種不安的感覺。他專注的程度明顯到讓莎莉覺得他一定認識那個女人。不過他當然只是在想辦法探聽消息而已，好回去告訴折磨他的人，以免再度遭受毆打。

en_text: Standing outside, watching Joe from the corner where he can’t see her, she cannot understand why he would have approached the woman, but she will keep on watching until she can ﬁnally help Joe out of whatever mess he has got into.
zh_text: 站在室外，從隱密的街角注視著喬，她無法了解他爲什麼會走到那個女人身邊，不過她會持續觀察，直到她終於幫喬脫離這池渾水爲止。

en_text: The Avon is full of ducks, beer cans, and empty chip bags. Friday night’s urine has drifted to wherever the hell urine drifts to. Patches of riverweed ﬂoat among the litter. Somebody—the guy with the worst fucking job in the world—has come along and picked up all the used condoms. Strangely, the view is still pleasant. The dark water reﬂects the sunlight and plays with the shadows, though I’m not really a nature lover. You could pave the whole river in concrete and I wouldn’t care.
zh_text: 雅芳河上隨處可見鴨子、啤酒罐，以及空的零食袋。禮拜五晚上的尿液全都漂到該漂的地方去了。還有大片野草漂在這堆垃圾之間。某人——擁有全世界最爛的工作的傢伙——已經把河裡所有用過的保險套都撿起來了。奇怪的是，這種景色依然令人心曠神怡。深色的水面反射陽光，產生奇特的光影變幻，不過我算不上是什麼自然愛好者。就算把整條河給填平了，我都不在乎。

en_text: As I approach her, Melissa stops watching me, as if I’m not even important enough for her to keep an eye on, and she doesn’t look back up at me until I’m only a meter away. I become aware of how painful my crotch still is. Like the remaining testicle is feeling pangs of loss, and is now feeling fear being in the presence of the woman who took away its brother. She remains sitting. My heart is beating hard, in time with my throbbing testicle. I can’t fathom why I’m suddenly so afraid.
zh_text: 來到她面前時，梅莉莎不再看我，彷彿對我不屑一顧般。數秒鐘後，她轉向我。我這才發現胯下有多疼痛。彷彿我剩下的那顆睾丸感應到了失去兄弟的痛苦，並且對於接近這個奪走它兄弟的女人而感到恐懼。我在一公尺外停步。她繼續坐著。我心跳劇烈，配合睾丸的抽痛。我不了解爲什麼我突然這麼害怕。

en_text: “Take a seat, Joe.” She keeps a tight hold of her smile.
zh_text: 「請坐，喬。」她臉上笑容不減。

en_text: I shake my head. “Next to you? You’re kidding.”
zh_text: 我搖頭。「坐妳旁邊？妳在開玩笑？」

en_text: “You still upset with me? Come on, Joe. It’s time to move on.”
zh_text: 「你還在生我的氣？拜託，喬，人生總要繼續走下去。」

en_text: Move on? I heard that after Dad died. People hear it all the time. Calhoun probably heard it after his son hanged himself. Are we living in such a throwaway society that we’re not even allowed to hang on to our hatred and remorse? I want to leap forward and show her that I’ll move on once I’ve taken care of a few things. But I can’t. Too many people around. Too many risks. Even if I could break her neck and get away, I have no idea where my gun is. I’m guessing it’s with somebody who will send it to the police if something ever happens to her.
zh_text: 繼續走下去？老爸死後我常聽人這麼說。人們常常會聽到這句話。卡爾霍恩在他兒子上吊自殺後或許也曾聽過。難道這個用過即丢的社會已經不容許我們懷抱仇恨與報復的心理了嗎？我很想撲上前去，讓她了解我只要解決一些小事，立刻就能繼續我的人生。但是我不能這麼做。附近太多人。風險太高了。就算我能扭斷她的脖子並且逃離現場，我也不知道我的槍在何處。我猜它就放在某個一旦她出事就會將槍轉交警方的人手中。

en_text: “Quite the job you have, Joe.”
zh_text: 你的工作不錯，喬。

en_text: I shrug. I see where she’s going with this, but force her to carry on.
zh_text: 我聳肩。我知道她想說什麼，不過還是讓她繼續下去。

en_text: “The cleaner at the police station. That must allow you access to some privileged information—evidence, reports, photographs. It must be fun seeing where the investigations are going. Tell me, did you ever want to become a cop? Did you try and fail? Or not try because you knew they’d realize what sick thoughts you harbored?”
zh_text: 「警局清潔工。這讓你有辦法接觸一般人無法接觸的資料——證據、報告、照片。觀察調查發展的感覺一定很棒。告訴我，你有沒有想過當警察？你是不是試過，結果失敗了？或是沒有嘗試，因為你知道他們會發現你腦中那些變態思想？」

en_text: “How about you, Melissa? Did you ever try?”
zh_text: 「妳呢，梅莉莎？妳有嘗試過嗎？」

en_text: “Do you ever try to contaminate the evidence?”
zh_text: 「你有試過竄改證據嗎？」

en_text: If this is all she has to say, then I’m not in any trouble. “You’re jealous.”
zh_text: 如果她想問的只有這些，那我就可以放心了。「妳在嫉妒？」「嫉妒你？」

en_text: “Of you?” “Of me working among all those cops, all that information.”
zh_text: 「嫉妒我跟這麼多警察一起工作，能夠取得這麼多資訊。」

en_text: She raises her left hand to her lips and begins rubbing her ﬁnger slowly back and forth, the same way she did the other night. She moistens her ﬁnger and keeps rubbing. Then she quickly pulls it away, brushes it against her chest on the way down, and rests it in her lap.
zh_text: 她伸起左手，將手指放入雙唇之間輕輕吸吮，就像那天晚上一樣。她吮濕了手指，然後繼續吸吮。接著她迅速抽出手指，掠過她的胸口，最後放上大腿。

en_text: “We’re not that different, you and I, Joe.” “I doubt that.”
zh_text: 「我們沒有那麼大的不同，你和我，喬。

en_text: “Do you notice the smell in there?”
zh_text: 「你有注意到那裡的味道嗎？」

en_text: “What smell?”
zh_text: 「什麼味道？」

en_text: “Working there every day, you’re probably used to it. But there’s this smell in there. Smells slightly like sweat and damp blood, but it’s power. Power and control.”
zh_text: 你每天都在警局工作，或許已經習以爲常。那裡有股味道。有點像汗，有點像血，不過那是權力的味道。權力與支配。

en_text: “It’s the air-conditioning.”
zh_text: 「那是空调的味道。」

en_text: “It was fun in there today, Joe. I got to see something you see every day. Seems like menial work for somebody like yourself.”
zh_text: 「今天在警局很有趣，喬。我有機會見識你每天都能看到的東西。那份工作對你這種人來說似乎有點低賤。」

en_text: “I do it for the love of the job.”
zh_text: 「我做這份工作是因為我熱愛這份工作。

en_text: “Does it pay well?”
zh_text: 「薪水優嗎？」

en_text: “Does it need to?”
zh_text: 「需要優嗎？」

en_text: “You know what confuses me?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你知道最讓我困擾的是什麼嗎？」

en_text: Her smile stretches. “How you can afford an expensive gun, nice clothes, a good watch, yet you live in a rat hole of an apartment.” I hate the fact that she’s been in my apartment. I hate the fact that this is the woman who tidied up my messy wound. No way in hell am I going to thank her for that. “I have a good accountant.”
zh_text: 她微笑擴大。「就是在有能力購買昂貴手槍、上好服飾、精美手錶的情況下，你卻依然住在那種破爛地方。」我不喜歡她到過我家這個事實。我不喜歡幫我療傷的就是這個女人。我打死都不會向她道謝的。「我有個高明的會計師。」

en_text: “Being a cleaner pays well, huh?”
zh_text: 「清潔工的收入不錯，呃？」

en_text: “It pays the bills.”
zh_text: 足以支付帳單。

en_text: “Lucky you earn cash from other areas.”
zh_text: 「幸好你能從其他地方賺取現金。」

en_text: “What’s your point?”
zh_text: 「妳到底想說什麼？」

en_text: “My point is you must have some money stored away.”
zh_text: 我想說你一定藏了不少錢。

en_text: “I have a couple of hundred dollars. Why?”
zh_text: 「我是有幾百塊錢。幹嘛？」

en_text: “Bullshit, Joe. How much you got?”
zh_text: 「狗屁，喬。你到底有多少錢？」

en_text: “I just told you.”
zh_text: 「我剛剛說了。」

en_text: “No you didn’t. It’s time you were honest with your partner, Joe.”
zh_text: 「不，你沒有。你該對你的夥伴坦白，喬。」

en_text: “What?” I ask, and suddenly I know what game we’re playing.
zh_text: 「什麼？」我問，我突然知道我們在玩什麼遊戲了。

en_text: “You heard,” she says.
zh_text: 「你聽到了。」

en_text: “Obviously I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「顯然沒有。」

en_text: She rolls her head back and laughs. Hard. This really pisses me off. Nobody’s laughed at me like that since those days at school when the laughter accompanied the words Numb Nuts everywhere I went. Other people are looking around. Nothing I can do but wait her out. Finally she ﬁnishes. “We’re partners, Joe, whether you like it or not. Especially after what I’ve just done for you.”
zh_text: 她仰頭大笑。笑得很用力。這下真把我給惹毛了。自從學校那段走到哪裡都被人一邊嘲笑一邊叫我「麻痺蛋蛋」日子以來，我再也沒有被人這樣笑過了。旁邊的人轉頭來看。我什麼都不能做，只能等她笑完。最後她終於笑完了。「我們是夥伴，喬，不管你喜不喜歡。特別在我爲你做了那件事後。」

en_text: “And what’s that?”
zh_text: 「什麼事？」

en_text: “Given the police a composite of what you look like.”
zh_text: 跟警方描述你的長相。

en_text: I tighten my ﬁsts.
zh_text: 我緊緊握拳。

en_text: “Calm down, big guy. I gave them a description of somebody else.” “Why?” But I know the answer: it’s because she wants money.
zh_text: 冷靜點，大傢伙。我描述的是另外一個人的長相。「爲什麼？」我知道答案：因爲她要錢。

en_text: “Why not?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼不呢？」

en_text: “Stop being so damn evasive,” I say.
zh_text: 不要一直逃避問題。我說。

en_text: “You don’t like it? What do you like, Joe?” “How about I tell you what I’d like to do?”
zh_text: 你不喜歡？你喜歡怎樣，喬？不如告訴妳我想怎樣？

en_text: “I can imagine. You know,” she says, “it was nice to go in there and talk to the detectives, to see for myself just how smart they really are, or, in this case, just how smart they aren’t. They’re easier to fool than I could ever have imagined. I always saw them differently, I guess. But they’re just people, Joe. Real people, like you and me. I guess that’s why you’re so successful. It was disappointing, really. In a way.”
zh_text: 「我可以想像。你知道，」她說。「跑去警局跟警探聊天的感覺不錯，這樣可以親眼看看他們有多聰明，或是在這個案例裡，有多不聰明。他們比我想像中好騙多了。我一直以爲他們與衆不同，我猜。不過他們只是平凡人，喬。真實的人，就像你和我。我猜想這就是你如此成功的原因。這很令人失望，真的。就某方面而言。」

en_text: “I’m not sure there’s anybody like you and me,” I say.
zh_text: 我不確定世界上還有像妳和我這種人。」我說。

en_text: Slowly she nods. “I guess you’re right.”
zh_text: 她緩緩點頭。「我想你說得對。」

en_text: “So why did you do it? Why go in there?”
zh_text: 「那妳爲什麼要那麼做？爲什麼要去警局？」

en_text: “For the money.”
zh_text: 「爲了錢。」

en_text: “We’re back to that, huh? You really ought to start listening. Let me explain it a little slower for you. I. Don’t. Have. Any. Money.”
zh_text: 「又回到錢上面了，呃？妳真的應該開始聽我說話。讓我放慢一點解釋給妳聽。我·沒·有·錢。」

en_text: “Come now, Joe, don’t be so modest. I’m sure that if you don’t have any money, a man of your abilities would be able to get money. A hundred grand should do.”
zh_text: 「夠了，喬，不要這麼謙虛。我很肯定就算你沒錢，像你這麼能幹的男人也有辦法弄到錢。十萬塊就夠了。」

en_text: “You’ve seen my place. How do you suggest I get that kind of money?”
zh_text: 妳到過我家。妳打算要我去哪裡生那種數目出來？

en_text: “You seem to be full of questions, Joe, when you should only be full of answers. Yes and no. That’s all I want to hear from you.” “Look, it just isn’t possible to raise that kind of cash.”
zh_text: 「你似乎有很多問題，喬，偏偏你應該充滿答案才對。給不給。我只想聽答案。」「聽著，我不可能弄到那麼多錢。」

en_text: “You could always turn yourself in. That’d cover half.”
zh_text: 你可以去自首。那就夠付一半了。

en_text: Melissa is referring to the ﬁfty-thousand-dollar government reward available to whoever provides the information that gets me caught. I can’t believe it’s so little, and surely it can’t stay that way. If Melissa wanted that kind of cash, she would have turned me in already. Either it isn’t about the money, or she’s waiting for it to climb up in value before she turns me in. She’ll just torment me and make some cash on the side ﬁrst. I’m just an investment for her. It’s like she’s buying a piece of stock.
zh_text: 梅莉莎指的是那筆發給任何能夠提供線索導致我落網之人的五萬塊政府懸賞。我不敢相信賞金這麼少，因為光是幾年前我殺的第一個人就已經提供過同等金額的賞金了。這證明了有些人的性命就是比其他人值錢。要抓到我光是這點賞金絕對不夠。如果梅莉莎只要這點錢，直接把我交給警方就好了。要嘛就是她並非當真要錢，不然她就是要等賞金升高之後再把我交出去。她打算持續折磨我，並且趁機弄點油水。對她而言，我只是一項投資。就跟買股票一樣。

en_text: “I’m going to kill you. You do know that, don’t you?” I tell her. “You know, Joe, I’m going to enjoy working with you. You really are quite a laugh.” She stands up, straightens her tailored outﬁt, sweeps her hair back. She’s so beautiful it’s heartbreaking. I wish she were dead. She hands me a box.
zh_text: 「我會殺了妳。妳知道這點，對吧？」你知道，喬，我一定會享受跟你共事的時光。你真的很好笑。」她站起身來，整理套裝，將頭髮撩到身後。她美到令我心碎。我真希望她死了。這時她交給我一個盒子。

en_text: “What’s this?”
zh_text: 「什麼玩意兒？」

en_text: “A cell phone. Keep it on you, because I’ll be calling in a couple of days.”
zh_text: 手機。帶在身上，我過兩天會打電話給你。

en_text: “When?”
zh_text: 「什麼時候？」

en_text: “Five o’clock. Friday.”
zh_text: 「五點。禮拜五。」

en_text: I look at the box. The phone is brand new. I wonder if she bought it with cash she stole from the dead hooker. “You know, Joe, I think this is the beginning of a beautiful relationship. Isn’t that what they say?”
zh_text: 我看著那盒子。電話是全新的。我在想她是不是用從妓女身上搜刮來的現金買的。「你知道，喬，我認爲這是一段美妙關係的開始。他們是不是這麼說的？」

en_text: It isn’t what I say. So I tell her to go to hell.
zh_text: 我不是這麼說的，所以我叫她去死。

en_text: “Obviously, it goes without saying that if anything should happen to me, the remaining evidence I have on you goes directly to the police, along with a detailed statement.”
zh_text: 「顯然不用我提醒你，如果我出了什麼事，剩下的證據就會直接送交警方，外加一份鉅細靡遺的證詞。」

en_text: Sure. It isn’t the only thing that goes without saying. Obviously I’m going to kill this woman at some point. I just need to do my homework ﬁrst. That’s something I’m good at. Life’s all about homework. And I have until Friday at ﬁve o’clock to get my assignment done. She starts telling me the rules of her game. I’m to charge the phone when I get home because she’ll be in touch. She reminds me that she still has my gun, which has my ﬁngerprints on it. It can be used as a future murder weapon. She tells me she wiped my ﬁngerprints off the knife before telling the police where they could ﬁnd it, but it doesn’t brighten this nightmare.
zh_text: 當然。這並非唯一不需要提醒的事情。顯然我必須找機會殺死這個女人。我只是得先做點功課。這是我很擅長的事情。人生就是不斷地做功課。而這份功課得在禮拜五五點之前做完。她開始說明她的遊戲規則。我回家後必須將手機充電，因為她會跟我聯絡。她提醒我槍還在她手中，上面還有我的指紋。那把槍未來可能成爲謀殺兇器。她說她在告訴警方上哪兒去找我的刀前已經抹除了刀上的指紋，不過這並沒有解除這場惡夢。

en_text: After she walks away, I stare at the water, drumming my ﬁngers against the top of my briefcase while watching the birds. I tap some rhythm that I’ve never heard before. It seems my life is following that rhythm. Some of the ducks look back at me. Perhaps they want money too.
zh_text: 她離開後，我注視著河面，一邊看鳥一邊用手指敲打公事包。我敲著我從未聽過的節奏，我的生活彷彿都跟著這個節奏在走。有些鴨子回應我的目光，或許牠們也想要錢。

en_text: One hundred thousand dollars is an amount I can’t fully comprehend, and I already know I’ll never be able to raise it. Does Melissa know that too? Even if by some miracle I could get the money, nothing is stopping her from asking me for more in another year, or another month, or even another day.
zh_text: 十萬塊是一筆超過我理解範圍的大錢，我也很清楚我絕不可能籌到這筆錢。梅莉莎是不是也知道這一點？就算奇蹟出現，我弄到了這筆錢，誰知道她會不會在一年後又來煩我，或是一個月後，甚至是隔天。

en_text: The bus driver is some bored forty-year-old guy who wears a hearing aid and yells Hello at me as I get on, and Have a nice day when I leave, even though the day is winding down. When I get home the light on my answering machine is ﬂashing. I push it, only to hear my mother’s voice, insisting I go around there for dinner tonight. When she insists, it’s best I go. She also tells me Walt Chadwick called and asked her out for dinner. She’s accepted, and tells me of their entire phone call until my machine eagerly runs out of tape.
zh_text: 公車司機是個四十來歲的無趣男子，戴著助聽器，在我上車時對我大喊哈囉，又在我下車時大聲祝我有個愉快的一天。當我到家時，答錄機的燈閃個不停。我按下按鈕，聽到我媽的聲音堅持要我今晚過去吃飯。每當她堅持時，我最好還是過去一趟。她也告訴我華特·查德維克打電話來約她吃飯。她同意了，然後把電話裡的內容通通講一遍，直到我的答錄機迫不及待地用光錄音帶爲止。

en_text: When I open the bathroom door the cat races out, and I feel bad because I’d actually forgotten about him. I take a shower, clean myself up, and dress in tidy clothes, hoping Mom won’t be able to ﬁnd anything in my appearance to complain about. I put the cat back into the bathroom when I ﬁnish, making him a promise that I’ll pick up some food later on tonight. I steal a car and park a block away from Mom’s house. The sound of the beach brings a smile to my face. I imagine walking down there and going for a swim. I don’t imagine hard enough to get wet.
zh_text: 我打開浴室門，那隻貓立刻衝出，我覺得有點過意不去，因為我完全忘記牠的存在。我沖了個澡，梳洗乾淨，然後換上整齊的服裝，希望媽沒辦法挑剔我的打扮。弄好之後，我把貓放回浴室，向牠保證晚上會帶吃的回來。我偷了輛車，停在距離我媽家一條街外的地方。海灘的聲音令我面露微笑，我想像自己在海灘上漫步，以及下海游泳的樣子。不過我並不想當真弄濕自己。

en_text: I’m halfway to the door when Mom opens it and comes outside. She looks better than I’ve seen her in years. Before I can even say anything, she’s hugging me. I hug her back—while subtly shielding my crotch—to stop her from clipping me over the ear.
zh_text: 快到門口時，老媽開門出來。她看起來比過去幾年更有精神。在我開口之前，她將我一把抱住。我也抱著她——巧妙地擋住胯下——以免她抱得太緊。

en_text: “I’m so happy to see you, Joe.”
zh_text: 「真高興見到你，喬。」

en_text: “I’m happy to see you too, Mom.”
zh_text: 「我也很高興見到妳，媽。」

en_text: She pulls away from me, but keeps her hands on my shoulders. “Walt’s taking me out to lunch tomorrow. You know, I haven’t seen Walt since the funeral, and your father’s been gone six years now.”
zh_text: 她鬆開我，不過雙手還是搭在我的肩膀上。「華特明天要帶我出去吃午飯。你知道，葬禮過後我就沒有見過華特，而你爸已經去世六年了。」

en_text: “Eight years, Mom.”
zh_text: 「八年了，媽。」

en_text: “Time does ﬂy,” she says, then leads me inside.
zh_text: 「時光飛逝。」她說，然後帶我進去。

en_text: It ﬂies when you’re having fun. I can’t see how it could have ﬂown for Mom, though. “So where are you going?” I ask.
zh_text: 時光會在人快樂的時候飛逝。不過我看不出媽的時間爲什麼會飛逝。「你們要上哪兒去？」我問。

en_text: “He hasn’t told me. Said it’s a surprise. He’s picking me up around eleven o’clock.”
zh_text: 「他沒告訴我。說是驚喜。他會在十一點左右過來接我。」

en_text: “That’s good.”
zh_text: 「那很好。」

en_text: “I’m going to go like this.” She twirls around to show me her dress, an ugly thing with long sleeves that looks like it’s been made from recycled sackcloth, then dipped in blood. “What do you think?”
zh_text: 「我打算穿這樣。」她旋轉一圈，讓我看清楚她的衣服，醜得要命，袖子看起來像用回收麻布做出來後再拿去泡血。「你覺得如何？」

en_text: “I can’t remember the last time you looked so good, or so happy, Mom.”
zh_text: 「我想不起來上次看妳這麼開心、這麼美麗是什麼時候，媽。」

en_text: “You’re saying I never look happy?”
zh_text: 「你是說我一直都不開心？」

en_text: “I’m not saying that at all.”
zh_text: 「我完全不是那個意思。」

en_text: She frowns. “So, you’re saying I never look any good, then.”
zh_text: 她皺眉。「那你是說我一直都不美麗了？」

en_text: “I’m not saying that either.”
zh_text: 「我也不是那個意思。」

en_text: “Then what are you saying, Joe?” she snaps. “That I don’t deserve to be happy?”
zh_text: 那你是什麼意思，喬？」她大聲道。「我沒資格過快樂的日子？

en_text: “I’m not trying to say anything,” I say, “other than you look really nice. I’m sure Walt will be thrilled.” I manage to say the right thing, because her face breaks out in a smile. “You think so?”
zh_text: 「我什麼意思都沒有。」我說。「除了妳看起來很美。我敢肯定華特會很開心的。」我終於說對話了，因為她臉上露出一絲微笑。「你這麼認爲？」

en_text: “He’d be crazy not to think so.”
zh_text: 「他要不開心的話肯定是瘋了。」

en_text: “You don’t have a problem with it?”
zh_text: 「你對此沒有意見？」

en_text: “A problem? With what?”
zh_text: 「意見？什麼意見？」

en_text: “Your father has been gone six years now—” “Eight.”
zh_text: 「你爸已經去世六年了……」八年。

en_text: “And I’m only going to lunch with Walt. I’m not marrying him. I’m not asking you to call him Dad.” “I know that.”
zh_text: 「而我只是跟華特去吃個午飯。我不是要嫁給他。我不是要你叫他爸爸。」「我知道。」

en_text: She leans forward, and instead of hitting me, she hugs me again. “We have you to thank for this, Joe,” she whispers. “If it wasn’t for you, he would never have called.”
zh_text: 她湊上前來，不是要打我，而是又來抱我。「這都得要歸功於你，喬。」她低聲道。「要不是你的話，他絕對不會打電話來。」

en_text: She dishes dinner. Instead of meatloaf, she’s cooked up one of the chickens she bought on special last week. It’s too damn big for two people, but she’ll throw half of it into the fridge as leftovers. Thankfully she’s cooked the chicken to perfection. It’s one thing my mother manages to get right. It’s juicy and full of ﬂavor, and chicken fat starts dripping down my ﬁngers.
zh_text: 她端出晚餐。今天不吃烤肉餅，而是上禮拜特價的雞肉。那隻雞大到兩個人根本吃不完，不過她會把剩菜丟回冰箱。幸虧她燒得一手好雞。那是我媽唯一做對的事情。那隻雞香嫩多汁，雞油自我的指尖滴落。

en_text:
“I’ll ring you tomorrow night, Joe, and tell you all about our lunch.”
“Uh huh.”
zh_text:
「我明天晚上打電話給你，喬，告訴你午餐的事情。」
「嗯哼。」

en_text: “Maybe this weekend the three of us can go out for dinner. Would you like that?”
zh_text: 「或許這個週末我們三個可以共進晚餐。你想要嗎？」

en_text: “Sure. That’d be nice,” I say, unable to think of anything worse. I clutch at a napkin Mom gave me. She’s always saying I’m a sloppy eater. She takes the empty plates and begins to clean up. I wrap some chicken into a napkin and put it into my briefcase for the cat. My hands are covered in chicken fat. “I’m just going to wash my hands, okay, Mom?”
zh_text: 「當然。那樣很好。」我說，完全想不出比這更糟糕的事情。我接過媽遞來的一條餐巾。她總是說我吃相很難看。她清空餐桌，開始洗碗。我拿餐巾包了點雞肉，放進公事包給貓吃。我的手上都是雞油。

en_text: “Good boy, Joe.”
zh_text: 「好孩子，喬。」

en_text: I walk to the bathroom, eating a piece of chicken on the way. Stepping past the toilet brings images of her sitting in there with her nightgown hitched up around her waist, her glasses resting on the tip of her nose as she puts a few more pieces of her jigsaw puzzle into place. I crouch to my knees and hang my head, focus my eyes on the bath mat. The nausea starts to fade. When I turn on the bathroom light, my hand slips from the switch. I pull back the shower curtain. Mom has one of those combined shower baths, but she always uses the shower. I try to turn on the tap, but my hands keep slipping off it, so I crouch down and begin smearing the chicken fat at the end of the bath instead. I spend a minute spreading it out, covering a good-sized area. It comes off my ﬁngers easily enough, and off my palms. It’s clear too, so Mom won’t notice the mess. The only way she’ll see it is if the angle and light are just right. I eat the rest of the chicken. It’s cold now. I grab the tap, and this time it turns easily enough. I wash my hands, then head back to the kitchen.
zh_text: 我前往浴室，邊走邊吃一塊雞。走過馬桶就讓我想到她穿著沾了大便的睡衣坐在上面，戴著眼鏡拼拼圖的模樣。我蹲在地上，垂頭喪氣，注視地毯。噁心感開始消失。打開浴室燈時，我的手在開關上滑了一下。我拉開浴簾。媽的浴室有淋浴又有澡盆，不過她總是用淋浴的。我試著打開水龍頭，不過我的手一直滑開，於是我蹲下去，把雞油擦在澡盆裡。我花了一分鐘的時間塗抹均勻，把澡盆弄得油油的。雞油輕易離開我的手指及掌心。油是透明的，所以老媽不會發現。除非角度跟光線剛好才有可能看見。我吃掉剩下的雞塊。雞已經冷了。我握住水龍頭，這一次輕鬆轉開。我洗了洗手，然後走回廚房。

en_text: “Walt was so nice on the phone, Joe.”
zh_text: 「華特在電話裡很有禮貌，喬。」

en_text: Walt. I’m regretting letting him go. “He seemed nice, Mom.”
zh_text: 華特。我有點後悔放過他了。「他似乎不錯，媽。」

en_text: I sit at the dining table while she ﬁnishes off the dishes. I offer to dry them, but she says no. I keep watching her, wondering how this could be the woman who gave me life. How can she think I’m gay? What have I done to this woman to make her possibly think that? I’m her son, and she won’t even give me the beneﬁt of the doubt.
zh_text: 我坐在餐桌上等她清洗餐盤。我說要幫忙擦乾，不過她拒絕了。我一直看著她，懷疑我怎麼可能是這個女人的。她怎麼會以為我是同性戀？我對這個女人做了什麼事情居然讓她以為我是同性戀？我是她兒子，而她竟然不由分說就認定我是同性戀。

en_text: I’m not gay, Mom. I’m not gay.
zh_text: 我不是同性戀，媽。我不是同性戀。

en_text: She drones on about Walt for another hour or so before ﬁnally letting me leave. As I stand on the doorstep, surrounded by night and the sound of the beach and by the muggy air touching my damp skin, I glance up at the stars, all of them overlooking my mother. One day her spirit will be ﬂoating up there, ﬁnding Heaven and ﬁnding God. She’ll be off to talk to Dad again.
zh_text: 她語氣單調地講了一小時華特的事情，然後終於讓我離開。當我站在門口台階上，身處夜色、海灘的聲音以及悶熱的空氣中時，我抬頭望向星空，它們全都在看顧著我媽。有一天，她的靈魂將會飄上天空，找到天堂，找到上帝。到時候她就能再度跟老爸聊天了。

en_text: I start grinning. Both God and Dad are going to be in for a hard time. I give her a hug before I go. I’ll miss her.
zh_text: 我開始微笑。到時候上帝和老爸的日子就不好過了。我離開前抱了她一下。我會想念她的。

en_text: I park the same stolen car a block from home. Friday is quickly approaching and . . . Jesus Christ!
zh_text: 我將同一輛偷來的車停在我家一條街口外。禮拜五很快就會來臨，而……耶穌基督啊！

en_text: I drop my briefcase and run over to the goldﬁsh bowl. Some of the knives slip out of their restraints and they sound like drum cymbals being smashed. I put both hands onto the glass bowl. The water inside is murky. A few dozen scales are ﬂoating on the surface. I thrust my hand in and grope for either of my ﬁsh and, while I’m searching, I ﬁnd them with my eyes. One is in front of my bed. The other near the kitchen. Each is covered in bloodless scratches. Melissa’s message is obvious. I make my way over to Pickle when the cat runs out from beneath the bed, hooks the dead ﬁsh in its claws, ﬁres it across the room, chases it, gets it in its mouth, then runs back toward the bed. The ﬁsh falls from its mouth, but the cat keeps on running, either knowing it’s been spotted and is about to be in a world of trouble, or still thinking it has the ﬁsh in its mouth. Either way, it’s running as if its leg was never broken, and I realize that Melissa hasn’t done this at all.
zh_text: 我丢下我的公事包，衝到金魚缸前。幾把刀滑出刀套，聽起來像是銅鈸砸爛的聲音。我雙手捧著玻璃魚缸。裡面的水十分混濁。幾打魚鱗漂在水面上。我伸手進去尋找我的魚，而在我摸索的同時，我看見了他們。一隻在我床前。另外一隻在廚房附近。兩隻身上都有不帶血的傷痕。梅莉莎的意思十分明顯。我朝向泡菜走去，那隻貓突然衝出床底，伸爪去抓死魚，將他撞到另外一邊，跟著連忙追上，將魚一口叼起，然後朝向床鋪奔回。魚從貓嘴裡滑落，不過牠繼續奔跑，要嘛就是知道牠被我盯上而且麻煩大了，不然就是以爲魚還在嘴裡。無論如何，牠跑得一副好像腳從來沒有斷過的樣子，我終於了解這件事情根本不是梅莉莎幹的。

en_text: “Fucking cat,” I yell, striding over to Pickle and kneeling down next to him. He looks dead. I pick him up—he’s cold, but ﬁsh are cold anyway, right? I carry him over to the ﬁshbowl and drop him in, hoping I have him back there in time. I pick up Jehovah, and carry her over and drop her in. Pickle is already ﬂoating on his side. A few seconds later, Jehovah joins him.
zh_text: 「天殺的貓。」我吼道，大步走向泡菜，跪倒在他身邊。他看起來已經死了。我撿起他——身體冰冷，不過魚本來就很冰冷，不是嗎？我帶他回到魚缸，放他進去，希望還來得及。我也撿起耶和華，帶她回到水中。泡菜已經側身漂在水面上。片刻過後，耶和華也加入他。

en_text: I swirl them around in the water, pushing them forward into a forced swim, and then I press on their little chests, and even though it seems none of this is of any use, I persist for another ten minutes before ﬁnally giving up. I whirl around and face the bed. This fucking expensive cat has killed my two best friends. I storm over, grip the edges of the bed, and lift it up on its side. A whole bunch of crap falls onto the ﬂoor. The mattress slides off and so do all the sheets. My groin is starting to hurt, but not as much as my heart. The cat looks up at me with shock, its head is tilted and its eyes wide open. When I lean down to pick it up, it backs away. Its ears are pricked back and it looks ready to kill me. I lean forward and try to stomp on its back, but it sees this and stops just before me, forcing me to stretch forward to correct my aim, and as I do, my groin screams out in pain. I stomp on the ﬂoor where the cat has just been, and the shooting pain in my phantom testicle drops me to my knees.
zh_text: 我伸手在魚缸裡轉圈，強迫他們自動游泳，然後我輕壓他們的小胸口，儘管這些作法看起來都毫無用處，我還是又搞了十分鐘才終於放棄。我轉過身去，面對床鋪。這隻貴得要命的貓害死了我最好的兩個朋友。我衝上前去，抓起床緣，用力掀開。一大堆東西掉到地上。床墊滑落，所有床單也一樣。我的胯下又痛起來，不過完全比不上我的心痛。貓神情驚恐地抬頭看我，腦袋微側，雙眼圓睜。我彎下腰去抓牠，牠後退。牠的耳朵向後豎起，一副準備殺我的模樣。我身體後傾，試圖踩牠的背，不過牠察覺我的動作，在我面前止步，迫使我必須向前修正這一腳的落點，而這麼做的同時，我的胯下傳來劇痛。我一腳踩在那隻貓原先的位置，那顆鬼睪丸所帶來的劇痛令我跪倒在地。

en_text: Puss stops in the center of the room and sits down. He looks at me silently. His ears are no longer pricked back. I loosely cup my remaining testicle. Okay. Time to change tactics.
zh_text: 貓咪停在房間中央坐下。牠沉默地看著我。耳朵不再豎起。我輕輕捧著僅存的睪丸。好吧，該是改變策略的時候了。

en_text: “Here, kitty. Come on, fella. I just want to pet you.” I start clicking my Goddamn ﬁngers because it seems to be the sort of thing that cats like. I keep clicking them, and in my mind a movie plays with me in the leading role, wringing the stupid cat’s neck. The cat must be watching the same movie, because it won’t come near me. I make my way toward my briefcase. Both the cat and I look at the knife I pull out, and both of us know what it can do. It knows I’m about to test the adage and see just how many ways I can skin the little bastard. I can see the reﬂection of my eyes in the blade. For a few seconds I just keep looking at them, and all I can think of is how I have my father’s eyes. Thinking of Dad makes me feel suddenly sadder at losing those I love, and then I get angry at the cat for making me feel sad.
zh_text: 「來吧，貓咪。過來，小夥子。我只是想拍拍你。」我開始彈我天殺的手指，因為那似乎是貓咪會喜歡的動作。我一直彈著手指，腦中播放一部電影，我是電影裡的主角，正在掐死那隻蠢貓。那隻貓肯定在看同一部電影，因為牠不肯靠近我。我走向我的公事包。貓跟我一起看著我拔出的那把刀，我們也都很清楚那把刀能做些什麼。牠知道我打算測試一下那句諺語，看看我能用多少方法剝掉那個小混蛋的皮。我可以在刀面上看見我雙眼的倒影。接下來幾秒內，我就這麼看著它們，腦中唯一想到的就是我的眼睛多像我爸。想到老爸就讓我突然間對於失去所愛感到更加悲哀，接著我又爲了讓我悲哀而更氣那隻貓。

en_text: “Good boy. Come on.” I keep clicking my ﬁngers. The cat meows. Then I throw the knife. I’m quick. The knife is quick. The cat’s even quicker. The blade digs into the ﬂoor exactly where he’d been sitting a split second earlier. Then he turns his back on me and slowly walks back over to the bed. I’m making my way to the knife when the phone rings. I don’t want to answer it. All I want to do is kill this Goddamn cat. My testicle hurts like hell. The phone keeps ringing, and ringing.
zh_text: 「好孩子。過來。」我不停彈著手指。貓叫了一聲。接著我射出飛刀。我動作很快。刀飛得很快。不過貓閃得更快。刀刃插入片刻之前牠所坐的地板。跟著牠轉身背對我，慢慢走回床下。我正要過去拔刀的時候，電話鈴突然響起。我不想去接。我一心只想殺死那隻可惡的貓。我的睾丸痛得要命。電話繼續響，不停響。

en_text: I pick up the knife and throw it toward the cat, and the cat darts forward a second later without a knife protruding from him. He looks back up at me.
zh_text: 我拔起刀，射向貓，片刻過後，貓向前一閃，沒有中刀。牠回頭看我。

en_text: “I’m going to kill you, you little bastard.”
zh_text: 「我一定要殺了你，你這個小混蛋。」

en_text: The cat hisses at me.
zh_text: 貓對我嘶嘶叫。

en_text: The phone keeps ringing. It’s giving me a headache. Ring, ring, fucking ring. Why isn’t the machine picking it up?
zh_text: 電話繼續響。聽得我頭都痛了。鈴，鈴，媽的鈴。答錄機為什麼沒有接聽？

en_text: I pick up another knife, then carefully make my way to my feet. The pain in my groin is going. I walk slowly over to the phone. It has stopped ringing and the answering machine is recording a message. The volume is turned down and I can’t hear it. I interrupt the message.
zh_text: 我拔出另外一把刀，小心翼翼地站起身來。胯下還在痛。我緩緩走到電話旁。鈴聲已經停了，答錄機正在錄製訊息。聲音調低了，所以我聽不見。我打斷錄音。

en_text: “Hello?” I say, hoping that my goldﬁsh are the only things I am losing today, but my gut instinct is that something has happened to Mom. That premonition is back, riding my inner thoughts. Why must life be so cruel to those I love? And why must those I love betray me? I took the cat in and gave it a home, and in return it has done this to me.
zh_text: 一哈囉？」我說，希望金魚是我今天唯一失去的東西，不過我的預感告訴我說媽出事了。那股預感乘著我的內心思緒回來了。爲什麼生活要對我所深愛的人們如此殘酷？而我所深愛的人們又爲什麼會要背叛我？我收養那隻貓，給牠一個家，結果牠竟然這樣回報我。

en_text: “Joe? Hi, this is Jennifer.”
zh_text: 「喬？嗨，我是珍妮佛。」

en_text: Jennifer? How does she know my mother? “What can I help you with, Jennifer?” I hear myself asking.
zh_text: 珍妮佛？她怎麼會認識我媽？「有什麼事嗎，珍妮佛？」我聽見自己問道。

en_text: “You’re not going to believe this, but we’ve just found the owner of the cat!”
zh_text: 「你不會相信這種事的，不過我們剛剛找到那隻貓的主人了！」

en_text: She sounds excited. I look over to my bed. The cat is still sitting there. I take aim with the knife.
zh_text: 她聽起來很興奮。我看向我的床。那隻貓依然坐在那裡。我舉刀瞄準。

en_text: “Really.” This means my mother is still alive and well. Thank God! “Really! Isn’t that exciting?”
zh_text: 「真的。」這表示我媽還好好活著。感謝上帝。「真的！這不是很棒嗎？」

en_text: “The cat isn’t here anymore,” I say, wondering how hard I need to throw the knife to pin him to the ﬂoor. “What do you mean?”
zh_text: 「那隻貓已經不在我這裡了。」我說，計算著我要丟多大力才能把貓釘在地板上。「什麼意思？」

en_text: “I gave him away to one of my neighbors.”
zh_text: 「我把他送给我的鄰居了。」

en_text: “Can’t you get him back?”
zh_text: 「不能要回來嗎？」

en_text: “Well, the thing is it kind of ran away.” I’m still talking, but hardly listening to her or even to myself. My brain’s on automatic. I can’t take my eyes from the Goddamn cat, and all I can think about is Dad. Dad killing himself. Dad being found locked inside his car.
zh_text: 「這個，問題在於牠跑掉了。」我還在說話，不過幾乎沒在聽她講話，甚至也沒聽我在講些什麼。我的腦子在自行運作。我沒辦法將目光自那隻天殺的貓身上移開，不過我腦中想的卻只有我爸。老爸殺了自己，老爸死在上鎖的車裡。

en_text: “You’re kidding,” Jennifer says, and for the ﬁrst time she doesn’t sound like she’s desperate to see me naked. I look from the ﬁshbowl to the cat.
zh_text: 你在開玩笑。」珍妮佛說，這是第一次她聽起來不像是想要把我剝光的樣子。我看向魚缸，然後又看回那隻貓。

en_text: “It gets worse,” I say.
zh_text: 「還有更糟糕的。」

en_text: “Worse? Did you say worse? How?”
zh_text: 「更糟？你說更糟？」

en_text: “Well, it didn’t just run away. It ran out into trafﬁc.” No way in hell is she getting the cat back. It represents too much. Melissa betrayed me. Dad betrayed me. I won’t be beaten by an animal with a brain a tenth the size of mine.
zh_text: 「這個，牠不光只是跑掉而已。牠直接跑到馬路上去。」我絕對不會讓她把貓要回去。牠在我心中代表重大的意義。梅莉莎背叛我。爸背叛我。我絕對不會敗在一隻腦袋只有我十分之一的動物手上。

en_text: “Is this for real, Joe? Or are you trying to keep the cat?”
zh_text: 「你是說真的嗎，喬？還是只想留下貓？」

en_text: “If you don’t believe me, you can come and dig the damn thing up out of the yard!”
zh_text: 「如果你不相信我，妳可以把那隻可惡的東西從花園裡挖出來！」「沒有必要……」

en_text: “There’s no need—” “I hate meatloaf!” I scream, and she hangs up on me without another word. Guess I won’t be seeing any more of Jennifer.
zh_text: 「我恨烤肉餅！」我大叫，她二話不說掛斷電話。看來我再也別想看到珍妮佛了。

en_text: Rather than throwing the knife, I decide to take another crack at being nice to the cat in hopes of getting near it. I glance at my ﬁshbowl. The murky water is dead still. This is what I get for trying to be a good person, a caring person.
zh_text: 我決定別丟飛刀，再來試試扮演好好先生，想辦法接近牠。我看向我的金魚缸。污濁的水完全靜止。這就是我嘗試當個好人、關懷動物的下場。

en_text: “Come on, pussycat. Come and see Joe.”
zh_text: 「來嘛，小貓咪。來看看喬。」

en_text: Slowly I lower myself to my knees. I am only a few yards from the thing now, and it has no idea what’s about to happen. I continue to make my way forward. The knife’s going to look good coming from the side of the cat’s head.
zh_text: 我緩緩跪下。如今我距離那玩意兒只剩幾公尺，而牠對於即將發生的事情毫無概念。我繼續前進。這把刀從貓腦袋側面插出的畫面一定很棒。

en_text:
“Come on. Come on. That’s a good boy.” I’m nearly there. I start to reach out with the knife. I’m going to teach it a lesson it will never forget. It moves into a standing position.
“Come on. It’s okay.”
Then the bastard runs. I bring the knife down hard and fast, but miss as it scoots around me. It heads toward the kitchen.
zh_text:
「來嘛，來嘛。真是個好孩子。」我只差一點了。我開始提起刀。我要好好教訓教訓這個傢伙。牠立起身來。
「來吧。沒事的。」

en_text: But then it sees the open door.
zh_text: 但是接著牠看見敞開的門。

en_text: I throw the knife at the cat as it skids on the ﬂoor, changes direction, darts past my briefcase, and heads for freedom. This time the blade sails just over the cat’s head and sticks into the door. He stops in the doorway, looks over at me, gives a meowing sound that makes me want to spend the next twelve hours stomping the life out of him, and then he’s gone. I get to my feet, race to the door, and look out into the corridor. If I had the ability, I would run after it, but my groin is throbbing and possibly bleeding. I close the door, slump onto the sofa, and stare at the goldﬁsh bowl. Pickle and Jehovah are still ﬂoating on the surface. I can’t tell who is who. And as I stare, my eyes mist over. I allow myself to cry. There’s no shame in crying.
zh_text: 我在牠打滑轉彎，衝過我的公事包，朝向自由邁進的時候射出飛刀。這一次刀掠過貓的腦袋，插在門板上。牠在門口停步，回頭看我一眼，發出一聲讓我很想花十二個小時把牠踩扁的貓叫，然後消失在門後。我起身衝往門口，看著門外的走廊。跑得動的話，我一定會去追牠，但是我的胯下在抽痛，很可能有流血。我關上門，癱坐在沙發上，楞楞地看著金魚缸。泡菜和耶和華依然浮在水面上。

en_text: I will ﬁnd that cat. I will ﬁnd it and kill it. I swear.
zh_text: 我無法分辨誰是誰。看著看著，我的視線開始模糊。我容許自己哭泣。哭泣並不丢人。我會找出那隻貓。我會把牠找出來殺掉。我發誓。

en_text: I get up and move into the kitchenette. The night is young, and even though I’m suffering from setbacks, I need to push myself forward. My eyes are blurry from tears and sore from being rubbed. I’m shivering even though it has to be ninety degrees in here. I hang up the phone, pull the bed back onto its legs, and tidy up.
zh_text: 我起身步入小廚房。時間還早，儘管遭受挫敗，我還是必須勇往直前。我的雙眼因為淚水而模糊，也因爲揉太用力而痠痛。室溫起碼三十度，不過我還是渾身發抖。我掛上電話，將床放回原位，整理床單被單。我唯一能做的就是繼續過活。泡菜和耶和華會希望我這麼做的。

en_text: All I can do is move forward. Pickle and Jehovah would want me to. I start to head down memory lane. Thoughts of buying my ﬁsh start ﬂooding my mind. I bought them because I was sick of living alone. At ﬁrst they only suited the purpose of giving my apartment a feeling of life, but within months there was a bond between us that I knew would one day be broken by death. But not this day. Not so soon.
zh_text: 我開始回想從前。當年買魚的景象歷歷在目。我買他們是因爲我受夠一個人住了。一開始他們的存在只是爲了給這間公寓增添生氣，不過幾個月後我們之間就形成了一種只有死亡才能切斷的羈絆。但是不該是今天。不該這麼快。

en_text: I pour the murky water from the ﬁshbowl down the sink. Dad keeps coming into my thoughts, and I wish he’d just leave me alone. I scoop my goldﬁsh into a clear plastic bag, then tie it shut before heading downstairs. In the front lawn of this apartment complex—and the word lawn is being generous—I pull aside some of the weeds, then use my hands to dig a hole. I put the plastic bag inside, then scoop dirt back over it. I could easily have ﬂushed Jehovah and Pickle away, but I did not want to insult their memories by having their bodies ﬂoat around for eternity with pieces of shit. I pat the dirt down nice and tight before saying some words over the piece of ground where my friends lie. My eyes ﬁll with tears. I swear revenge on their grave.
zh_text: 我將魚缸中的濁水倒入水槽。老爸不斷進入我的思緒，我真希望他能讓我靜一靜。我將我的金魚放入透明塑膠袋裡，綁好後走向樓下。站在這棟公寓大樓的花園裡，說花園純粹是好聽，我清開一片雜草，用手挖了個坑。我將塑膠袋放進去，然後把土撥回坑裡。我可以隨手將耶和華和泡菜放到馬桶裡沖掉，但是我不希望他們的屍體永遠和屎尿漂在一起。我將土壓實，然後朝我朋友長眠的地方說了幾句話。我眼中盈滿淚水。我在他們的墳前發誓一定要報仇。

en_text: I look for the cat, and though I can’t ﬁnd it, I can feel its eyes on me. After digging the dirt out from beneath my nails, I manage to get into bed early, which is the only good thing to happen to me all night. I dream of death, but of whose, I can’t be sure.
zh_text: 我尋找那隻貓，雖然找不到牠，但是我可以感覺到牠的目光。在清完指甲縫裡的土後，我提早上床睡覺，這就是今晚唯一發生在我身上的好事。我夢到死亡，但是死的是誰，我不確定。

en_text: Sally wouldn’t mind living on a street like this. Every night she would leave her window open, listening as the ocean crashed against the shore. Every summer morning she could go for a swim before heading to work. She’s sure the people living out here must be more laid back, more relaxed. Martin would have loved living out here, she thinks. He used to love the beach.
zh_text: 莎莉不介意住在這樣的街上。住在這裡的話她會每晚不關窗，聽著海浪打在沙灘上的聲音。每個夏日早晨她都可以趁上班前先去游泳。她認爲這裡的人必定都很悠閒，都很愜意。馬丁一定會喜歡住在這裡的，她想。他喜歡海灘。

en_text:
Yesterday afternoon, she stayed by the corner of the police station just out of sight watching while Joe talked to the woman. She fought with the idea of approaching Joe and asking him straight out what was going on; she was also regretting the chance she’d passed up to look through Joe’s briefcase. If the opportunity arises again, she will take it. Then she drove to the graveyard and, while standing above the grave of her dead brother, she concentrated less on grieving and more on Joe. She wanted to know, no, needed to know what was going on. She decided she couldn’t wait. She apologized to Martin, promised him she would return the following day, and drove toward Joe’s apartment. She was going to confront him. She had to, if she had any chance of helping him. Anyway, his stitches would need removing, and she had to give back the copy of his key she’d had made.
Only she didn’t make it all the way there.
zh_text:
昨天下午，她待在警局的牆角偷看喬和那個女人交談。她壓抑著一股想要直接跑去問喬的衝動；她同時也很後悔自己當初沒有把握機會偷看喬的公事包。如果再度遇上這種機會，她會動手。
接著她駕車前往墓園，站在死去弟弟的墳墓上時，她沒有花很多心思哀悼，反而都是在想喬。她很想知道，不，她必須知道究竟是怎麼回事。她認爲自己等不及了。她向馬丁道歉，保證隔天會再回來，然後開車前往喬的公寓。她打算直言相詢。她非這麼做不可，如果還想幫助他的話。反正他的縫線也該拆了，而且她也得要歸還她打的那把公寓鑰匙。
只不過她根本沒有開到他的公寓。

en_text: A few blocks from his apartment she saw him driving a car. And she is certain, absolutely certain, it was him.
zh_text: 她在離他公寓幾條街外看見他駕駛一輛汽車。她很肯定，絕對肯定，開車的人是他。

en_text: She drives her car slowly down the street, checking every few mailboxes, watching the numbers climb. Most of the houses look as though they’re only a coat of paint away from being charming character homes. When the door she wants opens not long after she knocks, she knows immediately she has the right place. The resemblance is obvious.
zh_text: 次日，她緩緩沿著馬路前進，沿途查看信箱，看著門排號碼數目轉變。大部分的房子看起來都像只要再上一層油漆就能展現迷人風格的房子。當希望開啓的門在她敲過片刻之後開啓之時，她立刻知道自己來對地方了。這個女人跟喬長得太像了。

en_text: “I’m sorry, but I’m not buying,” the woman says, and starts to close the door.
zh_text: 一很抱歉，但是我不買。」那個女人說，接著開始關門。

en_text: “I’m not selling anything,” Sally quickly says, but the door doesn’t slow down. “My name’s Sally. I work with Joe, and I was hoping—”
zh_text: 「我不是來推銷的，」莎莉立刻說道，但是對方關門的速度並未減緩。「我叫莎莉，是喬的同事，我是希望……」

en_text: “Well, why didn’t you say so,” Joe’s mother says, swinging the door open nice and wide. “I’ve never met any of Joe’s friends. I’m Evelyn. Please, please, come inside. Would you like a drink? A Coke perhaps?”
zh_text: 「哎呀，怎麼不早說呢？」喬的母親說道，立刻敞開大門。「我從來沒有見過喬的朋友。我是愛弗琳。請、請、快請進。要喝東西嗎？或許來瓶可樂？」

en_text: “Sure. That’d be nice.”
zh_text: 「當然。那太好了。」

en_text: “Sally, Sally. That’s a pretty name.”
zh_text: 莎莉、莎莉。真是個好名字。

en_text: Joe’s mother leads her down the hallway and into the kitchen. The décor is around thirty years old, Sally thinks, and suspects Joe’s mother has been living here that entire time. She sits down behind a Formica table, and Evelyn opens the fridge and a moment later joins her.
zh_text: 喬的母親帶她路過走廊，進入廚房。室內的裝潢有三十年了，莎莉想，並且懷疑喬的母親可能這三十年來都住在這裡。她在一張塑膠餐桌後坐下，愛弗琳打開冰箱，片刻過後也走過來。

en_text: “So what time is Joe getting here?” Evelyn asks.
zh_text: 「那麼喬什麼時候過來？」愛弗琳問。

en_text: “Joe’s coming here?”
zh_text: 「喬要過來？」

en_text: “That’s why you’re here, isn’t it? You’re meeting Joe? It’s a bit late for dinner, but I suppose I can still whip something up. Perhaps I’ll call him and see if he’s on his way.”
zh_text: 「妳是來找他的，不是嗎？妳跟他約在這裡？現在吃晚餐有點晚了，不過我可以弄點東西。或許我可以打電話看看他過來了沒。」

en_text: “Actually Joe doesn’t know I’m here.”
zh_text: 「事實上，喬不知道我在這裡。」

en_text: “I came here because I wanted to talk to you about Joe.” Now the rest of Evelyn’s features follow the direction of her mouth.
zh_text: 「我來是想跟你聊聊喬的事。」

en_text: “About Joe? Whatever for?”
zh_text: 他媽皺眉。「喬的事？爲什麼？」

en_text: From the moment Sally looked through Joe’s personal ﬁle earlier in the day to get his parents’ address, she knew the questions his mother was going to ask. “I, well, there were a few things I wanted to talk to you about. I have some . . . concerns.”
zh_text: 打從今天稍早莎莉從喬的個人資料中得知他父母的地址後，她就知道他媽會問這個問題。「我，呃，我有些事情想跟你談談。我有點……擔心。」

en_text: Evelyn starts nodding, slowly, as if she is suddenly saddened by Sally’s possible concerns. “I know what you mean, dear.”
zh_text: 愛弗琳開始點頭，慢慢點頭，彷彿她突然爲了莎莉所擔心的事情而悲傷起來。「我了解妳的意思，親愛的。」

en_text: “You do?”
zh_text: 「妳了解？」

en_text: “I have concerns of my own,” she says, the downturned features of her face softening. “Tell me, do you like my son?”
zh_text: 「我自己也有點擔心。告訴我，妳喜歡我兒子嗎？」

en_text: “Of course I do. That’s why I’m here.”
zh_text: 「我當然喜歡。所以我才會來這裡。」

en_text: Evelyn starts nodding. “I always thought more women would like him, but he doesn’t seem to have any interest in them. He’s . . . special, you know.”
zh_text: 我一直認爲會有其他女人喜歡他，但是他似乎對女人不感興趣。他有點……特別，妳知道。

en_text: “I know. He reminds me of my brother.”
zh_text: 「我知道。他讓我想起我弟弟。」

en_text: “Oh? Your brother is that way?”
zh_text: 「喔？妳弟弟也是那樣？」

en_text: “He . . . is,” she says, not saying was, because was has a ﬁnality about it that she doesn’t want to think about right now.
zh_text: 「他……是。」她說，沒說「以前是」，因為「以前是」有種已成定局的感覺，而她此刻不願多想那種感覺。

en_text: “And you like Joe.”
zh_text: 「而妳喜歡喬。」

en_text: “I like Joe a lot,” Sally says.
zh_text: 我很喜歡喬。

en_text: “But these concerns, well, I don’t really know where to start.” “We’ve already started, dearie.”
zh_text: 「但是我所擔心的事情，嗯，我不知道該從何說起。「我們已經開始說了，親愛的。」

en_text: “How long has Joe been able to drive?”
zh_text: 「喬會開車多久了？」

en_text: “What was that, dear?”
zh_text: 「什麼，親愛的？」

en_text: “I don’t see how this relates to you liking him.”
zh_text: 我看不出來這跟你喜歡他有什麼關係。

en_text: “Well, it doesn’t, not exactly. But I saw him driving last night, and—” “He was coming to see me. He’s such a good boy.”
zh_text: 「這個，是無關，沒有直接關係。不過我昨晚有看到他開車，而且……」「他是來看我的。他是個好孩子。」

en_text: “I know. It’s obvious Joe has a big heart. He’s really such a lovely guy. But I didn’t know he could drive.” “You didn’t know he could drive?” Evelyn asks, sounding surprised. “I thought you said you work with him.”
zh_text: 我知道。喬的心胸寬大。他真是個很窩心的人。只是我不知道他會開車。「妳不知道他會開車？我以爲妳說他是同事。」

en_text: “I do work with him.”
zh_text: 「我是他同事。」

en_text: “Then surely you must have seen him driving the cars around.”
zh_text: 「那妳當然看過他開車。」

en_text:
Does Joe tell her he drives the police cars around? It would be the sort of big-kid thing he’d do. She doesn’t want to spoil the illusion for Evelyn. It’s bad enough just being here, invading his privacy. Even now she’s fraught with guilt, and scared about how Joe will react. By trying to help him, she’ll likely end up hurting him, and he’ll likely end up hating her.
“Sure. I was just curious as to how long he has been able to do it, that’s all.”
zh_text:
開警車嗎？難道喬告訴她說他開警車？這聽起來像是會做的。她不想戳穿愛弗琳的幻想。光是來這裡刺探喬的隱私就已經夠糟糕了。就連現在她也覺得滿心罪惡，並且深怕喬得知後的反應。試圖幫助他的結果很有可能會傷害他，而他最後也很可能會討厭她。
「當然。我只是好奇他會開車多久了，如此而已。」

en_text: “Do you have family? Any other brothers and sisters? And what do you do with Joe? Are you his receptionist? Do you clean the cars? Are you a cleaner?”
zh_text: 「妳有家人嗎？其他兄弟姊妹？妳在那間公司是做什麼的？妳是他的櫃檯小姐嗎？妳洗車嗎？妳是清潔工嗎？」

en_text: “I live with my parents,” she says, wanting to get through this part quickly so she can get back to talking about Joe. “I don’t clean the cars, and I don’t think Joe does either.”
zh_text: 「我跟父母同住。」她說，一心只想盡快結束這個話題，回去談論喬。「我不洗車，我想喬也不洗車。」

en_text: “No, of course he doesn’t. Why would he?”
zh_text: 「當然不洗。他爲什麼要洗？」

en_text: Sally shrugs in reply. Why would a cleaner have a receptionist?
zh_text: 莎莉聳肩回應。清潔工要櫃檯小姐幹什麼？

en_text: “What do you do then?” Evelyn asks. “At work, I mean.”
zh_text: 「那妳是做什麼的？」愛弗琳問。「工作，我是指。

en_text: “Well, I’m a maintenance worker. I kind of keep things in order.”
zh_text: 這個，我是維修工。我算是維持工作場所一切的運作。

en_text: “Oh, that sounds very interesting, Sally. You don’t see many female mechanics. Do you want to sell cars one day?”
zh_text: 「喔，聽起來非常有趣，莎莉。女性維修工不常見。妳希望有一天也能賣車嗎？」「賣車？」

en_text: “Sell cars?” “Yes. Do you want to sell them?”
zh_text: 「是啊。妳想賣車嗎？」

en_text: Maybe selling cars is a dream of Joe’s. “I guess I’ve never thought about it.” She picks up her drink and takes another large swallow. Speaking to Joe’s mother is turning out to be just as difﬁcult as some of the conversations she has had with Joe. “The thing is, I came here to talk about something I think might be happening.” “Between you and Joe? Oh, that would be marvelous!”
zh_text: 或許賣車是喬的夢想。「我想我沒想過這個問題。」她拿起飲料，喝了一大口。跟喬的母親交談幾乎和有時候跟喬交談一樣困難。「重點在於，我是來談一些我認爲此刻正在發生的事情。」「妳和喬？喔，那眞是太好了。」

en_text: Sally leans back, struggling not to sigh. Suddenly she can’t go through with it. Joe has created a world for his mother to see him in, and no doubt it’s taken a long, long time. She could destroy all of that with some careless words. No, she is best to end this. There are no answers here as to why Joe can drive. No answers as to who attacked him. She takes another mouthful of drink, trying to get through it quickly, wanting to get out of here.
zh_text: 莎莉靠向椅背，壓抑著想嘆氣的衝動。突然之間她發現自己談不下去了。喬在他母親面前創造了另外一個世界，毫無疑問這花了他很長很長一段時間。她只要一不小心就可以摧毀這一切。不，她最好快點結束這次會面。這裡找不到喬能開車的原因。找不到襲擊喬的人的身分。她又喝了一口飲料，試圖盡快喝完，想要離開這裡。

en_text: “I knew Joe would ﬁnd somebody.”
zh_text: 「我就知道喬會找到對象的。」

en_text: “He really is something,” Sally says, unsure of what else to say. She takes another mouthful. Only another mouthful to go.
zh_text: 「他真的很特別。」莎莉說，不確定還能說什麼。她又喝了一口。只剩一口就喝完了。

en_text: “After his father died, well, I was unsure how that would affect him, you know what I mean? I thought it might mess him up a little. Make him a little odd.”
zh_text: 「在他父親死後，唉，我也不確定會對他造成什麼影響，妳知道我的意思嗎？我以爲那會打亂他的生活。讓他變得有點怪。」

en_text: Sally nods. She didn’t know Joe’s father had died.
zh_text: 莎莉點頭。她不知道喬的父親死了。

en_text: “Joe became quiet. Withdrawn. Not long after, he moved out. Do you know, I’ve never been to his house? I worry about Joe. I suppose that’s the job of a mother.”
zh_text: 「喬變得沉默、孤僻。沒過多久，他就搬出去了。妳知道我從來沒有去過他家嗎？我很擔心喬。我想這是母親的責任。」

en_text: “I worry about him too.” Sally ﬁnishes off her drink. “Well, I’d best be going.”
zh_text: 「我也擔心他。」莎莉喝完飲料。「我最好先走了。

en_text: “But you only just got here.”
zh_text: 「但是妳才剛來。」

en_text: “I know. Next time I’ll stay longer. I just wanted to come by and say hello.”
zh_text: 我知道。下次我會待久一點。我只是想要過來打聲招呼。

en_text: “You really are a nice young girl.” Evelyn walks her to the door and opens it. The night has cooled off in the ﬁfteen minutes she has been here. She thinks it’s going to start raining again. “Did Joe tell you about Walt?”
zh_text: 「妳真是個好女孩。」愛弗琳陪她走到門口，打開屋門。過去十五分鐘裡，外面的氣溫降低許多。「喬有跟你提過華特的事嗎？」

en_text: “Walt?”
zh_text: 「華特？」

en_text: Sally stands in the doorway with her arms wrapped around her body, listening as Evelyn recounts the story of Walt. When it’s over, she thanks Joe’s mother, then walks down the path to her car. She grips the steering wheel, but doesn’t start the engine.
zh_text: 莎莉站在門口，雙手緊抱自己的身體，聽著愛弗琳重複華特的事情。講完之後，她向喬的母親道謝，然後走向她的車。她握著方向盤，但是沒有發動引擎。

en_text: According to Evelyn, Joe is a car salesman. Joe was out test-driving a car when he ran into her old friend Walt.
zh_text: 根據愛弗琳所言，喬是個汽車銷售員。喬在外出試駕的時候遇上了她的老朋友華特。

en_text: She clutches the cruciﬁx around her neck. Joe has created a ﬁctional world to keep his mother happy. What else has he created? Joe is more than he seems and, in a way, that frightens her.
zh_text: 她握著脖子上的十字架。喬爲了讓他媽高興而創造了一個虛構世界。他還創造了什麼？喬不像外表那麼單純，而就某方面而言，這一點讓她害怕。

en_text: The next morning my internal alarm wakes me into what is another glorious Christchurch morning—according to some old guy giving the forecast on the radio. Looking out the window shows something different: gray skies and dark storm clouds on the horizon, which make me think the forecaster must be crazy or drunk. There is some condensation on the window and the ﬂoor is cold. I stare at the coffee table before leaving for work. There is a tin of ﬁsh food on it and no dead cat. I leave my apartment and head downstairs and out into the ﬁrst frost of the year. The lawn looks crunchy, and there are leaves ﬁlling the gutters. I’m shivering a little when I hand Mr. Stanley my bus ticket, and today he punches it. I wonder if this is an omen. I want to tell him about my goldﬁsh, and I don’t know why. I don’t even know if he would care.
zh_text: 第二天早上，我的生理時鐘帶我進入一個陽光普照的基督城早晨——根據某個老頭在電台裡的天氣預測。不過窗外的景象可不是這麼說的——灰濛濛的天空和地平線上陰沉沉的烏雲都讓我覺得報氣象的老頭不是瘋子就是酒鬼。我出門上班前盯著咖啡桌看了一會兒。桌上擺了一盒魚飼料，不過沒有死貓。我離開我的公寓，將公車票交給史丹利先生，今天他有剪票。我在想這是不是什麼不好的預兆。我想告訴他我的金魚出了什麼事，我也不知道爲什麼。我甚至不知道他在不在乎。

en_text: The day doesn’t suggest that it’s going to get much warmer. I keep my hands buried in my pockets as I make my way across the road. Sally catches me by the elevator. We make inane conversation up to my ﬂoor, but mostly Sally seems preoccupied, and then she is gone.
zh_text: 這就是基督城的天氣——一天之中能夠體驗五個可惡的季節。莎莉在電梯裡遇上我。我們在到我的樓層前閒聊了幾句，不過莎莉似乎心事重重，然後她就離開了。

en_text: I’m unable to gain access to the conference room, so I end up doing what I’m paid to do. I keep an eye on Detective Calhoun when he is around. I try to ﬁgure out just how he’s feeling, but I don’t know him well enough to see if he’s going through a personal crisis. I also keep an eye out for Melissa, but she doesn’t show. I vacuum and clean and wipe and do the general workday things that bring in the big janitorial bucks. Nobody treats me any differently. Nobody gives me the sort of look they’d reserve for a serial killer.
zh_text: 我不能進入會議室，只好去做我應該做的工作。卡爾霍恩警探在警局裡的時候，我會特別注意他。我很想知道他此刻心裡是什麼感覺，不過我跟他沒有熟到能夠看出他有沒有面臨心理危機的地步。我也有注意梅莉莎，不過她沒出現。我吸地、掃地、擦窗，做著那些賺取優渥工資的例行工作。沒有人改變對待我的態度。沒有人以看連續殺人魔的目光打量我。

en_text: The station doesn’t have the same buzz about it as yesterday, when everybody thought the case was about to bust wide open. Even the conference room is empty. I step inside and take a look around. The composite picture Melissa helped them with is on the wall. Dark, bushy hair; cheekbones that can’t be seen, let alone felt; lots of stubble. A ﬂat nose, big eyes, high forehead. The cold, calculating expression on his face looks mean, as though the person in this picture was born to be a criminal. The picture in no way represents how I actually look. My hair is ﬁner, swept back, and kept reasonably short. It’s dark, which is the only similar thing, but I have high cheekbones with no ﬂab, and my eyes are thinner too. And stubble? No way. I’m lucky if I need to shave once a month. I grin at the picture. It doesn’t grin back. On the table with the folders is the knife. Shrouded inside a plastic bag, sitting inside a cardboard box, it has already been studied for ﬁngerprints, blood, and DNA. If my ﬁngerprints were found on it, I would know by now. All employees in this building have been ﬁngerprinted. It’s standard. Melissa wasn’t lying. It isn’t standard for all of us to have given DNA samples.
zh_text: 警局裡不像昨天那樣籠罩在一股所有人都認爲即將破案的興奮氣氛中。就連會議室也空無一人。我走了進去，好好打量一番。梅莉莎描述給他們的拼貼照片就貼在牆上。濃密的黑髮，臉頰肥到看不見也感覺不出，很多鬍碴。扁平鼻，大眼睛，高額頭。老謀深算的表情看起來十分奸詐，彷彿照片中的人天生就是罪犯。這張照片跟我一點也不像。我的頭髮柔順，梳向腦後，而且很短。它是黑色的，這是唯一相似之處，不過我的頰骨很高，沒有贅肉，眼睛也沒那麼大。至於鬍碴？不可能。幸好我的鬍子少到一個月只要剃一次就好。我看著照片咧嘴而笑。如果照片算是我的鏡中倒影，他沒有回應我的笑容。跟檔案夾一同放在桌上的是一把刀。包在一個塑膠袋裡，放在一個紙箱子中，已經驗過指紋、血跡和DNA。如果上面有找到我的指紋，這時我應該已經聽說了才對。警局中所有的雇員都有記錄指紋。這是標準程序。梅莉莎沒有騙我。至於留下DNA樣本那就不是標準程序了。

en_text: I grip the handle tightly, feel it beneath the thin plastic. This knife was stolen from me in circumstances I can never possibly forget. This knife was there the night I suffered my greatest indignity, my greatest pain, and experienced my greatest hatred. I quickly put it back down. It isn’t mine anymore.
zh_text: 我緊握刀柄，感覺包在塑膠袋下的刀。這把刀是在我永遠不可能忘記的情況下自我手中被人奪走的。我遭受此生最大屈辱、最大痛楚、激起最強烈的恨意的那晚，這把刀就在現場。我很快就把刀放回去，它已經不屬於我的了。

en_text: I take time to read the reports. The prostitute I left in the alleyway has been identiﬁed. Charlene Murphy. Twenty-two years old. I’d pegged her at being closer to thirty. Prostitution ages people fast. She was, however, a mother of one. That much I’d guessed. Her boyfriend isn’t a suspect, since he was in jail at the time on unrelated charges. Her photograph is up on the wall keeping company with the other women.
zh_text: 我利用時間閱讀報告。被我棄屍在巷子裡的妓女已經鑑識出身分。夏琳·墨菲。二十二歲。我本來猜她比較接近三十。妓女是個老得很快的職業。不過她是個母親，這點我沒猜錯。她的男朋友不是嫌犯，因為案發當時他正因其他罪名待在監獄裡。她的照片貼在牆上，就在其他女人旁邊。

en_text: The second whore who died, Candy number two, is still to be identiﬁed. I don’t need to take any information away with me, but I ﬁnd myself collecting what I can anyway, more as mementos than anything else. I also take the tape from the recorder in the potted plant. I’m back in my ofﬁce when Sally knocks at the door and comes in.
zh_text: 第一名死者，坎蒂一號，身分依然有待鑑識。我不需要帶走任何資料，不過我發現自己還是盡力蒐集，有點像是紀念品性質。我也拿走了盆栽裡的錄音帶。回到我的辦公室後，莎莉敲門進來。

en_text: After the usual pleasantries, Sally stops talking, as if she’s used up all the words she’d remembered for the day. She just stands there as if somebody has reached inside her and ﬂicked the big off switch. About half a minute goes by, and then she just starts looking around.
zh_text: 正常寒暄過後，莎莉停止說話，彷彿她已經用光了當天所有記得的單字。她就那麼站在那裡，好像有人伸手到她體內關掉開關一樣。約莫半分鐘過後，她開始左顧右盼。

en_text: “Sure is a cold day,” she says, but the switch has been ﬂicked to automatic now, so she doesn’t really know what she is saying. She looks out the window. Looks at the ceiling. At the ﬂoor under the bench. Finally her eyes rest on my briefcase. “I forgot to make you lunch today. I’m sorry, Joe.”
zh_text: 「天氣真好。」她說，不過她的開關此刻轉到「自動」模式，所以她並不清楚自己在說些什麼。她看看窗外。看看天花板。看看工作台下的地板。最後她的目光停留在我的公事包上。「我今天忘了幫你做午餐。對不起，喬。」

en_text: “Don’t worry about it.”
zh_text: 「不必介意。」

en_text: She keeps staring at my briefcase, and I guess she’s ﬁguring I’d like her more if she went out and bought the same one. She’s trying to ﬁgure out whether I’d be impressed or devastated if she bought one that was better. The truth is she probably isn’t thinking anything at all. She is frowning slightly, which suggests something is going on inside her mind, but the way her face is slightly scrunched up suggests the only thing happening in there is a whole lot of confusion. It’s as if she wants to ask me a really big question, but has no idea what that question even is.
zh_text: 她一直盯著我的公事包看，我認爲她是在想如果她跑去買個一模一樣的，我就會更喜歡她。或者是在考慮如果她買了一個比我的好的公事包，我會開心還是不爽。事實上，她很可能什麼都沒在想。她微微皺眉，這表示她有心事，不過她臉上皺成一團的模樣顯示她內心極度困惑。那感覺像是她想要問我一個很嚴重的問題，偏偏又不知道是什麼問題。

en_text: “Well, thanks for dropping by. I got a lot of work I ought to get started on.”
zh_text: 「好了，謝謝妳過來看我。我還有很多工作要做……」

en_text:
This seems to snap her out of it. The switch inside of her doesn’t go to on, because that isn’t one of the positions. Other than off and automatic, she only has barely functioning, and she goes into that mode now.
“I’ll see you later on, Joe.”
zh_text:
這話似乎令她回過神來。她體內的開關沒有轉到「開啓」，因為根本沒有這個選項。除了「關閉」和「自動」外，她只有「勉強運作」模式，而此刻她就進入了這個模式。
「喔，好哇。」我說，努力讓這句話聽來像用唱的一樣。

en_text: “Oh. Okay then,” I say, trying to singsong the three words. She heads out of my ofﬁce but doesn’t close the door. I have to get up and do it myself.
zh_text: 她離開我的辦公室，但是沒有關門。我得要起身自己去關。

en_text: I listen to the tape from the conference room. Lots of different theories, none of them right. The police are freaking out because they think I’m escalating. They think soon it’ll be only a few days between my victims. Hell, maybe they’re right. It’s too early to tell.
zh_text: 我聽了會議室的錄音帶。很多不同的理論，沒有一個正確的。警方驚慌失措，因為他們認爲我開始加速犯案了。要不了多久我的犯案間隔就會縮短爲數日。見鬼了，說不定他們猜對了。現在還看不出來。

en_text: The Everblue Motel is one of those dives you see in movies where bad things happen to unlucky people who just happen to be staying there the same night as some escaped mental patient. It’s not far from town, but far enough for the land to be cheap, like those living nearby.
zh_text: 長藍汽車旅館就是你會在電影裡看到的那種倒楣鬼剛好跟逃出精神病院的瘋子同時過夜並且發生慘劇的地方。那裡離城區不遠，不過地租便宜，就像附近的住戶一樣。汽車旅館的房間排列成L狀，油漆斑剝，窗沿龜裂，雜草枯黃，灌木垂死。走道上的裂縫裡積滿鏽色的積水。我在停車場裡看到十來輛車，從最便宜的爛車到中產階級家庭轎車都有。或許今天妓女有禮拜三折扣日的活動。幾台破爛的超級市場推車躺在地上，圍繞在雜草和菸屁股中。霓虹招牌發出惱人的吱吱聲。

en_text: The motel is an L-shaped stretch of rooms with old paint and chipped windowsills, opposite brown grass and half-dead shrubs. The cracks in the sidewalk are full of rust-colored water. I count a dozen vehicles in the parking lot, ranging from the cheapest of the cheap to the most average, middle-class family sedan. Maybe it’s discount Wednesday for the hookers. A few corroding shopping carts are lying on their sides, surrounded by weeds and cigarette butts. The neon sign is making a loud buzzing noise. I park outside the ofﬁce. Long ribbons of thick plastic cover the doorway, the type you’d ﬁnd if you traveled back twenty years and entered a dairy. I brush them aside and make my way in. The room smells of latex and cigarette smoke. The walls and ceiling are stained. The carpet is patterned with cigarette burns.
zh_text: 我將車停在辦公室外，步入炎熱的夜晚中。今天一整天越來越熱。每隔十秒左右我就會感到有滴汗水自我腋下滑落。門上垂著長長的塑膠布簾，就是在二十年前乳品製造廠裡看到的那種。我撩開它們，進入辦公室。裡面瀰漫著一股乳膠和香菸的味道。牆壁和天花板上都是污垢，地毯上隨處可見菸頭燙出來的痕跡。櫃檯後方的男子看來四十幾歲，禿頭，過胖，直視著我，一副不信任我的模樣。彷彿他認爲我會扯下他的彩色塑膠門簾然後奪門而出。他身穿一件印有「種族歧視乃是最新潮流」字樣的汗衫。

en_text: The guy behind the counter must be in his forties. He’s bald and overweight, and he stares directly at me as if he doesn’t trust me. As if he thinks I’m going to grab his multicolored plastic ribbons from the doorway and take off. He is wearing a T-shirt that says Racism is the New Black. I ﬂash some police identiﬁcation that isn’t even mine—sometimes all you need is a policeman’s business card with a name and no photo and it can open any door—and he shrugs and hardly glances at it. When I ask to look through the guest book, he spins it around and tells me to go ahead. His ﬁngernails, long and dirty, ﬂick the pages open toward the date I indicate. Then he uses them to scratch at his barren scalp. He gets tiny pieces of skin stuck under them, and then he starts to pick them out. They drift onto the guest book, and he brushes them off with his hand. We make miniature conversation as I look through the book. He has dealt with police before, so he says, and even rented a room once to a murderer. Of course, he didn’t know the man was a murderer at the time. That hadn’t come out until the guy was caught.
zh_text: 我秀出一份根本不是我的警察證件——有時候只需要一張有名字沒照片的警察名片能就讓任何門爲你而開——他聳了聳肩，看都不看那張證件一眼。當我要求看看住客登記簿的時候，他把登記簿轉過來，叫我隨便看。他又長又髒的指甲將登記簿翻到我指定的那一天。接著他又用那些指甲去搔他的光頭。指甲上刮下了小小的頭皮屑，然後他開始挖出那些頭皮屑。它們飄到櫃檯上，他用手拍開它們。我們在我翻閱登記簿的時候隨口閒聊幾句。他曾與警方打過交道，他如此宣稱，甚至曾經把房間租給一名殺人犯。當然，當時他並不知道對方是殺人犯，那要等到那傢伙被捕之後才知道。「厲害厲害。」我對他說。

en_text: Fascinating. I tell him so. I search through the dates, looking for the room Calhoun used. Of course, it won’t be beneath his name, but I look nonetheless. My ﬁnger scrolls past lots of people called John Smith, and others with names like Ernest Hemingway and Albert Einstein. The Everblue seems a popular place for dead people, because even Abraham Lincoln has stayed here. I turn the guest book back around so it faces Mr. Greasy. Slap the photograph of Detective Calhoun down on top of it. “You recognize this guy?” “Should I?”
zh_text: 我翻閱登記簿，找尋卡爾霍恩住過的房間。當然，他會使用化名，不過我還是要找。我的手拍滑過很多名叫約翰·史密斯的人，還有像是厄尼斯·海明威和亞伯特·愛因斯坦之類的名字。我將登記簿轉回去面對油垢先生。把卡爾霍恩警探的照片丟在上面。「認得這傢伙嗎？」「應該認得嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah, you should.”
zh_text: 對，應該認得。

en_text: He takes a close look at it. “Yeah, I remember him. He came in a few months ago.”
zh_text: 他細看那張照片。「是啊，我記得他。他幾個月前來過。

en_text: “Out of all the people who come in here, you remember this guy? Why’s that?”
zh_text: 「這裡這麼多人來來往往，偏偏你就記得他？爲什麼？」

en_text: “I sure as hell remember the mess he made, and the noise he made while he was making it.” “You sure this guy did that?”
zh_text: 「我打死都記得他所留下的爛攤子，還有他在搞的時候發出的噪音。「你確定是這傢伙幹的？」

en_text: He shrugs again. “Does it matter?”
zh_text: 他再度聳肩。「有差別嗎？」

en_text: I guess it doesn’t. I don’t bother thanking him. Just nod, and leave. My next stop is a direct contrast to the Everblue. The Five Seasons Hotel is closer to the center of town, among a handful of hotels, most around ten years old. Land isn’t cheap here. It just looks it. I park the stolen car three blocks away and take my briefcase with me. The evening is getting darker and colder. There’s going to be another frost. The hotel is ugly. I don’t know quite how to describe it as anything other than an artistic dream turned nightmare. Architects using braille to draw their plans. Painters using materials from the seventies. It looks like a lava lamp. It’s ﬁfteen stories high—not huge, but big enough when your major color is lime green. Spotlights around the foundation light it up at night. The hotel would look more in place in Disneyland as some scary ride. Amazingly, it’s a ﬁve-star.
zh_text: 我想是沒差。我沒向他道謝。只是點頭離開。我的下一站與長藍旅館有著天壤之別。五季旅館接近市中心，座落在幾家旅館之間，大部分都只有十年歷史。這裡的地可不便宜。只是看起來很便宜而已。我將偷來的車停在三條街口外，帶著公事包下車。夜還不深，不過陽光依然炙烈耀眼。我汗流不止。這間旅館很醜。除了藝術家的美夢化爲惡夢之外，我不知道該如何形容這個地方。建築師根本是用盲人點字法去繪製設計圖的。畫家則採用了七〇年代的顏料。整棟旅館看起來像是一盞熔岩燈。十五層樓高，佔地不廣，不過在以萊姆綠作爲主色的情況下看起來並不算小。由地面打上去的聚光燈令它在黑夜中耀眼生輝。這棟旅館看起來比較像是迪士尼樂園雲霄飛車裡的裝飾。驚人的是，它竟然能被評爲五星級。

en_text: What’s also amazing is that police personnel from out of town are put up here. It’s taxpayers’ money going to good use.
zh_text: 同樣驚人的地方在於從外地調來支援的警方人員竟然安排入住這種地方，真是善用納稅人的錢。

en_text: I already have a picture in my mind of what the interior will look like, but I quickly ﬁnd I’m completely wrong. The walls are varnished wood, giving the foyer a strange type of antique look. A chandelier hangs from the ceiling with a million reﬂections of light. The carpet, a deep red color, is plush enough to sleep on and be comfortable. Where the carpet ends, checkered black-and-white linoleum takes over. The foyer is large enough to chase somebody around in for a good minute or so. The air is cool, and slightly scented. Could be jasmine, or lilac, or one of those other incense aromas that men all over the world have no idea how to distinguish from others.
