zh_text: 我以自己的頭撞向他的頭——我有多痛他就有多痛——把槍撞掉了。我眼冒金星，而且是上百個金星，不止，應該有上千個吧，它們突然以相同金色的形狀出現在我的眼前，只不過後來漸漸轉成紅色。我搖搖晃晃，向後傾倒，房間彷彿開始天旋地轉。就在我知道自己不能再給他逮到第二次機會的同時，我知道卡爾霍恩一定也和我有著相同的感受。我仍手握煎鍋，於是當機立斷，決定再次善用手上的利器。

en_text: When I look at him, there are two Detective Calhouns, two bedroom doors, two of everything. I shake my head and the room keeps spinning, but the images begin to form into one. I roll my body, raise my heavy arms, and swing the pan against the side of his head. It connects with his cheekbone and jaw, possibly breaking the former and maybe dislocating the latter. He falls back to the ground and doesn’t move. Exhausted, I let the pan fall to the ﬂoor.
zh_text: 當我盯著他看，我看到的是什麼東西都有兩個影子。我甩了甩頭，房間還是天旋地轉，只不過多重影像開始慢慢合而爲一。我轉了個身，舉起沉重的雙臂，拿煎鍋朝他側臉揮去。鍋身就打上他的顴骨和下巴，前者可能已經碎裂，後者或許也已易位。被我這麼一揮，他又摔倒在地、動也不動，我則是精疲力盡，手上一鬆，煎鍋就這麼落至地面。

en_text: I roll him onto his front and bind his hands behind him, then tie his legs. When I try to open his mouth, I discover I’ve dislocated his jaw. Since I need to make conversation with him later, I grip hold of his mouth and try to move it back. Nothing happens. I tap it with the hammer—softly at ﬁrst, then harder—and after a few blows it clicks back into place. I open his mouth and place the egg inside, then change my mind. I won’t risk the egg slipping to the back of his throat while he’s unconscious and killing him. I use a pair of the husband’s underwear to gag him instead.
zh_text: 我替他翻了個身，先反綁他的雙手，再綑起他的雙腿。當我試圖撐開他的嘴巴，我才發現他的下巴已經被我打歪。既然稍後還得和他對談，我得先撐住他的嘴巴，試圖接回下巴，但眼見這麼做無濟於事，我這才拿大榔頭敲了起來。起初我輕輕敲，後來越敲越重，而且在重重敲了幾下之後，下巴才「喀」一聲接回原處。我撐開他的嘴巴，放了顆蛋，卻隨即改變主意——我可不能冒險在他昏迷不醒時讓蛋滑下他的喉嚨然後將他噎死。於是我轉而拿起一條男主人的內褲當綁嘴布，好讓他開不了口。

en_text: By the time Calhoun wakes up I have him sitting in a chair I’ve brought up from the dining room. I’ve used rope to secure him to it and, because the chair has metal legs, even if he can somehow tip it over it won’t break. I wrap duct tape around his legs and reinforce them to the chair, and run more tape around his arms. Unless he’s Harry Houdini, he won’t be going anywhere.
zh_text: 待卡爾霍恩悠悠轉醒，我讓他坐在我從飯廳所拿來的椅子上，再用繩子加以固定。因為四個椅腳都是金屬，所以不管他用什麼方法把椅子翻轉過來，椅腳都斷不了。除了繩子，我還用膠帶把他的雙腿纏在椅子上，並在手臂多繞了好幾圈。除非他是逃脫大師胡迪尼，否則他根本就動彈不得、哪兒也去不了。

en_text: I crouch in front of him. He’s staring at me, as if the face he saw before being knocked out couldn’t possibly be the one he’s seeing now. How is it possible that Joe—Joe the cleaner, Joe the fucked-up retard—is doing this to him? Can it be that the man they’ve been looking for has been working for them all this time?
zh_text: 我跏在他的面前，他則盯著我看，彷彿他正盯著的這張臉，不可能就是他被打昏之前所看到的那張臉。喬，清潔工喬，去他媽的智障喬居然有辦法對他幹起這種事？他們一直在找的那個人難道一直以來都在替他們工作？

en_text: I nod, conﬁrming that yes, it is not only possible, but better than possible.
zh_text: 我點了點頭，確認答案就是「對，他不但有辦法，而且是很有辦法」。

en_text: He grunts, either to conﬁrm his surprise, or to ask me why, or perhaps to test the gag in his mouth. Whatever the reason, he can’t sustain much of a noise. The pain in his jaw must be killing him. Blood hangs off his bottom lip. I want to tell him it’s nothing compared to having a testicle torn off, but I don’t want anybody else knowing about that.
zh_text: 他「哼」了一聲，不是要證實自己非常驚訝，就是要問我幹嘛這樣，又或者只是想測試一下鄉嘴布管不管用。無論如何，他的下唇滴起鮮血，下巴鐵定也痛得要命，他可承受不了發出更多的噪音。我很想告訴他，比起一顆睾丸被人扯掉，這根本就不足爲道，但此事我並不想張揚。

en_text: “You killed her, didn’t you?” “Uh-uh.” He shakes his head. “I didn’t ki’ any’ody.”
zh_text: 「是你殺了她吧？」「呃啊……」他搖了搖頭，「偶耶欸額啊（我誰也沒殺）。」才怪，就是你殺的。」

en_text: “Yes, you did.” This time, shaking his head, he repeats himself. Almost. “No. No, I didn’t, you cwasy fasdid.”
zh_text: 這次他一邊搖頭，一邊盡可能地重複說著：「惡惡，偶額噁，以惡恨幹、哼個（不不，我沒有，你這混蛋、瘋子）。」

en_text: I think he has just called me a crazy bastard. Perhaps I am. Perhaps that’s my problem. I test his theory by standing up and punching him in the stomach.
zh_text: 我想，他剛是在罵我混蛋、瘋子。也許我眞的是。也許這就是我的毛病。我透過站起身子、一拳打在他的胃上證明他的論點。

en_text: Will you look at that? He was right. Only I’m a bastard who needs to make a deal.
zh_text: 你看到了嗎？他說得很對，只不過我是個需要交換條件的混蛋。

en_text: “I’m going to take off your gag,” I say, leaning forward once more. “You know the drill. If you don’t, then assume it. Any sound,” I say, raising the knife to his mouth, “has an unpleasant ending for you. Nod if you understand.”
zh_text: 「我打算拿掉你的鄉嘴布。」我說，再次向前傾身。「你知道電鑽吧？要是你不知道那是什麼，那就想像一下。要是你敢出聲，」我說，在他嘴邊舉起刀子，「就會死得非常難看。聽懂就給我點點頭。」

en_text: I’m still being a bastard, because I’m holding the tip of the blade directly beneath his chin, so as he nods, he keeps pricking himself. I ensure this by raising the knife higher every time his head rises. In the end, he nods with his eyes. I use the knife to cut his gag. It falls away and hangs around his neck like a collar.
zh_text: 我還是一副混蛋欠扁的德行，因為我就這樣拿刀抵住他的下巴，讓他在不停點頭時把刀給刺進肉裡。他每每抬起頭來，我就把刀頂得更高、確定我是認真的，最後他只好上下移動眼球代替點頭。我拿刀劃破鄉嘴布，它應聲而斷，有如領子那般掛在他的頸上。

en_text: “Better?”
zh_text: 「好多了吧？」

en_text: He nods. In fact, his whole body is nearly nodding.
zh_text: 他點了點頭。實際上，他幾乎全身上下都在點頭。

en_text: “Listen, Joe, do you know who I am?”
zh_text: 「喬，聽著，你知道我是誰嗎？」

en_text:
“Now, do you understand that it’s bad to do this? It’s bad to tie people up. Especially policemen.”
“I’m not a moron.”
zh_text:
「你知不知道自己現在這麼做很糟糕？把人家綁起來很糟糕，尤其當那人是個警察。」「我可不是笨蛋。」
「對、對，你當然不是。我了解人生對於……呃……對於像你這種特殊的人來說很不簡單，我了解……」

en_text: “No. No of course you’re not. I understand life is difﬁcult for . . . for, well, for special people like yourself. I understand . . .” I hold my hand up. “Listen, Bob, let me stop you right there. Just because I’m a cleaner doesn’t mean I’m a Goddamn moron, okay? You need to start realizing I’m not the same idiot you’ve seen every day since you’ve been in this city.”
zh_text: 我舉起單手。「鮑伯，等等，先讓我說。我是個清潔工並不代表我就是個他媽的笨蛋好嗎？你得知道，我可不是你待在這城市以來每天都會看到的那個白痴。」

en_text: He tilts his head slightly as he takes this information in, and slowly he starts to do the realizing he needs to do. He comes to the conclusion that I’m not Slow Joe, but Angry Joe. I’m Superintelligent Joe.
zh_text: 他聽進我的話後側了側頭，逐漸了解到我可不是智障喬，而是憤怒喬、天才喬！

en_text: “Look, Joe, I didn’t mean to offend you. It’s just that, well, it was one hell of an act. You can’t blame me for being fooled,” he says, which sounds like an attempt at ﬂattery.
zh_text: 「喬，聽著，我無意冒犯，只不過……呃……你裝得可真像，今天我被耍了，不能怪到我的頭上。」

en_text: “No, I can’t blame you, but you can stop sucking up, Bob.”
zh_text: 「對，不能怪到你的頭上，但是鮑伯，你能不能不要這麼機車？」

en_text: “You haven’t crossed the line here yet. If you let me go, I can forget this ever happened. We can both carry on with our normal lives. Once you do something, though, once you hurt me, there’s nothing I can do to help you out. You understand that, right? If I’m dead, I’m useless, right? Okay? You’re obviously an intelligent guy, I’m sure you understand. And I’m sure you know a useless dead cop means trouble for you, Joe, and neither of us wants any trouble, right?” he says, which is his way of assuming that neither of us wants a dead cop. “We both know that. It’s just too much hassle. So how about you untie me, huh? Untie me and we can discuss any concerns you have. We can talk about what you want.”
zh_text: 趁你還沒失控，要是你放我走，我可以當作什麼都沒發生，我倆可以繼續過著日常的生活。不過，要是你對我不利、動我一根寒毛，那我可就饒不了你。這你懂吧？我要是死了，那也就毫無用處了不是嗎？你顯然聰明絕頂，也相當清楚一具沒用的警官屍體其實相當麻煩。喬，無論你我，我們都不想惹上麻煩，也都不想處理屍體吧？我們都很清楚……所以，放開我如何？先替我鬆綁，我們可以談談你想要什麼、有什麼考量。

en_text: “Don’t you want to know what we’re going to be talking about?”
zh_text: 「你不想知道我們接下來會談些什麼嗎？」

en_text: “Sure I do, Joe, sure I do, but you’ve got to untie me ﬁrst, okay? Untie me and give me back my gun, and we’ll go downstairs, or wherever you want to go because it’s up to you, I promise. This is your ball game and you’re calling all the shots here, so we’ll go where you want to go and we can discuss whatever it is you have in mind, no matter how long it takes.”
zh_text: 「想，喬，我當然想，但你得先放開我，好不好？放開我，把槍還我，然後我們就下樓，又或者讓你決定、你想去哪就去哪。我保證你是老大，一切都由你發號施令，你想去哪，我們就去哪，還能一起討論你的想法，無論多久我都奉陪。」

en_text: “No guesses as to who I am? Other than Joe the Janitor?”
zh_text: 「除了我是工友喬，你不猜猜我的真面目嗎？」

en_text: “You’re just the cleaner. Joe the cleaner. Nobody else. I don’t care if you’re anybody else, and if you are, then it’s none of my business. You can be anybody for all I care. But to me you’re just the cleaner. Just Joe. Joe who hasn’t committed any crimes other than making us all think you were slow. How about it, Joe? How about you untie me?”
zh_text: 「你就是清潔工，清潔工喬，不是別人。我不在乎你是不是別人，就算是，那也不關我的事，你可以是我所在乎的任何一人，但對我來說，你就是清潔工，就是喬，那個老是讓我覺得他很智障，卻從來都沒爲非作歹、作奸犯科的喬。怎樣，喬，放開我好不好？」

en_text: He’s sweating so much I’m starting to worry that he might be able to slip out of the knots and that the duct tape will just run off him in long, silver streaks.
zh_text: 他汗流浹背，我開始擔心他或許可以藉此掙脫打好的結，不然就是黏好的長銀色膠帶會這麼從他身上鬆落。

en_text: “Do you know who I am?”
zh_text: 「你知道我是誰嗎？」

en_text: He shakes his head. “No.”
zh_text: 他搖了搖頭。「不知道。」

en_text: “Come on, you do know. I’m the Carver.”
zh_text: 「拜託，你一定知道，我是『基督城屠夫』呀。

en_text: “I don’t know who you are, and after you’ve let me go, I won’t even think about it. Okay, Joe?”
zh_text: 「我不知道你是谁，只要你肯放我走，这件事我连想都不會再想。喬，這樣好不好？

en_text: This, of course, is all bullshit. Bullshit that is taught to these guys when they become cops. He’s trying to negotiate with me, but he has nothing to bargain with. He knows that, but what else can he do? He keeps using my name, trying to relate to me, trying to make me see him as a real person.
zh_text: 這些全是狗屁，全是這些傢伙在當上條子之後學到的。他正試著和我談判，但他手上什麼籌碼都沒有，這他非常清楚，但他還能怎樣呢？他不斷地稱呼我的名字，試著和我拉近關係、要我把他當成活生生的人來看待。

en_text: “Let’s make a few assumptions. First of all, let’s assume I’m telling the truth. Secondly, let’s assume I’m not about to let you go. Thirdly, let’s assume you don’t cooperate with what I want. Do you know what happens then?”
zh_text: 「現在先做幾個假設。第一，假設我說的是實話；第二，假設我並不打算放你走；第三，假設你並不怎麼合作。你知道接下來會怎樣嗎？」

en_text: He nods. Assumptions are something that cops aren’t supposed to make. They’re supposed to use facts, not maybes. However, Calhoun has been to some of the crime scenes. He can safely assume what will happen to him without needing any further evidence. All he has to do is swap, inside his mind, his own body for that of one of the women.
zh_text: 他點了點頭。條子是不應該預先假設、先入爲主的。他們應該結合事實，而非單憑猜測。然而，卡爾霍恩曾到過幾處命案現場，他可以不靠進一步的探證，就信心滿滿地爲接下來的遭遇作好假設。在他心裡，他很清楚自己所能做的就是一命抵一命，拿自己的身體去交換其中一個被他謀殺的女人。

en_text: “Yeah, I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “Good. Then let’s get a few of the ground rules out of the way. First of all, you’re all alone. Help isn’t coming, and you have no way to escape. However, don’t let this get you down. You’ve probably ﬁgured out that if I wanted you dead, you’d be dead already, right?”
zh_text: 一很好，我們開門見山，直接說明幾項基本的遊戲規則吧。第一，你單槍匹馬、孤立無援、無從逃脫。不過先別失望，因為你很可能已經猜到我若要殺你，你應該早就死了，對吧？

en_text: He nods. He probably knew that from the moment he came to.
zh_text: 他點了點頭。從他赴約的那刻起，他很可能早就了解這點。

en_text: “Because if you agree to what I want, which is most likely, you’ll not only get out of here with your own life, but you’ll get paid an income for surviving.”
zh_text: 「你要是答應我的要求——目前這看起來可能性較大——你不但可以活著離開這裡，還會因為保住性命而賺到一筆。」

en_text: At this, he slowly starts nodding—at the word income, not life. Suddenly he not only survives, he becomes richer. This is sounding like a pretty good deal to him. He’s already paying for more hookers and he doesn’t even know yet how much he’s earning.
zh_text: 就在我說到「錢」，而非「活著」的當下，他慢慢點起頭來。突然間，他不但可以活命，還會變得更加富有。對他而言，這筆交易聽起來挺吸引人。他砸在嫖妓上的錢越來越多，而且都已經到了這種地步，他居然還不知道自己到底有多少收入。

en_text: “The second thing is that I ask the questions, and you answer them truthfully. Failure to do so will jeopardize both aspects of the ﬁrst ground rule. Any questions?”
zh_text: 第二就是我問什麼，你都要老實回答，否則就會危害到雙方在第一項遊戲規則下的立場。懂了嗎？

en_text: He opens his mouth, but nothing comes out. Yes, he understands. Perfectly.
zh_text: 他張口欲言，卻無言以對。懂，他完全懂。

en_text:
“I suppose you want to know how much money and what you need to do for it?”
“Please.”
zh_text:
「我猜，你想知道自己得怎麼做，以及會拿到多少錢吧？」
對，我洗耳恭聽。

en_text: “Twenty thousand dollars, and it’s simple to earn. You don’t need to kill anybody for it, because you’ll be leaving that to me.”
zh_text: 「兩萬紐幣。很好賺吧？而且你誰都不必殺，只要交給我就行。」

en_text: He nods at this. Thinks twenty grand isn’t a lot of money to get tied up for, but it’s better than getting tied up and shot. Twenty grand is a lot of money to earn for doing nothing. This is the part of the plan he likes. The part of the plan I knew he would like.
zh_text: 他點了點頭，心想才爲了兩萬紐幣就被人綁成這樣眞不划算，不過遭人綑綁總比中彈來得好，而且自己什麼都沒做就可以賺到兩萬紐幣，這也算是相當可觀了。他喜歡這部分的計畫，而我也清楚他會喜歡。

en_text: “I don’t want anybody to die,” Bob starts, as if he really means it, and as if I’d really care even if he did. People dying isn’t a relevant factor for him, or for me. Under other circumstances—better circumstances, he’ll be thinking—we could have laughed at his joke. What is relevant is Daniela Walker.
zh_text: 「我並不想鬧出人命。」鮑伯劈頭就這麼說，彷彿他是認真的，彷彿這若是他的真心話我就會非常在意那樣。無論對他或是對我，有沒有鬧出人命和我倆毫無關係，而真正和我倆有關的，其實在於丹妮耶拉·沃克這個人。

en_text: I lean back on my elbow. If I smoked, now would be the time to casually light up an expensive cigarette. If I were an evil mastermind, now would be the time I started petting my white Persian cat. But I’m just a cleaner with no goldﬁsh to feed. An average, everyday Joe. If I had my mop, then maybe I would stroke it. If I had my metal bucket, I could beat out a rhythm. All I can do is turn the knife over and over in my hands, watching him watching the blade.
zh_text: 我撐起手肘向後靠。要是我有抽菸的習慣，現在將會是信手燃起一根高檔菸的好時機；要是我是邪惡組織的首腦，現在也會是輕撫那隻白色波斯貓的好時機。但我只不過是一個沒有金魚可養的清潔工，只不過是大家日常所見的喬。要是我有抹布，我很可能會拿來擦地；要是我有金屬水桶，我很可能會敲敲打打、演奏起打擊樂。但我現在所能做的，就只是把玩著那把刀，看他盯著刀鋒。

en_text: “Come now, Bob, you’ve killed before. I don’t see how you can feel bad about somebody else dying.” “I haven’t killed anybody.”
zh_text: 「鮑伯，拜託，你又不是沒殺過人，我看不出來你會因爲出了人命而難過。」「我誰都沒殺。」

en_text: I shake my ﬁnger back and forth. “No, no, no. I said no lying. Do you remember what I said would happen if you lied?” He nods. He remembers.
zh_text: 我來回晃動手指。「錯、錯、錯，我說過要誠實。記不記得我說過不誠實會怎樣？」他點頭，他記得。

en_text: “Good. I know of a couple of ways we can do this,” I say, reaching into my briefcase and rummaging around. “I can start by using these,” I pull out a pair of sharpened gardening shears, “on your ﬁngers. For every answer I don’t want to hear, I’ll remove one ﬁnger.”
zh_text: 「那好。我知道要是你不誠實，我們可以有幾種處理方式。」我說，把手伸進公事包，東摸西找。「這個，」我掏出了一把磨好的園藝剪，「我可以用這剪斷你的手指。凡是聽到不想聽的答案，我就剪掉一根。」

en_text: Actually, I won’t. I’m not going to remove any of them, but as long as he believes I’m going to, that’s all that really counts. This is where his assumptions are going to lead him astray. I watch his face as he studies the gardening shears. It takes no effort to imagine how they can wrap around any one of his ﬁngers, how the blades can sink through his ﬂesh, and how with a little bit of extra effort I can get them to snap through the bone. His imagination already has all his digits scattered across the ﬂoor behind his chair.
zh_text: 實際上我不會這麼做，也沒打算剪去他半根手指，但只有讓他以為我會照做，他才會說起真話，也才會覺得自己太過異想天開。我看著他的臉，他正仔細端詳園藝剪，不費吹灰之力就能想像刀刃是怎麼夾住他的任何一根手指，刀鋒是怎麼劃進他的肉，而我又是怎樣輕輕鬆鬆地「卡」一聲就把骨頭給剪了斷。他已經開始想像自己一根根的手指就這麼慘遭毒手，散落在椅子後方的地面。

en_text: I’m capable of this. Melissa would be too. And so is he.
zh_text: 我辦得到，梅莉莎辦得到，就連他自己也辦得到。

en_text: The three of us have all killed.
zh_text: 我們都殺過人。

en_text: “You did kill her, didn’t you?”
zh_text: 「她是你殺的吧？」

en_text: He nods.
zh_text: 他點了點頭。

en_text: “Can you tell me why?”
zh_text: 「可以告訴我原因嗎？」

en_text: He shrugs. “I’m still not sure.”
zh_text: 他聳了聳肩。「我也還沒找出原因。」

en_text: Not a detailed answer, but I believe it to be the truth—at least as far as he understands it.
zh_text: 這回答不夠詳細，但我相信這是事實——至少他了解這一點。

en_text: “Would you like me to help you understand why?”
zh_text: 「那要不要我告訴你原因？」

en_text: He does the wise thing and nods.
zh_text: 這次他學聰明了，點了點頭。

en_text: “It’s because you can,” I start. “The ability is inside you. You’ve always wanted to feel the power. What would it be like to kill somebody? Imagine the control! You imagined it, but of course it’s only a fantasy. You couldn’t admit to yourself that it’s something you’d actually like to try. In your mind you think about the outcomes, of how you could escape the blame, of how to make yourself look like the innocent party. Plenty of ways of doing it, but why explore them? After all, you’re only thinking about it, you’re not exactly considering it. Then one day the fantasy is no longer enough. Not the fantasy of killing, but of sex. Violent sex. So you hire a whore, but it isn’t the same, because she isn’t a real victim. You want to kill her, because that’s ideally where the violent sex leads, but you know there’s no point in killing a whore because they’re already dead. They’re zombies tanked up on bad luck and bad breeding. You needed to kill a better class of person, and then along came Daniela Walker. A victim of domestic abuse who refuses to follow through with laying charges against her husband.”
zh_text: 「因為你能，」我開始說，「你本身就具備那種能力，而你一直都想感受那種力量。『殺人』的感覺如何？想像一下如今自己一手在握、掌控一切！你是想像過，不過那只是你天馬行空、隨意幻想，你不敢承認自己其實想試試。你一心想著事情的後果，也就是如何逃避刑責、如何讓自己看似清白無罪，其中方法一大堆，你還有什麼好找的呢？但你終究只是想想，而不是詳加考慮、縝密擘劃，結果有一天，隨意幻想已經無法滿足你了，我指的不是殺人的幻想喔，而是性幻想、性暴力的幻想。於是你找了個妓女，但因為她並不是真正的被害人，所以這和想像中並不一樣。於是你想殺掉她，因為理想中的性暴力都是以這種結尾收場，但你很清楚殺掉這種有如行屍走肉的人根本毫無意義可言。他們就像倒楣透頂又品種不良的殭屍。你得找個高檔一點的人來殺，結果丹妮耶拉·沃克出現了，一個堅持拒絕向家暴先生提出告訴的被害人。

en_text: He says nothing. I think about the indications in the pathology report that said Daniela had previous injuries. If she’d left her husband, she’d still be alive. And somebody else wouldn’t be. Calhoun surely would have found somebody else.
zh_text: 他不發一語。我想起了病理解剖曾明確指出丹妮耶拉·沃克在死前便已傷痕累累。要是她離先生而去，現在還能保住一條小命，然後死的會是別人——卡爾霍恩鐵定會找別人下手。

en_text: “She threatens him, she even goes to the police, but at the end of the day her fear of him and her love for him prevent her from acting. This woman is a loser. You can’t understand how she could even have married a guy like that, let alone have his children. But you forget he’d been charming when she met him, the same way you were charming when you met your wife.”
zh_text: 「她報警，但她對他的愛和恐懼終究還是讓她遲遲沒有行動。這女人是個窩囊廢，你無法理解她怎麼會跟這種男人結婚，甚至有了小孩。但你可能忘了他倆在邂逅之時，他可是風流倜儻、魅力無限，就和你當初和太太相遇時如出一轍。」

en_text: I look at him. My speech hasn’t made any impact. If it’s true, and I believe most of it is, then he isn’t going to let me know. This annoys me, but not enough to jump up and cut his throat. I sit and wait.
zh_text: 我看著他，剛剛的話一點影響力都沒有。要是我說的是事實——我相信八九不離十——他也不會讓我知道，我是覺得很煩，但還不至於跳起來劃破他的喉嚨。我靜靜坐著、等著。

en_text: “You’re new in the city,” I continue, “so the opportunity to act out is irresistible. You know her address and learn the pattern of her movements. Her husband’s at work, her children are away at camp, so what could be better? Before you attack her, you decide to frame the husband, because what possible candidate could look any more attractive as her killer? Then you answer the question. One person ﬁts the bill perfectly, and that person is me. So what do you do? You frame me for a murder I didn’t commit, and to be honest, Bob, I never really appreciated it. But you’re lucky, because you’re being given the chance to change the way I feel about you. You can either leave this house a richer man, in terms of both money and character, or you can leave inside a body bag on your way straight down to hell. Of course, needless to say, punishment down there will be eternal, and eternity, Bob, is a very long time.”
zh_text: 「你對基督城還不熟，」我繼續說，「所以不禁想逮住機會上演一齣戲。你拿到了她的地址、掌握了她的行蹤，等到她先生去上班、小孩參加校外露營，這不就是你的大好時機嗎？在你攻擊她之前，你決定要栽贓給她先生，因為你想，還會有誰比她先生看起來更像兇手呢？於是你找起答案，發現有個人百分之百可以勝任，那人就是我，所以你幹了什麼好事？我根本沒殺人，你卻栽贓給我，坦白說，鮑伯，我一點都不感謝你，但因為你一直都有機會改變我對你的觀感，所以你真是好狗運。今天，你可以活著離開這間屋子、一夜致富，也可以命喪黃泉、不得好死。

en_text: I start wondering what I’m talking about. Hell? Who gives a damn about Satan? The limp-wristed, red-skinned motherfucker is a ﬁgment of the Christian imagination, designed solely as a deterrent for killers, thieves, rapists, liars, hypocrites, and mime artists—yet a lot of bloody good that’s done.
zh_text: 當然，到了地獄你將受盡折磨，這不用我說。我開始納悶自己到底在說些什麼，地獄？撒旦？那個懦弱無能、紅色皮膚的軟腳蝦完全是基督教所想像出來的虛構人物，純粹設計用來嚇阻小偷騙子僞君子殺人犯強暴犯或是默劇演員之類的，只不過最後卻一點鳥用也沒有。

en_text: “Whether you rot in hell or not isn’t my concern. What is my concern is what you did to poor Daniela Walker. From what I’ve learned, and from being here,” I spread my arms out to encompass the room, “I’ve come to some expert and insightful conclusions.”
zh_text: 「我在乎的不是你會不會在地獄遭到酷刑，而是你對可憐的丹妮耶拉·沃克做了什麼。一路下來，」我張開雙臂，作勢包圍整個房間，「我推論出一些專業又深入的結論。」

en_text: “Good for you.”
zh_text: 「算你厲害。」

en_text: I smile. “You broke into her house during the late afternoon, climbed upstairs while she was showering, and waited for her in the bedroom. In this bedroom.” It’s a familiar scenario.
zh_text: 我莞爾一笑。「你在傍晚闖進她家，趁她入浴時上樓，然後在臥房等她。就這間臥房。」這個場景好熟悉。

en_text: “She had no chance. After all, you had the element of surprise on your side, as well as being bigger and stronger. Her fear, her imagination, made her react, but not quickly enough to escape you. You struggled with her, managed to force her onto the bed, and she managed to reach to the bedside table and clutch at the only weapon she could ﬁnd.” I point to the table for effect. “She fought with you and managed to stab you with the pen she’d been using to ﬁll in her crossword puzzles. The wound wasn’t deep, but it was enough to piss you off. You tossed it away, then got back to business. Except the pen was your mistake, Bob, but you know that, don’t you? At the time, after you killed her, nothing else mattered. The pain was gone, as was any concern of being caught. The pen was the furthermost thing from your mind. Until you came back. Then it became the biggest thing on your mind, and it was only a matter of good luck that you were able to swap it unnoticed. At least unnoticed by everybody except me.”
zh_text: 「她毫無勝算。和她比較起來，你又高又壯，嚇人的本事可是掌握在你的手裡。她的恐懼、想像力都激起本能反應，但不足以快到逃過你的手掌心。你和她發生扭打、打算逼她床上就範，她則打算爬到床頭櫃、抓起任何能夠取得的武器。」爲了增添效果，我手指櫃子。「你們大打出手，她拿起玩塡字遊戲的鋼筆朝你身上一刺，傷口雖然不深，卻足以讓你抓狂，於是你抓起筆向外一扔，才接著辦起正事。但你栽在那支筆上了。鮑伯，你自己也很清楚吧？就在你殺了她的當下，什麼都已經不再重要。你不再感到疼痛，也不再擔心自己會不會被抓，當時你根本就沒想到那支筆。直到回來之後，那支筆才成了你心中的一塊大石，而你只能企盼自己走運、可以趁人不注意時把換掉筆，對，你的確趁別人不注意時成功偷天換日，但你完全忘記還有我。」

en_text: “What is it you want?”
zh_text: 「你到底想怎样？」

en_text: I shake my head. “Bob, Bob, Bob. I thought we had an understanding. You know you’re not allowed to ask the questions.” “Just tell me what you want.”
zh_text: 我搖了搖頭。「我還以爲我們已經達到共識。你應該很清楚自己不准發問。」「你只要告訴我你想怎樣。」

en_text: “That’s another question.”
zh_text: 「你還問？」

en_text: “No, it isn’t. It’s a request.”
zh_text: 「我沒問，我只是拜託你。」

en_text: “And that’s a lie.” I hold up the gardening shears. “You’re just asking for it, aren’t you?”
zh_text: 「那就是你不老實了。」我舉起園藝剪。「這可是你自找的。」

en_text: He shakes his head. “No. I swear.”
zh_text: 他搖頭。「沒有，我真的沒那意思。」

en_text: “What about Daniela? Was she asking for it?”
zh_text: 「那丹妮耶拉呢？那也是她自找的嗎？」

en_text: Bob’s face is wet and he’s looking down into his lap. We’re both sweating. It’s not warm outside, but somehow this house is still retaining the heat from the summer. The windows have been closed for three months now, so the air is stale and tastes like bad meat. I move over to the window. Open it slightly. Suck at the air outside. The smell, the thick air, the pressure on my skin—it is similar to my apartment the week I spent in bed with a bleeding ball and a bucket full of piss. I’d got used to the feeling, but it is a great relief to be rid of it now.
zh_text: 鮑伯臉上汗如雨下，往下看起大腿。我倆都是揮汗如雨。那天晚上很熱，而臥房的窗戶仍舊緊閉。截至目前爲止，這裡已經三個月沒開窗，所以空氣帶了股腐臭味，聞起來就像壞掉的肉。我挪身窗邊，開了點窗，吸了一口外頭的新鮮空氣。那種氣味、滯悶的空氣、我皮膚所感受到的壓力……剛剛我雖然已經習慣這種感覺，但如今可以解脫眞是讓我鬆了一大口氣。這地方和我花了一個禮拜與血流不止的睪丸、整桶小便待在床上的那間公寓頗爲類似。

en_text: I sit down, remove my jacket, and clutch at my damp shirt. Thoughts of going to the beach are hammering the front of my mind. I can feel the pull of the sea and the sand, even though I’m ﬁve or six miles from the nearest drop and grain, even though a trip to the beach tonight would be a pretty miserable experience. “Answer the Goddamn question, Bob.”
zh_text: 我坐了下來，脫掉夾克，揪起濕掉的襯衫，腦海中還不斷浮現前往海邊的念頭。即便我距離最近的地點少說也有十公里之遠，我似乎可以感受到海洋、沙灘的拉扯。要是現在我有泳衣，也能穿起緊身的材質，那我一定會在搞定這事之後直奔海邊。「鮑伯，老實回答。」

en_text: He tilts his head to look at me. He looks sorry, but he’s sorry to have been caught, not sorry for killing Daniela Walker.
zh_text: 他側頭盯著我看，一臉遺憾，卻是對自己被人逮到感到遺憾，而不是對殺了丹妮耶拉感到遺憾。

en_text: “I didn’t mean to kill her.”
zh_text: 「我不是有意要殺她的。」

en_text: The air seems to be getting stickier by the minute. I don’t reply to his answer. I just sit still, silently reasserting my dominance over this man. The room is cooling. Somewhere, Melissa is dreaming about her money. Somewhere nearby a dog is barking. Some place further away the police are coming closer, if they’ve not done so already, to discovering a match for the ﬁngerprints on the murder weapon they found in the dumpster.
zh_text: 此刻的空氣感覺起來更爲滯悶。我並沒回應他的答案，只是靜靜坐著，再次宣稱這男人如今可是任我擺佈。房裡泛起了點涼意。此時梅莉莎正在某處幻想著她的錢，然後警方要是沒發覺那把曾被他們遺漏的兇器上沾有符合嫌犯的指紋，那麼他們可能也正朝這兒來。

en_text: Bob is now a condemned man. He’s effectively on death row. It’s just that nobody has told him. His family, especially his wife, will have to live with the stench of blame. How can she justify not knowing what a monster her husband really is? Or how does she explain that she knew and never did anything about it?
zh_text: 鮑伯現在已被定罪，即將執行死刑，只是沒人告訴他。他的家人，尤其是他太太，她將得活在衆人的辱罵之下。她要如何證明自己對於枕邊人是個禽獸一無所知？還是她要怎麼解釋自己明明知情，卻袖手旁觀、不爲所動？

en_text: I’ve been wondering whether Bob has an alibi for several of the killings. He was in Auckland for the ﬁrst few. However, because of the seriousness of this horriﬁc series of murders, the police will work their way around any small inconsistencies, and when nobody else shows up dead, they will be satisﬁed with labeling Calhoun the Christchurch Carver. I’ve learned enough from cleaning their hallways to know that they’re so hard-pressed for a suspect, they’ll keep their mouths shut, never mention all the DNA evidence that never quite matched up, and if a few more bodies show up every now and again they’ll use a copycat defense. It’ll keep them happy, and the media, and the country. It’ll even keep me happy.
zh_text: 我一直在想，在鮑伯犯下的幾次謀殺案中，他是否都具備有效的不在場證明。前幾次案發時他人在奧克蘭，然而，有鑑於這次連續謀殺案駭人聽聞、案情嚴重，警方將在矛盾處動些細微的手腳，一旦沒再出現其他被害人，他們就會樂於替卡爾霍恩貼上標籤，把他當成基督城屠夫。我一直都在替他們打掃走廊，久到足以得知他們結案壓力很大，大都選擇乖乖閉嘴，絕口不提DNA根本不合的事，然後要是一年內又發生了幾起命案，他們就會辯稱兇手是在模仿先前的殺人模式。這麼做會讓他們開心、媒體開心、國人開心，甚至讓我開心。

en_text: “Okay, Bob, explain how killing her was an accident.”
zh_text: 「好，請你解釋一下是怎麼失手殺了她吧。」

en_text: He looks up. Stares into my eyes. He shrugs, then he looks down at the ﬂoor, then he shrugs again. He seems really unsure. “I followed her home, to talk to her, right?” he says, still looking down. “I wanted her to charge her husband with assault, ’cause the guy’s a real asshole, right? Shit, you probably saw him. Stuck-up, arrogant bastard. So full of himself, sure that he’s above the law, that it’s his right to beat the crap out of his wife. So I follow her home to tell her she’s making a mistake, and when I get here, I ﬁnd that she’s home alone.”
zh_text: 他抬起頭來，和我四目交接。「爲了跟她聊聊——就只是聊聊——我先跟蹤她回家，要她控告自己先生家暴，因爲那傢伙眞是窩囊廢。那混蛋白大高傲、自以爲是、完全以自我爲中心、認爲自己把太太打到屁滾尿流全都是他身爲丈夫的權利而且絕對和『犯法』沾不上邊，也因此我才會跟蹤她回家、告訴她她錯了，然後一到這裡，我才發現原來她獨自在家。

en_text: “It wasn’t your job, Bob. You were here to work on my case alone.”
zh_text: 「鮑伯，這不關你的事，你搶走了我的案子。」

en_text: He sighs. “I know. I know that, but, well, it just happened.”
zh_text: 「我懂、我懂，不過……呃……事情就是這樣嘛。

en_text: “Did you know she was going to be home alone?”
zh_text: 「你知不知道她接下來會單獨在家？」

en_text: “Not really.”
zh_text: 「不太確定。」

en_text: “That sounds like a yes to me, Bob.”
zh_text: 「這聽起來像是你知道。」

en_text: “I suspected.”
zh_text: 我想過有這可能。

en_text: “Which is why you followed her, right? Because you could only talk to her while she was alone. Having her husband in the same room wasn’t going to make for a useful conversation.”
zh_text: 「那才是你跟蹤她的原因吧？因爲你只能在她獨自一人時才能和她說得上話。」他試圖聳一聳肩，礙於全身遭我綑綁，只能微微一動。

en_text: “I guess so.”
zh_text: 「是吧。」

en_text: “You guess so. Okay, then what happened?”
zh_text: 是吧？好，那接下來呢？

en_text: “I sat outside for a few minutes, considering what to do.”
zh_text: 「我在外面坐了一會兒，心想如何是好。」

en_text: “Considering whether to kill her or not?”
zh_text: 「心想自己該不該殺掉她吧？」

en_text: He shakes his head. “Nothing like that.”
zh_text: 「沒這回事。」

en_text: “What then?”
zh_text: 「不然咧？」

en_text: “I don’t know. I just sat there, watching the house, thinking about the best way to convince her of what she needed to do. Finally, when I went to the door and knocked, there was no answer. I was going to leave . . .” he says, but doesn’t ﬁnish the sentence. “But you stayed,” I tell him. “I stayed,” he says. “For some reason I couldn’t tell you, I stayed.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。我只是坐在那裡，望著房子，思考著說服她最佳方法。最後當我走到門邊敲了敲門、屋裡沒人應門而正打算離開時，不知怎麼搞的，我就是留在原地。」

en_text: “Because you saw an opportunity.”
zh_text: 「因爲你找到機會了。」

en_text: “No,” he says. “It wasn’t like that. I was worried. What if she wasn’t answering because her husband was home beating her up for not having dinner on the table or for not cleaning his shoes or whatever excuse the piece of shit needed? Anyway, I checked the door and it was locked, but I had some keys on me designed for picking most house locks, so I used them.”
zh_text: 「因爲我很擔心。我擔心她之所以沒來應門，全是因爲她老公爲了桌上沒晚餐、鞋子沒擦或是什麼鳥事就把她痛打一頓。總之，我檢査了一下門，發現門是鎖著的，但我握有幾把設計來打開多數門鎖的萬用鑰匙，於是用它開了鎖。

en_text: I know the keys well. I also know that domestic abuse isn’t about a man who is in love with his wife too much; it’s about a man who is in love with the ability to control her.
zh_text: 我很清楚那種鑰匙，也很清楚家暴的來由不是男人過度迷戀自己的太太，而是過度迷戀那種控制的能力。

en_text: “I checked around the kitchen, the living room, looking for her.”
zh_text: 「於是我在廚房和客廳東看西看，找起她人在哪。

en_text: “Did you call her name?”
zh_text: 「你有叫她嗎？」

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「沒有。

en_text: “Is that because you didn’t want her to know you were there?”
zh_text: 是不是因爲你不想讓她知道你就在那？

en_text: He shakes his head. “That wasn’t it at all. I didn’t want to let the husband know I was there, in case he was home and hitting her. I wanted to catch him in the act.” “That’s pretty lame, Bob.”
zh_text: 他搖了搖頭。「不盡然，她先生要是正在毒打她，我可不想讓他知道我就在那。」「這理由不充分。」

en_text: “No it’s not. This is a big house. I couldn’t be sure what was happening, and where.” “So then what?”
zh_text: 「是真的。這房子很大，我無法確定屋裡正在發生什麼事，還有發生地點在哪。」「然後？」

en_text: “She was upstairs sitting on the bed. Sobbing.”
zh_text: 「她人在樓上，坐在床邊，正在啜泣。」

en_text: “Which is why she didn’t answer the door, I suppose?”
zh_text: 「我猜那就是她為何沒去應門。」

en_text:
“That was my thought. When she saw me, she started to freak out. I quickly explained who I was, but she was recognizing me anyway.”
“She must have been relieved you were a cop and not a homicidal maniac,” I say.
zh_text: 「我也是這麼想。她一看到我就嚇個半死，我馬上跟她解釋我是誰，但她已經認出我來。」「聽到你是警察而不是瘋狂殺人魔，她鐵定鬆了一口氣。」我說。

en_text:
If he sees the irony, he doesn’t let it show.
“She sat down again, and we began to talk about her husband, but mostly about her. You see, the issue was her, not him. He was always going to be a wife beater. There was no way of stopping him. What people don’t understand is that these guys can’t be rehabilitated. I mean, what the hell are you going to rehabilitate them to? All he’s ever known is violence. I tried talking to her, calmly and reasonably, and that was okay, at ﬁrst.” He pauses and looks at me. His eyes look damp. I wonder if crying is beyond this madman’s ability to act. I prompt him to continue with a slight repositioning of the gardening shears. I’m eager to hear his thoughts.
zh_text:
他若聽得出我是在調侃他，也不會表現出來。
「她又坐了下來，我們開始聊她先生，他是個施予家暴的先生，沒人阻止得了他。人們不了解這種傢伙是不可能回復正常模樣的，我的意思是，大家是要他回復成什麼模樣？這種人的認知中只有暴力。我試圖冷靜又理性地和她聊聊，起初還很。。」
他停頓半晌，盯著我，雙眼滿是淚水。我心想，這瘋子的反應能力中是否具備「哭泣」這個項目。我微微動起園藝剪，慫恿他繼續說。我實在迫不及待想要聽聽他的想法。

en_text: “Pretty soon she couldn’t see my way of thinking, my way of understanding.”
zh_text: 她很快就無法理解我的思考和理解方式。

en_text: “The correct way, you mean?”
zh_text: 「也就是你心目中的『正確方式』吧？」

en_text: “Yeah. Do you know what it’s like, Joe, to know you’re absolutely right about something—I mean, beyond any doubt—but you can’t get somebody else to agree with you? It’s not that they don’t understand, or that they don’t want to. They’ve become so used to doing the wrong thing that there couldn’t possibly be another way.”
zh_text: 是的，我的意思是，當你在某方面的見解鐵定沒錯，但卻無法說服別人認同你的那種感覺。別人不是不懂，或是不想懂，而是他們對於錯事已經習以爲常，覺得事情不可能還有其他出路。

en_text: “Get back to the point, Bob.”
zh_text: 「鮑伯，請你回到重點。」

en_text: “We ended up disagreeing, pretty quickly actually, and then we were arguing. In the end she started screaming at me to leave. I asked her to calm down, but she wouldn’t. Then she tried to call the police, so I had to stop her. She slapped me, so then I hit her back. Next thing I knew she was dead and I was standing over her naked body.”
zh_text: 「結果我們各持己見，很快就發生爭執，最後她開始尖叫、要我離開。我要她冷靜下來，但她不肯，還企圖報警，所以我得阻止她。結果我被她摑了一巴掌才還手，然後等到我意識到怎麼回事的時候，她已經死了，而我就站在她赤裸裸的屍體旁。」

en_text: He stops talking. We both listen to the silent room. Peaceful, but still warmer than I’d like. I believe most of his story, but he’s left something out. “Next thing you knew,” I repeat. “I didn’t mean for it to happen.”
zh_text: 他不再說話。我倆都聆聽著這間萬籟俱寂的臥房，很平靜，也很炎熱。大部分他所說的我都相信，但有件事他漏掉沒說。

en_text: “A touching story, Bob,” I say, reaching to my eyes with an imitation hanky, wiping away pretend tears. “It seems you’ve gone for a classic defense strategy. Do they teach you that at training college, or did you pick it up being a cop? See, Bob, what you’ve done here is extremely common. You’ve shifted all the blame onto the victim. She’s the one who disagreed, she’s the one being unreasonable, and she’s the one who hit you. If she’d refrained from doing any of those things, then she’d still be alive today. Am I right?” No answer.
zh_text: 「鮑伯，這故事眞感人。」我說，作勢拿起手帕，擦去假裝流下的淚水。「你聽起來似乎上過經典的防衛策略課程喔。你是在培訓院學的，還是當上警察之後才會的？你現在的所作所爲太老套了，你把所有的錯全推給了被害人：是她和你意見不合、是她自己不合情理、是她先動手打你，要是她忍住不做以上那些事情，那她到了今天就還能保有自己的小命。我說的沒錯吧？他默不作聲。

en_text: “Am I right, Bob?”
zh_text: 「我說的沒錯吧？」

en_text: Again the shrug. “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 他又牽強地聳了聳肩。「我不知道。」

en_text: “Come on, Bob, you do know. It’s the whole domestic abuse scenario over again. She deserved to be punished, didn’t she, because she stepped out of line. If she’d done what she was told, if she’d simply obeyed, then she’d be living the contented and happy life. But she didn’t, so you killed her—not that you remember doing so. That’s the second common phase here, Bob. How many killers have you put away who’ve told you they don’t remember anything? How many have told you that if it weren’t for the crazy way this or that particular female acted, then none of this or that would have happened? Now tell me what really happened.”
zh_text: 「你明明就很清楚，整個家暴的場景再度上演。你覺得是她活該。要是她乖乖聽話，她就會活得心滿意足、幸福快樂。但她就是不聽，所以你就索性把她殺了——但你已經忘了。鮑伯，這太老套了。在你辦過的案子裡，有幾個殺人犯告訴過你他們記得過程？有幾個殺人犯告訴過你要不是這女人發瘋似的這樣或那樣，事情就不會這樣或那樣了？現在你給我說清楚到底怎麼回事。」

en_text: “That is what happened.”
zh_text: 事情就是這樣。

en_text: “Yeah, most of it probably did, but I’d bet my life on it . . .” I pause, create dramatic effect, then change my mind. “No, I’d bet your life on it that you do remember killing her, and were aware of every second of it.”
zh_text: 「是啊，或許八成就是這樣，但我敢打賭……」我稍作停頓，營造出戲劇性的效果，接著改變主意。「不對，我敢打賭你明明就記得殺了她，還對每分每秒的經過一清二楚。」

en_text: “I can’t remember.”
zh_text: 「我沒辦法記住。」

en_text: He sounds like a whining child. “There’s no such word as can’t, Bob.” I lift the gardening shears to prove my point. He says nothing until I start to rise.
zh_text: 他聽起來就像個哀嚎的孩子。「鮑伯。」我舉起園藝剪，證明我的論點他悶不作聲，直到我站起身子。

en_text: “Okay, okay.” He’d have his hands out in a defensive gesture if he could, waving them in the air like a maniac. “I do remember.”
zh_text: 「好好好，」他要是可以，就會像個瘋子伸出手在空中揮舞，做出一副「我怕了你」的手勢。「我記得。」

en_text: “Oh? And what do you remember?” I don’t need to know this for my plan to work. I’m just interested, as a fellow participant in this game of life and death.
zh_text: 「喔？那你記得什麼？」我其實不必知道這些就能執行這項計畫，但如今既然身爲這場生死遊戲的參賽者，我就是很感興趣。

en_text: “We argued, like I told you, and she picked up the phone and threatened to call the police. So I hit her, and once I did that, I knew there’d be no way to shut her up.”
zh_text: 「如我剛剛所說，我們發生爭吵，然後她拿起電話、威脅我要報警，結果我出手打她，而我一旦出手，也就明白自己再也無法讓她安靜下來了。」

en_text: “Come now, Bob. She’s a domestic-abuse victim. She’s used to keeping her trap shut when a man hits her.”
zh_text: 「拜託，她是家暴的受害者，一旦被人打了，必然習慣乖乖閉嘴。」

en_text: “Not this time. She told me I was going to lose my job for what I’d done, and she was right too, so I hit her again, this time harder. Then I shoved her onto the bed and . . .” He stops, either to think of what to say next, or to invent it. “Well, I needed to make it look like she was one of your victims, Joe.”
zh_text: 「這次不是這樣。她說我將失去工作，這聽起來挺有道理，於是我又出手打她，這次打得更重，然後再把她推到床上……」他就此打住，不是在想接著怎麼說就是故事怎麼編。「呃……喬，我得讓這看起來像是你下的手。」

en_text: “And you knew just how to do it. You screwed that prostitute I killed the other night. You did to her what your wife won’t let you even think about. And you take that experience from Becky the Whore to Little Miss Domestic Abuse.”
zh_text: 你知道該怎麼做。你和我那天殺掉的妓女上過床——你太太連想都沒想過同意你做的事，你全都要她做了——接著在家暴小姐的身上沿用你對妓女貝琪所做過的事。

en_text: “I had to make it look real,” he says, and he says it in a defeated tone, not the kind of tone somebody who stands by their work would use.
zh_text: 「我得讓這看起來像是眞的。」

en_text: “Is that all, Bob? Or did you want to enjoy yourself as well? Come on, you can tell me. I’m not here to judge you. I just want to hear how you’re no better than me.” He stares right at me. His face, tight with rage, spits the answer at me. “Sure, I enjoyed it. Like, I mean, what wasn’t to enjoy? Pure power.”
zh_text: 「鮑伯，就只有這樣嗎？還是你也很享受？拜託，你可以告訴我。我不是來這審判你，而是想要聽聽你也沒比我好到哪兒去的。」他直盯著我看。盛怒之下，他繃緊了臉上的肌肉，藉此表示對我的回答。「沒錯，我是很享受，就如我所說，這種單純的權力誰不享受啊？」

en_text: “Pure power. Isn’t that the answer, Bob? Isn’t that what we all look for?”
zh_text: 「單純的權力？這不就是答案嗎？這不就是衆人苦苦追尋的？」

en_text: “What do you want from me?”
zh_text: 「你想從我這得到什麼？」

en_text: “That’s a question, Bob.”
zh_text: 「鮑伯，問題就在這裡。」

en_text: “I don’t give a shit, Joe. Just tell me what you want, or fuck off. You’re wasting my time, you little asshole.” I’m not shocked at his sudden outburst. Over the last hour, I’ve touched several nerves. Before all of this is over, a knife is going to touch several more.
zh_text: 「喬，我什麼都不想管，你只要告訴我你想要怎樣，否則拉倒。你一直在浪費我的時間！」對於他突如其來的情緒爆發，我並不震驚。先前的一小時裡，我一直都在試探他的底限，搞得他戰戰兢兢、如履薄冰。

en_text: “The requirement is simple. All you need to do is listen.”
zh_text: 「我的要求很簡單。你只要乖乖聽話就好。

en_text: “That simple, huh?”
zh_text: 「喔？就這麼簡單？」

en_text: “That’s right.”
zh_text: 「就這麼簡單。」

en_text: “Bullshit,” he says. “What do I have to listen to?”
zh_text: 放你媽的屁！我會有什麼話要聽！

en_text: “A confession.”
zh_text: 「告解。」

en_text: “Yours?”
zh_text: 「你要告解？」

en_text: “Funnily enough, no. But it’s your job to be my security, my insurance if you like. You knew from the moment you saw my face I was either going to kill you or make a deal. Well, here’s the deal, Bob. I will give you twenty thousand dollars, in cash, tomorrow night, to listen to a confession. That’s all you have to do. Just sit and listen and remember. Do you think you can handle that?”
zh_text: 「這就妙了，不是我要告解。你如果願意，你的工作就是當我保鏢、保護我的安全。從你看到我臉的那一刹那，你就很清楚我不打算殺了你，想是跟你交易。所以鮑伯，現在交易來了。明晚我會給你現金兩萬紐幣，要你聆聽告解。你只要乖乖照做，只要坐著、聽著然後牢牢記住就行了。你覺得自己辦得到嗎？

en_text: “Then what? You let me go, is that it?”
zh_text: 「然後？然後你就會放我走了嗎？」

en_text: “That’s it.”
“And what’s in it for you?”
zh_text: 「這麼做究竟對你有什麼意義？」

en_text: “My freedom. Yours too.”
zh_text: 「這攸關我的自由，還有你的自由。」

en_text: “And if I refuse?”
zh_text: 「那我如果拒絕呢？」

en_text: “I’ll kill you. Right now.”
zh_text: 「那我現在就會幹掉你。」

en_text: “I want half the money now.”
zh_text: 「我要先拿到一半的現金。」

en_text: “You’re not really in a situation to ask for anything, Bob.” I stand and walk over to him.
zh_text: 「你現在的處境沒資格要求。」我站起身子，向他走去

en_text: “What are you doing?” I tilt the chair back and start dragging it across the carpet. It’s damn heavy, and my testicle starts to throb.
zh_text: 「你幹嘛？」我將椅子微微後傾，拖過地毯，媽的有夠重，害我的睪丸因使力而開始抖動。

en_text: “Joe? What the hell are you up to?”
zh_text: 「喬，你到底要做什麼？」

en_text: “Shut up, Bob.” I continue pulling on the chair, and it makes scuff marks across the carpet, but ﬁnally I manage to get Calhoun into the bathroom. “I’m afraid you’ll have to spend the night here.”
zh_text: 「閉嘴。」我一直拉著椅子，隨著它在經過的地毯留下磨痕，我還是努力地把卡爾霍恩拉到浴室。「恐怕你得在這裡過夜。」

en_text: “Why?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼？」

en_text: “Safer that way.”
zh_text: 「這樣比較安全。」

en_text: “For who?”
zh_text: 「對誰？」

en_text: “For me.”
zh_text: 「對我啊。」

en_text: I pull out some duct tape. “Anything else before I seal you up for the night?”
zh_text: 我拉開膠帶。「在我貼上你的嘴巴之前，你還有什麼要說的嗎？」

en_text: “You’re a real psycho, Joe, do you know that?”
zh_text: 「喬，你是個心理變態！你自己知不知道？」

en_text: “I know lots of things, Detective Inspector.”
zh_text: 「偵緝督察，我知道的可多了。」

en_text: I run the tape across his mouth. Then I head back into the bedroom and take the parking ticket from my briefcase. I squat down behind Bob, grab the skin on the back of his hand, and start twisting until he unclenches it, then I push his ﬁngertips against the ticket.
zh_text: 我用膠帶貼住他的嘴，回頭走進臥房，從公事包拿出了那張停車卡，接著蹲在鮑伯後面，抓住他的手背肌開始扭轉，直到拳頭鬆開，再把他的指紋按在票卡上。

en_text: “No going anywhere, Bob. Oh, and the toilet’s there if you need it.” I grin at him, then walk back into the bedroom, closing the door behind me. I put the ticket into an evidence bag, then into my briefcase. I lock the house before leaving. It’s dark when I get outside. I feel like I’m suffering from heat exhaustion, but after a minute in the cool air that problem disappears. The streetlights throw a pale glow into the black night. I drive Calhoun’s car into town and grab the ticket from the machine at the entrance to the parking building. I head up the ramps—the number of cars getting fewer the higher I drive—until I reach the very top, where there is only one. I don’t turn the car sharply enough, and end up scraping the corner of the front bumper all along the side of the other car, leaving a deep graze and a line of small dents. I notice that the tires on the other car have half deﬂated over time. I climb out. The smell coming from the trunk of the abandoned car is barely noticeable.
zh_text: 「鮑伯，待在這不許動。有需要的話廁所在那。」我朝他咧嘴一笑，走回臥房，關上身後的房門，然後把票卡放進證物袋，再放進公事包。夜幕低垂，我也精疲力盡，感到身子正在發冷。離開前，我替房子上了鎖。街燈在暗夜中投射出蒼茫的白光。空氣很溫暖，我透過陣陣吹來的微風嗅出修剪過後的青草味。我開著卡爾霍恩的車進城，從停車大樓的入口機器抽了張停車卡，徑往坡道開去，車子開上的樓層越高，車輛也就越少，直到我開上頂樓，那裡就只剩下一輛車了。我轉彎時不夠俐落，結果保險桿擦撞到另一輛車的車身，留下了深深的刮痕與長條狀的輕微凹陷。我注意到那輛車的輪胎隨著時間一久已經洩了一半的氣。我下了車，幾乎察覺不到那廢棄車輛後車廂所傳出的臭味。

en_text: With nothing else to do, I head toward home and toward the end of another long night.
zh_text: 閒來無事，於是我往自家住處、另一個漫漫長夜的盡頭而去。

en_text: Another phase completed.
zh_text: 另一個階段又完成了。

en_text: She doesn’t know this is where she is driving to until she pulls up the long, twisting driveway lined with beautiful trees, which is ironic because she wanted to come here earlier and found herself driving in a different direction. She can’t park in her usual spot because the church has become a crime scene, so she parks out on the street and uses a smaller entrance to walk through.
zh_text: 直到她把車停在細長、蜿蜒又種滿了美麗行道樹的車道後，她才知道自己正開往何處。她把車停在陰暗處，下了車，一腳踩上了綠油油的草坪。距離天黑還有一小時，她打算就耗在這裡。

en_text: Sally makes her way to her brother’s grave and crouches down next to it, not over it. She’s always careful about that. She has a whirlwind of scenarios racing through her head, but she can’t comprehend any of them, and the ones she can almost grasp keep ﬂoating away from her. Joe and the second man had been inside for at least an hour. She had been relieved when Joe came out okay, and tempted to follow him, but she was more curious about who the second man was. She’d waited another half hour, but he hadn’t shown up. Most likely he lived there. She starts brushing her hands back and forth through the grass, letting the soft textures tickle her palms. The grass is wet. She had written down the address before leaving. What she would do with that information she wasn’t sure. Probably just leave it scrawled across the notepad in her front seat for the next few weeks before balling it up and tossing it out. Joe driving different cars. Joe with ﬁles at his house. Joe with a missing testicle. Joe secretly meeting people.
zh_text: 莎莉一路走到弟弟墳前，趴在墓碑旁，而非墓碑上。她向來對此小心翼翼。此時她腦海中快速地湧現一個個的畫面，但就是沒一個她搞得清楚，而那些差點搞得清楚的卻「咻」一聲就不見蹤影。喬和之後來的那個男人在屋裡至少待了一個小時。當喬安然無恙地走出屋外，她鬆了口氣，打算跟蹤他，但這時她比較好奇的反而是之後的男人究竟是誰。於是她又等了半小時，只不過那人並沒出現，他很有可能就住在那。她來回摸起地面的草坪，讓草兒柔細的質地搔觸著掌心。她在離開前記下了地址。她到底留著這些連自己都不確定是什麼的資訊幹嘛呢？也許就只是把它寫在前座的筆記本上，擺在那幾個禮拜，之後再揉成紙團扔掉。

en_text: Well, okay, Joe went to somebody’s house, the same way she’s gone to other people’s houses. Gone there and had coffee, played some cards, killed some time, ate some dinner. What is so suspicious about that? Nothing. Except Joe parked two blocks away and left in a different car. Plus the house—somehow she knows that house.
zh_text: 喬這次開的車不一樣。喬的家裡放著資料夾。喬有一邊的睪丸沒了。喬偷偷摸摸和別人碰面。好，這麼說吧，就像自己去別人家裡喝杯咖啡、打打牌、消磨時間、用個晚餐那樣，喬也同樣會去別人家裡，所以這有什麼可疑的呢？除了喬把車停在兩個路口外、開了另一輛車子離開還有那間房子以外——不知怎麼她就是認得那間房子——其實沒啥大不了的吧。

en_text: “So what do I do, Martin?”
zh_text: 「馬丁，我該怎麼做？」

en_text: If her brother could reach out from his grave and offer her some advice, it wouldn’t be Do nothing. It was her doing nothing that had got Martin killed ﬁve years ago. It has been her lack of responsibility, her laziness, her unawareness. She was doing nothing ﬁve years ago when she should have been doing something. She should have been doing anything to stop Martin from being hit at forty miles an hour in a thirty-mile zone. It wasn’t the school’s fault. It wasn’t even really the driver’s fault. It was her fault. She knows some people would blame God, and she suspects her parents split the blame between her and Him.
zh_text: 要是她弟弟可以爬出墳墓給她一點建議，那麼他的建議會是「什麼都別做。」五年前，她就是懶惰、沒責任感、毫不留神、什麼都沒做才會害死馬丁。五年前，當她原本應該有所行動的時候，她什麼都沒做。她原本應該有所行動，好讓馬丁不致在速限五十五公里的地區被時速六十五公里的車撞上。這不是學校的錯，也不是司機的錯，而是她的錯。她知道有人會說是造化弄人，但她懷疑自己爸媽除了覺得造化弄人，也覺得她難辭其咎。

en_text: That’s why her mother ﬂinches when she puts an arm around her. That’s why her parents didn’t try to convince her to stay at nursing school, and allowed her to give up her career to help them pay the bills. It was difﬁcult not to hate God. It was His fault for making Martin intellectually handicapped. It was easy to lay blame with her, though. It was her fault that Martin had run out into trafﬁc. Her fault for forgetting how excitable he could be when she ﬁnished her studies early and got the chance to pick him up from school. She’d rung home to say she could pick Martin up. Her mother had told her not to worry, but Sally had gone ahead and worried. She loved the look on Martin’s face when he stepped out of school and saw her waiting there for him.
zh_text: 那也是她在抱住媽媽時身體猛地一縮的原因，也是爸媽沒試著說服她待在護校，而讓她放棄自己的事業、替他們還債的原因。不怨天尤人很難。要不是造化弄人，馬丁也不會生來就是智障，但把錯推到她的頭上總是比較容易。大家覺得馬丁衝到路上都是她的錯；忘了她去學校接他然後他會有多麼興奮也是她的錯。她打過電話回家，說她能去接他下課。媽媽雖然要她不用操心，但莎莉已經操起心來。她愛極了馬丁在走出學校、看到她就在那等他的表情。

en_text: The rules were always simple. Her parents had told Martin a thousand times. He was never to cross the road. And she knew the rules too. She was never to park across the road and wait for him there; she either parked on his side of the road, or she walked over. Her parents reminded her time and time again, but the problem when people remind you so often is that you start to ignore it. The words go in, but they don’t settle anywhere. The other problem was she was late. Only by two minutes. How many times has she remembered the route she took to his school that day? A red light there that could have been green. A person towing a trailer ahead of her at twenty-ﬁve instead of thirty miles an hour. A pedestrian crossing with people taking their time to cross it. It all added up, and in the end it came to two minutes. It all added up the same way all the ages in the graveyard add up and divide to get an average of sixty-two. Just simple mathematics combining to end a life.
zh_text: 規則一向非常簡單。爸媽已經告訴馬丁不下數次，不准他過馬路，而她也明白這項規則，所以她從來不會把車停在馬路對面、在那等他；她只會把車停在他那一邊，或者走路過去接他。爸媽不斷耳提面命、再三叮嚀，但問題就在於人家要是太常提醒你，你就會開始左耳進、右耳出，充耳不聞。另一個問題則在於那天她遲到了，只遲到兩分鐘。當天她開到學校前方的路——她不知回想起多少遍了——那裡的紅燈應該是綠燈才對。她前方有人以時速四十公里，而非五十公里的速度開著吊車。行人和其他人慢慢過著馬路。這一切的一切兜在一起，便讓事情有所耽擱，結果慢了兩分鐘；這一切的一切兜在一起，便有如把墓園裡的所有年齡加總，加以平均，就能得出了「六十二」的平均數字。數學何其容易，結合起來便足以結束一條寶貴的生命。

en_text: She’d pulled up outside the school two minutes later than she should have. She’d opened her car door two minutes after she should have opened it. And Martin had seen her from across the road. It all came down to mathematics, basic physics, and human dynamics. Martin getting excited. Martin running over the road to meet her while she was getting out of her car. Martin getting in the way of an object moving much faster than he was, weighing much more than he did. She’d run to him and knelt by his side. He was alive, but that had changed two days later. She’d let her brother down when he’d needed her most.
zh_text: 她把車停在校外，只不過慢了兩分鐘打開車門，馬丁就已經看到她在馬路對面。所有一切都可拆解成數學、基礎物理學還有人體動力學。馬丁非常興奮，在她準備下車時，他等不及要穿越馬路找她，結果被某個速度比他快、重量比他重的物體迎頭撞上。她跑向他，跪在他身旁，當下他還活著，但兩天後事態急轉直下——他走了。就在弟弟最需要自己的時候，她讓他失望了。

en_text: She won’t let Joe down. He needs her. He needs somebody to look out for him, to protect him from whatever madness he’s got himself involved in.
zh_text: 這次她不會讓喬失望。他需要她、需要某人替他留意，並保護他免於陷入那無法自拔的狂亂。

en_text: The walk home takes me through streets that smell like wet dog. My clothes stick to me, my underwear keeps on bunching up into my ass. When I get home, I bury the murder weapon and the gloves in the yard. I make my way upstairs, pulling my keys from my pocket to . . .
zh_text: 步行回家的途中，我穿越了一片霧濛濛且味似汗臭的空氣。我的衣服就這麼黏在身上，就連屁股也有如穿起丁字褲那樣緊緊夾著內褲。一回到家，我就把兇器和手套埋進庭院。我一路上樓，從口袋裡掏出鑰匙，正要……可惡！

en_text: For fuck’s sake! On the ﬂoor directly outside my apartment door is Pickle. Or Jehovah. It’s too damn difﬁcult to tell. I spin around, looking for the ﬂuffy bastard that did this, but it’s gone. I crouch down, and touch my dead ﬁsh with my ﬁnger. It feels rubbery.
zh_text: 就在我公寓門外的地上，我看到了泡菜——還是耶和華？眞的分辨不出。我繞了一圈，想找出是哪隻臭貓幹的好事，但就是遍尋不著。我蹲下身子，用手指碰觸我死去的魚，沒想到摸起來挺有彈性的。

en_text: I ﬁnd an evidence bag in the kitchen. I’m bending over the ﬁsh when I hear the meowing. I look up, and at the end of the hall is the Goddamn cat. On the ﬂoor ahead of it is the other goldﬁsh. Slowly the cat reaches forward with its paw, pushes the ﬁsh a few inches toward me, then pulls its paw back. He tilts his head, then meows at me. I take a knife from my briefcase, which is still by the door. Keeping his eyes on me, the cat reaches forward and pushes the ﬁsh even further toward me. Then it sits. What the hell is it trying to do? I get hold of the biggest knife I can ﬁnd.
zh_text: 我從廚房找來一只證物袋。正當我朝著小魚彎腰時，我聽到了貓叫聲，於是抬頭一看，那隻可惡的貓就在走廊的盡頭，他前方又躺著另一條金魚。那隻貓緩緩用爪子向前一撥，把魚向我推進了幾公分，之後再縮回爪子。牠側了側頭，對著我喵喵叫，我則從仍舊擺在門邊的公事包裡拿出刀子。貓兒直盯著我看，一邊往前一邊又把魚朝我推進了些，然後坐下身子。他到底想幹嘛？我拿起手邊所能找到的那把大刀。

en_text: “Come on, pussycat. Come on.”
zh_text: 「來呀，小貓，過來呀。」

en_text: It starts toward me, covers half the distance, stops, turns back toward the ﬁsh, stops, then turns back toward me. It meows. I tighten my grip on the knife. Then it moves slowly back to the ﬁsh, picks it up softly between its teeth, and carries it toward me. It stops a few feet away, lowers the ﬁsh to the ﬂoor, then takes a few steps back. Once again it meows. I get on my hands and knees so I can slowly crawl forward. I keep the blade of the knife ahead of me.
zh_text: 牠向我走來，走到一半之後停下腳步，回頭往金魚走去，然後停下腳步，再轉身向我走來，發出了喵喵叫。我把刀握得更緊，小貓又慢慢朝金魚移動，輕輕啣起金魚朝我走來。牠就停在約莫一公尺外，把魚放在地上，然後向後退了幾步，又喵了幾聲。爲了慢慢往前爬，這次我趴在地上，直讓刀鋒朝外。

en_text: And then I understand what it’s doing. It’s offering my ﬁsh back to me. It meows again, but this time it is more of a whispering whine.
zh_text: 後來我弄清楚牠在幹嘛了——牠正試著把魚還我。牠又開始喵喵叫，不過這次比較像是叨叨細語。

en_text: “There’s a good boy,” I say in my friendly voice, happy to lull it into believing I no longer have any urge to see it skinned. “Come on, fella. I’m not going to kill you, boy. I’m not going to break your neck.”
zh_text: 「這樣才乖。」我用友善的聲音說著，樂於引誘牠相信我沒有看著牠遭人宰殺的衝動。「過來呀，小夥子，我不會殺你，更不會扭斷你的脖子。」

en_text: It meows and comes another few steps closer. I keep moving toward it. Closer now. Less than an arm’s length away. Closer still . . . We reach each other, and it pushes its head down and head-butts my ﬁst.
zh_text: 牠開始喵喵叫，又朝我走近幾步。我則一直朝牠移動，越離越近，就連一隻手臂的距離都不到，而且持續接近中……當我們碰在一塊兒，牠低下頭來，在我拳頭上磨磨蹭蹭。

en_text: And me? What do I do?
zh_text: 那我呢？我該怎麼做？

en_text: I start petting the damn thing. I’m tickling it beneath its chin as if it’s just the greatest little cat in the world.
zh_text: 我開始摸起這隻小王八，把牠當成世上最棒的小貓那樣搔起牠的下巴。

en_text: I look to the ﬂoor where my two dead goldﬁsh are. I’m going to have to bury them again. I tighten the grip on my knife, then use the tip of it to start scratching the top of the cat’s head. It tilts its face sideways to get a better scratching position for itself.
zh_text: 我看著那兩條金魚所葬身的地面——這下又得替牠們收屍了。我把刀握得更緊，用刀尖輕輕摩擦起小貓的頭頂。牠一左一右側著頭，好替自己找起哪個姿勢磨起來比較舒服。

en_text: All I have to do is thrust down, and this little cat that I saved will . . . Saved. Now that’s the key word. I saved this thing, I spent money on it, I brought it into my home, it repaid me by killing my goldﬁsh, and after all of this I’m saving it again. Saving it by not killing it. I put the knife away. Under the observing eyes of the cat, I put the two goldﬁsh into an evidence bag. I will bury them later.
zh_text: 做的就是用力一刺，然後這隻被我救過一命的小貓就……救過一命。這成了關鍵。我救過他，在牠身上砸錢，帶他回到我家，結果牠以搞死金魚來回報，然後即便如此，我也還是手下留情、饒他不死。刀子被我放到一邊去。那隻貓看著我把兩條金魚放進證物袋。我打算晚點再埋金魚。

en_text: Back inside I sit down on the sofa. The cat jumps onto my knee and I keep petting it. After a few minutes it falls asleep. Before I go to bed, I stare at the coffee table and wonder if I will buy any more ﬁsh. Maybe when all of this is over. Without them, I feel like a piece of my life is missing. I feel empty. Though not as empty as I felt yesterday. When I wake the next morning, I’m sweating and the cat’s on the end of my bed. I’ve had another dream. I can remember Melissa. We were together somewhere, I think a beach or an island, and I realized I’d formed a misconception about our violent relationship. Rather than killing her, I was lying with her, both of us enjoying the sand, the sound of the sea, and the sun. It was as though we were having a good time.
zh_text: 我回到屋裡，坐上沙發。小貓跳上了我的膝蓋，接受我不斷輕撫，沒幾分鐘後就沉沉入睡。就寢前，我盯著咖啡桌，心想要不要再去買魚。也許等一切告一段落再說吧。少了魚，我總覺得自己的人生有如遺失了一角，感到非常空虛，但比不上昨天。我隔天醒來，小貓就睡在床尾，而我則是冷汗直流。我又做了個夢，夢裡的梅莉莎和我待在某處——海邊還是小島吧——然後我領悟到自己誤會了這段暴力的兩性關係，於是沒動手殺她，反而躺在她的身旁，和她雙雙享受起沙灘、豔陽與海浪聲，彷彿共度起美好的時光。

en_text: A nightmare. The smell of the sea comes with me from the dream and lingers in the room for a few minutes. I get away from it by climbing into the shower. I wash away the night, the tackiness, and the dregs of the dream. When I come out, the cat’s sitting on the kitchen ﬂoor cleaning itself. I ﬁnd something in the fridge that looks like meat and the cat seems happy enough to believe it.
zh_text: 海的氣味隨我由夢境進入現實，在房裡流連片刻。爲了將這拋諸腦後，我踏進浴室沖澡，沖去了前一晚身體的濕黏以及夢的殘渣。我一出浴室，小貓就坐在廚房地上替自己洗澡。我在冰箱找到像是肉的玩意兒，小貓似乎也樂於相信。

en_text:
Before leaving for work, and after making myself some toast, I check through the briefcase and study my assortment of tools. More importantly I check to make sure the Glock I took from Calhoun is fully loaded. It is. All ﬁfteen rounds ready to react to the tip of my ﬁnger pulling in the mechanical trigger. The ﬁrst cartridge ready to be introduced to the chamber, ready to be struck by the ﬁring pin, the powder inside ready to be ignited. The gas, the pressure, the explosion.
The power.
zh_text:
上班前，我先替自己烤了吐司，才把公事包從頭到尾檢查一遍，研究起各式各樣的工具。更重要的是，我之所以檢查，全是爲了確定我從卡爾霍恩取得的葛拉克手槍已經裝滿子彈。沒錯。裡頭的十五發子彈隨時等我用指尖扣起扳機。彈匣裡的第一枚彈藥只要上膛，經撞針一敲，就能引燃火藥。氣體、壓力，接著爆炸。
火藥。

en_text: It takes less than a quarter of a second for the trigger ﬁnger to obey the command of the shooter. Milliseconds later, the ﬁring pin is hitting. For the whole cycle to progress from nerve impulse to ﬁring of the cartridge, I’m looking at a third of a second. The bullet travels at nearly a thousand feet per second. The target can be dead in less than a second.
zh_text: 要食指恪守射擊手所接收的指令只不過是零點二五秒，而阻鐵釋放彈簧、透過彈力驅動撞針的時間則是更短，需要零點零零五秒。在這近零點三秒內，我聚精會神，好目睹人體從神經受到刺激、帶動制動器扣下扳機、直到發射彈藥的整體流程。子彈速度每秒高達三百公尺。目標可能不到一分鐘就遭擊斃。

en_text: I place the gun back in the briefcase. Let the cat out of my apartment. Go to work.
zh_text: 我把槍放回公事包，讓小貓走出公寓，接著上班去。

en_text: The place is a madhouse.
zh_text: 這地方是瘋人院吧。

en_text: I step into a ﬂurry of detectives and ofﬁcers. The buzz is much bigger than any of the previous days. The men have their sleeves rolled up, their ties loosened. Conversations are spilling from every corner, every cubicle, every ofﬁce. Excitement hangs in the air like a half-deﬂated balloon. I don’t hear any full conversations as I make my way through the clusters of people to my ofﬁce, but I pick up on several snippets.
zh_text: 我走進了警官和警探的一陣慌亂中，人們嘰嘰喳喳要比前些日子還要大聲。男人捲起衣袖，鬆開領帶。每個角落、每個隔間、每個辦公室都能聽見人們從那發出聲音、正在談話。興奮之情有如洩了氣的氣球掛在半空中。雖然我一路走往辦公室、穿過群聚人潮時所聽到的對話都不完整，但還是零碎偷聽到一些。

en_text: “How long have you known him?”
zh_text: 「你認識他多久了？」

en_text: “I heard his son killed himself.”
zh_text: 「聽說他兒子自殺了。

en_text: “Has anybody checked his hotel?”
zh_text: 「有人去過他的旅館喔？」

en_text: “Where else can he be staying?”
zh_text: 「不然他還能住哪？」

en_text: “How many do you think he’s killed?”
zh_text: 「你覺得他殺了幾個人啊？」

en_text: “And you knew him.”
zh_text: 「你不是認識他？」

en_text: “And you had dinner with him.”
zh_text: 「你不是和他吃過晚餐？」

en_text: “And you were working with him.”
zh_text: 「你不就和他同部門？」

en_text: They’re looking for Calhoun. Hunting him. I close the door to my ofﬁce. I’m only alone for ten seconds before Schroder knocks and walks in. “Morning, Joe.”
zh_text: 他們已經開始追捕卡爾霍恩。我關上辦公室的門，過了一會兒，史卓德敲門走了進來。「喬，早啊。」

en_text: “Morning, Detective Schroder.” “Have you heard?”
zh_text: 「史卓德警探，早啊。」「你都聽說了嗎？」

en_text: I shake my head. “Heard what, Detective Schroder?”
zh_text: 我搖了搖頭。「史卓德警探，聽說什麼？」

en_text: “When was the last time you saw Detective Inspector Calhoun?”
zh_text: 「上回你看到卡爾霍恩警探是什麼時候？」

en_text: I think about it. “Yesterday at work,” I tell him. “Didn’t you see him, Detective Schroder? He’s the guy with the gray hair.”
zh_text: 我聳了聳肩。「昨天工作的時候吧。史卓德警探，您沒看到他嗎？就是那個灰髮的傢伙啊。」

en_text: “Did he say anything to you yesterday at all? Anything out of character?” I think about our conversation, his description of killing Daniela Walker. “Not that I can think of.”
zh_text: 他昨天跟你說過什麼嗎？有沒有什麼出人意表之類的話？我想起了我們的對話，想起他描述殺害丹妮耶拉·沃克的細節。「我想不起來耶。」「你確定？」

en_text:
“You sure?”
“Umm . . .” I give my thought process around ten seconds, which is a long time when someone’s staring at you. I’m going for that dramatic effect thing, and then ﬁnally I repeat my original answer. “No, Detective Schroder. When was the last time you saw him?” I ask.
“Let me know if you think of anything,” Schroder says, ignoring my question.
zh_text:
「呃……」我大概想了十秒，當有人正盯著你看，這樣的時間並不算短。我打算營造出那種戲劇性的效果，所以最後還是重複我原本的答案：「史卓德警探，我確定。」
「你要是想起什麼再跟我說。」

en_text: Without waiting for an answer, he turns and hurries off, as if he needs to be everywhere else at the same time. He doesn’t tell me why they’re looking for Calhoun.
zh_text: 我還來不及回答，他就轉身匆匆離去，一副趕場的樣子。他並沒告訴我大家爲何都在找卡爾霍恩。

en_text: I start my working day by cleaning the toilets, which is one of those jobs that makes anybody reﬂect on the decisions they’ve made in life. By the time I ﬁnish, over half the people on the crowded fourth ﬂoor have gone. The rest are paying no attention to me. Are any of them checking the house where I left him? Apparently not. Why would they? Because he left two victims there?
zh_text: 一開工我就掃起廁所。掃完後，擁擠的三樓有一半的人潮已經散去，其他的人對我則是不以爲意。有沒有誰正查起我關起卡爾霍恩的那間房子呢？顯然沒有。他們怎麼不去查一查咧？難不成是因爲那裡出過兩條人命？

en_text: With plenty of ofﬁcers out there searching, with plenty of detectives thinking of places for them to go, it’s possible they’ll stumble across him. And if they do, what will Calhoun tell them? Can he risk telling them about me? No, he can’t, because then I’ll tell on him. I take some small relief that the police are thinking he’s in hiding, probably planning on leaving the country, not reminiscing about his crimes by hovering around old scenes.
zh_text: 找他的警察有一堆，想著要上哪兒找的警探也有一堆，所以說，無意間找到卡爾霍恩的機率算是不小。而且他們要是找到了，卡爾霍恩又會怎麼說？他會冒險告發我嗎？我只能往好方面想了。如今我不必有所預謀、提前計畫，這對我來說很有幫助。警方覺得卡爾霍恩目前沒在過去的犯罪現場徘徊、回溯起自己犯下的罪行，而是正在逃避追捕，甚至打算潛逃海外。

en_text: I lug the vacuum cleaner into the conference room. The room is a mess. Folders, photographs, statements. Cigarette butts squashed into full ashtrays, food wrappers balled on the table, empty take-out containers stuffed into the trash. Files litter the ﬂoor, and among them—lying in the center of the huge table—are two murder weapons. The ﬁrst is mine, which Melissa used. The second is from Calhoun’s hotel room. Both are covered in a thin, white powder.
zh_text: 我把吸塵器扯進會議室，裡頭有資料夾啦照片啦供述啦，亂七八糟的。菸屁股壓扁在滿出來的菸灰缸，桌上都是揉成一團的食品包裝紙，然後用畢的外帶容器全都塞在垃圾桶裡。檔案散落一地，然後正中央擺了張大桌子，上頭有兩把兇器。第一把是我那把，也就是梅莉莎用過的那把，第二把則是從卡爾霍恩旅館房裡拿來的那把，兩把都撒上了一層薄薄的白色粉末。

en_text: I look up at the composite drawing Melissa detailed for them a few mornings earlier. Pinned up next to it is the photograph of Calhoun. It’s a stretch to ﬁnd any real similarity between the two, but that doesn’t matter, because they have ﬁngerprints now, and that’s as good as a confession at this stage in the game. His absence today only helps make him look guiltier. He knew the murder weapon had been found, knew he had to get the hell out of Dodge.
zh_text: 我抬頭望起那張警方依據梅莉莎在前幾天早上所描述的細節而合成的畫像，然後畫像旁邊就釘著卡爾霍恩的照片。要從這兩者之間找出真正的共同點實在有點勉強，但這不重要，因為他們現在有了指紋，遊戲都已經進行到這個階段，這簡直就等同認罪一樣。況且今天他人不在場，這只會加深他的嫌疑而已。他很清楚警方已經找到兇器，也很清楚自己走為上策。

en_text: I sit at the table, pick up each of the plastic bags in turn, and study the knives. I don’t take them out, rather just admire them through the bags. Actually, admire is the wrong word. What I do is remember. Mine has a history. Calhoun’s has a story. Short story, perhaps, but oh so important. After cleaning the room then grabbing my cassette recorder (not just the tape), I go back to my ofﬁce and have lunch. The rest of the day is hectic for everybody but me. For me, it’s only stressful. I watch every person as though they’re watching me, ready to put me under arrest because they’ve found Calhoun tied and taped to a chair in Daniela Walker’s house. At four thirty, making sure nobody is looking, I hide the parking ticket with Calhoun’s fresh ﬁngerprints on it behind his desk. I can’t just put it in one of the drawers—the desk will have been searched already. This way it could have been overlooked, and when they search his cubicle again, they’ll ﬁnd it. If not, I’ll ﬁnd it when I vacuum and hand it to Schroder. I let it slip out of the evidence bag without touching it.
zh_text: 我坐在桌邊，輪流拿起個別的塑膠袋，仔細研究刀子起來。我沒拿出刀子，只是隔袋默默欣賞。其實我不該用「欣賞」，應該用「懷念」才對。我的刀是有故事的，卡爾霍恩的也是，噢，故事也許很短，但卻是至關重大。清理會議室後，我抓起錄音機（不只錄音帶）回辦公室吃起午餐。每個人接下來都是東奔西跑、忙翻了天，只有我例外。對我來說，我感受到的只有壓力，我在看著每個人時，都覺得他們似乎也在看我、準備當場將我逮捕。到了四點三十分，我確定四下無人後就把剛探到指紋的票卡藏到卡爾霍恩的辦公桌後。我不能就這樣把它放進其中一個抽屜，因為警方早晚會來搜起辦公桌，這麼一來很可能漏掉，但我要是放在辦公桌後，警方再來搜起這間辦公室時就會發現；要是他們也沒發現，那我就會在吸地時發現，然後把東西交給史卓德。我碰都沒碰，讓票卡自行滑出證物袋。

en_text: I’m twenty-ﬁve minutes into my stroll to the Walker house, on what is becoming a lovely Friday evening, when my cell phone rings. It plays a small tune that makes me cringe. I slip it from my pocket and ﬂip it open.
zh_text: 禮拜五的向晚時分氣候宜人，就在我散步至沃克家已有二十五分鐘時，手機響起，微弱的鈴聲引發我身子一陣抖索。我從口袋掏出手機，「啪」一聲掀開機蓋。

en_text: “Hello, Melissa.”
zh_text: 「嗨，梅莉莎。」

en_text:
“Hello, Joe. Having a nice evening are you?”
“I was.”
zh_text:
「嗨，喬，今晚還不錯吧？」
「不錯。」

en_text: “Oh, come now, Joe, that’s not very nice. I’ve been thinking about you, you know. Thinking I’d like to take you back to the park once more and show you the other half of a good time.”
zh_text: 「才怪，最好是不錯。你知道我一直在想你，想再帶你回到公園，讓你重溫一下當時的美好時光。」

en_text: “What do you want?”
zh_text: 「妳想怎樣？」

en_text: “My money. Have you got it?”
zh_text: 「錢啊。錢都湊到了嗎？」

en_text: “Not all of it.”
zh_text: 「還沒湊齊。」

en_text: “No? Well, that’s not really good enough, Joe, is it? I said a hundred grand. Anything less is wasting my time.”
zh_text: 「還沒？喬，這不行，我說過要十萬紐幣，少一毛都是在浪費我的時間。

en_text: “I’ve got eighty, and I can get the remaining twenty next week,” I lie, knowing it sounds far more realistic. She goes silent for a minute. That’s okay, she’s paying for the call.
zh_text: 「我已經湊到八萬了，剩下的兩萬要下禮拜才拿得到。」我撒了謊，很清楚這麼說聽起來實際得多。她大約沉默了一分鐘——甭擔心，反正電話是她打來，由她付費。

en_text: “Eighty grand will do for the weekend, Joe, but since you’ve let me down, it’s going to cost you another forty next week.” “I can’t get forty.”
zh_text: 「喬，週末就先拿八萬來吧，不過因爲先前你讓我失望，所以下禮拜再多給我四萬。」「四萬不可能。」

en_text: “That’s what you said about the hundred, and look how well you’ve done.”
zh_text: 「先前十萬你也說不可能，看看你現在做得多好。」

en_text: “Fine.”
zh_text: 「好吧。」

en_text: “Where do you want to meet?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你想在哪碰面？」

en_text: “You’re leaving it up to me?”
zh_text: 「妳要讓我決定？」

en_text: “Of course not. I just wanted to give you some hope. That’s all.”
zh_text: 「你，我只是想給你一點希望而已。」

en_text: “I’m not leaving it up to you. If you want the money, then it’s on my terms.”
zh_text: 「這次由我決定。要是妳想拿到錢，這次就聽我的。」

en_text: “If you don’t want to go to jail, Joe, then the terms are mine.”
zh_text: 「喬，要是你不想坐牢，這次應該聽我的才對。」

en_text: “Fuck you.”
zh_text: 「可悪！」

en_text: “Fuck you too, Joe.”
zh_text: 「你才可惡！」

en_text: Look at that. Just like a married couple.
zh_text: 我們就像新婚夫妻鬥起嘴來了。

en_text: “Listen, you’ve got my gun,” I tell her. “You shouldn’t be too concerned with where we meet.”
zh_text: 「聽著，妳手上有我的槍，根本不必太過關切我們要在哪裡碰面。

en_text: “I don’t trust you, Joe.”
zh_text: 「喬，我不相信你。」

en_text: “It’s a house where I killed somebody.”
zh_text: 「就約在我殺過人的那間房子吧。」

en_text: “They still there?” Her voice picks up an octave. I shake my head, even though I’m on the phone.
zh_text: 「屍體都還在那？！」她提高嗓音，聽起來高了八度。

en_text: “Is this the place you took the whore to the other night?” “That’s the one,” I say, knowing she followed me there and killed the hooker I had in the trunk of the car while I was inside. She seems to like this idea. “I’ll meet you there at six o’clock, Joe. Don’t make me wait.”
zh_text: 「對。」我說，很清楚她曾跟蹤我到那裡，然後趁我人在屋裡殺了當時被我關在後車廂的妓她似乎覺得這主意不錯。「我六點在那等你，別遲到喔。」

en_text: She hangs up. Damn it, that doesn’t give me long. I catch the bus. Don’t want to steal a car. Of all the times to be caught, today would be it. I can sense it. The day is warming up, as if summer is making one last stand and it’s doing it this evening. Christchurch weather. Schizophrenic heat and all that.
zh_text: 她掛斷電話。可惡，這樣我沒剩多少時間了。雖然我每次偷車都很有可能被抓，但我總覺得今天難逃一劫，於是選擇搭起公車，連偷車都不想偷。天候暖和舒適，不像往常那樣霧濛濛的——至少還沒起霧。基督城的天氣向來會熱到讓人精神錯亂。

en_text: I reach the house and enter my ﬁnal evening as the Christchurch Carver.
zh_text: 我抵達那間房子，即將邁入我化身基督城屠夫的最後一夜。

en_text:
I decide to pass the house and keep walking. It’s ﬁve forty-ﬁve. I walk to the end of the block, then come back. I don’t spot any odd-looking vehicles. No signs of a stakeout. No Melissa. It’s suburbia at the height of normalcy. Walking the front path to the doorstep feels like coming home. I’ve been here so many times over the last few weeks it’s becoming a regular part of my life. The husband of the dead woman will probably start charging me rent. At least this will be my ﬁnal time here. I take the sights in without any feelings of nostalgia. No tears to be shed.
The house is still warm. Seems it will stay that way until winter kills off every green thing in sight. If the police have been here today, now will be the time they burst in to apprehend me. Not that they will, of course. They’re not here. I’m sure of it. However . . .
zh_text:
我決定路過房子，繼續行走。現在是五點四十五分。我走到街區的盡頭才又走起回頭路，途中既沒發現什麼行蹤可疑的車輛、警方跟蹤的跡象，也沒看見梅莉莎的蹤影。這郊區可說是毫無異狀。
走在通往屋前台隍的小徑感覺就像回家一樣。過去幾個禮拜以來，我來過這不下數次，早已把它當成了我生活中規律的一部分。丹妮耶拉的丈夫很可能打算收我房租吧。管它的，反正這是最後一次了。我將一切盡收眼底，不帶任何懷念之情，甚至並未流下一滴淚水。

en_text: I close my eyes. Wait. Count off a slow minute in which I listen to every sound in the house and in the street. A lawn mower, some woman shouting to her son to hurry up, a car moving by. Inside all I can hear is my own breathing. If the cops are here, I’ll tell them that I thought it was part of my job to clean this place. That I thought it was an extension of police headquarters since dozens of detectives have been here a few times now. I’ll mispronounce extension and pause for a few seconds looking for a replacement.
zh_text: 屋裡依舊溫暖。這裡似乎都會這麼溫暖，直到夏去秋至。要是今天警方來了，那麼現在就是他們闖進屋裡、直接逮捕我的最佳時機。但我很確定他們不在，遑論把我帶回警局了，不過……我閉上雙眼，靜靜等待。隨著時間慢慢流逝，我一邊倒數，一邊聆聽屋裡、街上所發出的聲響：鋤草機的聲音、某個女人喊兒子「快點、快點」的聲音、車輛經過的聲音；至於屋裡呢，我能聽到的就只有自己的呼吸聲。要是條子來了，我會告訴他們，我覺得打掃這裡算是我工作的一部分，也覺得既然截至目前已有幾十位警探來過這裡好幾次，這裡儼然就像警局的分局。

en_text: I open my eyes. Nothing. I’m still alone.
zh_text: 我睜開雙眼。這裡空無一物，我仍是獨自一人。

en_text: When I reach the bedroom I move straight through to the bathroom and smile at the man bound to the chair inside. At some point during the night, or perhaps today, he has pissed himself. The room stinks and he’s a mess, the whole scene is somewhat sad and pathetic.
zh_text: 我爬上樓梯，不像往常那樣習慣去冰箱找東西、稍作停留。雖然我現在很渴，但我得辦起正事。一走到臥房，我就直接穿過房間、走到浴室，對著裡面被鄉在椅上的男人微微一笑。就在今晚，又或者就在今天的某個時候，他尿濕了褲子。

en_text: I meet his eyes and see the hatred I saw last night. They’re red and puffy as though he has been rubbing them, but I know he hasn’t. He looks like he hasn’t slept since I saw him yesterday. His shirt is hanging out, and the collar is stained with blood. His arms are red from trying to break the tape and rope. Even his short hair looks rufﬂed. Flecks of blood have dried on the surface of the duct tape. The right side of his jaw has turned a dark gray. A large bump has risen on the front of his forehead. He must know they’re there, since he can get a good view of himself in the mirror.
zh_text: 我和他四目交接，他就和昨晚一樣，雙眼流露出恨意。他雙眼紅腫，彷彿一直揉個不停，但我知道他並沒有。看來自從我昨晚來這看過他後，他就再也沒闔過眼了。他的襯衫外露，衣領沾上血跡，雙臂因爲試圖扯斷繩子、膠帶而顯得紅通通的，就連一頭短髮看起來也是亂七八糟。膠帶表面一點點的血跡已經乾掉。他的下巴右側已經轉爲深灰色，前額也腫了個大大的包。因爲他可以清楚地從鏡中看到自己，所以他鐵定知道自己現在就是這副德行。

en_text: “No, no, don’t get up,” I say, putting out my hand. He doesn’t laugh, or for that matter, even attempt to make conversation.
zh_text: 「不、不，別起身。」我一邊說，一邊伸手制止他。他笑也沒笑，甚至沒試著和我對話。

en_text:
“Okay, Detective Inspector, here’s the deal. Twenty grand buys your ears and your mind, okay? Just don’t forget I have the gun, and I also have a tape of last night’s conversation.” I show him the tape recorder that’s been living inside a potted plant for months. “You try anything, or anything happens to me, that tape goes to your colleagues. Nod if you understand.”
He understands.
zh_text:
好，偵緝督察，現在交易來了。我想用兩萬買下你的聽力和專注力，行不行？別忘了我手上有槍，而且昨晚的對話我還錄了音。」我拿給他看那台已在盆栽裡藏了好幾個月的錄音機。「要是你試著玩什麼花樣，還是我發生不測，那麼這卷錄音帶就會直接送到你同事的手裡。僅了給我點點頭。」
他僅了。

en_text: “Here’s the thing. In another,” I glance at my watch, “ﬁve minutes, we’re going to have a visitor. She’s going to be coming up here, and she’s going to be blackmailing me. However, like you, she’s also a murderer. I imagine you’ll recognize her. It’s your job to remain quiet here in the bathroom. Once she’s confessed, I’ll open up the door, she’ll see you, and she’ll be just as incriminated as you and I are. What we’ll have then is a three-way stalemate. Agreed?”
zh_text: 「重點來了。」我瞄了手錶一眼，「五分鐘後我們會有訪客，她會來這向我勒索、敲我一筆。但她和你一樣也是殺人魔，我想你應該認得她。到時你只要給我安靜待在浴室就好。等她告解完畢，我才會打開浴室的門，讓她看到你，然後她就會和你我一樣通通有罪，同時我們三方也會陷入僵局。你同不同意？」

en_text: He grunts.
zh_text: 他哼了一聲。

en_text: “I’ll take that as a yes.”
zh_text: 我把這當成同意。

en_text:
Another grunt. He shakes his head, perhaps seeing a problem with the plan, but it doesn’t matter. I close the door, then wait on the edge of the bed with my briefcase and without the eighty thousand dollars. Ten minutes later I hear the front door downstairs open. I stay where I am. She’ll ﬁnd me without too much difﬁculty.
This is it. This is where my phases and plans have led me.
zh_text:
他又哼了一聲，搖了搖頭，但這並不重要。我關上門，拿著並沒裝進八萬紐幣的公事包在床邊等著。
十分鐘後，我聽到了樓下前門的開門聲，於是待在原地——她很容易就會找到我的。這就對了。這就是我透過諸多計畫及步驟所得到的結果。

en_text: I hear Melissa walk into the kitchen. The fridge door opens. Then it closes. Are we really that alike? I hope not.
zh_text: 我聽見梅莉莎走進廚房，打開冰箱門，緊接著「啵」的一聲，她開了罐啤酒。我倆眞的那麼像嗎？希望不是。

en_text: A minute later she comes up the stairs.
zh_text: 一分鐘後，她走上樓來。

en_text: “Damn hot up here, Joe.”
zh_text: 「這裡怎麼這麼熱呀！」

en_text: I shrug. “No air-conditioning.”
zh_text: 我聳了聳肩。「沒有空調。」

en_text: “I’m surprised there’s still any power to this place. That the money?” she asks, nodding toward the briefcase.
zh_text: 「我真的很驚訝這種鬼地方還會有電。錢呢？」她問，朝著公事包抬了抬下巴「嗯哼。」

en_text: “Uh huh.” I keep staring at her. She’s more beautiful than the night we met. More beautiful than the day she blackmailed me. Her black miniskirt is showing long, tanned legs. She’s wearing a dark purple jacket, which matches her purple shoes. Her blouse is silky black. She is going for some type of power dressing look, and succeeding. She steals a look at her expensive-looking watch. Once again I wonder what she actually does, and how she gets her money. Maybe she really is an architect.
zh_text: 我直盯著她看，她看起來要比我們相遇時的那晚還美，也比她勒索、敲詐我的那天更美。黑色的迷你裙讓她修長又曬成古銅色的雙腿一覽無遺，她搭配紫色的鞋穿起深紫色的外套，而絲綢般的上衣則是呈現黑色。她打算透過裝扮讓自己看似專業、深具權威，然後她辦到了，直到她瞄了一眼那只看似昂貴的錶，我才又納悶起她到底從事哪一行，還有怎麼賺到這麼多錢。也許她真的是位建築師吧。

en_text: “Got a date?” I ask.
zh_text: 「妳有約會？」

en_text: She laughs. “You can always make me smile, Joe.”
zh_text: 她笑了笑。「你總是這麼幽默。」

en_text: “I try.”
zh_text: 「我只是問問。

en_text: “Actually I was just seeing how long it was going to take you to cut the crap and give me my money.”
zh_text: 「其實我是在等你何時才能少說廢話，直接把錢給我。

en_text: I lean back on the bed. “I still have some concerns.”
zh_text: 我靠回床上。「我還有幾個考量。」

en_text: “Oh, is that so. Well, poor little Joe, tell Melissa all about it.”
zh_text: 「噢，這樣啊，可憐的小喬，快快告訴梅莉莎吧。

en_text: “Once I give you the money, what’s stopping you from going to the police anyway?”
zh_text: 「要是我把錢給了妳，妳要怎樣才不會報警？」

en_text: “I’m a lovely person, Joe. I’d never lie.”
zh_text: 「我從不騙人的。」

en_text: Yeah. Damn lovely. “You lied to me.”
zh_text: 是啊，人好到不行。「妳騙過我。」

en_text: “You’re lie-worthy.”
zh_text: 「那是因為你好騙啊。」

en_text: “You haven’t answered my question.”
zh_text: 「妳還沒回答我的問題。」

en_text: “Come now, Joe. What you’re buying here is trust. What kind of world is this if we can’t all trust one another? Once I have the money, everything I have on you, Joe, goes in a safe place so if something should happen to me,” she waves her hand around in the air, “oh I don’t know—maybe something along the lines of having my throat cut—then what I have on you goes to the cops. And only then.”
zh_text: 「幫幫忙，你現在買的是『信任』好嗎？要是我們都不能信任彼此，那這世界會變成什麼模樣？一旦我拿了錢，有關於你的把柄，我都會全部保密，但我要是有個三長兩短……」她揮了揮手，「我不知道，也許是遭人割喉之類的，那麼警方就會握有這些把柄。但前提是我如有不測。

en_text: “And how do I know you won’t keep coming back for more?”
zh_text: 「我怎麼知道你不會持續勒索？」

en_text: She shrugs. “I guess you don’t.” She lets her words hang in the air. She’s thinking she’ll be back for more money at some point.
zh_text: 她聳了聳肩，「我猜你也不會知道。」她啜飲了一口啤酒，然後就此打住、沒再說話。她心想到了某個時間點自己還是會回來跟我要錢。

en_text: “So how does it feel to be up here,” I ask, “in the presence of death?”
zh_text: 「跟死人在這的感覺怎樣？」

en_text: “There’s nothing dead up here.”
zh_text: 「這裡哪有死人？」

en_text: “There was.”
“Where did you kill them?”
zh_text: 「你是在哪動手的？」

en_text: I stand up and walk to the opposite corner, so now I’m standing along the same wall as the bathroom door, but at the other end. “I killed each of them on the bed,” I say, taking the credit for Daniela Walker’s death.
zh_text: 我站起身子，走到對角，正站在和浴室門同一邊的牆上，只不過是在另一頭。「床上。兩人都是在床上殺的。」我說，把丹妮耶拉·沃克的死當成是自己下的手。

en_text: “This bed?”
zh_text: 「這張床嗎？」

en_text: It’s unmade, the blankets and sheets wrinkled from use. You can still see dried drops of blood. “That’s the one.”
zh_text: 床連鋪都沒鋪，毯子、床單因為用過而皺成一團，上面還可以看到乾掉的血跡。「就這張床。」

en_text: She makes her way toward it. I can clearly see the Glock in her hand. My Glock. Even as she studies the bed she keeps the weapon pointed at me. Steadily.
zh_text: 她一路朝著床走去。我可以清楚看見她手裡拿著葛拉克手槍，就我那一把。甚至在她研究床的當下，她也還是拿槍穩穩地指著我。

en_text: “How did it feel?” she asks.
zh_text: 「感覺怎樣？」她問。

en_text: “You ought to know.”
zh_text: 「妳應該知道啊。」

en_text: She turns to me and smiles. “That’s true, Joe. You know, sometimes I feel as though we have something special between us.” “Blackmail?”
zh_text: 她轉身向我，面帶微笑。「真的，你知道嗎？有時我覺得我倆之間有種特殊的連結。」「妳是指我們都會勒索嗎？」

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「不是。」

en_text: “We’re both killers?”
zh_text: 「或者我們都是殺人魔？」

en_text:
She shakes her head. “No, not that either.”
“What then?”
zh_text:
她搖著頭。「也不是。」
「不然是？」

en_text: “I think it’s our love of life.”
zh_text: 「是我們對人生的愛。」

en_text: I haven’t insisted on anything. “So how did it feel for you, Melissa?”
zh_text: 我可沒咬定就是這樣。「所以，妳感覺怎樣？」

en_text: “How did what feel?”
zh_text: 「什麼感覺怎樣？」

en_text: “Killing.”
zh_text: 「殺人。」

en_text: “I’ve done it before.”
zh_text: 「我以前就殺過人。」

en_text: “You’re kidding me.”
zh_text: 「少來。」

en_text: “Only a couple of times. Nothing as fun as the other night, though.”
zh_text: 幾次而已，不過都沒那晚來得好玩。

en_text: I have to agree. “They are kind of fun, aren’t they?”
zh_text: 我不得不承認。「殺人挺好玩的吧？」

en_text: “See? We’re sharing. We aren’t so unalike, Joe.” She begins rubbing her free hand over the bed, as if she’s trying to feel the death that took place here, trying to soak it up into the pores of her skin.
zh_text: 「你看，我倆挺像的吧，喬，我就說我們有些共通點。」她用空下來的那隻手揉搓起床彿試圖體驗在那發生過的命案、試圖讓死亡的感覺滲進肌膚的毛孔。

en_text: “I think we’re more similar than you really know.”
zh_text: 「我覺得，我倆比妳實際了解的還要像。」「因為我發現妳也很好騙。」

en_text: Hand still on the bed, she turns to face me. The gun is still pointed in my direction. “And how’s that?” “Because I also ﬁnd you lie-worthy.”
zh_text: 她轉過身子面向我，手仍放在床上，槍也還是對準我這個方向。「怎麼個像法？」

en_text: She straightens up, glances at the briefcase.
zh_text: 她站起身子，瞄了一眼公事包。

en_text: I nod toward it. “Go on, open it.”
zh_text: 我朝公事包抬了抬下巴。「去吧，妳自己打開。」

en_text: Keeping the gun on me, she reaches over and snaps the left clip, then the right. Looking back to me, she opens the lid, then turns to look inside.
zh_text: 槍還是對著我。她走到公事包，「啪」一聲彈開左邊的扣夾，接著右邊，然後回頭看了我一眼，再掀開上蓋，轉而往裡一瞧。

en_text: “What the hell are you up to, Joe? Where’s my money?”
zh_text: 「喬，你到底在搞什麼鬼？錢呢？」

en_text: “You’re not getting any money, Melissa.” She looks genuinely surprised. It seems she never thought I wouldn’t actually pay her. “If that’s the way you want to play it, then I’m going directly to the police.”
zh_text: 梅莉莎，妳一毛錢都拿不到。她似乎沒料到我居然不付錢給她，看起來真的相當驚訝。「你要是搞這一套，那我打算直接報警。」

en_text: “Oh? And how are you going to explain your involvement?”
zh_text: 「那妳打算怎麼解釋自己也是共犯？」

en_text: “I won’t need to.”
zh_text: 「我沒必要解釋。」

en_text: “Think again, bitch.” I nod toward the bathroom.
zh_text: 「妳最好想清楚點。」我朝浴室抬了抬下巴。

en_text:
“You got a video camera set up, Joe? Come on, don’t be so childish. I’ll just take the tape with me now. Then I’m going to shoot you in the balls.
Oh, what I mean is ball.”
zh_text: 「喬，難不成你裝了攝影機？拜託，別這麼幼稚好不好？現在我會直接拿走帶子，然後一槍打爛你的睪丸，噢，我指的是『那顆』睪丸。」

en_text:
“What I have is even better than a video camera. Why don’t you check it out?”
She moves toward the bathroom door, keeping the gun pointing ahead of her. When she reaches it, she opens it slowly. She peers inside, then laughs. Maybe she thinks I’ve bought her the ultimate gift.
zh_text:
對於她這番冷嘲熱諷，我並不爲所動。「妳可以親自確認。」
她朝浴室門移動，仍然把槍拿在前面對準我。一到浴室門口，她緩緩把門打開，探頭一看，然後噗嗤一笑。她也許覺得我給她買了什麼超級禮物吧。

en_text: “A cop? You’re going to kill a cop?” she asks.
zh_text: 「警察？你打算殺掉警察？」她問。

en_text: “I’m not going to kill him. He’s too valuable for that.”
zh_text: 「我可沒打算殺掉他，是他自己太嫩、耐不住我這麼操。」

en_text: Behind her, I can see Calhoun’s eyes wide open in surprise at seeing Melissa. He recognizes her from the station. His eyes dart from left to right, deciding which of us is more dangerous. This is the woman who gave him a description of the killer. This is the woman who has me at gunpoint, yet I’m the man who knocked him out and tied him up. What in the hell, he’s wondering, is going on? And when will he be getting his money? I can also see the thoughts going through Melissa’s mind. She likes collecting police things, and she’s wondering if she can collect this guy. She’s measuring him up to see if she has room for him in her house. Perhaps the corner of the living room, or next to the fridge.
zh_text: 我可以從她身後看到卡爾霍恩因為看到梅莉莎拿槍而瞠目結舌，一會兒左看看、一會兒右看看，評估著我倆究竟誰比較危險。這就是那個向他描述兇手特徵的女人，也是拿槍指著我的女人，而我剛好又是那個把他打昏外加五花大綁的男人。他必然心想，到底是怎樣？他要何時才會拿到錢？我也能看出梅莉莎在想些什麼。她很喜歡收集警方的東西，這下她不但想著自己能否把這傢伙當成收藏品一併帶走，還把他全身上下打量一番，看看自己家裡是否還有容納他的空間——可能是客廳的一角，又或者是冰箱的隔壁。

en_text: “I don’t understand what you’re playing at, Joe,” she says.
zh_text: 「我搞不懂你在玩什麼把戲。」

en_text: “He’s my witness to what you really are.”
zh_text: 「他可以替我見證妳其實是個怎樣的人。」

en_text: “Oh? And what do you have on him?”
zh_text: 「喔？你是不是握有他什麼把柄？」

en_text: “Enough.”
zh_text: 「夠了。」

en_text: She looks around the room. It’s obvious that she hates losing. Slowly she begins shaking her head. I can hear her teeth grinding. She looks angry. “You’re forgetting one thing, Joe.”
zh_text: 她環顧房內，顯然輸不起，然後緩緩搖著頭，看起來氣急敗壞。我還聽得見她的磨牙聲咧。「喬，有件事你忘了。」

en_text: “And what’s that?”
zh_text: 「什麼事？」

en_text: “I don’t need him.”
zh_text: 「我根本不需要這傢伙。」

en_text: Before I can react, she grabs a knife from my briefcase and runs into the bathroom.
