She stands behind Calhoun and his eyes widen in fear because he knows as well as I do what’s about to happen. The chair jerks beneath him as he tries to pull away, but it’s no good. She holds the knife to his throat and watches my eyes. I look from the eyes of the detective, who has just become as still as stone, to the eyes of the woman behind him. Hers reﬂect amusement, a sense of enjoyment. Not for what she’s about to do to the cop, but what she’s about to do to my witness. I’ve hardly taken a step, but now I don’t dare move any closer.
zh_text: 我還來不及反應，她就從公事包裡抓起刀子衝進浴室，直接站到卡爾霍恩身後。嚴重驚嚇的他把雙眼睜得偌大，因為他和我一樣清楚接下來將會如何，所以試圖逃脫、搖晃起下方的椅子，卻還是無濟於事。她拿刀抵住他的喉嚨，和我四目相望。我先和警探對望——他已經呆若木雞、絲毫不敢動彈——接著才和他身後的女人對望。她的眼神反映出一絲絲的快感，看得出她以此爲樂，只不過樂的不是「對警察下手」，而是「對我的證人下手」。原本我就不敢輕舉妄動，現在更是不敢越雷池一步。

en_text: “Think about this, Melissa,” I say, my words almost ﬂustered. I put my hands ahead of me, palms outward. “Think about what you’re doing.” Calhoun is pleading with his eyes, and as Melissa takes the knife away from his throat, his pleading moves to relief—then to horror as he sees the knife plunge back into sight on the way toward his chest. His eyes sparkle with fear, then all the sparkle evaporates in an instant as the knife punches into his body.
zh_text: 「梅莉莎，妳想想。」我說，幾乎字字都透露出我驚慌失措。我手放身前，掌心朝外。「想想妳在幹嘛。」卡爾霍恩流露出乞求的眼神。就在梅莉莎把刀子從他喉嚨拿開時，那眼神暫時轉爲寬慰，接著直到他看見刀子再次映入眼簾、逕往胸口刺來的那一刹那，這才又轉爲驚恐。他眼中閃耀著恐懼的火花，隨著刀子就這麼刺進，所有火花也在轉瞬間消失殆盡。

en_text: A sound, which is both gurgle and grunt, comes from him at the same time, and he struggles harder against the rope, as if the metal blade that has punctured his chest isn’t a knife, but a high-voltage battery from which he’s drawing power. Even so, it’s not enough to give him the strength to break the rope and tape that bind him. The chair dances back and forth as his body weight waltzes it across the ﬂoor. Blood squirts up from his chest. It pools around the blade of the knife and quickly blossoms over his shirt. Melissa leaves the knife in him, then steps away to watch. Blood has splashed onto the mirror, and even the ceiling. He begins trying to cough more of it up, but because of the tape across his mouth it becomes impossible. He begins choking, his face turns red, and I’m not sure if he’s choking or bleeding to death. The front of the duct-tape gag turns red. His face turns from red to purple, the same purple the sky was when I viewed it from the park with my testicle turned to pulp. The chair waltzes faster over the linoleum ﬂoor, the legs tap-dancing to some dying rhythm. His eyes are as wide as they can be, and in them I can see all sorts of fear and knowledge. Fear of dying. Knowledge that his last few seconds in this world are happening right now.
zh_text: 他更死命地想要掙脫繩索，同時發出了打嗝與呻吟聲，好像刺進胸口的不是金屬的刀鋒，而是供他汲取能量的高壓電池。即便如此，這仍不足以給他充分的力量扯斷綁起他的繩索和膠帶。他的體重帶動整張椅子一前一後，從左到右在地面跳起華爾滋。他的胸口先是血流如注，然後鲜血很快就從刀鋒四周暈開，最後染紅了整件襯衫。梅莉莎就這樣把刀留在他的體內，站到一邊冷眼旁觀。鮮血濺到了鏡子上，就連天花板也慘遭池魚之殃。他試圖咳出更多血來，但嘴巴貼住膠帶，非但咳不出來，反而被血嗆個正著，整張臉漲得通紅，導致我無法確定他到底是嗆到窒息還是流血致死。綁嘴布貼上膠帶的部位開始轉紅，他的臉更是由紅轉紫，和我人在公園、睪丸變得稀巴爛時所看到的天空呈現出一樣的顏色。椅子在地板上舞動加速，椅腳跳起了類似瀕死節奏的踢踏舞。他的雙眼大到不行，而我透過他的眼神看到了各式各樣的恐懼與體悟——也就是對於死亡的恐懼，還有自己來日無多的體悟。

en_text: He looks at me and I think he wants me to help, but I can’t be sure. I stand motionless, unable to do a thing to save him. His throat begins to swell and his mouth is full of blood. It’s a race to see which will kill him— the stab wound or the choking—and when he stops moving, his head slumped forward and his ragged breathing eerily silent, I can only guess. I stand with my mouth open and my tongue nearly hanging out, sweat dripping down my forehead. “You stupid bitch,” I manage to whisper. “How could you do such a thing?”
zh_text: 他盯著我瞧，我想他是要我幫忙，但我無法確定，就站在原地不動，對於救他這事完全使不上力。他的喉嚨開始腫脹，口中滿是鮮血。這是場觀察他是如何死於非命的比賽——他究竟是遭刺失血致死呢，還是無法呼吸窒息而亡。一旦他頭一垂、兩腿一蹬、停止動彈，甚至連紊亂的呼吸聲也變得異常安靜，結果到底如何，我也只能自行猜測了。我愣在原地，瞠目結舌，額頭滴下了涔涔的汗水。「臭婊子，」我小聲說，「妳怎麼會做出這種事？」

en_text: She reaches over to him and pulls away the duct tape. Blood gushes from between Calhoun’s lips and spills over his shirt. “I’m surprised that you thought I wouldn’t. I told you no tricks, Joe.”
zh_text: 她向他走去，一把撕去膠帶，鮮血就這麼從卡爾霍恩的唇間噴湧而出，濺得他整件襯衫都是。「我很驚訝你覺得我不會這麼做，喬，我都已經說過別玩什麼把戲了。」

en_text: “No, you didn’t.”
zh_text: 才怪，妳沒說。

en_text: “Well, you should have assumed it. I still want my money.”
zh_text: 「那你也應該早就想到才對，我還是要拿到錢才罷休。

en_text: “I don’t have it.”
zh_text: 「我沒錢。」

en_text:
I look back at the body. “Maybe he’s still alive,” I whisper. I’m about to move forward to check when she interrupts me.
“Maybe,” she agrees, and she grabs hold of the knife and pulls it away. “Don’t . . .” I say, letting my voice trail off.
zh_text:
我回頭看著屍體，「或許他還沒死。」我低語，打算向前確認，然而遭她打斷。「或許吧。」她同意，一口氣拔出刀子。
「別……」才說了一個字我就乖乖住嘴。

en_text: She leans in close and listens for a pulse. Whether she hears one or not, I can’t know. What she does do is drag the knife across his throat. Then she steps back. Dips a ﬁnger into the wound and puts that same ﬁnger into her mouth. She sucks on the blood.
zh_text: 她緊緊挨著他的身子，聽起心跳聲，至於有沒有聽到，我則是不得而知。緊接著她拿刀朝他喉嚨慢慢劃了一刀，後退一步，用手指伸進傷口，再把同一根手指放進嘴裡——她吸起鮮血來了。

en_text: “If he wasn’t dead, he sure as hell is now. And unless you want the police busting your ass on Monday, I suggest you give me my money.” “Give me four hours.”
zh_text: 「現在鐵定掛了。你若不希望警方禮拜一就把你逮個正著，那我建議你現在就交出錢來。」「給我四小時。」

en_text: Melissa looks down at her jacket and sees a few splotches of blood. She takes it off. Her nipples are standing out as if she’s got small coins tucked in the front of her bra. She drags the knife over the dead man’s throat once more, making a squelching sound that reminds me of walking in wet shoes. Then she steps around behind him to cut the ropes and tape. After she drops the knife to the ﬂoor, she raises one of Calhoun’s arms and places his hand on her right breast. Softly she moans.
zh_text: 梅莉莎低頭看起自己的外套，發現幾處血跡，於是脫下外套，露出了硬挺的乳頭，有如在胸罩尖端塞進了小枚的硬幣。她又拿刀在死人的喉嚨劃上一刀，發出「啾啵啾」的吸吮聲，讓我想起穿著濕掉的鞋子走路的聲音。然後她繞到他身後，割斷繩子、膠帶，待把刀子扔到地上，這才舉起卡爾霍恩的其中一隻手臂，放上自己右胸，然後輕輕哀嘆。

en_text: When she looks over at me, she is smiling. “You want to try it?”
zh_text: 她看向我時，笑臉盈盈。「想不想試試？」

en_text: “You promise not to slap me?”
zh_text: 「妳敢保證不會摑我耳光？」

en_text: “No, you idiot. Do you want to see how he feels?”
zh_text: 笨蛋，我才不會！想不想感覺他？

en_text: “He feels dead.”
zh_text: 「感覺不就是死人嗎？」

en_text: “If you can get the money that quickly, Joe, we’ve still got a deal.”
zh_text: 要是你能盡快把錢湊齊，那麼交易還算數，否則感覺像死人的很快就會換成你了。」「給我時間地點吧。」

en_text: “Where and when?” She drops the arm and takes a look at her watch, mentally studying her schedule. “Ten o’clock. Our park. Don’t be late.”
zh_text: 她放下手臂，瞄了一眼手錶，默默盤算著自己的行程。「十點吧，就約在我們的公園，別遲到。」

en_text: Our park. Sure, I won’t be late. “I’ll be there.” “No tricks, Joe.”
zh_text: 我們的公園，好，我不會遲到。「我會準時到。「喬，別再耍什麼把戲。」

en_text: With that, she turns to leave and I’m left alone with a useless corpse.
zh_text: 說定後，她轉身離開，我則獨自離去，還附帶一具毫無用處的屍體。

en_text: Be prepared. That’s the Boy Scout motto. It applies to anything in life. It’s like doing your homework. I simply can’t stress enough how important that is.
zh_text: 童子軍的銘言之一就是「準備」（Be prepared），人生中各方面都適用。我實在無法強調這點有多重要。

en_text: I stand at the window for a few more minutes watching in case Melissa comes back. It’s a clear evening, a few stars are out already, a faded moon growing in strength. Melissa disappears between streetlights and reappears at the following one until she reappears no more. When I’m satisﬁed she’s gone, I point the remote control at the wardrobe. With the push of one button I turn off the video camera that’s running in there. The crippled chick’s video camera.
zh_text: 我又在窗邊站了幾分鐘，直到梅莉莎並未去而復返，我放了心，這才拿起遙控器對準衣櫥按下按鈕，關掉裡頭一直開著的攝錄機——那台殘障女的攝錄機。

en_text: I rewind the tape, then sit on the edge of the bed to watch tonight’s footage through the small viewﬁnder. I hadn’t started the unit recording until I moved over into the corner of the bedroom. The lens was zoomed out to capture most of the room, which included the bed. I continue watching the tape. I can see Melissa stroking the covers, then, soon after, opening the bathroom door and murdering the policeman. Because of the angle of the lens I’ve managed to stay out of the footage. If I was in it, I would have edited it out. Seems I don’t need to.
zh_text: 我倒轉帶子，坐在床邊透過小小的觀景窗看著今晚的片段。一切都如我所願。直到躲進臥房的一角，我這才啟動單位攝影，逐步拉遠鏡頭，好讓房裡絕大部分都能入鏡，包括床在內。我繼續看著帶子，還看得見梅莉莎輕撫床單，接著很快就打開浴室門殺了那名警察。鑑於取景的角度，我一直努力不讓自己出現在畫面中，要是一不小心入鏡，我也會把那幾幕「卡」掉——但目前似乎沒這必要。

en_text: I take the dead detective’s gun out of the waistband of my pants and set it on the bed for easy access. The gun’s ready to ﬁre, has been the entire night. It was my protection against Melissa in case anything went wrong. As it turned out, everything went perfectly.
zh_text: 我從褲子腰帶抽出了已故警探的槍，然後放在床上，這樣比較好拿。那把槍整夜都保持在待發狀態，以防事情一旦出錯，我才能以此自保、對抗梅莉莎。結果事事都盡善盡美，進行得相當順利。

en_text: Melissa didn’t cut all the bindings away from the policeman, so I grab a knife and ﬁnish the job. He smells of piss and death as I drag his heavy corpse into the bedroom, careful not to get any blood on me. When I dump him on the bed, he bounces once before becoming still.
zh_text: 梅莉莎並沒全部切斷綁起警察的膠帶和繩子，於是我抓起刀子完成了這件差事兒。當我把他沉重的屍體拖進臥室、小心不沾上血跡時，他整個人盡是尿臭和屍臭，而我把他扔到床上時，屍體還彈了起來，之後才靜止不動。

en_text: I look around the room for something I can use to wrap the body. The blood will just soak through the sheets, so I go back into the bathroom and rip down the shower curtain, scattering the plastic rings to all four corners. I roll it around him. The end result is an odd-looking cocoon, which looks ready to hatch a being from some 1950s B-grade sci-ﬁ movie. His blood smears across the inside of it, painted on the curtain of this womb. I use duct tape and his shoelaces to secure the curtain. Back in the bathroom I wash down the knife Melissa used to kill him, dry it, and put it back into my briefcase.
zh_text: 我環顧四周，想找找看有什麼可以用來包裹屍體。血跡會直接滲透床單，所以我走回浴室扯下浴簾，連帶讓塑膠環散滿了各個角落，並用浴簾綑起屍體，結果綑成了一個奇形怪狀的繭，彷彿正要孵出五〇年代三級科幻電影中才會出現的玩意兒。浴簾有如畫上圖案的子宮，從頭到尾都抹上了他的血跡，我用膠帶和他的鞋帶加以固定。回到浴室後，我把梅莉莎用來殺他的刀沖洗乾淨，擦乾，再放回公事包。

en_text: I drag the cocoon downstairs by the feet, its head thudding on every step, then across the ﬂoor and into the adjoining garage. He leaks from the shower curtain where I haven’t done the best of wrapping jobs (men can’t wrap—simple fact) and stains the carpet. I dump him on the garage ﬂoor, turn on a light, and look around. The tools of my trade are here. I pick up a plastic can of gas from next to the lawn mower and shake it. Seems mostly full. Perhaps around three gallons. I carry it back into the house. The idea is simple. Fire isn’t a foolproof way of destroying all evidence, but it sure is a hell of a lot better than cleaning the house from top to bottom. Even then, if anything was suspected, chemicals can be used to show washed-away blood, and from there a link to Calhoun could easily be made. Fire is a far greater guarantee that nothing will be found. Naturally, burning the corpse here isn’t such a good idea. It takes extreme heat to burn through bone, and depending on how quickly the neighbors contact the ﬁre department, the chances of the body burning into dust before they arrive or of the house burning down completely are about as great as my testicle growing back. The pathologist will study the body, the damage to the severed throat, the bruised jaw. He may even ﬁnd tape residue on the face and rope burn on the ankles and hands. Even if it’s burned to a skeleton he’ll ﬁnd serrated edges in the sternum from the knife. They’ll know Calhoun was murdered and framed.
zh_text: 我拖著屍體的足部下樓，讓頭部「咚咚咚」撞著每一層樓梯，接著把它拖過地面進到了隔壁的車庫。浴簾有個地方沒綑好——這種綑綁包紮的事男人就是不行，真的——於是屍身從那外露，弄髒了地毯。我把他扔在車庫地面，開燈，然後左右張望。我的行頭都在這裡。我從鋤草機旁撿起一個塑膠汽油罐，搖了搖——那聽起來幾乎還是滿的，約莫有十五公升吧——再把它拿回屋內。我的想法很簡單。透過縱火來湮滅證據並無法保證萬無一失，但這肯定要比從頭到尾打掃整間房子來得好。即便房子已經打掃得一塵不染，其中要是有可疑之處，警方仍會透過魯米諾偵測血液法（Luminol test）顯示出哪裡的血跡曾被人抹掉，然後就會很輕易地聯想起卡爾霍恩。你要是希望警方無從掌握到一絲線索，那麼縱火保證遠比打掃來得管用。當然，焚屍也算不上什麼好點子。要把人骨燒成灰燼需要極度高溫，同時這也取決於鄰居打給九一一的速度有多快。一個人要在消防隊抵達或房子徹底焚毀之前就被燒了個屍骨無存的機率，差不多和我要再長回睪丸的機率一樣微乎其微。病理學家驗屍時不但會發現被害人遭人割喉、下巴瘀青，甚至可能在他臉上找到殘餘的膠帶、在腳踝和雙手找到燒剩的繩子。即便卡爾霍恩被燒得只剩白骨，病理學家仍會發現胸骨中鋸齒狀的刀傷，進而推知他是被人謀殺、遭人栽贓。

en_text: I take the lid from the gas can and begin splashing it across the carpet and bed. The smell of gas quickly ﬁlls my nostrils. At ﬁrst, maybe for a few seconds, I like it, but then it quickly becomes nauseating and I want to throw up. When the room’s wet enough to burn quickly, I make my way through the other upstairs rooms, leaving a trail of gas as I go. Downstairs I do the same, leaving a trail on the stairs. I save some for the trip. I grab my briefcase and head outside. I suck in a few deep breaths of air to clear my lungs, then spit the taste of gas from my mouth.
zh_text: 我掀開汽油罐的蓋子，在床和地毯上上下下潑灑汽油，汽油味很快撲鼻而來。起初也就起初的那幾秒——我挺喜歡這種味道，但它很快就變得教人反胃、作嘔。當臥房灑滿汽油、足以瞬間起火，我也陸續走過其他位於樓上的房間，人走到哪汽油就跟著潑到哪；樓下我也比照辦理，在走過的樓梯潑起汽油，最後只留下一些中途備用。我打開冰箱，想喝啤酒卻一罐也找不到，於是替自己斟了杯水，從樓上抓起公事包向外走去。我深吸了幾口氣，清一清肺裡的廢氣，再吐掉嘴裡的汽油味。

en_text: I go for a walk. The car I stole yesterday after work is still where I left it a few blocks away. I drive it to the house, back it into the garage, close the door, then stuff the body in the trunk. I didn’t want to risk driving a stolen car tonight, but now I can’t risk not to. Carrying a limp body draped in a shower curtain over my shoulder and walking through town with it would look suspicious, even for this city.
zh_text: 我漫步而行。昨天下班後所偷的那輛車現在還停在幾個路口外。我把車開進屋裡，倒車入庫，關起車庫門，再把屍體塞進後車廂。我今晚原本不想冒險開起贓車，如今卻不得不以身犯險。扛著裹起浴簾的跛行屍體走過小鎮看起來相當可疑，甚至在城市中也一樣。我找起火柴，遍尋不著，車裡的點菸器再度派上用場。

en_text:
I look for a match and can’t ﬁnd one. Again the cigarette lighter from the car comes in handy. Thirty seconds later it’s glowing red. I hold it onto a rag in the garage, then throw the burning rag into the house. Fire spreads across the ﬂoor and climbs the walls, racing quickly up the stairs. Born from nowhere and now it’s alive everywhere. Alive and hungry. I don’t need to supervise it. The rest should be child’s play.
I open the garage door and drive out into the street. I glance back at the house through the mirrors but can’t see any signs of ﬁre. I don’t bother to wait around. It’ll happen.
zh_text:
點菸器在半分鐘後亮起紅光，我拿它接起車庫裡取來的破布，等布著了火，便往屋裡一扔。火勢瞬間延燒過整個地板，竄上四周的牆壁，並飛快地攀上樓梯。屋裡原本無煙無火，如今卻噴吐著致命的火舌，亟欲吞噬這裡所有的一切。接下來的事就簡單多了，我根本就沒監督的必要。我打開車庫門，開車上路，並透過鏡面瞄起後方的房子，但就是看不到任何火災的跡象。反正我又不趕時間，四處晃晃等等好了。
就在我開離這座城市時，我打開音響，聽著安琪拉在遭我謀殺那天在房裡所播的那首歌曲。

en_text: As I drive away from the city, I turn the stereo on to hear the same song that was playing in Angela’s bedroom the day I killed her. It seems so long ago. It must be an omen, and I take it to be a good one. I can’t help but sing along as I head north. My spirits are high, the evening is warm, and things are going well. Life is good.
zh_text: 這鐵定是種預兆，但我把這視爲好預兆。隨著我一路北上，我忍不住哼唱起來。我心情很好，向晚的天候溫暖宜人，事情也進行得非常順利……人生真是美好啊。

en_text: Tonight I’m looking for an ideal place to dump a body. I can’t afford for this one to be found. I drive through the plains that make up Canterbury, searching for one of those crazy dirt roads that take you approximately nowhere. After an hour, I ﬁnd one. A wire fence closes it off from the public. I fumble with the lock.
zh_text: 今晚我正要找理想的棄屍地點。屍體要是被人發現，我擔當不起。我開過了坎特伯里一片片的大平原，找起有沒有哪條髒到不行又不知把你帶往何處的路。一小時後，我找到了。那條路的外側圍起鐵絲欄，沒有對外開放，然後我胡亂摸索，找起鎖頭在哪。

en_text: When I’ve eventually driven far enough, I stop the car, open the trunk, and drag the cocoon through the trees. I spend half an hour digging a pit knee-deep with a shovel I borrowed from the garage. I am still wearing gloves. My ﬁngers are wet-rubber damp again. When the hole’s deep enough, I kick the side of the corpse and it rolls into the grave with a thud. This is option country. If I leave the pit open, the body will rot quickly beneath the sun, and the small animals that live out here will make sure any evidence is quickly gnawed away. However, this is risky. Should some hick farmer wander by, he’ll be making the most exciting discovery of his life. Plus there probably won’t be a lot of sun over the following days and weeks.
zh_text: 等到最後開得夠遠了，我才停下車子，打開後車廂，把屍體拖過一棵棵的綠樹，然後花上半小時用從車庫所借來的鏟子挖起深度及膝的坑洞。我仍戴著橡膠手套，十指全都濕透。待洞挖得夠深，我就往屍體側邊一踹，接著它「咚」的一聲滾進墓穴。這是個自由選擇的國家。要是我沒埋起坑洞，屍體在陽光的曝曬下很快就會腐爛，然後住在這裡的小動物鐵定火速就會把證據給啃個精光。不過這麼做很冒險，因為某個鄉下農夫要是路過，他便即將面對此生中最驚人的發現。

en_text: I climb into the pit and, using a knife, I slice the cocoon open. With the gardening shears, some pliers, and the hammer, I start removing his teeth and his ﬁngertips. A grisly job, but I whistle as I work and the mess isn’t as bad as I would have thought. I keep things pointed away from me to lessen the chances of getting blood on myself, but I still fail. After a while I get into the swing of things and the time goes quickly.
zh_text: 我爬進坑洞，把屍體一層層割開。我手上握有園藝剪、鉗子和大榔頭，開始敲掉他的牙齒、剪去他的指尖。這工作挺嚇人的，但我還是一邊做一邊吹口哨，結果也沒我預想的那麼混亂。爲了減少沾上血跡的機率，我不讓屍體朝向我這，但我起初不太成功，直到過了一會兒才進入狀況，感覺到時光飛逝。

en_text: I dump the teeth and ﬁngers into a separate plastic bag, along with his wallet and identiﬁcation. Then I douse the rest of the corpse with the last of the gas, use the car lighter again to light another rag, then toss it in with the corpse. It smells like a barbecue. After ﬁfteen minutes most of him has burned away and I’m feeling hungry. Whistling again, I ﬁll the hole in, stamp it ﬂat, then drag some leaves and dead grass over it. I walk back to the car and toss Daniela Walker’s spade into the trunk.
zh_text: 我把牙齒、手指連同皮夾、身分證全丟進一只塑膠袋裡，把僅剩的汽油灑在屍體的其他部位，再拿車子的點菸器燃起另一塊破布，最後往屍體一扔。這聞起來就像BOO。十五分鐘後，屍體多半已被燒得焦黑。我又吹起口哨，埋起坑洞，用腳踩平，然後拔起幾片葉子、幾絲枯草鋪在上頭。我走回車裡，把丹妮耶拉·沃克的鏟子扔進後車廂。

en_text: I stop a half mile or so from home, soak the car in gas, and set it on ﬁre. In this part of town nobody will care enough to call the ﬁre department. I walk the rest of the way to my apartment, carrying the video camera and the plastic bag.
zh_text: 我把車停在距離家裡大約一公里的地方，在車上灑濾汽油，然後放火一燒。在這種鳥不拉屎的小鎮裡，根本就沒人在意打不打電話給消防隊。我走起剩下的一小段路，拿著攝錄機和塑膠袋往公寓邁進。

en_text: It’s nine thirty. I still have half an hour.
zh_text: 九點半。我還剩下半小時。

en_text: I make two copies of the videotape, though I need only one. I store one in my apartment. The second I put in my briefcase to store later in a safe place. I strip the detective’s wallet of cash and fold it into my pocket, then toss the wallet into the plastic bag. The ﬁngers I’ll grind up later and feed to the neighborhood dogs. The teeth I’ll take a hammer to.
zh_text: 即便一片帶子就已綽綽有餘，我還是拷貝了兩片，一片放在公寓，一片放在公事包，待稍晚再移放安全之處。我抽光了警探皮夾裡的現金，摺好放進口袋，再把皮夾扔進塑膠袋。晚點我還會把磨碎的手指拿去餵鄰居的狗，至於牙齒嘛，我則會用大榔頭敲碎。

en_text: At nine ﬁfty, I walk to the park. It’s still a warm night and the moon is out in full and the stars unusually bright, but maybe I’m just seeing things clearer now. What’s deﬁnitely clear is that it’s a perfect evening for romance and death. In the waistband of my pants is the dead man’s ﬁrearm, which I’ve no intention of using. Also tucked into a sheath in the back of my pants is my small knife with the two-inch blade.
zh_text: 九點五十分。我走到公園。玉盤似的月亮高掛天際，晚間的天候仍舊溫暖，這種時候談穩愛、殺殺人再完美也不過了。腰帶上插著死去男人的那把槍——我一直都不想用——而那把厚達五公分的小刀正插入刀鞘、在褲子後面動來動去。

en_text: The park is completely empty when I get there. I step onto the grass and walk to the place where I lost my testicle. It feels colder here. The trees stand out in the moonlight and point at me with dark ﬁngers, covering most of the stars. I stand by the patch of grass where my life changed forever. I wonder if it’s still stained with my blood, but it’s too dark to tell. At ten o’clock, a lone ﬁgure walks toward me.
zh_text: 拒違公園時，那裡匹下無人，我踩上草坪，走到先前痛失睾丸的地方。這裡冷颼颼的，我不住哆嗦。群樹昂然挺立於皎潔的月光下，用黑色的枝枒指著我，而我就站在自己人生就此改變的那塊草地上，心想上頭不知仍否沾有我的血跡，只不過這裡實在太過漆黑，無從得知。十點整。有個人朝我走來，形單影隻。

en_text: She’s in bed when they come for her. In bed thinking about Joe. Wondering where he was tonight when she went to his apartment and knocked on the door. She hadn’t gone inside. Hadn’t driven to his mother’s in case he was there. Hadn’t driven to the house where she saw him last night, even though she supposed she should’ve.
zh_text: 他們找上門時，她正在床上想著喬，想著她今晚到他家公寓敲門時他人究竟在哪。她並沒進屋，沒開車到他媽家看看他是否在那，也沒開車到她昨晚看到他的那間房子——即便她覺得自己應該這麼做。

en_text: The last time the police came to her house was ﬁve years ago. They came two days after Martin had died. Back then it had been one police car. They had come to take statements in the most gentle way they could. This time several of them are parked right outside. They have their lights ﬂashing, but their sirens are muted. The banging on the door, however, is not. The lights send red and blue patterns racing left and right across her wallpaper through thin gaps around the curtains. There is nothing gentle about this.
zh_text: 上回警方登門拜訪是在五年前，也就在馬丁過世後的第二天。當時他們只開了一輛警車，這回卻開了好幾輛停在外面、閃起警車燈，並散發出紅藍交錯的閃光，透過窗簾周圍的狹縫在壁紙左右急速掃動。車子雖沒發出警笛聲，他們卻「砰砰砰」大聲撞起門來。

en_text: She hears her mother and father asking what’s going on, then her name. She climbs out of bed and puts on a robe just as the door opens. Detective Schroder is there, looking stressed and tired and pissed off. He’s looking at her as if she’s guilty of something.
zh_text: 她聽見爸媽問起怎麼回事，接著聽到了自己的名字。她下了床，穿上浴袍，就在此時，門打了開，而史卓德警探就在那裡，看來又疲憊又緊張又抓狂。他盯著她看，一副她犯了什麼重大罪刑。

en_text: “What’s going on?”
zh_text: 「怎麼了？」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Come on, Sally.”
zh_text: 「走吧，莎莉。」

en_text: “Can I change?”
zh_text: 「能讓我換件衣服嗎？」

en_text: He stalls, obviously wanting to say no, but then calls for a female ofﬁcer, who comes into the room. “Make it quick,” he says, then closes the door behind him.
zh_text: 他愣在原地，顯然想要說不，但還是叫了名女警進到房裡。「快點。」他說，然後關起身後的門。

en_text: The ofﬁcer doesn’t talk to her as she changes into a pair of jeans and a T-shirt. She recognizes the woman, has seen her around at the station and even spoken on occasion, but right now this woman is acting like a stranger. She tugs on a jacket, some socks, and her shoes.
zh_text: 當她著手換起T恤和牛仔裤的同時，那名女警並沒和她說話。她認得那個女人，但不知她叫什麼名字。她用力拉起外套，並穿起襪子、鞋子。

en_text: “Let’s go,” the woman says, and opens the door.
zh_text: 「走吧。」那女人說，然後把門打開。

en_text: Half a dozen policemen stand in the hallway. They’re asking her parents questions and not answering the questions her parents are asking them. She tries to tell them everything’s okay, but she doesn’t know if that’s true. They don’t handcuff her, but they put her in the back of a squad car and rush her away. She notices that over half of the police cars stay at her house. If they’re searching her room, she hopes they’ll tidy it up afterward.
zh_text: 有六名警察站在門廳，問起她爸媽問題，但對於爸媽反問的問題卻是拒絕回答。她試著告訴爸媽一切沒事，卻不知是否真是如此。他們沒替她戴上手銬，卻把她押進警車後座，急忙帶走。她注意到局裡有一半以上的警車都停在她家。他們若要搜索她的房間，真希望他們在搜完之後會收拾乾淨、物歸原位。鄰居全都站在自家前方的草坪看著，一臉好奇。

en_text: Almost all her neighbors are standing on their front lawns watching. She doesn’t know what’s going on. She’s scared and confused. Has she done something wrong at work? Do they think she’s stolen something? Have they decided, ﬁve years later, to charge her for her brother’s death? The drive to the police station is the quickest she’s ever had. The urgency to get her there seems undermined when they take her into an interrogation room, leave her alone, close the door, and disappear for half an hour. She paces the room, sits down, then paces it again. Her heart’s racing, her hands are shaking slightly, and she’s becoming more frightened with every passing minute She’s never been in here before. The room is cold and she’s thankful for her jacket. The chairs are uncomfortable. The table is marked with the passages of other people’s time. Fingernails, keys, coins, anything they could ﬁnd to scrape messages into the wood.
zh_text: 她從沒這麼快就搭車抵達警局，這可是第一次。原本警方看似急著把她帶回局裡，但一把她帶進了偵訊室，他們就留下她獨自一人、關起門來消失了半個小時，一切似乎變得有點急又不太急。她在偵訊室裡來回踱步，坐下，然後又繼續踱步。她心跳加速，雙手微顫，一想到自己完全搞不清楚狀況，她就感到非常害怕。她究竟做了什麼？她從沒來過這裡。裡面好冷，還好自己穿著外套。椅子坐起來很不舒服，桌上還有一堆記號，顯示出別人在這接受偵訊時是如何打發時間。指甲、鑰匙、硬幣，當時人們手邊有什麼，就拿什麼在木頭上刻下記號、留下訊息。

en_text: She doesn’t know the man who comes into the room at the thirtyminute mark. Just an average-looking guy with average features, but he frightens her. He asks her to hold out her hands and she does. He takes swabs of her skin and when she asks why, he doesn’t tell her. Then he leaves.
zh_text: 指針一指到六，就有個男人進到偵訊室。這傢伙相貌普普，莎莉雖不認識，卻還是嚇了一跳。他要她伸出手來，她依言照做，接著他在她皮膚上採樣。當她問起原因，他什麼都沒說就離開了偵訊室。

en_text: It’s another ten minutes before Detective Schroder comes into the room, by which point she’s crying. He sits down opposite her and places a folder on the desk. He doesn’t open it.
zh_text: 史卓德警探進到偵訊室時，她淚眼盈盈。他就坐在她的對面，放了個資料夾在辦公桌上，但並沒打開。

en_text: “Sorry for all the drama, Sally, but this is important,” he says, and smiles at her as he slides a coffee across the table toward her. It’s as if he’s suddenly become her best friend. But there isn’t any trace of warmth in that smile.
zh_text: 「莎莉，有關這一切我先跟你道歉。但這真的非常重要。」他說，並推了杯咖啡到她面前時向她微微一笑，彷彿頓時成了她最好的朋友。她長期在這工作，久到已經相當清楚這只不過是他們慣用的伎倆。

en_text: “What’s going on?”
zh_text: 「發生什麼事了？」

en_text: “How well do you know Detective Calhoun?” The detective who went missing? What has that got to do with her?
zh_text: 「妳和卡爾霍恩警探熟不熟？」

en_text: “Not well. Why?”
zh_text: 「不太熟。幹嘛？」

en_text: “Do you ever socialize with him?”
zh_text: 「那妳有和他來往嗎？」

en_text: “Never been for a drink with him? Never run into him at a restaurant? At a shopping mall?” She glances at the coffee, but doesn’t touch it. “I already told you never,” she says, annoyed that Schroder thinks she’s lying.
zh_text: 「連一起喝杯茶都沒有？那麼在餐廳還是購物中心裡和他不期而遇呢？」她瞥了咖啡一眼，但碰都沒碰。「也沒有。」

en_text: “Ever been in his car?”
zh_text: 「那也沒搭過他的車嗎？」

en_text: “What?” “His car, Sally. Ever been for a ride with him?”
zh_text: 他的車啊，莎莉，妳有沒有坐過他的車？

en_text: “Seen him today at all?”
zh_text: 「今天見過他了沒？」

en_text: “You asked me that this morning.”
zh_text: 「這你今早已經問過了。」

en_text: “I’m asking you again.” “Why don’t you believe me?” she asks. “Answer the question, Sally.”
zh_text: 「我現在再問妳一次。」

en_text: “No. I don’t know the last time I saw him. Yesterday, maybe.” “Maybe?” “I see everybody here all the time. I don’t even know if I saw you yesterday but I’m sure I probably did.”
zh_text: 「沒見過。我也不記得上次見到他是什麼時候，應該是昨天吧。

en_text: He nods, accepting her answer. “Do you like ﬁre, Sally?”
zh_text: 「莎莉，妳喜歡火災嗎？」

en_text: “Fire. There was a ﬁre tonight. That’s why your hands were swabbed. We were looking for signs of any accelerants.”
zh_text: 「火災啊。今晚發生了一起火災，那也就是我們幹嘛要在妳手上採樣的原因，大家都想找出祿索，盡快釐清案情。」

en_text: “But you didn’t ﬁnd any, did you,” she says, not as a question but as a statement.
zh_text: 「但你什麼線索也沒找到吧。」她說，聽起來不像問題，反倒像是聲明。

en_text: “You could have worn gloves.”
zh_text: 「妳當時可能戴著手套。

en_text: “But I didn’t set ﬁre to anything!” she says, her voice raising.
zh_text: 「我可沒對什麼東西縱火呀。」

en_text: Schroder leans back and sighs. “Come on, Sally. Just be honest and you won’t need one,” he says, which is something else the cops say on TV too. “How long have we known each other?” She thinks about it. She doesn’t see the harm in answering this one without a lawyer present. “Six months.”
zh_text: 史卓德靠向椅背，嘆了口氣。「莎莉，妳幫幫忙，只要妳老實說，妳根本就不用請律師。我認識多久了？」

en_text: “You trust me?”
zh_text: 「妳信不信任我？」

en_text: He grunts, then leans forward again. “The place that burned down, it was a crime scene. It’s where Daniela Walker was killed. It was also where Lisa Houston was murdered.”
zh_text: 他哼了一聲，又向前傾身。「那棟被燒掉的房子曾經是犯罪現場，也就是丹妮耶拉·沃克被人殺害、麗莎·休士頓遭人謀殺的地方。」

en_text: She recognizes the names: both victims of the Christchurch Carver.
zh_text: 她聽過這兩個名字——她們都曾慘遭基督城屠夫的毒手。

en_text: “I didn’t burn the place down.”
zh_text: 「縱火的人不是我。」

en_text: “And you’ve never been in Detective Calhoun’s car.”
zh_text: 「妳也沒搭過卡爾霍恩警探的車？」

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「沒有。」

en_text: “And we have your word for that.” “Yes.” “Okay. Then you’ve got nothing to worry about. No need for a lawyer.”
zh_text: 「好，那妳就沒什麼好擔心的了。」

en_text: He smiles at her, but she can’t ﬁnd any warmth in it. “Let me show you two things,” he says. He opens up the folder, revealing a plastic ziplock evidence bag sitting on top of a photograph. It has a parking ticket in it. She can’t get a clear look at the picture beneath it.
zh_text: 他朝她一笑，她卻感受不到其中的善意。「給妳看看三樣東西。」他說完後打開資料夾。她看得出裡頭放了一只夾鏈式的塑膠證物袋，袋裡有張停車卡，然後袋子下方壓著一張照片，至於是怎樣的照片，她就看不清楚了。

en_text: “We found this today behind Detective Calhoun’s desk. It’s quite interesting really, what we learned from it. It has his ﬁngerprints on it. We know that, because everybody who works here has their ﬁngerprints on ﬁle. Everybody. Even people who aren’t police. The cleaners, for example. Even Joe. Even you.”
zh_text: 「我們今天在卡爾霍恩警探的辦公桌後發現了這個，從中獲得了一些線索，這上面有卡爾霍恩的指紋，這沒問題，大家都很清楚在這工作的每一個人指紋都有建檔，我是說每一個人喔，即使不是警察也一樣，舉例來說，清潔工也不例外，像是喬啦、妳啦。」

en_text: She doesn’t know what to say, so she says nothing. She tightens her grip on her cruciﬁx. She’s been hanging on to it since the moment she arrived here. “The second set of ﬁngerprints on the ticket belongs to you.”
zh_text: 她不知該說什麼，於是默不作聲，緊緊揪住胸前的十字架，從她一到警局，她就一直戴著。「票卡上的第二組指紋則是來自妳的。」

en_text: “What does that mean?”
zh_text: 「什麼意思？」

en_text: “In itself? Not much. It means you and Detective Calhoun each held this ticket at one point. You know, we went to the parking building this belongs to. The date on it is ﬁve months old.”
zh_text: 「妳是說指紋本身嗎？沒什麼意思，就是妳曾和卡爾霍恩警探同時拿著這張票卡而已。我們去了一趟這張票卡所屬的停車大樓，發現上面的時間已經是五個月前了。」

en_text: “Five months?”
zh_text: 「五個月前？」

en_text: “That’s right.”
Five months? A small bell starts ringing in the back of her mind.
zh_text: 五個月前？她腦海中隱隱想起了什麼。聽起來有點耳熟……但到底是什麼事呢？啊，她早就知道了。

en_text: Something familiar, but what? “We went to the parking building and we drove up each level. We weren’t sure what we were looking for. It was probably just a false lead. Only on the top we found Detective Calhoun’s car. The ticket wasn’t for that, though, because his car could only have been there for a day at the most. When he parked it there, he hit the car next to him. Left a huge scrape all the way along the side of it. We’d found his car, that was good, but it meant we had to deal with the owner of the second car. Insurance companies were going to have to get involved. No doubt the owner would be pissed off. Any idea what happened then?”
zh_text: 「我們去到停車大樓，開上每一層樓，也不確定在找些什麼，或許只是亂走一通，結果呢，居然讓我們在頂樓找到了卡爾霍恩警探的車。但這張票卡不是他的，因為他的車頂多只能停個一天，不過他在那停車時，撞上了隔壁的車，沿著車身留下了一道重重的刮痕。我們找到了他的車是很好，但這也意味著我們得和第二輛車的車主打交道，還得把保險公司扯進來，也難怪車主會抓狂。結果妳知道怎麼樣嗎？

en_text: She shakes her head, too scared to speak.
zh_text: 她搖了搖頭，嚇得啞口無言。

en_text: “We ran the plate. Turned out the car was reported stolen ﬁve months ago. Reported one day after the time code on the parking ticket. That means the car was stolen at night, parked there, and the following day the owner went to drive to work and found out he couldn’t. So we opened up the car. Want to guess what we found in there?” She shakes her head. “We found a body in there.”
zh_text: 我們查起車牌號碼，發現這輛車五個月前就被偷了，然後車主報案的那一天，正好就是票卡上時間的隔天。這表示這輛車是晚上被偷，停進大樓，等到隔天車主走去開車上班，這才發現車子已經不見蹤影。於是我們攝開車子，發現後車廂有具屍體。

en_text: She gasps and tightens her grip. The corners of her cruciﬁx puncture her skin. “It was wrapped in plastic, and surrounded by ninety pounds of cat litter.”
zh_text: 她深吸了口氣，把十字架越揪越緊，四個端點都刺進了皮膚。「屍體用塑膠袋包著，周圍還堆滿了四十公斤的貓沙。」

en_text: “Cat litter?”
zh_text: 「貓沙？」

en_text: “It absorbs the smell.”
zh_text: 「貓沙會吸臭。」

en_text: “I had nothing to do with it.”
zh_text: 「這不關我的事。」

en_text: “It seemed odd that Detective Calhoun would dump his car next to a car with a body hidden in it. Odd that we would ﬁnd the ticket for that car after we’d already searched his desk. It was as though it were placed there for us to ﬁnd. Odd that your ﬁngerprints are on it. Any idea why he would park there? Any idea how this ticket showed up?”
zh_text: 「卡爾霍恩警探會把車子扔掉、棄之不理，然後隔壁車子還藏著屍體，這似乎很怪，而我們在搜查完他的辦公桌便馬上找到了那輛車的票卡，這也很怪，就連票卡都沾上了妳的指紋，這更是怪到不行。妳知不知道他幹嘛這麼做？還有，票卡究竟是怎麼來的？

en_text: “No,” she says, but that’s not strictly true. She does have an idea, and she doesn’t like it. Not at all.
zh_text: 「我不知道。」她說，但並未完全坦誠。她的確知道原因，只是她厭惡那個原因，而且是厭惡極了。

en_text: He lifts the plastic bag away. The photograph beneath it is of the car she saw parked up the driveway of the house yesterday. The same car Joe left in.
zh_text: 他拿起塑膠袋放到一邊，袋下的照片上面有著她昨天看到停在車道上的那一輛車，也就是喬所開走的那一輛。

en_text: “This is his car. You’re telling me you’ve never seen it?”
zh_text: 「這就是他的車。妳不會說妳沒看過吧？

en_text: He lifts the photograph away, and beneath it is another evidence bag. Inside it is the small pad she wrote on yesterday. It’s the address of the house where Joe went.
zh_text: 他拿起照片放到一邊，然後下面又放有另一只證物袋，裡頭是她昨天所寫的那張小紙條，上面記下了喬所前往的那個地址。

en_text: “Why did you write down this address?”
zh_text: 「妳為什麼要寫下這個地址？」

en_text: “Is that . . . is that the house that burned down?” she asks.
zh_text: 她聳了聳肩。「你想起自己燒了房子吧？」「什麼？」

en_text: “Yes, it is,” he says. “You had the address written down on a pad in your car.”
zh_text: 「今晚發生火警的房子就位在這個地址，過去曾有兩人分別在這被殺，而且我們在妳車裡找到這個。」

en_text: “Oh Lord,” she says—not to Detective Schroder, but to herself. She knows why the house looked familiar to her. She saw a photograph of it in the folders at Joe’s house when she ﬂicked through them. The same day she picked up the parking ticket from beneath his bed.
zh_text: 「天啊！」她說，但不是對史卓德警探說，而是對她自己說。這下她終於明白這房子爲何看起來這麼眼熟了，她在喬家翻遍資料夾時曾經看過這房子的照片。這和她從床下撿起票卡是同一天。

en_text: “Joe,” she whispers.
zh_text: 「是喬。」她低聲道。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: She starts to sob. It’s all starting to make sense. The folders. The wound. Joe driving the detective’s car. “I . . . I had nothing.” She chokes on a sob, can’t catch her breath, and feels like she’s going to pass out. She shakes her head, grits her teeth, and inhales loudly. Then, surrounded by more tears, she ﬁnishes her sentence.
zh_text: 她開始啜泣，一切都開始變得合情合理。資料夾、傷口、喬開著警探的車……「這……這不……」她一邊啜泣，一邊哽咽。「不關我……我的事。求求你……求你一定要相信我。」

en_text: “I had nothing to do with this. Please, you must. Must believe me.” “Then tell me, Sally. Tell me how I’ve added all of this up wrong. Tell me where I should be looking.” So she does. She starts by telling him about the smile Joe gave her that day in the elevator two weeks ago, she tells him what a sweet guy Joe is, then starts to tell him the rest.
zh_text: 「那麼莎莉，請妳告訴我，告訴我哪裡錯了、告訴我應該怎麼看才對。」於是她坦誠相告，說起喬曾對她一笑，緊接著娓娓道來。

en_text: The homework has been completed. The work carried out. Now it comes down to the sales pitch.
zh_text: 功課已經完成，工作也已順利做完，現在推銷時間到了。

en_text: Melissa walks slowly across the grass toward me. My gun in her hand. She trusts me enough to meet me in a dark park at night, but not enough to come unarmed. No surprise there. Nor is there any surprise for her when I produce Detective Calhoun’s gun and point it at her.
zh_text: 梅莉莎從草坪對面緩緩朝我走來，手裡握著我的槍。她和我約在晚上黑漆漆的公園裡見面，算是對我非常信任，只不過信任歸信任，但還沒信任到空手而來的程度。對此我泰然自若，而在我亮出卡爾霍恩警探的槍瞄準她時，她也是一臉老神在在。

en_text: I stand my ground and wait patiently. She stops a few feet away. She’s not smiling. Perhaps she sees no humor in the situation. Nor does she show any fear.
zh_text: 我站在原地，耐心等待，她則在一公尺外停下腳步，看起來一副天不怕地不怕的樣子，笑也不笑。也許在這種情況下她看不出有何好笑之處。

en_text: “Seems you can’t get enough of me,” I say, looking her up and down.
zh_text: 「看來妳打算把我榨乾。」我說，上下打量著她。

en_text: She looks good. “Does seem that way, doesn’t it? You got the money?”
zh_text: 「錢湊齊了嗎？」

en_text: I shake the plastic bag I’m carrying. “I’ve got something better than money.”
zh_text: 我晃了晃手裡的塑膠袋。「我帶了比錢更棒的東西。」

en_text: She lifts the gun to my face. “Oh?”
zh_text: 她把槍舉到我面前。「喔？」

en_text: I hand her the plastic bag. Both of us are keeping our guns trained on the other. She quickly glances into it.
zh_text: 我倆都拿槍瞄準對方。我把塑膠袋交給她，她很快地瞄了袋子一眼。

en_text: “A video camera.”
zh_text: 「是攝錄機。」

en_text: “That’s right.”
zh_text: 「答對了。」

en_text: “What’s this for?”
zh_text: 「你拿這幹嘛？」

en_text: “You may want to watch the tape.”
zh_text: 「妳或許會想看看帶子。」

en_text: “You bastard.”
zh_text: 「你這混蛋！」

en_text: She ﬂings the camera back at me. “You fucking bastard.”
zh_text: 她把攝錄機甩回給我。「你這超級大混蛋！」

en_text: I start to laugh. From her abuse it’s obvious she’s ﬁgured things out.
zh_text: 我噗嗤一笑。根據她咒罵的語氣，她顯然已經知道怎麼回事。

en_text: “You played me,” she says.
zh_text: 「你也有出現在畫面裡。

en_text: “Wasn’t difﬁcult.”
zh_text: 「實際上並沒有。反正這也不重要。

en_text: She grunts. “You’re on that tape too, Joe.” “Actually, I’m not. Not that it matters. If you kill me, what are the police going to do? Dig me up and arrest me?” She stares at me silently for a few more seconds, then sighs. “It’s a stalemate then. Just as if anything happens to me, Joe—to use your phrase, oh, I don’t know, anything at all—copies of everything I know about you will make their way to those same people.”
zh_text: 她又默默瞪著我幾秒，接著嘆了口氣。「喬，我只是事先聲明，要是我怎麼了，那麼有關你的事也全都會傳到警方的耳裡。」

en_text: “Sounds like a pretty good deal,” I say, and this is the best result I can hope for. It’s the result I’ve aimed for. Sure, I still want to feed her through a branch chipper, but with self-preservation in mind, it’s not the sort of thing I can do. Maybe one day if I can get my hands on the evidence she has against me, or if I ever discover I have cancer and only weeks to live. She nods and slips the gun back into her handbag. “Well, I can’t say it’s been fun, Joe.”
zh_text: 「這交易聽起來不賴。」我說，這既是我所期盼，同時也是我所希冀的最佳結果。沒錯，我還是很想把她整個人丟進碎紙機裡絞它個稀巴爛，但有鑑於自我保護的心態，這種事我做不來。黠頭，把槍插回手提袋。「我覺得這一點都不好玩。」

en_text: “Nor can I.” I too put my gun away.
zh_text: 「我也這麼覺得。」我也把槍拿開。

en_text:
“What did you do with the cop?”
I shrug. “The usual stuff.”
zh_text:
你是怎麼處理掉那個警察的？
我聳了聳肩。「老樣子。」

en_text: Neither of us turns away. The conversation is over. The rules have been stated and we both understand them. Yet here we are, a few feet apart, neither of us able to turn our back on what’s happened. We’ve gone through so much, and for us to walk away empty-handed would be heartbreaking. It’s anticlimactic. It would be like waking up on Christmas morning and ﬁnding out everybody you know has given you the same style of socks.
zh_text: 我倆都沒轉身。談話結束。遊戲規則已敘述得相當清楚，我們也完全了解，但我們身在此地，相隔一公尺，就是沒人轉頭就走、爲此事隨便劃下句點。我倆歷經了太多事，對我們來說，空手離開會教人多麼失落，就有如你在耶誕節一早醒來，結果發現每個認識的人都送給你同一款襪子那樣。

en_text: The moonlight strikes her face and makes her skin look pale. Again I’m struck by how beautiful she is. If it wasn’t for the fact I wanted to take a knife and . . . We both step forward into an embrace and start kissing. She’s stufﬁng her tongue into my throat as if the Holy Grail is down there somewhere, and I’m trying to stuff mine into hers. Our bodies grind into each other. My hands are roaming behind her back. Hers are behind mine and she’s not trying to get my gun.
zh_text: 月光就灑在她的臉上，她看起來面無血色。若非我想要拿起刀子然後……她那美若天仙的容貌著實教我如痴如醉。我們都向前一步，擁抱對方，開始親吻。一如我喉嚨深處藏著衆人苦尋的寶物那般，她給了我法式熱吻，我也試著回應起她的吻。我們開始纏綿。我伸手在她背後來回輕撫，她也是，而且並未試圖奪走我的槍。

en_text: I can’t understand it, and for a moment I think of Calhoun’s original description of killing Daniela Walker. One second he’d been talking to her, the next she was dead. It’s happening to me right now and I’m hardly aware of it because my body’s on automatic. Ten seconds ago I was staring at her, and now I’ve got my hands digging into her back and squashing her perfect breasts against my chest. After a few seconds we pull back and look at each other, neither of us sure what to say, neither of us sure what the hell is going on. I think she’s in as much shock as I am.
zh_text: 我想這就像卡爾霍恩最初向我描述他是如何謀殺丹妮耶拉·沃克的經過——前一秒鐘他還在跟她說話，後一秒鐘她便已命喪黃泉。同樣的事情正在上演，但有礙於身體的自然反應，我幾乎沒察覺到這點，而且其中最大的不同，在於我真的不懂自己怎麼會這樣。十秒鐘前我還瞪著她看，如今卻把手探入她的衣裳，揉撫香背，再讓她完美無瑕的動人雙峰緊緊貼在我的胸膛。過了幾秒，我們推開彼此，凝視對方，沒人知道該說什麼，也沒人知道究竟怎麼回事。

en_text: I can see hatred in her eyes, and I’m sure there must be anger in mine . . . and then we’re kissing again, harder this time.
zh_text: 我看得見她眼中的憎恨，我看起來也一定是怒火中燒……我們雙唇又合而爲一，這回吻得更加激情。

en_text: We pull back. I can’t tell if the hatred and the anger are fading away or increasing. She opens her mouth to say something, I do the same, but all we end up doing is grabbing hold of each other. We lock in a passionate embrace, our lips mashing and our tongues darting. Nothing else matters anymore, and I have no doubt that all across the world people are ﬁnding love at this exact moment. I’ve no idea what I’m ﬁnding, but I like it. Like the week I spent in bed with my ball sac in tatters, time seems to come and go, as though I am in a place where time doesn’t really matter at all, but only events. The moon is still out and we are walking beneath it, trying to hold each other while stumbling . . . where?
zh_text: 我倆又推開彼此。我已經無從得知憎恨、怒火如今是逐漸消逝，還是愈益澎湃。她張口欲言，我也是，但最後我們卻緊緊相擁，雙唇緊貼，舌尖顫動，沉醉於這激情的擁抱之中，其他一切都已不再重要。我深信世界各地的人就是在此刻找起良伴、覓起真愛。即便我不清楚自己正在找些什麼，但我很喜歡自己所找到的。正如我帶著傷重累累、碎爛不堪的睪丸臥床的那一個禮拜，如今時光飛逝，彷彿我正置身於時間毫不重要、唯有事件才重要的地方。月娘仍高掛天際，我們頂著月色漫步而行、試著在跌跤時牽起對方的手……我究竟身在何處？

en_text: She takes me back to her place. She drives us there. We keep looking at each other, and every intersection, every trafﬁc light, I keep waiting for the spell to break, but it doesn’t. Then we’re in her bedroom, and if I could think I’d be thinking she’s going to kill me. Only we’re not killing each other, instead we’re both naked and she’s lying on top of me with my testicle pressing against her, and I have no idea how much time has passed since we ﬁrst kissed. I expect to feel the damp grass on my back, even though I can see her ceiling.
zh_text: 她將我帶回住處，進入她的臥房，要是我能思考，我想她正打算殺人滅口。就在我弄清楚怎麼回事之前，我和她已經全身赤裸，她處於上位，壓迫著我的睾丸。自我們最初接吻以來，我已經搞不清時間過了多久。即便我看得見她家的天花板，我還是期待在背後感覺到濕潤的青草。

en_text: Is this really happening? I look up at her, and she’s got this grin on her face. It’s a similar grin to when she ripped apart my left nut, but I can’t see any pliers nearby. The hatred has gone.
zh_text: 這是不是一場夢？我抬頭看她，她臉上掛著一絲笑容，和她扯掉我左側睪丸時的笑容十分類似，只不過這附近看不到鉗子。

en_text: Yeah, this is happening.
zh_text: 不，這不是夢。

en_text: Time becomes muddled again as we play beneath the sheets for what feels like forever, then we’re lying side by side and staring at the ceiling. Finally I fall asleep. Saturday rolls around and starts with us being all over each other. We take a lunch break. It’s pouring with rain outside, it lands heavily on the roof and I never understood until now how the sound of rain can be romantic. It’s just like all those books I read said it’d be like. We eat cheese on toast and we don’t really talk about much, if anything really, yet there is nothing awkward about the long patches of silence, just as there is nothing awkward about the fact I’m down to one testicle because of her. She doesn’t apologize for it and I don’t tell her how annoyed I am by it. We spent the afternoon in her bed and the room gets darker as the evening sets in. The rain keeps getting heavier. The house is comfortably warm. We soak in the bathtub for an hour and now we ﬁnally do talk beyond things like are you hungry and do you like how this feels. We talk movies and books and music.
zh_text: 當我們在被窩下盡享歡愉，接著並肩而臥、盯起天花板時，我又開始頭昏眼花，對於經過多久毫無概念。最後我沉沉睡去，直到鬧鐘響了才醒過來。這個週末我就耗在這了，挺棒的，因為……

en_text: Saturday becomes Sunday and the rain eases but doesn’t disappear. I wake up and stare at Melissa and I can honestly say I feel no desire to kill her. I watch her sleep, but I’m thinking about how it would feel to tear her apart, to dig my ﬁngers and a knife into her ﬂesh, and deconstruct her as painfully as I can. . . . And I could too . . . and it would be fun—but I would never hurt her.
zh_text: 收音機裡的傢伙告訴我今天居然已經禮拜天了！我坐起身子，看著她，坦白說我完全不想殺她滅口。我看她酣然入睡，心裡卻想著費盡力氣將她肢解又碎屍萬段的感覺會是如何——這應該挺有趣的，其實我老早能下手——只是我不打算傷害她。

en_text: I know what this feeling is. Watching her, knowing I could kill her at any second, I know that eventually—if not today, if not tomorrow—I am going to need to sort out my life. She wakes and smiles and wishes me good morning.
zh_text: 現在我知道那是種怎樣的感覺了。就在看著她、了解自己隨時就能取她性命的同時，我終於知道那是種怎樣的感覺——不是今天就是明天，我得要整頓一下自己的人生。我用刀抵住她的喉嚨，而她醒了過來微微一笑，向我道了聲「早」。

en_text: “So, Melissa, apparently you kill people,” I say, after wishing a good morning back to her. “Apparently.”
zh_text: 「梅莉莎，妳真的會殺人。」在我也道了聲「早」後，我如是說。「真的。」

en_text: “You any good at it?”
zh_text: 「很拿手嗎？」

en_text: “Exceptionally.”
zh_text: 「讚到不行。」

en_text: “You want to meet my mother?”
zh_text: 「妳想不想見見我媽？」

en_text: She laughs, and we end up making love. Afterward, I think back to that moment when I stood in the crippled woman’s house, looking at her ﬁsh. At the time I didn’t take any because I knew they would not ﬁll the emptiness I felt. Did I know then what I know now? That I was in love with Melissa?
zh_text: 她噗嗤一笑，結果我們又開始做愛。完事後，我回想起自己站在殘障女家中盯著魚看的那一刻，當下我之所以一條魚都沒帶走，就在於我很清楚這並無法填補我內心的空虛。那時我知不知道自己現在的想法呢？也就是如今我已經愛上梅莉莎？

en_text: All the killings, the fantasies, and now they’ve ended and what I’ve found is love. It seems as though my life has followed the pages of a typical romance novel. I feel like a regular Romeo, and Melissa the beautiful Juliet. I get up, get dressed, make conversation, and suddenly I am on the street, walking to my apartment, cars and pedestrians moving around me, and life is still a blur. Every now and then I’ll realize I’ve crossed a street or gone around a corner without being aware of it. The city looks pretty good on a Sunday morning. I get wet as I walk, but it doesn’t bother me. I think of my future, which is something I never really think too much about. I know that I’ll never be caught. I’m far too clever for that. In contrast to what everybody learns, in contrast to what they believe, sometimes the bad guy will get away with it. That’s just life. Live and learn.
zh_text: 所有的殺害、幻想如今皆已邁入尾聲，我已經覓得真愛，彷彿拿起自己的人生寫起一頁頁典型的愛情小說。我就像相貌堂堂的羅密歐，而梅莉莎就像美麗動人的茱麗葉。我起身著裝，聊一聊天，突然就到了街上，朝著四處移動的車子、行人和自己的公寓走去，偶爾才會意識到自己居然過了條街、轉過了彎都渾然不知。這座城市在禮拜天一早看起來真是迷人。我很清楚自己絕對不會被抓。有時壞人就是可以逍遙法外，這和大家學到的、相信的恰好相反。人生就是這樣——活到老學到老。

en_text: A happy ending to a happy life. That’s what it comes down to. I was happy as Joe the Christchurch Carver, but now I’m even happier as Joe the Romeo. This crazy mixed-up world has taken it upon itself to ﬁnd me true love, to ﬁnd me companionship. I’ll leave my job and ﬁnd something far less menial. With a cat, and with a wife-to-be, the possibilities for my future are endless. I’ve lost two ﬁsh, but I have gained something even better.
zh_text: 快樂的人生、快樂的結局。就是這麼回事。以往我很樂於當起化身基督城屠夫的喬，但現在我更樂於當起化身羅密歐的喬。這個瘋狂又混雜的世界自然而然地爲我找到真愛。我會辭職，然後找起其他事做，不再把自己搞得像下人一樣。有了貓和未婚妻的陪伴，我的未來機會無限。我雖然失去了兩條魚，卻反而得到了更可貴的東西。

en_text: I’m at the steps to my apartment building when a car screeches to a halt right next to me. I start to go for my gun, but then I see that it’s Sally driving. That’s why the car screeched—people like her are crap drivers. I can’t even imagine how somebody with her condition can have got a license, but ﬁgure it must be in the same tradition that they are given jobs —that whole forcing her kind into trolley-pushing positions. She opens the door and races around the car toward me, leaving it running. She’s pufﬁng, as if the twenty-feet jog has taken it out of her. I have a can of cat food in my hand that I can’t even remember buying. My briefcase is God knows where. The sun is out, the breeze is warm, and for once it isn’t too hot. It’s just perfect. One moment I am alone, the next Sally is here. And she is crying.
zh_text: 就在我走上公寓樓梯時，有輛車疾駛急停，「吱——」一聲停在了我身旁。我拿出槍，但後來看到開車的人正是莎莉（那正是車子爲何會發出「吱——」的聲音，因爲她的開車技術實在很爛，我甚至無法想像她怎有辦法考上駕照。我猜這鐵定是沿襲求職的傳統，也就是人人都該假裝自己和別人沒有兩樣、就和其他人一樣棒）。她打開車門，急忙繞過車子朝我而來，同時氣喘吁吁，彷彿才跑了六公尺就把她給累個半死。我拿著一只貓罐頭，早就忘了何時買的，就連公事包丟在哪裡我都搞不清楚。夕陽西下，微風徐徐，這會兒天氣不算太熱。一切都是那麼剛好——我才剛剛落單，莎莉就出現了。這時她一把鼻涕一把眼淚。

en_text: Sighing, I put a hand on her shoulder and ask her to tell me what’s wrong.
zh_text: 我嘆了口氣，把手放在她的肩上，要她告訴我究竟怎麼了。

en_text: I’m worried that my neighbors will walk by and stare at me. I’m worried they might think this woman is my girlfriend. I can do much better than Sally. In fact, I already have.
zh_text: 我很擔心路過的鄰居會盯著我看，也很擔心他們可能會誤認這人是我女友。我可以表現得比莎莉從容，實際上我也一向如此。

en_text: “Sally? What’s wrong? Why are you here?”
zh_text: 「莎莉？怎麼了？妳怎麼會在這裡？」

en_text: “Because you live here,” she says, trying to catch her breath. I wonder where she got my address from.
zh_text: 「因為你住這裡啊。」她說著，試圖喘口氣。我很納悶她是怎麼拿到我家地址。「好好好，你想幹嘛？

en_text: “Okay. What do you want?”
zh_text: 「好好好，你想幹嘛？」

en_text: She looks up and down the street, but for what I don’t know. There are only two parked cars. One’s empty. The other has two people in the front seat facing each other and talking animatedly. I ﬁgure the passenger is a hooker, and the driver a man short on cash.
zh_text: 她看看街頭巷尾，但不知在看些什麼。這附近就停著兩輛車，其中一輛空無一人，另外一輛則有兩人坐在前座對望、聊得相當起勁。我猜那名乘客是個妓女，而駕駛則是正好缺錢、找她調起頭寸的男人。

en_text: “To talk. To ask you something.”
zh_text: 想找你講話、問你一些事。

en_text: I suck in a mouthful of air and swallow it down. She’s going to cry even more when she asks her question and I have to reject her. One woman in my life is enough. Given the speed at which she pulled up, I ﬁgure she’s been busting for a while to get her feelings for me off her chest.
zh_text: 我吸了一大口氣吞進肺部。當她提出問題而我得要拒絕她的時候，她應該會哭得更慘吧。在我生命中有一個女人已經綽綽有餘。依她停車的速度看來，我想她鐵定是掙扎了好一陣子，才毅然決然坦承她對我的感受。

en_text: “Okay. What is it you want to ask?”
zh_text: 「好，那妳想問什麼？」

en_text: “I don’t want you lying to me anymore, Joe,” she says, her voice suddenly getting louder. “What?”
zh_text: 「喬，我希望你別再騙我了。」她說，登時擴大嗓門。「啊？」

en_text: “No more lies,” she says, and she adds anger to her increasing volume. I’ve no idea where any of this is coming from, and I’m not sure what to say. I can’t ﬁgure out what she means by my lies. I didn’t even know people like her were aware when they were being lied to.
zh_text: 「別再騙我了！」她說，提高音量的同時夾雜著憤怒的情緒。我搞不清楚她哪來這種念頭、不確定該說什麼、想不出她說的「騙」所指為何，甚至搞不懂像她這種人在被騙的當下居然還會知道自己被騙。

en_text: “Okay, Sally, just take a deep breath,” I say, and then, just to prove I’m just like her, I add, “Oxygen comes from trees.” She takes in a deep breath and her face seems to settle, but only a little. I ﬁgure she’s preparing herself to ask the big question, but she probably isn’t preparing herself to receive the big rejection. I will have to tell her that it’s not that I’m not interested in having a relationship with her, it’s that I’m not interested in having a relationship with anybody. It’s times like this that I see that having women like me this much can be a curse. It’s best to get this over with. “Okay, Sally, Joe can’t listen long. I’m on my way out.”
zh_text: 「莎莉，妳先深呼吸。」我說，然後爲了證明我就和她一樣，我又說：「樹會釋放氧氣。」她深吸了一口氣，從表情看來似乎已經平靜下來，但只是平靜一些而已。我想她正做起心理準備，要問重要的問題，但或許還沒準備好接受別人無情的拒絕。到時我得告訴她，我不是沒興趣和她交往，而是我根本就沒興趣和任何人交往。也就在這種時候，我才會了解有個女人這麼喜歡自己可是種災難。我最好速戰速決。「好，莎莉，我正要出門，沒辦法聽妳說太久。」

en_text: “But you’re just arriving!” she shouts, the frustration back on her face within seconds. “I saw you! I’ve been waiting since Friday night! I had to keep coming back, and back. I wanted to wait inside your apartment, but I couldn’t. I chose different corners to wait around. Sometimes I’d fall asleep. Sometimes I’d go home and rest a few hours. Sometimes I’d drive around the block, looking for you. I didn’t think I’d get a chance. I wouldn’t have, not on Friday night. Not yesterday either. But they don’t think you’re coming back. That’s why hardly anyone is left.”
zh_text: 「你不是才剛到家而已？！」她大叫，短短幾秒內又浮現起挫折的神色。「我看到你！我從禮拜五晚上就在等你了！我得這樣來來回回、去而復返。我原本想在你家裡等你，但我不能這樣，於是選了不同的角落乖乖等著。有時我會睡著，有時會回家休息個幾小時，有時還會開車在這一區晃晃，找找看你在哪裡。我覺得自己應該沒機會碰到你，鐵定沒機會，特別是在禮拜五的晚上，就算昨天也一樣。他們認爲你不會回來，所以幾乎沒人留下。」

en_text: Her face is red and puffy. It looks like she’s spent much of her waiting in tears. “They? Left? What are you talking about, Sally?” I ask, but of course she probably doesn’t know. She never does. Her world is full of kittens and puppies and good-natured, God-loving, extra-smiley people. She doesn’t have the ability to really understand anything at all. It’s probably a nice innocent life to be living if you aren’t aware of it.
zh_text: 她的臉又紅又腫，好像等我的時候都是以淚洗面。「他們？留下？莎莉，妳在說什麼啊？」我問，但她鐵定是不太清楚，她也從沒搞清楚過。她的世界全是貓啦狗啦外加生性善良、蒙主寵愛又笑臉盈盈的人，她根本就無法真的弄懂什麼事。要是人們自己不以爲意，或許這樣天眞爛漫的度過此生也不錯。

en_text: She wipes a palm across her cheeks, smearing the tears. “You have to tell me, Joe.”
zh_text: 她以掌心拭過臉頰，擦去淚痕。「喬，你要老實告訴我。

en_text: “Look, Sally, take a deep breath and tell me what’s so important.”
zh_text: 「莎莉，聽著，妳先吸一口氣，然後告訴我什麼事情這麼重要。」

en_text: “I want to know about your scars.”
zh_text: 「我想知道你身上的疤是怎麼回事。

en_text: Her comment throws me off balance. “What?”
zh_text: 我不禁心下一凛。「什麼？」

en_text: “I was thinking about them. They didn’t look old enough to be from your childhood.”
zh_text: 「我之前一直在想，那些疤並不像是你小時候的疤，反倒像最近才有的。

en_text: I remember coming home Friday and feeling that things in my apartment were slightly out of whack by a few degrees. I’m getting that same feeling now. Only it isn’t my apartment, but the entire street. The entire world. I tighten my grip on the can of cat food. I take my hand off Sally’s shoulder and rest it next to my pocket. The one with the gun in it. The people in the car parked up the road are looking at us. The passenger door has opened slightly. The driver is talking on a cell phone, probably organizing another date. The hooker is getting ready to leave.
zh_text: 我還記得禮拜五曾經回家一趟，感覺到公寓裡的東西有點反常、不太對勁，而我現在也浮現起相同的感覺，只不過這次不僅止於我的公寓，而是整條街、全世界都是如此。我緊抓住貓罐頭，放下搭在莎莉肩上的手，然後平放在口袋旁，也就是放著槍的那一邊口袋。車裡的人都在看著我們。乘客座的門開了個縫隙，駕駛正講起手機，可能是在安排其他日期，而那名妓女則是準備離開。

en_text: “Have I ever told you about Martin?” she asks, changing the subject. She obviously doesn’t care about the scars anymore. She’s probably even forgotten that she asked. She lifts a hand up to her face and takes another wipe at the tears.
zh_text: 「我有沒有告訴過你馬丁的事？」她如此問道，轉移話題，顯然一點都不在乎那些疤，甚至可能忘了自己問過這個問題。她舉起手，再次擦起淚痕。

en_text: “That’s your brother, right?”
zh_text: 「那不是妳弟弟嗎？」

en_text: “You used to remind me of him. But not anymore.”
zh_text: 「你常會讓我想起他，但現在不會了。」

en_text: “Okay . . .”
“Are you really retarded, Joe?”
zh_text: 「喬，你眞的是智障嗎？」

en_text: “What?”
“It was the parking ticket. That’s why I’m here. The address in your ﬁle at work is your mother’s address. The police had no idea where you live.
zh_text: 「停車票卡。我是爲了票卡的事來的。你工作的地方留的是你媽的地址，警方根本就不知道你住哪裡。不過我……」

en_text: But I . . .” “The police?” I ask, my stomach suddenly tightening and taking a sudden lurch downward. “What about the police?”
zh_text: 「警方？」我問，胃部霎時糾結成團，轉而下垂。「警方怎樣？」

en_text: “The police don’t think you’re coming back. They waited, but you never showed. I told them where you lived because I’ve been here. I helped you, Joe. At work. In life. I helped heal you when you were attacked. It’s my fault more people have died since then.”
zh_text: 「警方認爲你不會回來。他們等過，但你從來沒有出現，後來因為我來過，所以就跟他們說了你的住處。喬，不論工作還是生活上，我都在幫你，就連你遭人攻擊，我也幫你療傷，但從那之後卻有更多人死於非命，這一切都是我的錯。」

en_text: “You didn’t help me, Melissa did,” I snap, but of course she doesn’t know what I’m talking about. “Look, Sally,” I say, trying to sound calm, but the problem is I’m not calm. My voice is wavering; I feel like the world is crashing down on me. “What do you mean about the police?”
zh_text: 「幫我的不是妳，而是梅莉莎！」我厲聲說道，但她當然不懂我在說些什麼。「等等，莎莉。」我說，試著讓自己聽起來沉著鎭定，但我實際上非常激動。我聲音微顫，同時感到天崩地裂。「妳說警方？」

en_text: “You phoned me. I came around. I helped you, Joe.”
zh_text: 「你打給我我就來了。喬，我是在幫你。」

en_text: I look up and down the street. Cars are pulling into it from both ends. Vans too. Both doors on the parked car are open now. Neither of the occupants is a hooker. Both of them start toward us. The guy is tucking his cell phone into his pocket and reaching into his jacket for something else. Sally looks around at the noise of the sudden trafﬁc. She looks surprised to see so many vehicles in such a crappy street. Her mention of the parking ticket and the police not knowing my address is setting off a lot of warning bells. It’s shifting the world off its axis. I unzip my jacket pocket and slip my hand inside. I look at the approaching cars and vans. I look at the couple walking toward us.
zh_text: 我看起街頭巷尾，前前後後的車子都慢慢朝著路上靠攏，就連貨車也是。原本停在那裡的車子現在兩側車門都打了開，裡頭的兩人朝我走來——他們既不是妓女，也不是皮條客。那傢伙正把手機塞進口袋，然後伸進外套拿起其他東西。突如其來的車陣發出了巨大聲響，致使莎莉東張西望。一看到這條亂七八糟的街上停了這麼多車，她一臉詫異。當她一提及票卡還有警方不知道我住哪的事，這全都對我發出警告。世界開始天旋地轉。我拉開外套口袋的拉鍊，把手伸進口袋，並看著逐漸逼近的汽車、貨車以及朝我們走來的那兩人。

en_text: “I thought you were special,” she says, and she sounds disappointed. “I . . . I am special.”
zh_text: 「我還以爲你與衆不同。」她說，語氣聽起來十分失望。「我……我是啊。」

en_text: “I can’t believe you killed them.”
zh_text: 「真不敢相信那些人是你殺的。」

en_text: I take a step back. Slow Sally has ﬁgured out something the police haven’t been able to.
zh_text: 智障莎莉居然發現了連警方都發現不了的事

en_text: “What are you talking about?” I ask, looking over her shoulder. “You’re him. You’re the Christchurch Carver.”
zh_text: 「妳在說什麼？」我一邊問，一邊望過她的肩膀。你就是他，你就是基督城屠夫。

en_text:
I tighten my grip on the gun. I can’t use it out here because it’s too loud. But I can use it to force Sally up to my apartment, where I have other tools. Or to go for a drive in her car. Maybe somewhere scenic, like a trip into the bush. Anything. I just need to get the hell off this street.
“You’re wrong, and you can’t go around saying things like that. Look, come upstairs and . . .”
zh_text:
我緊握住槍。在這開槍聲音太大，我雖不能這麼做，卻能用槍脅迫莎莉進到公寓——我在那還有其他工具——或者要她開車載我前往森林旅行之類的風景區。哪裡都好，就是趕快從這條街上脫身。
「不對、不對，聽著，妳先跟我上樓，然後……」

en_text: “I gave them your address. I had to. What choice did I have? The house you went to on Friday, why did you burn it down?”
zh_text: 「你爲什麼要放火燒掉禮拜五去過的那間房子呢？我別無選擇，只好把你的地址給他們。一切都是不得已的。」

en_text: She glances over her shoulder in the direction I’m looking. Suddenly all the trafﬁc comes to the same kind of screeching halt that Sally’s car came to a minute ago. The two people walking toward me start to run. The warning bells get louder. The world shifts even further, things are spiraling out of control.
zh_text: 她也順著我看的方向瞄過自己的肩膀。剎那間所有車子都不約而同地發出了「吱」的煞車聲，和莎莉的車子在前一分鐘所發出的聲音一模一樣。朝我走來的那兩人開始奔跑。我心中警鈴大作，就連原本就已天旋地轉的世界也越轉越快、幾近失控。

en_text: “Jesus, what are you talking about?” I ask, watching the doors on the vans and cars opening. People in black clothing are starting to emerge. They start toward me. A wall of people wearing body armor. I recognize most of them.
zh_text: 「天啊，妳在說什麼呀？」我問，看著汽車、貨車全開了車門。一群黑衣人朝我而來，還有身穿盔甲的人圍成一道人牆，而且其中的成員我多半認識。

en_text: “I’m sorry, Joe.”
zh_text: 「喬，我很抱歉。」

en_text: “What have you done? What have you done?”
zh_text: 「妳做了什麼？妳究竟做了什麼？」

en_text: “Step away from him, Sally,” somebody yells. It’s Detective Schroder’s voice. No, this is impossible. “Impossible.”
zh_text: 「莎莉，離他遠一點！」某人大叫，那是史卓德警探的聲音。不，不可能。不可能。」

en_text: Sally shakes her head. She’s probably wondering how she could have got things so wrong over the last few months. I’m thinking the same thing. I drop the cat food, pull the gun from my pocket, and pull Sally toward me, my ﬁngers looping over her cruciﬁx and shirt. I point the gun at the side of her head. She cries out, but says nothing.
zh_text: 莎莉搖了搖頭，現在她或許心想自己過去這幾個月來怎能把事情搞得如此糟糕——我也是這麼想。我扔下貓罐頭，一手揪住了莎莉的襯衫和十字架、把她拉了過來，一手從口袋拔出槍來，並拿槍瞄準她的側臉。她雖驚叫失聲，卻啥都沒說。「你們抓錯人了。」我說，帶著智障喬的口音。

en_text: “You’ve got the wrong man,” I say, talking in my Slow Joe accent. I push the weapon hard against Sally’s skull. Somebody screams at me to put it down, to put it down, but they’re still too far away to stop me. Unless they shoot. And they won’t shoot, will they? I’m Joe. Everybody likes Joe. And I ﬁgure some of them probably like Sally too. I tighten my grip. I can’t face spending the rest of my life in prison. I can’t face that at all. Because that’s what’ll happen. They’ll see the gun I’m holding belonged to Calhoun. They’ll search my apartment. They’ll ﬁnd my knives. They’ll ﬁnd the videotape I made with Melissa. There’s no way I can Slow Joe my way out of that one. No way at all.
zh_text: 我拿著武器用大抵住莎莉的頭麤。此時有人朝我尖叫，高喊「放下、放下」，但警方和我相距太遠，遏阻不了我的所作所爲——除非開槍。不會吧？我是喬。人人都喜歡喬，而且我想有些人可能也喜歡莎莉。我握緊槍枝，無法接受自己將在獄中度過我的後半輩子。正因此事即將成真，我完全無法接受。他們將會看到我手裡拿的正是卡爾霍恩的槍、將會發現我的兇刀、將會搜起我的公寓、將會找到裡頭有我和梅莉莎的錄影帶……我無法讓智障喬逃過此劫，這回我束手無策。

en_text: “Put the gun down,” Schroder says. I’ve never seen him look so mad.
zh_text: 「把槍放下。」史卓德說。我從沒看過他這麼生氣、這麼……精明。

en_text: So . . . cheated. “You put your guns down,” I respond. “Or I’m going to shoot her.” “We’re not putting them down. You know that, Joe,” he says, trying to sound calm, but being betrayed by the slight tremor in his voice. “You know we can’t risk letting you go. Just put the gun down and nobody here has to be hurt.”
zh_text: 「我們是不會放下槍的，喬，這你非常清楚。」他說，試圖讓自己聽起來沉著鎮靜，但他語調中的微顫洩露出他的底細。「你很清楚我們不可能冒險放你走。你只要乖乖把槍放下，那麼在這的每個人都能毫髮無傷。」

en_text: Schroder’s a moron if he thinks I’m going to put the gun down. I wish Melissa were here. She would know what to do. Or Mom.
zh_text: 要是史卓德真以爲我會把槍放下，那他可是蠢到不行。眞希望梅莉莎在這。她要是在這，她就會知道該怎麼做。要不然媽在也好。

en_text: “I’m Slow Joe,” I say, but nobody answers. “I’m Joe!” I shout. They can’t do this to Joe. I’m one of them.
zh_text: 「我是智障喬，」我說，但沒人回答。「我是喬！」我大喊他們不能這麼對待喬，我是他們的一份子。

en_text: But they are doing it. They’re in control here, and that’s the last thing I want. Why are they so conﬁdent I’m their man? The answer suddenly hits me. My fear of what they’ll ﬁnd if they search my apartment has already come true. Sally said they were here on Friday night. They’ve already found the tape. Found the knives. Found the folders and the audio tapes. There’s nothing I can do here. No way for me to gain the upper hand, unless . . .
zh_text: 但他們就是這麼對待我。他們掌控了這裡的局勢，而那正是我最不樂見之事。他們如何肯定我就是他們要抓的人呢？我頓時找到了解答。之前我怕他們一旦搜起公寓就會找到什麼證據，此事早已成真。莎莉說他們禮拜五晚上就在這了，這意味著他們早已找到錄影帶、兇刀、資料夾還有錄音帶。如今我無計可施，全然處於劣勢，除非……

en_text: The idea doesn’t jump out of nowhere, because it’s always been there, a plan B always hiding in the depths, just waiting for the opportunity to jump out and kick me in the ass. Jesus, it’s still possible to regain control, but it’s the worst fucking way imaginable. Still, it’s either that or spend the rest of my life in prison. It’s a decision I need more time to consider, but I don’t have more time. I don’t have anything. Other than a gun.
zh_text: 我一直都有個念頭，這念頭一直躲在暗中、伺機「砰」一聲出現然後給我來個當頭棒喝，所以我不是天馬行空、胡思亂想。噢，我還有可能奪回主導權，只不過方法絕對教人意想不到。要嘛就那樣，要嘛就是後半輩子蹲起苦牢。我原本得花多點時間思考這個決定，但如今我時間所剩不多。除了槍，我一無所有。

en_text: The men are only a few yards away now, all their guns pointing at me. I decide to take away their control. I decide to make this all about Joe. I shift the gun from Sally’s head to my own. I dig it under my chin so the barrel points upward. Sally gasps when she sees what I’m doing. Nobody else does. I think of Melissa. I’m going to miss her. I would have thought having control would make me feel stronger for these few seconds, but it doesn’t.
zh_text: 現在那些人離我只剩幾公尺，槍口一致對著我。我決定奪去他們的主導權，決定爲了喬豁出去。我把槍從莎莉的頭移向自己的頭，頂住下巴，好讓槍管朝上。一看到我這麼做，莎莉倒抽了一口氣，其他人則是屏住呼吸。我想起了梅莉莎，我就快要失去她了。我還以爲一旦握有掌控權，就會讓我覺得自己在這短短幾秒間變得更強，但事實不然。

en_text: “Put down the gun,” somebody else screams, but I don’t.
zh_text: 「把槍放下！」某人尖叫，但我置之不理。

en_text: “Please, Joe. Please, we can help you,” Sally says, but if she had any clue at all she would know that nobody can help me now. I’m Joe. Slow Joe. I’m the Christchurch Carver. I’m the one who calls the shots. I’m the one in control. I’m the one who decides who lives and dies. My legs feel weak. I feel like I want to be sick.
zh_text: 「喬，拜託，大家都會幫你。」莎莉說，但她要是有大腦，她就會明白現在誰都幫不了我。我是喬，智障喬，基督城屠夫，同時也是那個下達命令、掌控一切並且定人生死的人。

en_text: I suck in a deep breath, close my eyes, and squeeze all the way on the trigger.
zh_text: 我深吸了口氣，閉上雙眼，然後直接扣下扳機。

en_text: Police Conﬁrm “Melissa” Link to New Murder Police have conﬁrmed that the ofﬁcer found dead in a central city park four days ago is a likely victim of Christchurch’s Uniform Killer.
zh_text: 警方確認「梅莉莎」涉嫌最新一起兇殺案警方已經確認四天前於中央市立公園所發現的警官屍體極可能就是基督城連續制服殺人魔（Christchurch's Uniform Killer）的被害人。

en_text: “We have evidence to believe that this new murder, of Ofﬁcer William Sikes, is related to the three others that are already linked with the woman calling herself ‘Melissa,’ ” said Detective Inspector Carl Schroder, who is leading the investigation.
zh_text: 負責偵辦的卡爾·史卓德偵緝督察表示：「有名自稱『梅莉莎』的女子涉嫌三起兇殺案，而警方業已掌握證據，相信先前所提的三起案件應皆與威廉·賽克斯警官（Constable William Sikes）遭到謀殺的最新案件有關。」

en_text: In all four cases, the victims were law-enforcement ﬁgures. Two of them were security guards whose bodies were naked when discovered by members of the public, and their uniforms were missing from the scene. The body of Melissa’s ﬁrst alleged victim, Detective Inspector Robert Calhoun, has never been found, but a video of a woman killing him was found at the home of cleaner Joe Middleton, whose trial for the Christchurch Carver murders is set for next month.
zh_text: 上述四起案件的被害人皆爲執法人員，其中兩人爲保全，遭民眾發現時全身赤裸，制服也不見蹤影，而疑似梅莉莎手中的第一位被害人羅伯特（暱稱鮑伯）·卡爾霍恩偵緝督察，其屍體至今雖未尋獲，警方卻在一位名爲喬·米德頓（Joe Middleton）的清潔工家中發現一卷卡爾霍恩慘遭某女殺害的影片。米德頓曾化身基督城屠夫犯下多起兇殺案，並將於下個月接受法院開庭審理。

en_text: The trial date depends on Middleton’s continuing recovery from wounds sustained during his arrest. Witnesses told the Christchurch press that he was holding a gun to his head when an unnamed woman knocked it and he ﬁred into his face, resulting in injuries that were serious but not life threatening.
zh_text: 米德頓遭捕期間曾受重傷，開庭日將視傷口復原狀況而定。根據《基督城快報》（Christchurch Press），目擊證人表示當事人持槍抵住頭部時，槍枝曾遭某位不具名女子敲落，導致子彈擊中臉部，雖然傷重卻無性命之虞。

en_text: Police have interviewed Middleton, but gained few leads in their hunt for Melissa, whose name is believed to be a pseudonym. The woman had been helping with their investigation days before Middleton’s arrest for the Christchurch Carver killings. Detective Inspector Schroder will not comment further, other than to say that she was a key witness.
zh_text: 警方曾多次借提米德頓問訊，惟對追捕梅莉莎一事所獲不多，且推測「梅莉莎」應爲假名。米德頓因基督城屠夫兇殺案被捕之前，上述該女連日來協助警方調查，史卓德偵緝督察除了聲稱該女爲重要證人外，並未對此多加評論。
